roles.title: Morticians, Undertakers, and Funeral Arrangers
roles.description: Perform various tasks to arrange and direct individual funeral services, such as coordinating transportation of body to mortuary, interviewing family or other authorized person to arrange details, selecting pallbearers, aiding with the selection of officials for religious rites, and providing transportation for mourners.

tasks.label: Oversee the preparation and care of the remains of people who have died.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Prep-room care of a decedent scheduled for viewing at a small/mid-size funeral home: verify identification and embalming authorization, position the limp body on the embalming table, wash/disinfect, shave, set features (eye caps, mouth closure), raise a vessel, cannulate and inject arterial fluid while massaging and monitoring drainage, aspirate and inject the cavity, close incisions, final bathe and dry. Includes the harder subset (autopsied remains, decomposition, edema, trauma requiring restorative art/wax and suturing, infectious cases, infants) where technique must be improvised case by case.

Presentation work in the dressing/casketing area: apply mortuary cosmetics and restore natural color, style or restore hair, manicure, dress the body in family-supplied clothing (limp limbs, rigor, fragile skin), place it in the casket with a lift, position head, shoulders and hands, arrange clothing and interior, then inspect and make touch-ups against the family's photograph before and during visitation.

First-call removal and transfer from an institution — hospital morgue, nursing home or hospice-facility room, or medical examiner's office: confirm identity and paperwork with staff, lift or slide the unclothed, sometimes heavy body from bed or morgue tray onto a cot, cover and strap, maneuver through corridors and elevators past staff and visitors, load into the removal vehicle, unload into the prep room.

First-call removal from a private residence after a home hospice or unattended death: enter an unfamiliar house at any hour, work around family members, pets and furniture, move the body from a bed, recliner or floor onto a cot in a cramped bedroom or bathroom, negotiate narrow stairs or doorways, and load the vehicle with dignity in front of onlookers.

Custodial holding and tracking between first call and disposition: tag and log the remains, place them on a rack, tray or cot in the refrigerated cooler, maintain chain of custody and ID over days, monitor temperature and condition, retrieve for identification viewings, dressing, shipment or release, and prepare/retrieve remains for air-tray shipment.

Crematory care of remains: verify identity and cremation authorization, place the body in a cremation container, transfer the container to the charging bier and charge the retort, monitor and adjust the cycle, cool, rake out and sweep the chamber to recover all fragments, remove metals with a magnet, process fragments in a cremulator, and transfer cremated remains into the urn with the ID disc.

sources.title: Japan's Lastel 'Corpse' Hotel Allows Check in Only to the Dead (PHOTOS) | IBTimes
sources.claim: A Yokohama 'corpse hotel' (Lastel) uses an automated storage-and-retrieval system that chills coffined bodies in a purpose-built rack structure and mechanically delivers them through hatches into viewing rooms on demand.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the custodial holding/retrieval portion of care of remains: refrigerated storage of the body in a container and machine retrieval for viewing, in a purpose-built rack-and-crane structure.

sources.system: Daifuku automated columbarium (AS/RS with stacker cranes)
sources.title: Innovating Remembrance – The Elegance of the Automated Columbarium | DAIFUKU
sources.claim: Daifuku sells and has deployed automated columbaria in which stacker-crane AS/RS racking stores urns of cremated remains and delivers a requested urn to a prayer booth when a family member scans an ID card.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated custody, storage and retrieval of cremated remains containers. Transfers to the holding/retrieval part of care of remains — same handling of a standardized container in a purpose-built rack, though not to handling an uncontained body.

sources.system: DFW Europe Automatic Insert Machine (AIM) charging bier; comparable B&L automatic loader
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: Automatic coffin insert machines (charging biers) transfer a coffin into a cremator fully automatically after a human moves the coffin onto the charger and presses the touchscreen; the loading door opens and closes automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Covers only the retort-charging step of crematory care of remains; the machine is loaded and started by a human and performs no identification check, chamber recovery, processing or urning.

sources.system: BodyHoist / mortuary hydraulic body lifts and cadaver carriers
sources.developer: American Mortuary Coolers, Mopec, PMT Scientific (equipment vendors)
sources.title: Raise the Bar with These Reliable Mortuary Hydraulic Body Lifts – American Mortuary Coolers
sources.claim: State-of-the-art mortuary body-handling equipment (hydraulic body hoists, cadaver lifts and carriers) is operator-positioned and operator-driven; the machine has no perception or autonomy for locating, grasping or moving a body on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the deployed technology for moving a deceased body is a human-operated lift, not an autonomous robot, so body transfer/removal instances have no autonomous cited system.

sources.system: Two-armed assistive dressing robot (learning from demonstration)
sources.developer: University of York Institute for Safe Autonomy, with TU Delft and Honda Research Institute Europe
sources.title: New dressing robot can 'mimic' the actions of care-workers | ScienceDaily
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing of a human remains laboratory research: a two-armed system learned care-worker dressing motions from demonstration and has only been tested in the lab, with a cooperative live person and simple garments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dressing a person's arm through a garment. Even for a cooperative living subject it is lab-stage, so it does not substantiate dressing a limp adult decedent in street clothes at funeral-home quality.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine - PubMed
sources.claim: The only robotic system regularly used on human remains is a forensic-imaging manipulator that performs automated surface documentation and image-guided post-mortem needle placement on a corpse fixed in a CT suite; it performs no washing, embalming, dressing or casketing.
sources.transferJustification: Closest robotic work on cadavers (imaging and needle sampling in a purpose-built forensic suite). It bounds the state of the art: no manipulation, positioning, embalming or cosmetic care of remains is demonstrated.

tasks.label: Obtain information needed to complete legal documents, such as death certificates or burial permits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Perform embalming duties, as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult case, unautopsied body in good condition, in the funeral home preparation room: disinfect and position the remains, shave and set the features (eye caps, mouth closure), raise and cannulate the right common carotid/internal jugular, run the arterial injection machine while massaging and monitoring distribution and drainage, treat cavities with a trocar, close incisions, wash and dry the body.

Difficult circulatory case in the prep room: obese, edematous, jaundiced, febrile, long-refrigerated or early-decomposition remains needing chemical strength adjustment, multi-point/split injection (femoral, axillary, subclavian), hypodermic and surface treatment, and re-aspiration hours later.

Autopsied or organ/tissue-donor case: sectional embalming of six regions through the open Y-incision and cranial cavity, treating and returning viscera, packing and suturing the cranium and torso, ligating vessels, in a funeral home prep room or hospital/medical-examiner morgue.

Trauma, burn, or post-surgical case requiring restorative art alongside embalming: closing wounds, suturing and waxing tissue, reconstructing facial features, bleaching and cauterizing, before or during arterial treatment.

Finishing work after arterial treatment plus small/infant cases: applying cosmetics and hair styling to the face and hands to match a photograph, dressing the remains, and casketing for viewing; includes small-vessel embalming of infants and children.

sources.developer: Institute of Forensic Medicine, University of Zurich (Virtopsy project)
sources.title: Virtobot 2.0: the future of automated surface documentation and CT-guided needle placement in forensic medicine - PubMed
sources.claim: Virtobot 2.0, a robotic system at a forensic medicine institute, autonomously performs 3D surface scanning of corpses and CT-guided needle placement for post-mortem tissue and liquid sampling — the closest demonstrated autonomous robotic intervention on a human cadaver, but it only inserts needles and does not raise or cannulate vessels, manage arterial injection and drainage, aspirate cavities, suture, or cosmetize.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic post-mortem needle placement in human cadavers. It is the nearest robotic capability to embalming's vascular access, on the same objects (human remains) in a mortuary/imaging suite, which is why it is cited; but it performs one imaging-guided needle insertion, not the multi-step dissection, injection-monitoring, aspiration, suturing and restorative work an embalming requires, so it does not transfer to completion of this task.

sources.title: SRT-H: A hierarchical framework for autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning - Johns Hopkins University
sources.claim: The most capable demonstrated autonomous soft-tissue surgical robot, SRT-H, performs one trained procedure (gallbladder removal) on ex vivo porcine tissue in a laboratory; nothing comparable has been shown for full-body cadaver dissection, vessel raising, cavity treatment or closure on human remains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous soft-tissue surgical manipulation (dissection, clipping, cutting). Cited as the ceiling of demonstrated autonomous tissue work; it operates on isolated ex vivo organs in a bench setup, not on whole human bodies with variable anatomy, and covers none of embalming's fluid management, aspiration, feature setting or cosmetic steps, so it does not transfer.

sources.title: US3528146A - Embalming machine - Google Patents
sources.claim: Automation in embalming is confined to fluid-handling equipment — arterial injection pumps and aspirators — which pressurize and deliver fluid after a human embalmer has made the incision, raised the vessel and inserted the cannula; these machines perform no manipulation of the body.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related equipment for this task: it is the only automated device in routine embalming use, and it establishes that the automated portion is fluid pumping, while all manipulation of the remains (incision, cannulation, massage, trocar guidance, suturing, cosmetics) remains manual.

tasks.label: Consult with families or friends of the deceased to arrange funeral details, such as obituary notice wording, casket selection, or plans for services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Remove deceased remains from place of death.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: House-call removal after an expected home/hospice death: director drives to a private residence at any hour, meets family and hospice nurse, confirms identity, transfers a limp 60-140 kg body from a bed (sometimes floor, bathroom, or recliner) onto a folding cot, shrouds and straps it, maneuvers through narrow halls, doorways and sometimes stairs, loads the cot into a removal van and drives to the funeral home.

Removal from a nursing home, assisted living, or memory-care facility: staff-escorted entry, deceased in a resident bed in a shared or private room, transfer bed-to-cot with a sheet slide, cover for dignity, route through corridors and elevator avoiding residents and visitors, exit at a service door, load into van.

Hospital or inpatient-hospice pickup: paperwork and release with nursing/morgue staff, remains in a pouch on a cooler tray or still in a patient room bed, transfer onto the funeral home cot, ID tag check, transport via service corridors to the loading dock, load and secure in the removal vehicle.

Transfer of already-containerized remains between institutions: pickup from a medical examiner/coroner facility, another funeral home, or airport air-cargo counter, where remains are already in a pouch, tray, or shipping container; verify paperwork and seals, move the container onto a cot or into the van, secure and transport.

Scene call under coroner/police direction: unattended, traumatic, or decomposed death in a home, vehicle, or outdoors; work alongside investigators, use PPE, place remains (sometimes fragile, soiled, or in pieces) into a pouch on a cot or backboard, extract from awkward positions and uneven ground, load into the van.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion automated pallet truck (vision-guided vehicle)
sources.date: 2020-12 (product page; product line in commercial deployment through 2026)
sources.title: Automated Pallet Trucks VGVs | Seegrid
sources.claim: Commercially deployed self-driving pallet trucks autonomously pick up, transport and deliver heavy palletized loads (up to 8,000 lb) in purpose-built industrial facilities, which is the mode in which a fixtured, presented load (e.g., remains on a standardized tray/pallet) would be moved to a transfer point.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous heavy-load material handling. Under the E1 counterfactual the remains arrive fixtured on a standardized tray/pallet in a known position, so the residual work is pickup, transport and delivery of a ~60-140 kg unit load inside a machine-built setting - well within demonstrated payload, precision and environment of these vehicles.

sources.title: Innovating Remembrance – The Elegance of the Automated Columbarium | DAIFUKU
sources.claim: Automated storage and retrieval systems handle human remains containers under machine control in purpose-built death-care facilities, gently storing and retrieving each container and delivering it on demand to a designated booth.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous conveyance of human remains within a purpose-built facility. It shows machine handling of remains to an accepted, dignity-sensitive standard in a setting built around the machine; payloads are lighter than a body, so heavy-load capability is supplied by the AGV evidence.

sources.system: Lastel automated coffin storage system (corpse hotel, Yokohama)
sources.title: Japan's Lastel 'Corpse' Hotel Allows Check in Only to the Dead (PHOTOS) | IBTimes
sources.claim: Purpose-built death-care facilities already move coffined adult bodies between refrigerated storage and viewing rooms with an automated storage system, i.e. full-body loads are handled by machine in a setting built for the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanized movement of coffined remains inside a facility. Corroborates that full-body loads are moved by fixed automation in purpose-built death-care settings; autonomy of the cycle is not documented, so it is treated as non-decisive corroboration only.

sources.title: RIBA-II, the next generation care-giving robot | RIKEN
sources.claim: The closest robotic capability to lifting and transferring a limp adult human body between surfaces remains an operator-guided research prototype that was never deployed in care facilities; no fielded system transfers a body from a bed onto a cot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bed/floor-to-chair transfer of a human body, the core physical act of a removal. The robot is guided by a caregiver through tactile controls and remained a prototype, so it cannot support an autonomous E2/E3 judgment.

sources.title: Industry Insights: Rovex Makes Autonomous Transport Robots for Hospital Patients | Automate.org
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots in healthcare facilities can tow occupied stretchers along corridors, but the demonstrated function is in-facility wheeled transport only - not transferring a body between surfaces, securing it, or loading a removal vehicle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a person on a stretcher through a human work facility. Shows only the corridor-transport fragment of a removal is automated at E2; the bed-to-cot transfer, shrouding/strapping and vehicle loading are unaddressed, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion at E2.

tasks.label: Close caskets and lead funeral corteges to churches or burial sites.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Funeral home chapel/visitation room: at the close of the visitation the director invites the family for a last farewell, removes flower pieces and personal items from the casket, adjusts the interior overlay, clothing and hands of the deceased, then lowers and latches the hinged lid (half- or full-couch) with mourners present.

Church or graveside: casket closed at the church before the recessional, or under the tent at the cemetery on a lowering device before committal — offsite, casket on a church truck over uneven turf, variable weather, family and clergy standing nearby.
Funeral home prep/staging area, no audience: casket lid closed and the gasket crank-sealed before transfer to another firm, air shipment, or direct burial; casket on a church truck or bier.

Leading the cortege by driving the lead car or hearse on public streets and highways from the funeral home to the church or cemetery: setting a slow pace, keeping the line of family vehicles together through signals and traffic, working with police/motorcycle escorts, and staging the vehicles on arrival.

Leading the procession on foot or through cemetery lanes: the ceremonial walk-out ahead of the hearse for a block on a public street, then guiding the cortege along cemetery roads to the correct section, halting the line, and positioning the hearse and pallbearers at the grave.

sources.system: Risong Technology flexible intelligent door/hood/lid assembly line (Changan Mazda)
sources.title: Flexible Intelligent Door Assembly Line of Changan Mazda Automobile Co., Ltd. — IFR case study
sources.claim: Robotic production lines automatically mount, position and fasten large hinged closure panels — engine hoods and trunk lids — onto fixtured car bodies using vision guidance and automated tightening, in mass production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic closure-panel assembly. A casket lid is a hinged panel of comparable mass and size that must be lowered onto a fixtured shell and latched/torqued; the automotive line does exactly this (vision-guided positioning plus intelligent tightening) at production quality, so the mechanical act transfers when the casket is presented fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.system: Batesville Manchester casket plant robotic paint line (four robots, overhead conveyor)
sources.title: How a Casket Is Assembled | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Casket lids and shells are handled as workpieces in a robotic manufacturing cell: matched, conveyed and finished by robots on an overhead conveyor in a casket plant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic finishing of casket lids and shells. It establishes that caskets and their lids are routinely presented, fixtured and handled by machines in a purpose-built cell at commercial quality, the environment assumed by the E1 counterfactual.

sources.system: DFW Europe automatic charging bier (coffin insert machine)
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: Full-automatic coffin charging machines transfer an occupied coffin along guided rails into the cremator in commercial crematoria, with the machine executing the transfer cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of a loaded coffin in a funeral facility. It shows machines can move and place whole caskets safely and with dignity when the casket is presented on a purpose-built rail/bier, supporting the E1 counterfactual for casket work.

sources.title: Las Vegas joins growing list of cities with fully autonomous Waymo rides — Las Vegas Sun
sources.claim: Waymo runs fully driverless passenger vehicles on public roads in many US cities, but the service is point-to-point ride-hailing; no cited system leads a multi-vehicle funeral procession.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous driving on public roads. It does NOT transfer to leading a cortege: the lead car must pace a line of human-driven mourner vehicles, hold the procession together through intersections, coordinate with escorts and stage vehicles on arrival — none of which Waymo's ride-hailing operation performs.

tasks.label: Provide information on funeral service options, products, or merchandise, and maintain a casket display area.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: At-need arrangement conference in the funeral home: director presents the General Price List and service packages to a bereaved family, then escorts them into the carpeted selection room, opens casket lids, demonstrates gauge, interior, hardware and personalization options, compares vaults/urns, answers questions and records selections on the statement of goods and services.

Routine upkeep of the selection room between families: dusting and polishing high-gloss casket shells and hardware, wiping fingerprints, straightening crepe interiors, pillows and throws, cleaning glass urn/keepsake cases, checking and adjusting display lighting, and replacing price cards, tags and brochures per FTC casket price list rules.
Room readiness before a family visit or visitation: vacuuming the carpeted selection room and adjoining hallway/lobby, in a building whose layout and furnishings the funeral home controls.

Reconfiguring the display: receiving a delivery of new full caskets or quarter-panel display corners, cutting bands and removing crates/shrouds, lifting and positioning 150-300 lb units on display stands or a rotating rack, removing discontinued models to storage, and restaging urn shelves and vault cutaways.

Off-site or remote merchandise information: telephone price quotes required by the FTC Funeral Rule, emailing or printing and mailing price lists and pre-need packets, and in-home pre-need presentations using a printed or tablet catalog at a family's kitchen table.

sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics America (navigation by Brain Corp)
sources.title: Whiz | Commercial Robot Vacuum | SoftBank Robotics America
sources.claim: SoftBank Robotics' Whiz is a commercially sold autonomous vacuum sweeper for carpeted commercial spaces that follows taught routes and reacts to obstacles without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: carpet vacuuming of a customer-facing room in a commercial building. Transfers to the funeral-home floor-care instance because the surface (commercial carpet), the room scale, and the institution-controlled layout with furniture obstacles are the same.

sources.title: Hotel Cleaning Robot | SoftBank Robotics America
sources.claim: Whiz units are deployed in operating hotels, vacuuming large areas of guest-facing carpeted space as part of housekeeping routines.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (carpet floor care in a public-facing room of a human work facility), evidencing sustained real deployment rather than a demo.

sources.title: Tennant Releases Small, Agile Autonomous Floor Cleaner – Ideal For Small Facilities
sources.claim: Tennant's T7AMR autonomous floor scrubber is deployed at scale in retail stores open to the public in North America.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended floor care in a merchandise showroom with public present; supports that E2 floor maintenance of a sales display area is routinely automated today.

sources.title: Building Robotics That Work Outside the Lab
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields an autonomous mobile manipulator that cleans hotel bathroom fixtures and surfaces in operating hotels, accumulating thousands of commercial cleaning hours; its skills are fixture wiping, not merchandise detailing, fabric arranging, or signage handling.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed analogue to detail-cleaning a display room with an arm; cited to show the frontier of autonomous surface cleaning is restroom fixtures with fixed geometry, not polishing casket finishes, straightening crepe interiors, or swapping price cards.

sources.title: 1X's $20,000 NEO Humanoid Robot Launches With A Catch: It Needs Humans To Do Your Chores
sources.claim: The leading general-purpose home/consumer humanoid marketed for tidying and fetching relies on remote human operators for real tasks rather than autonomy.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to support negative judgments: general-purpose mobile manipulation of varied household/showroom objects remains teleoperated, so it cannot substantiate casket detailing, staging, or merchandise demonstration.

sources.title: Innovating Remembrance – The Elegance of the Automated Columbarium | Daifuku
sources.claim: Automated columbaria use stacker-crane AS/RS to store and gently retrieve funeral urns in purpose-built racking, i.e. funeral merchandise handled by machines only inside machine-designed structures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated handling of funeral-industry goods. It shows machine handling exists only for small, uniform, palletized-style loads in purpose-built racking, not for uncrating and staging heavy finished caskets on showroom stands.

sources.system: Modular autonomous shelf-stocking mobile manipulator (ROS2/behavior-tree system)
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: Autonomous restocking of merchandise on shelves by a mobile manipulator remains a laboratory-stage system relying on fiducial markers and small packaged goods.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: arranging and replenishing merchandise displays. Cited for a negative judgment: even for light grocery items in a marker-instrumented mock store, the capability is a lab demo, far below staging 200 lb caskets or restaging urn shelves.

tasks.label: Provide or arrange transportation between sites for the remains, mourners, pallbearers, clergy, or flowers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: First-call removal: director drives the removal van to a hospital, nursing home, hospice or medical examiner's office (occasionally a private residence with stairs and family present), moves a cot to the bedside or morgue tray, transfers the deceased onto the cot, secures and loads the cot into the van, drives back on public roads and unloads into the prep room.

Funeral-day hearse operation: casket loaded onto a church truck and rolled into the hearse at the funeral home, driven in cortege on public streets to the church, unloaded with pallbearers, reloaded after the service, driven into the cemetery's internal lanes and carried to the graveside lowering device.

Family limousine/coach in the cortege: collect the family at the residence or funeral home, open doors and assist elderly or infirm mourners, follow the hearse in procession through traffic and into the cemetery, wait during services, return the family afterward.

Point-to-point passenger runs outside the cortege: fetching the clergy from the parish, driving out-of-town family from a hotel or airport to the church, shuttling pallbearers between the funeral home, church and cemetery on ordinary public roads at scheduled times.

Flower and equipment van runs: load floral sprays, easels, register stand, church truck and graveside equipment into the van at the funeral home, drive to the church and cemetery, unload and arrange the tributes around the casket or grave, then collect and redistribute them afterward.

Arranging outside transportation from the funeral home office: booking a livery/limousine company and a removal service, arranging airline shipment of remains (flight booking, known-shipper paperwork, permits, coordination with the receiving funeral home), and scheduling arrival times with clergy, cemetery and crematory. Phone, email and paperwork.

sources.title: Columbarium | Solutions | Daifuku Logistic Solutions
sources.claim: Daifuku's automated columbarium uses AS/RS stacker cranes that, on a card scan, autonomously retrieve an urn of cremated remains from storage racking and convey it to a worship booth in a purpose-built facility; commercially installed (e.g., Jigenji Temple, 2017).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage/retrieval of cremated remains. It is transport of remains between two fixed locations inside a purpose-built machine environment, with the load fixtured in a standard urn box and delivered on demand without human handling — the E1 form of 'transport the remains between sites'.

sources.title: Rising To Heaven: Japan's High-Rise, High-Tech Solution To A Shortage Of Cemetery Spaces
sources.claim: At the Kuramae Ryoen columbarium in Tokyo (opened 2017), a robotic system moves the family's remains container from a storage facility to the altar/booth for visitors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieval and delivery of remains to a ceremony space. Same object class (human remains) and the same purpose — moving remains to where mourners receive them — accomplished by machine in a purpose-built building.

sources.system: DFW Europe Automatic Insert Machine (automatic charging bier) and catafalque
sources.title: Charging Bier DFW Europe Manual / Automatic Coffin Insert Machine
sources.claim: DFW Europe supplies a full-automatic charging bier (AIM) that transfers a coffin from the charging position into the cremator, and catafalques used for internal transport of the coffin inside the crematorium; sold since 2008.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a loaded coffin between stations inside a crematorium. Same object (a casket of comparable size and 100-250 kg mass), presented fixtured on rollers, moved and delivered by machine in a purpose-built setting — the E1 form of casket transport.

sources.date: 2026-07 (product page retrieved; product in commercial sale)
sources.title: Powered Cremator Charger - LEEC
sources.claim: LEEC's powered cremator charger is marketed as an automated coffin-charging solution that removes manual handling of the coffin at the crematorium.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling and conveyance of a coffin within a purpose-built crematorium, corroborating that fixtured casket movement is routine commercial automation.

sources.system: Seegrid Palion AMRs (tow tractor, pallet truck, lift truck)
sources.title: Seegrid Celebrates 13M Autonomous Miles Driven to Date
sources.claim: Seegrid's autonomous mobile robots (tow tractors, pallet trucks, lift trucks) move palletized and fixtured loads between fixed pickup and drop-off points in customer facilities, with over 2,000 units deployed at 200+ sites and 13-18 million autonomous production miles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated material transport. Flowers, equipment cases, a bier or a body tray presented on a standard pallet or cart are loads of the same size and weight class that these AMRs pick up, move between stations and drop off unattended.

sources.system: Hong Kong International Airport Automated People Mover
sources.developer: Airport Authority Hong Kong / Mitsubishi Crystal Mover
sources.title: Automated People Mover, Airport Facilities & Services - Hong Kong International Airport
sources.claim: Hong Kong International Airport's Automated People Mover is a driverless train that carries passengers between separate terminal buildings at about 7,200 passengers per hour on a purpose-built guideway; in service since 1998.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless conveyance of people between two sites. Passengers board and alight themselves and are delivered on schedule by machine within a purpose-built guideway — the E1 form of 'provide transportation for mourners between sites'.

sources.title: Waypoint - The official Waymo blog
sources.claim: Waymo operates a fully driverless, paid ride-hailing service open to the public in multiple US metros, carrying passengers door to door on public streets and, since November 2025, on freeways in Phoenix, San Francisco and Los Angeles.

sources.title: Aurora Begins Commercial Driverless Trucking in Texas, Ushering in a New Era of Freight
sources.claim: Aurora runs commercial driverless Class 8 freight deliveries with no human aboard on public Texas highways, operating ten driverless routes across the Sun Belt by mid-2026; loading and unloading of the freight is done by people at the terminals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous road haulage of goods between two sites. It shows the driving leg of between-site transport is solved on public roads, while the loading/unloading at each end remains human work.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators autonomously fetch and deliver items (pharmacy bags, supplies) inside hospitals, using arms to open doors and ride ..., with over 300,000 pharmacy deliveries and 100,000+ autonomous elevator rides.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point delivery of small items inside a structured facility. It marks the current E2 ceiling — bagged items in bins — and does not extend to lifting a body, a casket, or large floral tributes.

instances.label: Funeral home chapel/visitation room setup: wheel the loaded casket (250-400 lb on a church truck) to the head of the room, square and level it, open the lid and dress the interior, then place 8-20 floral pieces (sprays on easels, baskets, standing crosses) around it, position register stand and photo boards, and adjust chapel/casket lighting and dimmers before the family arrives.

Church, synagogue, or temple funeral: roll the casket from the hearse over thresholds, carpet and steps to the chancel or center aisle position the clergy specify, orient it per the rite, drape the pall, and relocate floral pieces from the funeral home to the altar area within the church's rules on what may be placed where.

Graveside/committal at the cemetery: set the tent, chairs, greens and artificial turf over an open grave, position the casket squarely on the lowering device, place the casket spray and standing pieces brought from the chapel, and keep everything stable on sloped or muddy turf in wind, heat or rain.

Off-site or non-traditional venue: home visitation, VFW hall, hotel ballroom, park pavilion or beach memorial. Layout is unknown until arrival; furniture must be moved, the casket or urn table carried through narrow doors or up steps, floral pieces and portable lighting improvised into a space never built for a service.

Display and fixture work at the funeral home between services: receive and lay out arrangements delivered by florists, refresh and rearrange them for the next visitation, position candles, kneelers, flags, memorial tables and easels, and place or aim portable casket lamps and adjust track lighting for the room.

roles.description: Provide barbering services, such as cutting, trimming, shampooing, and styling hair; trimming beards; or giving shaves.

tasks.label: Clean and sterilize scissors, combs, clippers, and other instruments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-client sanitation at the barber chair: after each haircut the barber brushes/blows loose hair out of the clipper and trimmer blades, sprays them with a clean-cool-lubricate-disinfect spray and wipes them, drops the used combs and shears into the wet-disinfectant jar for the required contact time and takes out pre-disinfected replacements, and wipes down guards. Done in one to two minutes at the station while the next client waits.

End-of-day deep clean of the whole kit in the shop's back bar/dispensary: combs and brushes washed with soap and water to strip hair, gel and powder, then fully immersed in EPA-registered disinfectant for the labeled contact time, rinsed and dried; clipper blades unscrewed, hair brushed out, cleaned, disinfected, oiled and reassembled; everything dried and stored in a covered sanitized drawer or UV cabinet.

Shaving implements and blood-exposure protocol: spent single-use razor blades removed from the shavette/straight-razor holder and dropped in the sharps container, razor handles, tweezers and shears cleaned and immersed in hospital-grade disinfectant (or autoclaved where the state board requires it for implements exposed to blood), then dried and stored.

Maintaining the sanitation station itself: emptying and washing the wet-sanitizer jar, mixing and refilling fresh disinfectant at the correct dilution, labeling it, topping up spray bottles, wiping out the UV/dry sanitizer cabinet, and keeping the station inspection-ready for the state board.

On-location barbering (house calls, nursing-home rooms, dorms, weddings/film sets): tools cleaned and disinfected out of a portable kit using whatever sink, counter or floor space is available at the site, layout and water access differing every visit.

sources.system: Robosonic robotic ultrasonic cleaning cell (Blackstone-NEY / Cleaning Technologies Group, Fanuc CR-7i)
sources.title: Ultrasonic Robotic Parts Cleaning Cell Provides Precision Cleaning and Maximum Efficiency
sources.claim: Blackstone-NEY/Cleaning Technologies Group sells the Robosonic robotic parts cleaning cell: a Fanuc CR-7i collaborative robot moves small workpieces (up to 15 lb) through spray wash, ultrasonic immersion wash, ... and a dryer inside a purpose-built cell, with optional vision and force sensing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial precision parts cleaning. Transfer holds because the objects are small rigid metal items of the same size and mass class as combs, shears, razor handles and clipper blades, the process steps (spray wash, ultrasonic immersion, rinse, dry) are the same ones prescribed for salon implements, and the robot performs the load/unload/transfer between tanks that the barber otherwise does by hand.

sources.title: An Ultrasonic Cleaner for Barber Shops and Beauty Salons
sources.claim: Ultrasonic cleaning units are sold for and used in barber shops and salons to clean scissors, clippers and combs, and match the state-board-prescribed workflow (enzyme presoak, timed ultrasonic cycle, rinse, dry, chemical disinfectant or FDA-registered autoclave, storage).
sources.transferJustification: Same task and same objects: it establishes that machine cleaning of barber implements meets the regulatory standard once the implements are presented to the machine, which is exactly the condition assumed at E1.

Transfer holds because the objects are the same class of steel hand instruments, the required output (validated cleaned, disinfected and sterilized instruments) is stricter than a barber's, and the robotics cover the loading/unloading of the washing and sterilizing machines.

sources.title: Automated Washing Dosing Systems Replacement Parts | Shop STERIS
sources.claim: Automated dosing systems deliver instrument cleaning and disinfection chemistries into washer/disinfectors automatically, and industrial parts-cleaning systems include on-board chemical analyzers with integrated concentration control, so bath chemistry is maintained without a person mixing it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: maintaining correct disinfectant chemistry in an instrument-reprocessing machine. This is the machine-side form of the barber's wet-sanitizer upkeep — replacing spent solution at the labeled dilution — with the same accuracy requirement and stricter documentation.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing
sources.claim: Armstrong Robotics operates three 7-DoF arms with custom grippers that autonomously wash dishes in live restaurants around the clock, picking greasy, wet dishware out of bus tubs in an ordinary commercial dish room.

It is the closest E2 evidence found, but it handles large rigid dishware fed to a fixed station and a commercial dish machine; it does not substantiate hair removal from clipper blades, handling of open shears and razors, timed chemical immersion, or retrieving tools from barber stations.

tasks.label: Cut and trim hair according to clients' instructions or current hairstyles, using clippers, combs, hand-held blow driers, and scissors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard men's taper/fade haircut at a barbershop station: clipper work up the sides and back with multiple guard lengths, open-fade blending, scissor-over-comb and point-cutting on top, trimmer edge-up at hairline/ears/nape, finish with blow-dry and product, to the client's spoken instructions and a reference photo.

Longer scissor cut or textured/curly cut in a shop chair: sectioning, layering, thinning, blending to the client's requested shape, blow-dry styling to finish; hair type (straight, wavy, coily) and density vary widely between clients.

Simple uniform clipper cut ('number 2 all over', induction/buzz cut) in a quick-cut shop or a military-base barbershop: one or two guard lengths over the whole head, tapered neckline, quick trimmer cleanup, minimal styling.

Maintenance trim-up / line-up between full cuts in the shop: sharpening the existing hairline and temple lines with a trimmer or straight razor, cleaning the nape and around the ears, light clipper touch-up on sides; millimetre-level edge precision on skin.

Cutting a child, an elderly client, or a client who cannot hold still, in the shop: head moves unpredictably, the barber repositions the head by hand, works around ears and squirming, reassures the client, and still delivers a symmetric cut.

Cut performed away from the shop: home visit, mobile barber van, or a nursing-home resident's room, with a kitchen chair or bedside chair, improvised lighting, cape and portable clippers, and no fixed station.

sources.system: Survey of existing haircutting robot systems and prototypes (Gronier patent, Wighton arm, Stuff Made Here UR5e, Aldabbah patent, front-hair styling system)
sources.developer: A. T. Khan and Shuai Li (University of Oulu / VTT), Journal of Artificial Intelligence for Automation
sources.title: CNC-Inspired Robotic Hair Cutting: A Comprehensive Survey on Precision Personal Care Automation
sources.claim: A January 2026 peer-reviewed survey of robotic hair cutting reports that the hairstyling industry is still essentially entirely manual, and its comparison table of every known haircutting system lists only patents, DIY prototypes and single-purpose demos with no validated autonomous cutting system.

sources.system: Current haircutting robot demonstration prototypes (as reviewed)
sources.developer: A. T. Khan and Shuai Li, Journal of Artificial Intelligence for Automation
sources.title: CNC-Inspired Robotic Hair Cutting: A Comprehensive Survey on Precision Personal Care Automation
sources.claim: The same survey states that reliable, drift-corrected operation over a full haircut is beyond what existing prototypes can do; they run only briefly under constrained conditions, and no accepted quality metric for a finished hairstyle exists.

sources.developer: Shuai Li, University of Oulu / VTT Technical Research Centre of Finland (journal Automation, MDPI)
sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: A September 2025 peer-reviewed perspective paper on haircutting robots concludes that fully autonomous robotic haircutting is not currently achievable, and proposes teleoperation plus barber-supervised autonomy as the only near-term commercial route.

sources.system: Wighton custom scissor arm (2020) and 'Stuff Made Here' UR5e haircutting robot (2021)
sources.title: CNC-Inspired Robotic Hair Cutting: A Comprehensive Survey on Precision Personal Care Automation
sources.claim: The most-cited physical haircut robots are one-off DIY builds using depth cameras and pre-programmed paths that cut a single style, without systematic autonomy or safety guarantees.

sources.title: CNC-Inspired Robotic Hair Cutting: A Comprehensive Survey on Precision Personal Care Automation
sources.claim: The only commercialized robot that works on a client's head in a salon chair is Panasonic's head-care robot, which shampoos and massages the scalp with pressure sensors and fixed motion patterns; it performs no cutting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic shampooing/scalp massage in a salon chair. It shares the setting and safe scalp contact, but it applies fixed patterns with a soft washing head and removes no material; it cannot measure hair length, follow a cutting toolpath, or produce a requested style, so capability does not transfer to cutting and trimming hair.

sources.title: Automatic Hair Cutting Machine Video Is FAKE / AI-Generated
sources.claim: Viral videos circulating in 2025-2026 that appear to show fully automatic hair-cutting machines were analysed and found to be AI-generated rather than footage of real hardware, so such clips cannot substantiate a working system.

tasks.label: Clean work stations and sweep floors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-client floor sweep in a working barbershop: after a haircut the barber sweeps/vacuums the pile of clippings around the chair pedestal, footrest, along the baseboard and under the counter, while other clients, capes, cords and dropped clips are present, and must clear it before the next client is seated.

Between-client workstation clean-down: brush cut hair off the chair, headrest and armrests, spray and wipe the vinyl chair and headrest with disinfectant, wipe hair and product residue from the counter around laid-out clippers, guards, combs and bottles, wipe mirror smudges, discard used neck strips and cape hair into the bin.

End-of-day close-down: sweep and mop the whole shop floor including waiting area, wipe down every station counter, chair and mirror, empty the hair/trash bins, wipe the door glass and tidy retail shelves so the shop is ready for opening.
Periodic deep clean: scrub and disinfect the shampoo bowl and sink and the wet area around it, move chairs and rolling carts to clean behind and underneath, clean baseboards, vents and the hair trap.

Mobile/off-site barbering (private home, nursing-home room, event): after the cut, sweep clippings off carpet or an as-found floor, wipe down the portable chair/cape and any borrowed table used as a station, and pack up, in a room the barber does not control.

sources.title: π0.5: A VLA with Open-World Generalization

sources.claim: A humanoid performed multi-minute household chore sequences (unloading and loading a dishwasher, resetting a bedroom, taking out trash) autonomously from onboard sensors, in the developer's own staged home environments; press coverage of comparable demos recorded repeated failures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household object handling and tidying. Cited as the frontier of general manipulation cleaning; it is a curated lab demo (TIME observed dropped-laundry failures), so it does not establish worker-quality station cleaning in a real shop.

tasks.label: Drape and pin protective cloths around customers' shoulders.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine adult haircut in a barbershop: barber takes a cape off a hook, snaps it open, sweeps it across the seated customer's chest and shoulders, brings both ends around the neck over a paper neck strip, fastens the velcro/snap closure snugly but comfortably, and smooths/tucks the cape. Done in a few seconds, dozens of times a day, on customers of varying size and clothing.

Beard trim, shave, or neck clean-up: barber places a small cape or barber's cloth plus a towel around the reclined customer's neck and chest, tucks the cloth into the collar so hot lather and clippings do not reach clothing, and re-adjusts the drape as the chair reclines.

Child customer on a booster board or parent's lap: barber drapes a smaller cape on a squirming, sometimes resistant child, fastens the neck closure loosely enough not to alarm the child, and re-secures it repeatedly during the cut.

Shampoo or chemical service: barber applies a waterproof cape plus a folded towel at the neck at the shampoo bowl, arranging the drape so water and product do not run down the customer's neck or back, then swaps to a dry cutting cape afterward.

Mobile/on-location barbering: nursing-home room, private home, hospital bedside, or event pop-up. Customer sits in a wheelchair, dining chair, or bed; the barber drapes and pins the cloth around limited-mobility or frail customers in whatever seating and space is available.

sources.system: One Policy to Dress Them All (CMU robot-assisted dressing system, Sawyer/Franka-class arm)
sources.title: One Policy to Dress Them All: Learning to Dress People with Diverse Poses and Garments
sources.claim: Best-in-class autonomous robot-assisted dressing puts a single garment sleeve onto a seated person's arm in a lab, with the garment already grasped by the robot; it covers on average 86% of the arm and does not fasten any closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted dressing of a garment onto a seated human. It is the closest demonstrated capability to draping a cape on a customer (deformable fabric, contact with a live person). Performance does not carry over: the robot starts with the garment pre-grasped ('we assume that the robot ... a part of the garment around the opening of the garment shoulder'), dresses only one sleeve, reaches 86% coverage rather than reliable completion, and never fastens a neck closure.

sources.title: Bimanual Robot-Assisted Dressing: A Spherical Coordinate-Based Strategy for Tight-Fitting Garments
sources.claim: Bimanual robot-assisted dressing of tight-fitting garments onto human arms is still a laboratory imitation-learning study validated on arm postures, not a deployed service capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: two-armed dressing of a person, the arm configuration a caping robot would need. It shows only arm-sleeve trajectory generation in a lab; no grasping a cape from storage, no wrapping around the neck, and no fastening, so it does not substantiate completing the caping task.

sources.title: Close-Fitting Dressing Assistance Based on State Estimation of Feet and Garments with Semantic-based Visual Attention
sources.claim: Autonomous close-fitting dressing with force/tactile control has been demonstrated only on small garments (socks on feet) with a small number of seated human participants in a laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot dressing of a body part with force-sensitive contact. It marks the frontier of safe garment-on-human manipulation, but the object (a sock on a foot) and the absence of any neck-region work or closure fastening mean it does not transfer to draping and pinning a cape around a customer's neck and shoulders.

sources.title: Self-Wearing Adaptive Garments via Soft Robotic Unfurling
sources.claim: A soft 'self-wearing' garment prototype that unfurls itself around a wearer has been demonstrated in the lab as an alternative to manipulator-based dressing; it is a research prototype demonstrated on limited garment configurations, not a barber cape with a neck closure.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automatic donning of a garment onto a person without a human helper. It could in principle substitute for a draped cloth, but it is an early prototype with no reported reliability on a barber-style cape, no neck fastening, and no salon deployment, so it cannot substantiate worker-quality completion.

sources.system: Haircutting robots (survey of prototypes; proposed supervised-autonomy business model)
sources.developer: University of Oulu (S. Li), MDPI Automation

sources.claim: Robotics work aimed specifically at barbershops covers hair cutting and remains at the prototype/teleoperated or 'supervised autonomy' stage with a human barber present; no system is reported that prepares the customer by draping and fastening a cape.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic barbering in the same workplace. The review documents that even the cutting step is unproven and human-supervised, and describes no robotic handling of capes or customer preparation, so it provides no support for autonomous caping.

tasks.label: Apply lather and shave beards or neck and temple hair contours, using razors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-haircut neck cleanup in a barbershop: hot lather applied to the nape, behind and around the ears, then shaved with a straight/shavette razor so the skin is clean right up to a crisp blocked, rounded or tapered neckline, without cutting into the hair above; client seated in a barber chair, head tipped forward, skin stretched by hand.

Line-up / edge-up: razor used to finish temple points, front hairline and sideburn edges after clipper work, producing sharp, symmetric geometric lines on a seated client (common in fade and urban barbershop work).

Full traditional shave service: hot towel, pre-shave oil, brush-applied lather, two razor passes (with and against grain) over cheeks, jaw, chin, upper lip, under nose and throat, re-lather, wipe, cold towel and aftershave; client reclined in the barber chair.
Beard shaping on a bearded client: lather applied outside the intended beard line, razor used to shave cheeks and neck clean and to cut a defined beard outline along the cheek line and neckline.

Mobile / house-call or nursing-home shave: barber travels to a private home or care facility and shaves a client who may be elderly, frail, seated in a wheelchair or bed, with variable lighting, no barber chair and limited ability to hold the head still.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cutting/shaping of hair on a human head, which is the contour ('line-up', neckline, temple) component of this task; the review establishes that no fielded system performs such edge work.

tasks.label: Shape and trim beards and moustaches, using scissors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Barbershop chair: beard shape-and-trim included with a haircut. Barber drapes the client, combs the beard, scissor-over-comb to reduce bulk on cheeks/chin, point-cuts to blend the beard into the sideburns and haircut, checks symmetry from both sides while the client breathes, talks and shifts; finished to the client's stated preference in ~5-10 minutes.

Standalone beard trim service in a barbershop: consultation on desired shape, scissor work to set beard length and outline (cheek line, chin, jaw, under-lip), scissor detailing before/after clipper or straight-razor line-up, with hot towel and beard oil finish. Requires judgment on face shape and growth pattern.

Moustache-only scissor trim in the shop: trimming hair off the upper lip line, evening the two sides, tapering the corners; for handlebar or long moustaches, combing out and snipping stray hairs to a specific style, working within millimetres of the lips and nose on a live, mobile face.

Heavy, long, coarse or tightly curly beard in the shop: sectioning and combing wet or dry, repeated comb-and-cut passes, thinning shears, correcting asymmetry and patchiness, working around scars, moles, glasses and the client's jaw movement; longer service with frequent re-checks.

Off-site/mobile barbering: house call, assisted-living room or hospital bedside, client seated in a wheelchair, recliner or propped in bed under variable lighting with no barber chair; beard and moustache trimmed with scissors around tubing, hearing aids or limited head mobility, sometimes with a frail or non-cooperative client.

sources.system: Haircutting robots (field-wide survey of prototypes, patents and demo videos)
sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed perspective paper surveying the field reports that robotic haircutting remains essentially unexplored in the robotics literature and that no commercial haircutting robots have ... as of 2025; the authors propose supervised (human-in-the-loop) autonomy as a path to future commercialization.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task: robotic haircutting/hairstyling with scissors or clippers. It bounds the state of the art for scissor work on human hair; the review finds only prototypes and videos, none doing facial-hair shaping to a professional standard.

sources.title: Video Friday: This Terrifying Robot Will Cut Your Hair With Scissors - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: A hobbyist-built haircutting machine cuts head hair with scissors under computer control, probing the head to set length; the subject is the builder himself, restrained in a purpose-built rig, and the result is described as a passable, not professional, haircut. No facial-hair or beard work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting scalp hair with scissors. It shares the tool and the live-human hazard, but the machine works on a fixtured scalp with a vacuum-held single strand region and produces a rough cut; it does not shape facial hair around lips, nose and jawline to a client-specified outline.

sources.system: Force-controlled shaving robotic arm (unnamed Shanghai developer)
sources.title: China-made robotic arm autonomously shaves beard - Xinhua
sources.claim: A robotic arm from a Shanghai company was shown autonomously shaving a man's beard, using force sensing to adapt contact pressure; this is razor/shaver stubble removal in a staged demonstration, not scissor shaping of a beard to a style.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shaving facial hair on a live face. It shows contact-safe motion on a face, but removing stubble with a shaver is a different operation from scissor shaping, which requires length judgment, blending and outline design that this demo does not address.

sources.developer: Ajani, Assal & El-Hussieny (Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology)
sources.title: Towards Development of an Autonomous Robotic System for Beard Shaving Assistance for Disabled People (IEEE SMC 2019)
sources.claim: An assistive robotics research system used a UR-10 arm with an attached electric beard trimmer, with Kinect-based face detection and force-tracking impedance control, to plan autonomous shaving of a beard region; the feasibility was evaluated in simulation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated beard shaving assistance. It is the nearest published work on facial-hair robotics, but it is trimmer-based and evaluated in simulation, so it does not substantiate completed scissor shaping on a client.

sources.system: Front Hair Styling Robot System (myCobot 280 M5 with soft comb)
sources.title: Front Hair Styling Robot System Using Path Planning for Root-Centric Strand Adjustment (arXiv:2501.10991)
sources.claim: A research robot that styles front hair autonomously uses a small myCobot arm with a soft comb and closed-loop image feedback; experiments were run on a mannequin head with stiff ..., and the system combs and aligns strands rather than cutting them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of human hair for styling. It marks the frontier of autonomous hair handling — comb strokes on a mannequin — well short of scissor-cutting a beard on a live face.

sources.title: Remote Razor Shaving: The Ultimate Test of Human-Robot Trust
sources.claim: A widely reported robotic straight-razor shave of a human face used a fluid-driven teleoperation system with haptic feedback; the operator, a human barber, controlled the razor remotely, and the robot was explicitly not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: blade work on a live human face. Because control is continuous teleoperation by a human barber, it cannot support a positive judgment on autonomous beard shaping.

instances.label: Barber watches short-form and long-form video content (Instagram Reels, TikTok, YouTube) showing current fades, tapers, textured crops, and beard sculpting techniques, between clients or after closing, on a phone or shop tablet.

Barber reads trade press, brand newsletters, and product literature (new pomades, tonics, clipper/trimmer models, blade care), plus online forums and manufacturer spec sheets, to keep current on products and technique write-ups.
Barber attends a barber expo, trade show, or platform demonstration where educators perform live cuts on stage and vendors demo tools; the barber observes, takes notes, and photographs results.

Barber talks shop in the salon/barbershop: conversations with coworkers and distributor reps, watching a colleague execute an unfamiliar cut, and noting which styles clients are requesting week to week.

Barber completes formal continuing education or a manufacturer certification class (state CE hours, brand technique workshop), including classroom instruction and supervised practice on mannequin heads.

tasks.label: Shampoo hair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine shampoo of a male client's short-to-medium hair at the shop's backwash bowl before or after a cut: client reclined in the shampoo chair, barber wets hair, works in shampoo, scrubs the scalp, rinses to clear suds, towel-dries and wraps.
Post-cut wash/rinse to flush loose clipper hair and styling product out of the hair and off the neck after a fade or clipper cut, followed by a quick towel dry so the barber can finish and style.

Premium wash service in the barbershop: shampoo plus a several-minute scalp massage, conditioner or scalp/tea-tree treatment left on and rinsed, often with hot towel, sold as part of an executive cut or standalone head-spa service.

Client with long, thick, curly/coily or locked hair, or hair with heavy product/pomade buildup: barber sections the hair, works shampoo through the lengths, scrubs and detangles by hand, and rinses thoroughly until squeaky clean.

Shampoo as part of a chemical service in the barbershop: rinsing out gray-blending color, bleach, a relaxer or perm neutralizer at the bowl on a timed schedule, keeping product off the face and scalp irritation to a minimum, then a neutralizing/clarifying wash.

Off-premises barbering: shampooing a mobility-limited or bedridden client in a nursing home, hospital room, or private home using a portable basin, no-rinse shampoo, or a bedside rinse tray, with the client positioned as found.

tasks.label: Curl, color, or straighten hair, using special chemical solutions and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Gray blending / color camouflage on a male client's short hair in a barbershop: barber consults on shade, mixes a low-volume color and developer, applies it with brush or comb to temples, sideburns and top while blending against natural hair, protects the client's skin and cape, times the process (5-15 min), then rinses at the shampoo bowl, shampoos/conditions, dries and styles. Client is seated and moving/talking; result must look natural and unstriped, with no scalp irritation or skin staining.

Full-head permanent color, or bleach-and-tone / highlights on medium-to-long hair in a barbershop or barber-salon: sectioning the head, foiling or free-hand lightening, precise root vs. mid-length/end application, monitoring lift by strand-testing during processing, then rinsing, toning, neutralizing shampoo/conditioner, and blow-drying. Requires judgment about porosity, previous color, and scalp condition.

Beard, mustache or eyebrow coloring in the barber chair: applying a fast-acting dye or gray-coverage product close to facial skin and eyes, keeping color off the lips, cheeks and nose, timing a few minutes, then wiping/rinsing at the bowl and towel-drying. Very small tolerances near sensitive skin on a face that moves.

Chemical relaxer, texturizer or curl-softening service on coily/textured hair in a barbershop: basing the scalp, applying relaxer cream section by section starting away from the scalp, smoothing it through, watching processing time closely to avoid burns or over-processing, rinsing thoroughly, applying neutralizing shampoo until pH normalizes, conditioning and styling.

Permanent wave or chemical/keratin straightening on longer hair in a barbershop: winding dozens of small rods with end papers at even tension and consistent partings (or, for straightening, applying and flat-ironing product strand by strand), saturating with waving/neutralizing solution, processing with test curls, rinsing, blotting, neutralizing, and finishing.

Mobile or on-site chemical service: barber visits a client's home, a nursing-home room, or a group residence and performs a color or relaxer touch-up with a portable kit, no shampoo bowl (rinsing at a kitchen or bathroom sink), variable lighting, furniture and floor to protect, and a client who may be seated in a wheelchair or recliner.

sources.title: Panasonic to Unveil Innovative Communication Assistance Robot "HOSPI-Rimo" and New Models of Hair-Washing Robot and "RoboticBed" at International H.C.R. 2011
sources.claim: Panasonic's Hair-Washing Robot is the closest deployed/demonstrated machine that applies liquids to a human head: it 3D-scans the head and runs the wash cycle automatically, but only for shampoo/conditioner, in a purpose-built washing station; it does not section hair or apply oxidative color, relaxer or waving lotion, nor does it judge processing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated shampooing/rinsing of a human head. It shows a robot can wet, lather and rinse hair in a fixtured basin, but chemical curling/coloring/straightening additionally requires sectioning, selective root-versus-length placement, strand testing, timed neutralizing and skin protection, none of which this system performs; it therefore does not substantiate completion of this task at any tier.

sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed perspective on haircutting robots reports that the field is in its infancy, that robotics work on hair is limited to adjacent tasks such as brushing, combing, washing and scalp ..., and that fully autonomous operation on a human head is not currently feasible.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic haircutting and hair care on a live human head. The review surveys all known hair-directed robots and finds only brushing, combing, washing and massage systems, establishing that no fielded system performs chemical curling, coloring or straightening.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University / University of Southern California
sources.title: MOE-Hair: Soft and Compliant Contact-Rich Hair Manipulation and Care
sources.claim: MOE-Hair, a soft robotic manipulator with visual force estimation, autonomously performs three hair-care skills on human heads in a laboratory: head patting, finger combing, and .... It handles hair contact safely but performs no chemical application, sectioning, or processing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact-rich manipulation of hair on a human head. It represents the research frontier for touching and gathering hair, but its skill set stops far short of applying and processing chemical solutions, so it cannot substantiate this task even in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: DYMO-Hair: Generalizable Volumetric Dynamics Modeling for Robot Hair Manipulation
sources.claim: DYMO-Hair, a model-based robot hair-care system, performs visual goal-conditioned hair styling autonomously, but real-world validation is on wigs in a laboratory, and the manipulations are mechanical (brushing/detangling-style styling), not chemical application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robot hair styling. Even in a controlled lab on static wigs the system only reshapes hair mechanically; it does not mix, apply, time or rinse chemical solutions, so it does not carry over to curling, coloring or straightening services.

tasks.label: Provide face, neck, and scalp massages.

instances.label: Scalp massage at the shampoo bowl during a wash that accompanies a cut or shave: client reclined at the sink, hair wet and lathered, barber kneads the scalp with fingertips for 1-3 minutes, adjusting pressure to the client's reaction and avoiding sore or sensitive spots.

Brief neck and shoulder massage finishing a haircut: client sitting upright in the barber chair, caped, barber kneads the trapezius and back of the neck for 1-2 minutes, sometimes with light percussion, while the client moves and talks.

Face massage as part of a hot-towel shave or barber facial: client reclined in the barber chair, hot towels and massage cream applied, barber works cheeks, jaw, temples and forehead in circles with fingertips, working around eyes, nose, beard line and any nicks.

Dry scalp massage with tonic or treatment product: client seated upright in the chair after the cut, barber applies tonic/oil and works it into the scalp with fingertips through dry, styled hair for a few minutes without wetting the client.

Extended premium relaxation service (head-spa or 'royal shave' package): 10-20 minutes combining scalp, face and neck massage with hot towels, oils and client-specific requests for pressure and problem areas, managed conversationally throughout.

sources.claim: DeyeeMed's robotic-arm massage systems, which press and knead skin directly using Chinese massage techniques, are in service at clinics across several Chinese provinces, with staff overseeing several machines each.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: body massage by robotic arm in clinics/salons. Shows commercial robotic kneading of human soft tissue in human-facing premises, but demonstrated on the torso, not the head or face.
