tasks.label: Provide skin care and nail treatments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hot-towel facial as part of a shave/beard service in a barbershop: barber reclines the client in the chair, cleanses the face, applies steamed towels, works in pre-shave oil, then finishes with astringent and post-shave balm plus a brief face and temple massage. Client's face is uncovered and mobile; products must be kept out of eyes, nose and mouth.

Full men's facial in a barbershop or grooming lounge (30-45 min): deep cleanse, steam, exfoliating scrub, manual extraction of blackheads/whiteheads, mask application and removal, facial massage, moisturizer and eye cream, adapted to the client's skin type and beard line.

Targeted skin treatment after cutting/shaving: assessing and treating razor bumps, ingrown hairs, irritation or a nick — applying styptic, astringent, exfoliant or soothing/medicated product to specific spots on the face and neck, plus advice on aftercare.

Full men's manicure at a barbershop nail station: soak the hands, clip nails to length, file and shape, push back and tidy cuticles, buff the nail plate, hand and forearm massage with lotion, cuticle oil, sometimes a clear or matte coat.

Quick nail-grooming add-on after a haircut: file and shape the fingernails, buff them to a shine, light cuticle tidy, and apply a clear top coat and hand lotion; roughly 10-15 minutes at a station in the shop.

Mobile or off-site grooming visit: barber travels to a client's home, an assisted-living room or a hospital bedside and provides skin care (cleansing, moisturizing, post-shave skin treatment) and nail trimming/filing for an elderly or homebound client seated in whatever chair or bed is available.

sources.title: Fast Company Features 10Beauty, Robotic Manicure Machine (Fast Company article republished by Whipsaw)
sources.claim: 10Beauty's robotic manicure machine, piloted on the sales floor of Ulta Beauty stores in Massachusetts, autonomously scans the inserted hand with seven cameras and then removes polish, shapes nails with a crystal file (no clippers), pushes cuticles with a brush, buffs and paints.

sources.title: Fast Company Features 10Beauty, Robotic Manicure Machine (Fast Company article republished by Whipsaw)
sources.claim: In the same first-hand test the robot's cuticle step barely made contact and its polish application left gaps and polish on skin, so a human nail technician stepped in to finish the service; the reviewer concluded the robot is not yet as good as a human manicurist.

sources.title: Will Robotic Manicures and Lash Appointments Go Mainstream in 2026?
sources.claim: As of January 2026 the 10Beauty machine was in commercial service in two Ulta Beauty stores at $30 per manicure, 25-45 minutes, with more than 100 manicures completed since launch; full start-to-finish operation without a technician present was still anticipated for summer 2026.

sources.title: Nail Painting Robot Debuts in Beverly Hills
sources.claim: Clockwork's MiNiCURE, a fully autonomous nail-painting robot, has been deployed for paying walk-in customers in retail settings (Target stores, a Beverly Hills location) delivering a 10-minute nail service; Clockwork was acquired by 10Beauty in 2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (nail polish application) shares the workpiece — a client's fingernails presented to the machine — and the millimetre-scale precision and safe human contact needed for a barbershop nail finish, in an institution-controlled retail facility.

sources.title: Equinox Locations Add Aescape, a Fully Automated Massage Bed
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage table is in paid commercial service in Equinox gyms and Hyatt hotels, delivering 30-minute robot-administered massages to clients' bodies without a therapist guiding it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic massage) is the closest deployed case of a robot making autonomous, force-controlled contact with a paying client's body in a structured facility; it treats the back and limbs through clothing on a fixed table and does not cleanse, steam, extract or apply products to a face.

sources.title: The future of beauty treatments is…robots?!
sources.claim: LUUM's lash robot applies eyelash extensions autonomously to clients in studio and retail (Nordstrom/Ulta) locations, with a human attendant present but not guiding the robot in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (lash extensions) shows autonomous precision work on the face of a reclining client in a retail studio, but the client's head is immobilized and the robot only places individual lashes — it does not cleanse skin, apply towels/masks or extract, so it does not transfer to facial skin care.

sources.title: Panasonic Head Care Robot applies hot water and shampoo and wash the customer's hair
sources.claim: Panasonic's head-care (hair-washing) robot autonomously scans a seated client's head and washes it with water and shampoo using mechanical fingers; it was tested alongside hairdressers in a Japanese salon and in hospitals, but remained a prototype and was never sold as a commercial grooming service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated scalp washing) is the closest robotic care of the head with water and product in a salon, but it works on the hair-bearing scalp with the head cradled in a basin and performs no facial cleansing, extraction or product application on facial skin.

tasks.label: Identify hair problems, using microscopes and testing devices, or by sending clients' hair samples out to independent laboratories for analysis.
Measure, fit, and groom hairpieces.

roles.title: Hairdressers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists
roles.description: Provide beauty services, such as cutting, coloring, and styling hair, and massaging and treating scalp. May shampoo hair, apply makeup, dress wigs, remove hair, and provide nail and skincare services.

tasks.label: Keep work stations clean and sanitize tools, such as scissors and combs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-client reset of a styling station in a commercial salon: remove and shake out the cape, drop cape/towel in the hamper, sweep or vacuum hair clippings from the chair and the floor around it, wipe down chair arms and the counter, return brushes/dryers/product bottles to place, all within a few minutes while the next client waits.

Sanitizing hand tools after each client per state board rules: pull hair from combs and brushes, wash them, fully immerse in EPA-registered disinfectant for the labeled contact time, brush and spray clipper blades, wipe shears with alcohol and oil the pivot, then rinse, dry and store in a covered/labeled container ready for the next service.

Closing or mid-day whole-floor cleaning of the salon: sweeping/vacuuming hair and debris across the styling floor, reception and backwash area, then damp-mopping the hard floor, working around chairs, carts, cords and fixed furniture.

Cleaning the backwash/shampoo area and sinks: scrubbing and disinfecting shampoo bowls, faucets, hoses and drains, wiping the surrounding wet hard surfaces and the floor beneath, typically at close or between color services.

Linen and supply upkeep: gathering used towels and capes from hampers, laundering and drying them, folding and restocking each station, refilling color bowls, spray bottles and product, emptying station trash.

Mobile/in-home or nursing-home stylist cleanup after a service: sweeping hair off the client's kitchen, bathroom or bedroom floor, wiping the chair and any surface used, and cleaning/disinfecting the portable kit's combs, shears and clippers before packing them, in a room the stylist did not set up.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is a commercially deployed autonomous cleaning robot that navigates buildings on its own and cleans restroom fixtures (toilets, urinals, sinks) and floors and picks up trash using a no-touch spray/vacuum system, with near-zero staff intervention after a one-time site setup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cleaning and disinfecting of hard fixtures, basins and floors in a fixed-layout human facility. Salon backwash bowls, counters and hard floors are comparable objects and soils (water, hair, product residue) requiring spray, scrub and vacuum rather than fine manipulation.

sources.title: AB Vassilopoulos Deploys 25 Gausium Autonomous Cleaning Robots Across Greece — First Large-Scale Retail Rollout
sources.claim: Gausium Omnie scrubbers and compact Phantas S1 Pro cleaning robots were rolled out across a Greek supermarket chain's national store network between January and May 2026, autonomously sweeping, vacuuming and scrubbing floors in furniture-dense retail spaces during operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-floor sweeping/vacuuming and damp scrubbing of a small commercial retail floor cluttered with fixtures. A salon floor is the same class of hard-floor space and debris load; Phantas is explicitly built for compact, furniture-dense facilities.

sources.title: Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport to Deploy Floor Cleaning Robot
sources.claim: Avidbots Neo is a fully ... deployed in airports, malls, universities and warehouses, navigating with AI, cameras and 3D sensors and adapting to obstacles rather than following a fixed pre-programmed route.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous floor cleaning inside a busy institution-controlled human facility, establishing that whole-floor sweep-and-mop work of the kind done at salon close is completed autonomously at commercial quality in E2 settings.

sources.title: Bryan Health Uses New Robotic Technology to Clean and Sterilize Surgical Instruments
sources.claim: At Bryan Medical Center, the STERIS ATLAS Workflow Automation Vehicle autonomously collects racks of pre-cleaned surgical instruments from the decontamination sink counter, transports them and loads them into washer-disinfectors, navigating around staff with laser and sonar guidance as part of a department that processes over 5,000 instruments a day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling and reprocessing of racked hand instruments (including surgical scissors) to a validated disinfection standard — the same operation as immersing salon shears and combs for a labeled contact time, but with the tools presented in fixtures.

sources.system: Autonomous instrument tray assembly system (Staubli TX2-60L + YOLO12/ResNet perception)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Instrument Tray Assembly for Sterile Processing Applications
sources.claim: A fully automated robotic cell ... Staubli TX2-60L arm with a custom gripper and a trained vision pipeline autonomously sorts individual surgical instruments and packs them into sterile trays with 3D-printed dividers and holders, with fewer tool-to-tool collisions than human-assembled trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grasping, sorting and racked storage of small metal hand tools of the same class as barber shears and clippers, in a fixtured cell — the load/unload and put-away steps that bracket disinfection of salon tools.

sources.title: Sterile Reprocessing Goes High Tech - Hot Technology
sources.claim: Automated washer-disinfectors with conveyors that pull racks of instruments through validated wash and thermal-disinfection cycles are standard, widely offered reprocessing equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine cleaning and disinfection of racked hand instruments to a documented contact-time standard, equivalent in output to immersing combs and shears in an EPA-registered disinfectant and drying them.

sources.title: Intelligent robots for commercial laundries (IFR case study)
sources.claim: sewts' VELUM robotic system autonomously picks limp, crumpled terry towels and feeds them crease-free into existing folding machines in industrial laundries, installed and running in production at Greif Textile Mietsysteme since November 2022 at roughly 500-600 textiles per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic handling of used terry towels through wash-dry-fold lines — the same deformable objects (salon towels and capes) and the same laundering output, achieved where the textiles are presented to the machine.

sources.system: Commercial cleaning robots (CC201 vacuum-scrubber; commercial vacuum bots)
sources.title: Commercial Cleaning Robot CC201 / Exploring commercial cleaning robot solutions for large hotel spaces
sources.claim: Commercial autonomous vacuum and vacuum-plus-scrubber robots sold for hotels, offices and retail are specified for dry debris removal including hair, with a front vacuum stage collecting dust and hair ahead of the scrubber.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous removal of hair and fine debris from commercial floors, the specific soil produced at a salon station, confirming the debris type is within the machines' rated duty.

sources.title: pi-0.5: a VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 vision-language-action model let a mobile manipulator perform multi-stage cleaning behaviors — picking up items, wiping spills, putting dishes in the sink — in homes never seen in training, but the developers state it is far from perfect ... frequently errs in both semantics and motor commands.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general tidying/wiping in unstructured homes; cited to show the frontier of unstructured-setting cleanup, which remains below the reliability an employer would accept for a paid post-service cleanup.

tasks.label: Bleach, dye, or tint hair, using applicator or brush.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Salon chair, single-process permanent color / root retouch with gray coverage: stylist drapes the client, mixes color and developer, sections the head into quadrants, applies with a tint brush to 1/4-inch regrowth line without staining scalp or skin, then pulls through ends; timed processing then rinse.

Salon chair, lightening service: weaving fine sections with a tail comb, placing bleach on foils or freehand balayage painting with a brush/board, feathering the bleach away from the root band, saturating evenly on a moving, seated human client.

Salon: toner, gloss or demi-permanent applied at the chair or shampoo bowl after lightening, worked through wet or towel-dried hair with brush and gloved hands, monitored for a few minutes and rinsed at the exact moment the target tone is reached.

Salon: vivid/fashion color or color correction on previously colored, damaged or textured hair — multi-zone placement of two or more formulas, careful bleach placement to avoid overlap, adjusting formula mid-service based on how the hair lifts.

Mobile/in-home service: stylist colors a client's hair in the client's kitchen, living room or a nursing-home bedroom, with an ordinary chair, a towel, ad-hoc lighting and no salon fixtures; client may be frail or unable to hold still.

Salon: small-area tint work — men's gray blending at the temples, beard/mustache tint, eyebrow tinting with a small applicator brush, or refreshing color on a wig or hairpiece mounted on a block at the station.

sources.developer: MIT CSAIL / Harvard Soft Math Lab
sources.title: MIT unveils robot that can brush your hair
sources.claim: MIT CSAIL's RoboWig is an autonomous robot arm with a sensorized soft brush and camera that plans and executes brush-outs; it was tested on wigs of varying curliness in a lab, not on live clients, and it only combs hair — it does not section, foil, or apply chemical color.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic manipulation of human hair with a brush. It is the closest demonstrated robotic hair-handling capability, but it operates on static wigs in a lab, handles no chemicals, and performs no sectioning, root-line precision, foiling or timed processing, so it does not substantiate completing a coloring service at worker quality.

sources.title: Panasonic Testing Head Care Robot At Salon
sources.claim: Panasonic's Head Care Robot autonomously washes and massages a client's scalp with 24 sensor-guided fingers and dispenses shampoo/conditioner; it was trialed in a Japanese salon, but it only rinses/lathers a supine head in a basin and performs no brush-applied, sectioned color placement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = machine application of liquid product to a client's hair in a salon. It shows a machine can safely contact a human head, but the product is sprayed over a whole scalp in a fixed basin; it cannot place bleach on a regrowth band, weave foils, or judge processing, so it does not transfer to bleaching/dyeing with an applicator or brush.

sources.title: L'Oreal unveils Colorsonic at-home hair coloring device at CES 2022
sources.claim: L'Oreal's Colorsonic automates mixing and even dispersal of hair color, but it is a handheld wand that a person combs through the hair — a human, not a machine, positions and moves it, so it is not a robotic system and cannot perform the service unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Same task (applying hair color), but the device is human-held and human-guided; the placement judgment and all motion come from the person, so it cannot support a positive robotic judgment.

tasks.label: Cut, trim and shape hair or hairpieces, based on customers' instructions, hair type, and facial features, using clippers, scissors, trimmers and razors.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Women's haircut in a salon: consultation about desired length/shape, shampoo, sectioning and wet scissor-cutting of layers, graduation and perimeter line, cross-checking, then dry refinement after blow-dry; the client's head moves and hair type varies.

Men's/short haircut in a salon or barbershop chair: clipper taper or fade with guard changes, scissor-over-comb blending, detailing around ears, sideburns and nape with trimmer and razor, plus neck line-up.

Quick trims and simple cuts: bang/fringe trims, dusting split ends, one-length trims between appointments, and children's cuts where the client fidgets; usually done dry in the salon chair in 10-15 minutes.
Textured, curly or coily hair cut curl-by-curl or dry, and specialty techniques (razor cutting, thinning/texturizing shears, point cutting) chosen for hair density and facial features, in the salon.

Cutting and shaping hairpieces, wigs, toppers and extensions: trimming a wig on a canvas block or mannequin head at a workstation, and customizing/blending it after it is installed on the client's head.

Mobile/on-site cutting: the stylist travels to a client's home, an assisted-living resident's room, or a hospital bedside and cuts a seated or reclined client with portable clippers and shears in a space not laid out for the work.

sources.system: Haircutting robots (field-wide review of architectures and prototypes)
sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed 2025 perspective on haircutting robots concludes that fully autonomous robotic haircutting is not currently feasible and proposes teleoperation/supervised autonomy as the near-term path to commercialization.
sources.transferJustification: Directly about this task; cited as evidence on the state of the field, not as a capable system.

sources.title: Video Friday: This Terrifying Robot Will Cut Your Hair With Scissors - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: A real purpose-built haircutting machine using scissors, a vacuum to tension hair and computer-controlled positioning cut a seated person's hair; covered by IEEE Spectrum.

sources.title: This inventor built a quarantine haircut robot and bravely tried it on himself
sources.claim: That same haircutting machine's output fell short of professional quality and it could not cut hair around the ears and neck, so it did not deliver a finished, salon-acceptable haircut.

sources.system: Viral 'automatic hair cutting machine' / barber pod videos
sources.title: Is the Dubai haircutting machine real? Viral barber pod videos debunked - Primetimer
sources.claim: The widely circulated viral videos of automatic hair-cutting machines and robot barber pods are AI-generated fabrications, not demonstrations of a working system.
sources.transferJustification: Bears on this task by showing that the popular claims of deployed haircutting robots are not real demonstrations.

sources.system: Noematrix Brain 2.0 robotic arm shaving demo
sources.title: Shanghai's Noematrix Goes Viral with Brain 2.0 Robot Shaving Demo
sources.claim: A robotic arm applied shaving cream and shaved a person's face with a razor in a company demonstration, showing blade contact work on a human head; autonomy was not independently established and no hair shaping was performed.
sources.transferJustification: Face shaving is the nearest grooming task involving a blade on a human head, but it does not transfer to cutting and shaping a hairstyle to a customer's instructions, and its autonomy is unclear.

sources.system: ARTAS / ARTAS iX robotic hair restoration system
sources.title: ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplants | Robotic FUE Hair Transplants - Bernstein Medical
sources.claim: The only robotic system routinely working on scalp hair in commercial settings is a hair-transplant harvesting robot used in physician-run clinics; it identifies and extracts follicular units rather than cutting or shaping hair to a style.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precision robotic work on hair on a live human head in a controlled facility. It substantiates only follicle punching on a shaved donor area, not scissor/clipper shaping of a hairstyle.

tasks.label: Shampoo, rinse, condition, and dry hair and scalp or hairpieces with water, liquid soap, or other solutions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard shampoo-bowl service in a full-service salon or barbershop before a cut or blow-dry: adult (or child) client reclined at the bowl, hair wet down, one or two shampoo lathers with scalp massage, thorough rinse, conditioner applied and rinsed, hair towel-wrapped and rough-dried/blow-dried. Hair length, density and texture vary widely; water temperature and pressure adjusted to client comfort.

Rinse-out and cleanse following a chemical service: foils, caps or perm rods removed at the bowl, color/bleach/relaxer rinsed until water runs clear, product emulsified and shampooed out without staining skin, ears or clothing, neutralizer/toner or acidic conditioner applied and rinsed, hair blotted and towel-dried. Timing-sensitive and done on a processing client.

Deep-conditioning or head-spa wash: clarifying or protein/moisture mask or bond treatment applied after shampooing, processed (sometimes under heat), then rinsed thoroughly and dried; client chosen mode depends on scalp/hair condition (dry, oily, damaged).

Targeted scalp work: stylist parts the hair into sections and applies a medicated, exfoliating or dandruff solution directly along the partings, works it into the scalp by hand, then rinses and dries; includes visual/tactile assessment of the scalp skin and adjusting product accordingly.

Shampooing clients who need extra care: frail elderly or mobility-limited clients at a salon or a care-facility/assisted-living salon (occasionally at the bedside or in a client's home), where the head must be supported, water kept out of eyes and ears, and the wash done gently and quickly around limited neck extension.

Washing, conditioning and drying hairpieces off the head in the salon back room: wig, topper or clip-in extensions detangled, soaked and washed with wig shampoo in a basin, conditioned, rinsed, blotted and set on a block/stand to dry before styling.

sources.title: Hair care gets a high-tech upgrade with AI-powered washers | EYESHENZHEN
sources.claim: Shenzhen EAIN Technology's AI hair-washing machine, a dual-robotic-arm unit installed in dedicated hair-washing shops in Shenzhen (500+ stores reported, ~50 customers/day per store), autonomously washes a reclining customer's hair after the customer lies down.

sources.title: Hair care gets a high-tech upgrade with AI-powered washers | EYESHENZHEN
sources.claim: The deployed EAIN machine runs a complete shampoo-and-condition cycle (two shampoos, a conditioning cycle, final rinse, ~15 min for long hair) and selects a treatment mode from a staff scalp test; customers dry their hair afterwards with the shop's dryer options.

sources.title: Tangled in debates, AI makes an entry to salons - Chinadaily.com.cn
sources.claim: Automated 'AI hair washing' machines are in commercial use in salons/shops across several Chinese cities; the machine performs rinses, shampoo rounds and conditioner application while a shop employee only does a pre-wash scalp check and points the customer to a dryer.

sources.title: Panasonic's robot gives a 16-finger, automated hair washing - Computerworld
sources.claim: The Panasonic hair-washing robot was built specifically to take over hair washing of elderly and disabled people for caregivers in hospitals and health-care ..., scanning each head in 3D to set pressure.

sources.title: Tetoit Wig Cleaning Machine for Human Hair and Synthetic Wigs
sources.claim: A commercially sold automated wig-cleaning machine runs a hands-free fill/clean/rinse/spin cycle on a human-hair or synthetic wig loaded into its basket with cleanser added.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed off the head: washing, rinsing and water-extracting a hairpiece. The object (wig hair fibres) and the chemistry (cleanser/conditioner plus water) match the salon hand-wash of a wig; only the presentation differs, and at E1 the wig is loaded into the fixture by the environment.

tasks.label: Analyze patrons' hair and other physical features to determine and recommend beauty treatment or suggest hair styles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: New client's first-time consultation before a haircut in a salon chair: stylist looks at face shape, head shape, hair texture, density, growth/cowlick patterns and current condition, asks about lifestyle and styling time, and recommends a cut/style. Output is a spoken recommendation and agreed plan.

Color consultation: stylist assesses natural level, existing artificial pigment or prior box color, regrowth, porosity, elasticity and overall integrity, plus skin tone and eye color, then recommends a color service (gloss, balayage, full color, correction) and a formulation approach, including whether it should be staged over multiple visits.

Returning regular client at the start of a routine appointment: brief check of regrowth, fade of previous color, condition changes since last visit, and whether the existing shape still works; confirms or adjusts the standing plan and suggests add-ons such as a gloss or trim.

Hair and scalp problem assessment: client presents breakage, dryness, chemical damage, flaking, itching, or noticeable thinning; stylist inspects scalp and strands, recommends in-salon treatments and a home product regimen, or advises referral to a dermatologist and declines a requested service.

Chemical texture consultation (relaxer, perm, keratin/smoothing): stylist evaluates curl pattern, previous chemical history, porosity and elasticity, may perform a strand or test-curl, and recommends whether the service can be done safely and which formulation strength to use.

Special-occasion, bridal, wig or extension consultation: stylist assesses hair length, density, attachment points, facial features and the client's outfit or event, and recommends an updo, extension method, or wig style, often with photo references.

tasks.label: Massage and treat scalp for hygienic and remedial purposes, using hands, fingers, or vibrating equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard shampoo-bowl service in a full-service salon: client reclined at the shampoo bowl, hair wetted, shampoo applied, 2-5 minutes of fingertip scalp massage in circular motions with pressure adapted to the client, then rinse. Routine hygienic purpose, ordinary indoor salon conditions.

Routine scalp treatment at the bowl: applying a medicated/anti-dandruff shampoo, scalp oil, or deep conditioner over the whole scalp, massaging it in to stimulate circulation and distribute product, holding for a few minutes, then rinsing. Salon shampoo area, standard equipment.

Premium head-spa / remedial scalp service (30-60 min): scalp scope or visual analysis, product chosen for the condition, hair parted into sections and an exfoliating scrub or serum worked into specific areas with fingertips, steam or hot towel, extended massage of scalp plus nape, neck and shoulders, rinse and finishing treatment. Salon or day-spa treatment room.

Dry scalp massage at the styling or barber chair: client seated upright, stylist/barber gives a short stimulating fingertip massage or runs a handheld vibrating/electric scalp massager over the dry scalp, sometimes with tonic, as an add-on to a cut or shave. Salon or barbershop floor.

Scalp care for elderly or limited-mobility clients in an institutional setting: nursing-home or hospital beauty room (or bedside with a portable basin), fragile or sensitive scalps, clients who cannot hold position well, gentler pressure and hygiene-focused cleansing and massage.

Mobile / house-call service: stylist travels to a client's home, improvises a wash station at a kitchen sink or with a portable basin, and gives a shampoo with scalp massage and treatment. Layout differs at every house, lighting and water access vary, pets and family present.

sources.title: Robotics in Massage: A Systematic Review - PMC
sources.claim: A peer-reviewed systematic review of massage robots reports a robotic scalp massage system that used machine-learning-planned water-jet trajectories aimed at desired positions on the human scalp and was used with bed-bound patients in a care setting.

sources.system: ARTAS iX Robotic Hair Restoration System
sources.title: ARTAS Robotic Hair Restoration Treatments | Venus Concept
sources.claim: The ARTAS iX robot is an FDA-cleared, commercially installed 7-axis robotic arm that images and works directly on a patient's scalp and hair with 0.1 mm repeatability in clinics under physician supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic follicular-unit harvesting. It shows commercially accepted, image-guided, force- and position-controlled robotic contact with a live human scalp through hair inside an ordinary human-run facility (a clinic), i.e. the sensing and safe-contact problem of scalp work is solved at that structure level, though it is not massage.

sources.title: AI Massage Startup Raises $83 Million, Brings Robots to Equinox - Bloomberg
sources.claim: Aescape's autonomous robotic massage tables, which 3D-scan the body and apply personalized pressure with two arms, are being installed commercially in dozens of Equinox gym locations and hotels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous body massage. It substantiates that force-controlled robotic massage of a paying human client is delivered at commercial service quality inside ordinary human-work facilities (gyms, hotels), the same class of premises as a salon; it does not itself treat the scalp.

tasks.label: Apply water or setting, straightening or waving solutions to hair, and use curlers, rollers, hot combs and curling irons to press and curl hair.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Salon blow-dry/finish styling: after shampoo and rough dry, stylist mists water/thermal-protect or setting spray, sections the hair with clips, and curls it section by section with a curling iron or wand on a seated client, then brushes out and sets the shape; must avoid burning scalp/ears and match the requested curl pattern.

Salon silk press / hot-comb or flat-iron press on textured (coily) hair: apply pressing product, blow dry with comb attachment, then pass a hot comb or flat iron through small sections at high heat, working close to the scalp without burning skin and without reverting the hair.

Salon wet set / roller set: dampen hair with water and setting lotion, part hair into a roller pattern, wind each section onto rollers or pin curls with even tension, seat the client under a hood dryer, then remove rollers and comb out into the finished style (common with older clientele).

Salon chemical texture service: section hair and wind onto perm rods (or apply chemical relaxer/keratin straightener to new growth), apply waving/straightening solution and neutralizer at timed intervals, monitor processing on a live client, rinse, and finish; scalp burns and over-processing are damaging errors.

Off-site styling: stylist works in a client's home, a nursing home room, or a bridal-party hotel room, using portable irons and a spray bottle, with variable seating, lighting, and outlets, to set and curl hair.

sources.title: Untangle your hair with help from robots | MIT CSAIL
sources.claim: MIT CSAIL's RoboWig used a robot arm with a sensorized soft brush and camera to autonomously brush out tangled wigs of varying curliness in a laboratory; it brushes hair but does not apply solutions, wind rollers, or use heated styling tools.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: brushing/detangling hair. Same workpiece (human hair on a head form) and comparable safety constraints, so it marks the frontier of robot-on-hair manipulation; it does not establish thermal styling, roller winding, or chemical application.

sources.system: Hair combing system on a general-purpose robotic arm (Dennler et al.)
sources.title: Design and Evaluation of a Hair Combing System Using a General-Purpose Robotic Arm (arXiv:2108.01233)
sources.claim: A USC lab system automatically combed the hair of human users with a general-purpose lightweight robot arm, planning paths through hair from segmentation; evaluated in a lab, limited to combing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: combing a live person's hair. Same material and safety envelope, but the demonstrated skill is combing strokes only, not applying setting solutions or curling hair with heated irons.

sources.title: MOE-Hair: Soft and Compliant Contact-Rich Hair Manipulation and Care (project page, HRI 2025)
sources.claim: MOE-Hair, a compliant soft robotic manipulator, performed head patting, finger combing and ... on 12 human participants in a lab user study; the demonstrated hair-care skills stop well short of setting, pressing, or curling hair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact-rich hair care on live people. It shows the research frontier for force-safe robot contact with hair and scalp; no heat-tool handling, sectioning, roller winding, or chemical application is shown.

sources.title: HaloBraid raises $7M from Seven Seven Six to end the six-hour hair salon appointment | TechCrunch
sources.claim: HaloBraid is a salon-chair-mounted braiding device being launched to salons; a human stylist must start every braid by hand and the machine only finishes that braid, so it is an assistant rather than an autonomous stylist, and it performs braiding, not setting or curling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: braiding a client's hair in a salon chair. It is the closest commercial machine acting on client hair, but it requires a stylist to set up each braid and never applies solutions or uses heated curling tools.

sources.title: Robotic hair washer to enter Hong Kong market in June after gaining interest on mainland | South China Morning Post
sources.claim: Faxiaoka's hair-washing machine, deployed in roughly 40 shops in southern China, washes a customer's hair with high-pressure water tubes inside a helmet-shaped module; it applies water to hair inside a purpose-built fixture but performs no setting, roller work, or thermal styling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying water and shampoo to a client's hair in a shop. It covers only the 'apply water' fragment with the head fixtured in a helmet; it cannot section hair, wind rollers, or handle irons.

sources.system: Survey of haircutting and hair-care robots
sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed survey of hair-related robotics reports that robotic haircutting is largely unexplored and that robotics research on hair is confined to brushing, combing, washing and scalp ..., i.e., no demonstrated robotic thermal styling or chemical texture service.
sources.transferJustification: Field-state survey of hair-care robotics; it documents that no system performs setting-solution application, roller setting, pressing, or curling, supporting the negative judgments.

tasks.label: Shave, trim, and shape beards and moustaches.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Barbershop: beard trim and line-up as part of a men's haircut service. Client seated upright in a barber chair, talking and shifting; barber uses clippers with guards to take the beard down to a set length, then a trimmer/foil shaver to define cheek line, neckline and moustache edge, blending the sideburn into the fade, checking symmetry from both sides.

Salon/barbershop: moustache and short-beard tidy-up with scissors and comb on an older client, detail work around the lips, nostrils and chin, following the client's verbal description of how short to go, avoiding cutting the lip or nose.

Barbershop: shaping a longer, full beard to a requested style — sculpting the perimeter, tapering the sides, rounding or squaring the chin, then outlining edges with a foil shaver or razor and applying beard oil/balm.

Barbershop: traditional hot-towel straight-razor shave — reclining the chair, hot towels, lathering with brush, multiple razor passes with and against the grain over cheeks, jaw, upper lip, chin and neck, stretching the skin by hand, cold towel and aftershave, with no nicks.

On-site service inside an institution: barber/cosmetologist visiting a nursing home, assisted-living facility or hospital, trimming and shaving beards of frail or partly immobile residents in a facility salon room or at bedside, working around wheelchairs, tremor and limited head control.

Mobile/at-home service: barber travels to a client's house, hotel room or event (e.g., wedding party, homebound client), sets up in a bathroom or kitchen chair with improvised lighting and mirror, and trims/shapes the beard and moustache.

sources.system: Whitney lab fluidic remote direct-drive teleoperated manipulator (Northeastern University)
sources.title: Remote Razor Shaving: The Ultimate Test of Human-Robot Trust
sources.claim: The best-known robotic straight-razor face shave was performed under continuous human teleoperation: a professional barber drove a fluidic remote direct-drive manipulator that held the razor against the roboticist's face. No autonomous shaving of a human face was involved.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (shaving a human face with a straight razor), but it is human-driven teleoperation, so under the autonomy rule it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: unnamed robotic arm from a Shanghai company
sources.title: China-made robotic arm autonomously shaves beard-Xinhua
sources.claim: A short Xinhua news video shows an unnamed Shanghai company's force-controlled robotic arm shaving a man's beard, described as autonomous. The system is not named, no technical documentation, quality/coverage of the shave and repeatability are not established, and it is an exhibition-style clip rather than a service delivered to customers.
sources.transferJustification: On-task (beard shaving), but the system is unnamed and autonomy cannot be established from a caption-only news clip, so per the autonomy rule it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.system: survey of haircutting robot prototypes (vision-based, cobot-based, teleoperated systems)
sources.developer: Shuai Li (review of the field), MDPI Automation
sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice (Automation 2025, 6(3), 47)
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed perspective paper reviewing the state of haircutting/grooming robots states that full autonomy in robotic haircutting is not currently feasible and proposes supervised autonomy (with a local human barber taking over for precise or corrective action) as the only near-term commercial route; existing examples are research prototypes and YouTube demos, plus Panasonic's hair-washing product.
sources.transferJustification: Haircutting on a live human head is the closest neighboring task to beard trimming/shaping — same moving human workpiece, same cutting tools, same safety constraints — so the reviewed infeasibility of full autonomy carries over as negative evidence for beard work.

sources.system: UR-10 based autonomous beard-shaving assistance system (simulated)
sources.developer: Ajani, Assal & El-Hussieny, Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology
sources.title: Towards Development of an Autonomous Robotic System for Beard Shaving Assistance for Disabled People (IEEE SMC 2019)
sources.claim: The main academic effort on autonomous beard shaving (UR-10 arm with an electric beard trimmer, face detection and force-tracking impedance control) was evaluated in simulation only; no hardware shave of a human face was reported.
sources.transferJustification: On-task (beard trimming/shaving) but simulation-only, so it does not substantiate physical completion of any instance in any environment.

tasks.label: Comb, brush, and spray hair or wigs to set style.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service salon: finishing a women's cut or blowout on a seated client — sectioning, round-brushing/combing damp-to-dry hair into the finished shape, smoothing flyaways, then a finishing hairspray. Client is a live person who talks, shifts and tilts; hair length, density, texture and product response vary every time.

Barbershop / short-hair salon: after a clipper or scissor cut, combing the hair into its part and direction, setting the fringe, working in a light product and a quick spray to hold. Fast turnaround, tight tolerance around ears, neckline and hairline.

Special-occasion set in the salon: bridal, prom or formal updo — sectioning, back-combing/teasing for volume, smoothing panels over pins, arranging curls, and heavy hairspray to lock the shape for hours. Judged visually against a reference photo and the client's approval.

Wig, hairpiece or extension work: the wig is pinned on a wig block or mannequin head at a bench in the salon back room, wig shop or theatrical shop; the stylist combs it out, brushes and arranges it into the finished style and sprays it to set. Workpiece is detachable and can be fixtured.

Nursing home, assisted-living or hospital beauty shop: comb-outs and roller-set finishing for elderly residents — teasing, shaping, and firm-hold spray on thin, fragile or permed hair. Residents may have tremor, limited neck mobility, hearing loss, or sit in a wheelchair.

On-location / mobile styling: bridal party in a hotel room or private home, film/TV or photo set, or a homebound client's living room. No salon chair or fixed station; improvised lighting and seating; several heads styled and sprayed back to back under time pressure.

sources.developer: MIT CSAIL and Harvard Soft Math Lab
sources.title: This hair-brushing robot could be the future of grooming | Dazed
sources.claim: RoboWig, a robot arm with a sensorized soft brush and camera, autonomously detangles and brushes hair using closed-loop force feedback, but was only tested on wigs mounted in a lab setup, not on people and not to produce a finished style.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic hair detangling/brushing. Directly relevant to the brushing element of this task, but detangling is a sub-step; the demonstration produces no set style and applies no spray.

sources.system: Front Hair Styling Robot System (root-centric strand adjustment)
sources.developer: Kim, Kanazawa, Hasegawa, Kawaharazuka, Okada — JSK Lab, University of Tokyo (IEEE SII 2025)
sources.title: Front Hair Styling Robot System Using Path Planning for Root-Centric Strand Adjustment (arXiv 2501.10991)
sources.claim: A University of Tokyo JSK Lab system autonomously combs front hair toward a target hairstyle from an image using vision-based path planning; experiments ran on a mannequin head with stiff ..., pre-wetted with water, with a small myCobot arm and soft comb in the lab, evaluated only by strand-orientation similarity.
sources.transferJustification: Closest published system to "comb hair to set style": it combs a fixtured mannequin head toward a target front hairstyle, but covers only the fringe, applies no fixative, and reports similarity metrics rather than salon-acceptable output.

sources.developer: Yoo, Dennler, Nikolaidis et al. (CMU / USC), ACM/IEEE HRI 2025
sources.title: Soft and Compliant Contact-Rich Hair Manipulation and Care (arXiv 2501.02630)
sources.claim: MOE-Hair, a soft tendon-driven end-effector on a robot arm, performs head patting, finger combing and ..., evaluated on a force-sensorized mannequin head plus a 12-participant perception study; it is a safety/compliance study of hair contact, not a styling system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact-rich hair manipulation on a human/mannequin head. Shows the state of the art is gentle contact and combing motions, with no demonstrated ability to arrange and fix a hairstyle.

sources.system: Survey of haircutting/hair-care robots (RoboWig, combing systems, Panasonic head-care robot)
sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed perspective review of hair robotics finds the field essentially undeveloped: about 30 papers across brushing, combing, washing and scalp ..., mostly lab prototypes, with the only commercial product identified being Panasonic's hair-washing/massage unit, and proposes supervised autonomy as a future path to commercialization.
sources.transferJustification: Field-level survey covering hair brushing, combing and styling robots; establishes that no fielded system performs salon styling autonomously, including on wigs or mannequin heads.

sources.title: A Hair-Braiding Robot Is Coming to Salons This Fall
sources.claim: HaloBraid, the nearest-to-market salon hair robot, is a braid-finishing assistant clamped to the salon chair: a human stylist starts every braid by hand and hands off the repetitive weaving; product launch was announced for September 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated manipulation of a client's hair in a salon chair. It is the most advanced salon hair robot, yet it needs a stylist to start and supervise each braid and does not comb out, style or spray hair.

sources.title: Japan's Panasonic develops robot hair-washer
sources.claim: Panasonic's head-care robot 3D-scans a seated client's head and shampoos and massages the scalp with robotic fingers over a fixed basin; this washing function is the only hair robot that reached product form, and it does not comb, style or spray hair.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of hair on a live seated human head. It shows the ceiling of deployed hair robotics — washing with the head immobilized in a basin — and no styling, combing-out or spray application.

tasks.label: Develop new styles and techniques.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Stylist experiments with a new cutting technique on a mannequin/practice head clamped to a station in the salon back room or at home after hours: sectioning, elevation and over-direction trials with shears/razor, evaluating the shape, and iterating until a repeatable method emerges.

Stylist develops a new color or lightening technique (e.g., a new balayage/foil placement or toner formula) on a live model or willing regular client in the salon chair — mixing test formulas, strand-testing, adjusting placement/processing, and judging the result against the intended look.

Stylist adapts and invents a variation on the spot during a paid client service in the salon — improvising a cut/finish for the client's hair type, face shape and cowlicks, then refining it into a technique they can repeat and teach.

Hands-on advanced education: attending an academy class, brand workshop or trade-show stage session and practicing the new technique on a mannequin head or model under an instructor, then translating it into their own method.

Creating and testing an editorial/bridal/competition look on a model on location or backstage — building the style with heat tools, pins and product, testing hold and camera appearance, and revising the construction until the look works.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University (Robotics Institute) et al.
sources.title: DYMO-Hair: Generalizable Volumetric Dynamics Modeling for Robot Hair Manipulation (arXiv 2510.06199)
sources.claim: DYMO-Hair is a model-based robot hair-care system that performs visual goal-conditioned hair styling; real-world tests are limited to two wigs on a bench in a lab, and the work is framed as a research foundation toward future robot hair styling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic brushing/reshaping of hair toward a target hairstyle. It is the closest machine analogue to hands-on style experimentation, so it bounds what robots can do with hair; it reaches only coarse goal-matching on wigs, not creative development of new cutting/coloring methods.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University / University of Southern California
sources.title: MOE-Hair: Soft and Compliant Contact-Rich Hair Manipulation and Care (IEEE/ACM HRI 2025)
sources.claim: MOE-Hair, a soft robotic manipulator, performs three hair-care skills (head patting, ..., hair grasping) in a lab user study; it does not cut, color, or design styles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: contact-rich hair manipulation on a human head. It shows the frontier of safe robot-hair contact is combing/grasping, far short of the dexterous, judgment-driven manipulation needed to invent and test new styles.

sources.title: A Hair-Braiding Robot Is Coming to Salons This Fall (Allure via Yahoo Tech)
sources.claim: HaloBraid, the most advanced commercial salon hair robot, is a braider's assistant attached to the salon chair: a stylist starts and hands off each braid, and the device can only plait a classic three-strand braid on mid-lengths to ends.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: executing a hairstyle element (a braid) in a salon. It shows even the leading commercial salon robot executes one fixed, pre-specified pattern with human setup, providing no capacity to originate or evaluate new styles.

sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed perspective on haircutting robots treats the field as emerging and proposes supervised autonomy as a route to early commercialization, indicating no autonomous haircutting robot is deployed at worker quality.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic haircutting. Establishes that the underlying manual skill of the task (cutting and shaping hair) has no deployed autonomous system, so trial-and-error development of new cutting techniques is out of reach.

tasks.label: Demonstrate and sell hair care products and cosmetics.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Order, display, and maintain supplies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail product stock check and reorder: stylist walks the salon's retail shelf, notes which shampoo/styling SKUs are low or sold out, checks the POS/inventory sheet, and places a replenishment order online or with the brand rep. Open shelving, barcoded standard SKUs, done between clients.

Professional back-bar supply inventory and ordering: counting color tubes, developer, lightener, foils, gloves, capes, cotton, gallon shampoo/conditioner stored in station drawers, wall racks, and a small back room; judging partly used tubes/jugs, setting quantities, and phoning or web-ordering from the distributor.

Receiving a distributor delivery: taking in cartons at the back door, opening them, checking contents against the packing slip, noting shorts/damages, breaking down boxes, and putting product away on crowded stockroom shelves and in cabinets by brand and line.

Day-to-day upkeep during service hours: refilling shampoo/conditioner pump bottles at the backwash bowls from gallon jugs, restocking each station with foils, gloves, neck strips and clean folded towels, clearing empties, and wiping down the trolley and shelves while clients are in chairs.

Retail display work: pulling stock from the back, pricing/labeling bottles, placing and facing mixed-SKU products on the front display shelves and window, dusting testers, and setting up a seasonal or promotional display with signage.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: TX SCARA restocks beverage bottles and cans onto convenience-store display shelves, running mostly on its GORDON AI with remote teleoperation only for failure recovery; deployed at 300 FamilyMart stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing bottled/canned product onto a retail display shelf. Same object class (rigid bottles) and same act (placing product on a shelf face) as stocking a salon retail display, but performed from a rail-mounted station inside a cooler with product presented in standard crates.

sources.title: Telexistence and Physical Intelligence Announce Partnership to Automate Drink-Restocking Operations in Retail Stores
sources.claim: As of mid-2025 Telexistence's in-store restocking robots automate the majority of drink-restocking, with remote operators still needed for unpredictable error cases such as toppled bottles inside display shelves.
sources.transferJustification: Currency evidence for the same related task: autonomous shelf restocking of bottled product in retail stores, with occasional remote assistance for recovery.

sources.title: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force sensing to stow items - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously picks and stows roughly 75% of item types into fabric storage pods at purpose-built stow stations in fulfillment centers, at human-comparable speed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting individually packaged consumer goods away into fixtured storage. Comparable objects (bottles, boxes, small consumables) and comparable placement precision to putting salon stock away, but with totes and pods presented to a fixed station.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously unloads cases from trucks and containers at DHL sites, with 10 units deployed across three countries as of June 2025 at rates of 700 cases per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking in a delivery of cartons. Same object class (shipping cases) and same act (removing cases from a delivery and moving them onto a receiving line), though in a warehouse bay fed by conveyors rather than a salon back door.

sources.title: BJ's Wholesale Club to Power Up Shelf-Scanning Robots at All Locations - Retail TouchPoints
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally autonomously roams store aisles during trading hours, scanning shelves to report stock levels, placement and pricing, data the retailer uses to drive restocking and replenishment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: checking which retail SKUs are low or out and feeding the reorder. Same objects (packaged retail goods on open shelving) and same accepted output (a stock-level record that triggers replenishment ordering).

sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Tally shelf-scanning robots remain in commercial deployment in late 2025, going live across 17 stores of US grocer Harmons after a five-store rollout, replacing manual shelf verification and scanning by associates.
sources.transferJustification: Currency evidence for the same related task (autonomous shelf stock counting feeding replenishment ordering) as of late 2025.

sources.title: Automatic Towel Folding Machines for efficient laundry | Girbau
sources.claim: Girbau's FT automatic towel folders are commercial machines that fold towels lengthwise and crosswise at up to 1,200 towels per ... for hotels, gyms, spas and laundries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing the stack of clean folded towels that station restocking consumes. Same deformable objects and same accepted output (uniformly folded towels), achieved with the linen fed to a fixed machine.

sources.title: China's first pharmacy robot goes into service in Beijing - CGTN
sources.claim: A Galbot G1 wheeled humanoid entered service in a Beijing drugstore in March 2026, locating packaged products on shelves, picking them and packaging them for customer pickup, operating around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: handling mixed-SKU packaged retail goods on shop shelving. Comparable objects (boxes and bottles of similar size to salon retail product) and comparable precision, in a small store whose shelving is laid out around the robot.

sources.title: Diligent Robotics completes 300,000 pharmacy deliveries with Moxi - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulators autonomously carry supplies, specimens and medications around occupied hospitals, with more than one million deliveries across over 25 US hospitals.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving supplies through a staffed human facility. Shows autonomous transport and drop-off in occupied corridors, but the robot hands off totes rather than placing individual consumables onto workstations or shelves.

tasks.label: Operate cash registers to receive payments from patrons.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Full-service salon front desk: stylist or receptionist rings up the service ticket on a POS terminal/tablet, presents the tip prompt, the client taps or inserts a card, the terminal captures tip/signature and the receipt is printed or emailed, ticket closed. Indoor salon, fixed counter.

Cash payment at the salon: client pays for a $40-$120 service with bills, the worker takes the bills, makes change from the register drawer, accepts or records a cash tip, hands back change and a printed receipt, and the drawer must balance at end of day.

Mixed ticket: service plus retail take-home products scanned by barcode, a redeemed gift card, series/package or promotional discount, sometimes split tender (gift card plus card, or card plus cash), on the salon's POS.

Booth-renter or commission stylist checks the client out at the styling chair or a small station using a mobile card reader/tablet (Square, Vagaro, Boulevard) inside the salon; card tap plus occasional cash tip, digital receipt, rebooking.

Mobile/independent stylist working on location - client's home, an assisted-living room, or a wedding/event site - collects payment with a phone card reader or in cash, with no fixed register, no counter, and no institution controlling the premises.

sources.title: Square Kiosk Arrives to Make Ordering Faster and More Intuitive for Restaurants and Diners
sources.claim: Square Kiosk is a commercially sold self-service terminal combining hardware, software and embedded contactless/chip payment that lets customers place and pay for ... in quick-service restaurants, with no staff operating the register.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: counter checkout in a small service business. The objects (payment cards, contactless phones, printed receipts, a tip prompt on a ticket) and the transaction precision are identical to salon checkout, and a QSR counter is the same class of small structured commercial premises as a salon front desk.

sources.title: Adjust Square Kiosk checkout and order notification settings - Square Support Center
sources.claim: The deployed Square Kiosk also handles the tipping and gift-card parts of a checkout: merchants configure tip options and gift card acceptance in the self-serve checkout flow.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: QSR self-checkout including tip and gift-card tender. Salon checkout differs only in the line items; tip prompts, gift-card redemption and card capture are the same operations on the same instruments.

sources.title: Transforming the Checkout Experience | Consumer-Facing Cash Recyclers - CIMA
sources.claim: CIMA's INLANE300 is a consumer-facing note and coin recycler sold to sit on the checkout counter of small retailers; the customer inserts cash and the machine validates, counts and dispenses the ..., replacing the manual cash drawer.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cash tender and change-making at a small retailer's counter. The physical objects (US bills and coins), the accuracy requirement (exact change, counterfeit rejection, drawer balancing) and the counter setting match a salon register serving a cash-paying client.

sources.system: Glory CASHINFINITY CI-50 / CI-5 / CI-10 cash recyclers
sources.title: Glory | CI-50 Compact Front Office Cash Recycler | Glory Global
sources.claim: Glory's CASHINFINITY compact cash recyclers (CI-5, CI-50, CI-10 note+coin units) are sold for integration into point-of-sale counters and self-checkouts, automating acceptance, authentication, storage and dispensing of notes and coins at the lane.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail point-of-sale cash handling. Same currency handling, same counter-height installation and same reconciliation standard as a salon register drawer.

sources.title: GLORY Confirmed as Global Leader in Retail Cash Recycling Solutions by RBR Data Services
sources.claim: Glory retail cash recyclers are in large-scale real deployment (a 285-unit rollout at Waitrose stores underway), and independent RBR/Datos research confirms them as the market-leading deployed retail cash automation hardware.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated counting and dispensing of store cash. Establishes that machine cash handling runs in routine commercial service at retailer-accepted error rates, the standard a salon drawer must meet.

sources.system: Self-checkout terminals (NCR Voyix, Toshiba, Diebold Nixdorf and others)
sources.developer: RBR Data Services / Datos Insights (study of deployed systems)
sources.title: Refreshes and Rollouts Lead to a Record Year for Self-Checkout | Datos Insights
sources.claim: Self-checkout terminals - machines that scan barcoded merchandise, take card or cash tender, dispense change and issue receipts without a cashier - are deployed at very large scale in US supermarkets and convenience chains, with more than 217,000 terminals shipped worldwide in one year.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended retail checkout. It covers the same operations a salon register performs - itemizing a ticket, taking card or cash tender, making change, issuing a receipt - at commercially accepted reliability inside staffed commercial premises.

sources.title: NCR Voyix Delivers Flexible, Future-Forward Next Generation Self-Checkout Solution for Retailers and Shoppers
sources.claim: NCR Voyix's current-generation self-checkout, sold to retailers, completes customer transactions using barcode scanning, computer vision and RFID and can be run as cash or cashless lanes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scanning barcoded merchandise and tendering payment. Salon retail add-ons (shampoo, styling products) are ordinary barcoded consumer goods, so the scanning and tender steps transfer directly.

sources.title: Self Service Kiosks for Restaurants | XPR POS
sources.claim: Cash-accepting self-service kiosks that take banknotes and coins and dispense ... are supplied to and used by major QSR chains, stadiums, parks and airports for customer ordering and payment.

tasks.label: Shape eyebrows and remove facial hair, using depilatory cream, tweezers, electrolysis or wax.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Salon/brow-bar eyebrow shaping with soft wax plus tweezer cleanup: consult on desired shape and map the brow to the client's face, trim long hairs, heat and apply wax with a stick along the underside/top, press and pull a strip, tweeze remaining strays, apply soothing lotion; client reclined in a styling or facial chair, hair color and skin sensitivity vary.

Salon eyebrow maintenance by tweezing/trimming only (clients on retinoids, sensitive or thin skin, sparse or over-plucked brows): hair-by-hair plucking with the skin held taut, constant visual judgment of symmetry, working right around the eye.

Salon facial waxing of upper lip, chin, cheeks or sideburns, usually as an add-on: hard or soft wax on small sensitive areas, checking wax temperature, multiple pulls, tweezing missed hairs, post-care product.

Other facial hair-removal modalities performed in a salon: threading, depilatory cream applied to lip/chin with patch-testing and timed removal, or electrolysis in which a fine probe is inserted into individual follicles by a licensed operator.

Off-site or mobile brow/facial hair-removal service: client's home, hotel room for a bridal party, assisted-living room, or a film/TV set; improvised seating and lighting, portable wax pot, layout differs every time.

sources.title: I Got Eyelash Extensions From An AI Robot And I'm Hooked | Marie Claire
sources.claim: LUUM's Precision Lash robot commercially applies individual eyelash extensions to paying clients in a salon: robot arms isolate a natural lash and apply an extension under computer vision, while a human lash artist consults, preps, supervises and finishes the set. It is the closest deployed robot working on hairs of a human face, but it adds lashes rather than removing hair and does no brow shaping, waxing or tweezing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: eyelash extension application. Same environment (salon) and comparable sub-millimeter precision on individual hairs near the eye, but transfer to this task is NOT established: the robot attaches extensions with adhesive rather than gripping and extracting hairs, handles no hot wax, tweezers or probe, and the human artist still performs the shape consultation, prep and finishing touches.

sources.title: Luum launches next-generation AI eyelash extension robot with faster application and national rollout
sources.claim: LUUM's next-generation lash robot was launched in Nov 2025 with a rollout into Nordstrom and Ulta locations; the service remains lash extension application only, with lash artists still running appointments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: eyelash extension application. Establishes that the only commercially deployed beauty robot acting on the human face as of 2026 performs lash application, not eyebrow shaping or facial hair removal.

tasks.label: Administer therapeutic medication and advise patron to seek medical treatment for chronic or contagious scalp conditions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Salon shampoo area: while shampooing, the stylist sees flaking, redness or itching; switches to an over-the-counter medicated/anti-dandruff or tea-tree therapeutic shampoo or scalp treatment, works it over the whole scalp, lets it process, massages and rinses, then tells the client to see a doctor if it does not clear.

Styling chair consultation: stylist parts the hair into sections under a light, inspects the scalp, recognizes a chronic condition (seborrheic dermatitis, psoriasis, chronic dryness), applies a therapeutic lotion/serum with an applicator-tip bottle along the parts onto the affected patches while avoiding broken skin, explains findings and advises a dermatologist visit, notes it on the client card.

Suspected contagious condition (head lice/nits, tinea capitis, impetigo, infected folliculitis) found at the hairline or nape: stylist inspects, stops or declines the service, applies no chemicals, discreetly advises the patron (or parent) to seek medical treatment, then disinfects combs, clippers, cape, chair and bowl and rebooks.

Barbershop / short-hair client: after a clipper cut or shave the barber applies a medicated tonic, astringent or antiseptic to an irritated, flaky or bumpy scalp and neckline, and advises the client to see a physician for persistent folliculitis or ingrown-hair infection.

Head-spa / scalp-treatment service booked for a chronic scalp problem: multi-step protocol at the treatment basin (scalp analysis, exfoliating scrub, steam, medicated serum or ampoule, massage, rinse, dry), with advice on a home regimen and on seeing a dermatologist for the underlying condition.

tasks.label: Train or supervise other hairstylists, hairdressers, and assistants.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Senior stylist or salon owner supervising junior stylists and assistants across a shift in a commercial salon: assigning clients and stations, monitoring turnaround and service quality, checking color formulations and finished results before the client leaves, and giving corrective feedback.

One-on-one on-the-job training of a newly hired shampoo assistant: explaining and demonstrating the salon's shampoo, conditioning, towel-drying, and blow-dry protocol, then watching the assistant perform it on a client and verbally correcting hand position, water temperature, and timing.

In-salon education session on a cutting or coloring technique (e.g., balayage, graduated bob) using mannequin heads: the senior stylist demonstrates the technique step by step while narrating, then observes each trainee's attempt and critiques sectioning, elevation, and product application.

Mentoring an apprentice or cosmetology student toward licensure: reviewing progress against a competency checklist, coaching on client consultation and sanitation rules, documenting and signing off practice hours, and counseling on areas needing improvement.

Classroom or platform instruction at a beauty school or a manufacturer's education event: lecturing on chemistry, safety, and technique to a group, answering questions, and evaluating students' practical work.

tasks.label: Attach wigs or hairpieces to model heads and dress wigs and hairpieces according to instructions, samples, sketches or photographs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Salon or wig-studio stylist blocks a client's new human-hair or synthetic wig on a canvas/mannequin head, secures it with T-pins, then washes/detangles, sections, cuts and styles it (blow-dry, iron, product) to match the client's reference photo before the fitting.

Theatrical, film or TV wig dresser blocks a wig on a canvas head, sets it on rollers or in pin curls per the designer's sketch, dries it, then combs out, backcombs and pins the finished period style; hairpieces are dressed to match a sample wig.

Wig retail boutique or salon retail area: staff mount stock wigs and hairpieces on display heads, pin them straight, comb/finger-style them into the catalog look, and refresh displays that customers have handled.

Cosmetology school or training lab: student/instructor secures a wig or hairpiece to a mannequin head on a clamp and sets, curls, or braids it to reproduce a style shown in an instructional diagram, sample, or photo for practice or a practical exam.

Mobile or home-based stylist services a client's wig at the client's residence or in a home studio: puts the wig on a portable stand, detangles, restyles and finishes it to the look the client asks for, working around household furniture and lighting.

sources.claim: RoboWig, a robot arm with a sensorized soft brush and camera, autonomously plans and executes brush-outs and was tested on wigs of varying curliness in a lab; it only detangles/brushes, it does not mount wigs on blocks, cut, set or dress them to a target style.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic hair brushing/detangling performed on wigs mounted on a stand. It is the closest demonstrated manipulation of wig fibers, but covers only combing out; it provides no evidence of blocking/pinning a wig or of cutting, setting and dressing it to a photograph, so it cannot substantiate completion of this task.

roles.description: Apply makeup to performers to reflect period, setting, and situation of their role.

tasks.label: Clean supplies such as makeup brushes.
Duplicate work precisely to replicate characters' appearances on a daily basis.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Film/TV episodic or feature production: in the makeup trailer before call, re-create a principal actor's established character look day after day — colour-matched base, brows, eye design, lip, character details (freckles, scars, dirt, tan lines) — matched against continuity stills and the designer's notes so consecutive shooting days cut together.

Theatre/live show: in a backstage dressing room before each performance, repeat a designed stage character look on the same performer nightly (heavy base, sculpted highlight/shadow, exaggerated eyes, drawn lines, lashes), matching the approved design and adjusting for sweat, quick changes and house lighting.

Prosthetic/character SFX repeated daily: glue pre-made silicone/foam appliances to the performer's face and body, blend and seal edges invisibly, then stipple/paint the same colour scheme, stubble and texture to match the previously approved look over a multi-hour session in a makeup room.

Maintenance and continuity touch-ups during the working day on set or backstage — often on location (exterior sets, heat, wind, rain, cramped positions) — restoring the character's established look between takes and scenes so the appearance is identical shot to shot.

Volume/ensemble work: apply one standardized character or chorus look repeatedly to many performers in sequence (theme-park character performers, dance corps, cruise/repertory chorus), each face different, under tight pre-show time pressure, matching the show's fixed design each day.

Body makeup duplication: daily even body base/tan, tattoo covering, body shading or painted patterns on arms, legs, chest and back so the performer's exposed skin matches the established character appearance and the face makeup.

It substantiates only a single standardized element (lash extensions), not the multi-element, design-matched character makeup this task requires, so it does not substantiate completion of any instance.

tasks.label: Apply makeup to enhance or alter the appearance of people appearing in productions such as movies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Beauty/"straight" makeup for a principal actor in a film or episodic TV production, done in the makeup trailer or studio makeup room: skin prep, color-matched foundation and concealer, contour/highlight, eye makeup and lashes, lip, powder — matched to the DP's lighting, HD camera scrutiny, and continuity notes from prior shooting days.

On-set touch-ups and continuity maintenance between takes, frequently on location outdoors (heat, sweat, rain, wind, dust) or on a crowded stage: de-shining, reapplying color, refreshing sweat/dirt/blood effects, matching a shot filmed weeks earlier, working in seconds between takes around cameras, cables, and crew.

Character/period makeup for a live theatre or performance production in a dressing room: bold stage makeup readable at distance, aging or period-specific looks (drawn lines, stippling, greasepaint, rouge, false lashes/beards), applied to a rotating cast of performers on a tight pre-curtain schedule.

Special-effects / prosthetic makeup in a shop or makeup room: adhering and blending silicone or foam appliances, bald caps, wounds and scars, seam-blending with adhesives and solvents, painting/stippling in multiple layers, blood and sweat rigs — a multi-hour application on a seated performer.

Quick straight makeup for broadcast/live-event talent in a studio makeup room: base, powder, eyes, lips for a rotating roster of anchors, guests, or performers under HD studio lighting, each in 10-20 minutes with fast turnaround before air.

Body makeup and large-area airbrushing in a makeup room or tent: tattoo cover-up, evening skin tone on arms/legs/back, full-body color or dirt/grime for background performers and extras, often several performers in sequence.

It shares the human-face workspace and sub-millimeter precision of theatrical makeup, so it bounds the frontier; but it applies one engineered consumable to isolated lashes rather than blending pigment across facial contours, so it does not transfer to completing a makeup application.

sources.title: I Got Eyelash Extensions From An AI Robot And I'm Hooked

sources.title: Why Ulta, Nordstrom, and Walmart Are Betting on Beauty Robots

sources.title: Austin-based Blackdot launches futuristic way to tattoo

It shares contact work on a live person at high precision, but the workpiece is a flat stabilized body area and the output is a fixed vector design, so it does not substantiate color-matched, blended makeup on a mobile face.
