tasks.label: Alter or maintain makeup during productions as necessary to compensate for lighting changes or to achieve continuity of effect.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standby touch-ups on a soundstage/studio film or TV set: between takes the artist steps in for a few seconds to blot sweat and shine, re-powder, refresh lip and eye color, and fix smudges so the face matches the previous setup under changing key/fill lighting; judged against continuity photos and the director's/DP's eye, done fast without disturbing the actor's position or wardrobe.

Touch-ups on a practical location shoot (street, field, night exterior, boat, period house): artist works out of a belt bag in heat, wind, rain or cold, chasing actors between setups, controlling sweat and melting product, adding or killing sheen for the sun or a lighting change, with no fixed station and crew/crowds moving around.

Live theater during performance: in the wings or a quick-change booth, the artist blots sweat, re-powders, reapplies lip/eye color and adds or intensifies effects (aging, dirt, blood, tears) between scenes in seconds under dim blue work light, so the makeup reads from the house under stage lighting and stays continuous across acts.

Broadcast/live-event studio: news, talk show, awards show or concert; the artist powders shine between segments under hot studio lights, adjusts intensity when the lighting or camera setup changes, and refreshes performers in the green room or at the set edge during commercial breaks.

Prosthetic/SFX maintenance during a shoot: re-gluing lifting appliance edges, re-blending and re-coloring seams, re-wetting or re-applying blood, sweat, grime and injury effects between takes so damage and dirt levels match earlier footage.

sources.title: Beauty Meets AI: World's First Prototype Smart Lipstick | Grupo Boticario
sources.claim: The closest robotic system to applying cosmetics to a human face is Grupo Boticario's Smart Lipstick prototype: a chin-rest kiosk whose robotic arm applies lipstick automatically in about two minutes for users with motor or visual disabilities. It handles one product on the lips of a stationary, self-presenting user and remains a prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (robotic application of a cosmetic to a human face). It is the nearest demonstrated capability, but covers only lipstick on a head immobilized in a chin rest, with no assessment of shine, lighting, blending or continuity, so it does not transfer to on-set maintenance touch-ups.

sources.title: Target shoppers can get a $10 manicure from a robot at 2 Fort Worth stores - CultureMap Fort Worth

It bounds the frontier: deployed autonomy exists only for a fixtured hand and one product, not for facial touch-ups requiring blending and continuity judgment.

tasks.label: Select desired makeup shades from stock, or mix oil, grease, and coloring to achieve specific color effects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Film/TV/commercial production: in a studio makeup room or makeup trailer, the artist assesses a performer's skin tone under the day's camera lighting, picks base/concealer shades from the kit, and custom-blends two or three creams or liquids on a palette or the back of the hand to a matching shade before application.

Live theatre, opera, dance or variety show: backstage/dressing room, the artist pulls greasepaint, cream and powder shades from stock pans and cases for a cast per the designer's character/color chart, mixing highlight, shadow, rouge and character tints to read correctly under stage lighting.

Special-effects/character work: in a prosthetics shop or on-set SFX kit, the artist mixes pigments into silicone, PAX, greasepaint or alcohol-activated palettes to color appliances or create bruises, burns, aging pallor, fantasy skin tones, judging translucency and matching the performer's skin.

Non-institutional/on-location work: outdoor shoots, pageants, conventions, community/school theatre, hotel rooms or clients' homes; the artist works out of a case in improvised space and variable light, selecting and mixing shades on the spot.
Department stock work: pulling and restocking specified products/shades from a production's makeup stock room or shelved inventory for the show's kits, retrieving named SKUs and shade numbers.

sources.system: Lancome Le Teint Particulier custom-made foundation blending machine (L'Oreal Technology Incubator)
sources.title: Lancome expands Custom Made Foundation service to the UK and Canada
sources.claim: Lancome's Le Teint Particulier service, deployed at Nordstrom and Harrods counters, uses an on-site machine that determines and blends a custom foundation shade (72,000 possible shades) after a skin-tone scan, dispensing the finished product into a bottle.

sources.system: Yves Saint Laurent Rouge Sur Mesure powered by Perso

sources.claim: The YSL Rouge Sur Mesure device, a commercial consumer product, holds color cartridges and dispenses a made-to-order lip color matching a target color specified by the user (including a color captured by camera).
sources.transferJustification: Same task family: producing a specific cosmetic color on demand by machine-metered combination of pigment cartridges rather than by hand-mixing shades.

sources.system: Datacolor Autolab TFD automated dispensing system
sources.title: Datacolor Unveils Next-Generation Dual-Arm Automated Dispensing System with Launch of Autolab TFD
sources.claim: Datacolor's Autolab TFD is a commercially launched, enclosed dual-arm robotic dispensing system that gravimetrically meters colorant recipes into containers at +/-0.02 g accuracy, running batches of recipes generated by color-matching software.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mixing colorants into a base to hit a specified color. It is the same physical operation as mixing oil/grease bases with coloring to a target shade - metered pigment dosing into a base with weighed precision - performed inside a purpose-built enclosed cell.

sources.system: COROB automatic paint dispensers (e.g. D180 sequential dispenser)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: tinting a base with measured colorants to reach a specified shade, with pastes of comparable viscosity to cream/grease makeup bases; substantiates machine mixing of coloring to a target color in a purpose-built dispensing station.

sources.claim: Point-of-sale tinting systems integrate a spectrophotometer reading of a target color sample with automatic transmission of the computed colorant recipe to the dispenser, which then tints the base without manual metering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: measuring a target color from a physical sample and mixing to match it. This is the color-determination-plus-mixing loop the makeup artist performs by eye, executed by instrument and dispenser in a fixed station.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving a named cosmetic item from stocked inventory, which is the 'select desired makeup shades from stock' half of the task once the shade/SKU is specified.

sources.title: Autonomous Robotic Piece-Picking System - Logistics Business
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick 4 is a commercially available autonomous piece-picking cell that picks a broad range of individual SKUs from bins in distribution centers with reduced human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking specified small consumer items from stock bins in a fenced robotic cell; supports the stock-retrieval half of this task when the work is presented to the machine.

instances.label: Theatrical production, dressing room: after designing and applying a character's makeup, the artist completes a face chart/makeup sheet recording products, shades, brushes and application order, and shoots front and profile reference photos of the performer with a phone for the production's continuity binder.

Film/TV continuity on set: between setups the artist photographs each performer's face, hairline blend and applied wounds/tattoos with a phone or tablet and logs touch-up products, scene and slate numbers into a continuity app or notebook.

Prosthetics/SFX application: the artist photographs each stage of a multi-piece prosthetic build (adhesive, seam blending, painting, powdering) and writes a step-by-step product, quantity and timing sheet so the look can be duplicated on later shoot days.

Editorial or commercial shoot: the artist documents the finished beauty look under studio lighting for the client's records and for their own portfolio, listing brands, shades and notes on how the product reads on camera.
Off-site portfolio and archive work: hand-drawn or digital face charts, product spreadsheets and organized photo libraries assembled or updated away from the performer, between engagements.

tasks.label: Attach prostheses to performers and apply makeup to create special features or effects, such as scars, aging, or illness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Film/TV makeup trailer or studio makeup room: artist glues a pre-made silicone or foam-latex appliance (scar, wound, nose, aging piece) onto a seated actor's face, blends and dissolves the edges with adhesive/solvent, then paints, stipples and powders it to match surrounding skin under camera scrutiny; actor talks, breathes, and moves.

Theatrical dressing room before a stage call: painted old-age or illness makeup — highlight/shadow following the performer's own expression lines, latex/stipple wrinkling, pallor, sunken eyes, painted scars — scaled for stage lighting and distance, on several cast members in sequence under time pressure.

On location/on set between takes: fast application or repair of blood, bruises, dirt, sweat, burn or wound effects on face, arms and torso; continuity matching to reference photos, in variable light, weather and cramped positions, often with the performer already in costume.

Multi-hour character build in a makeup studio: bald cap application, multiple overlapping prosthetic pieces on face, neck and hands, hair punching/laying, full body coloring for a creature or heavy-aging character, finished to a supervisor's approval.

Theme park, haunted attraction or live event backstage room: rapid special-effects makeup (transfer wounds, scars, aging, decay) on a queue of many performers with a fixed house look to match, repeated nightly.

sources.system: LUUM Precision Lash next-generation lash robot

sources.transferJustification: Related task: attaching small elements to a client's face with adhesive under machine vision. It shows the frontier of machine work on a live human face is single-purpose, fixtured, and limited to lashes — it does not transfer to placing, edge-blending and painting prosthetic appliances.

sources.title: Austin-based Blackdot launches futuristic way to tattoo | KXAN Austin
sources.claim: Blackdot's automatic tattooing device applies high-resolution pigment designs into human skin at a commercial studio, showing machine-controlled precise pigment deposition on a live person in an institution-controlled studio; it produces pre-programmed dot designs on stabilized limbs, not blended, sculpted makeup effects on a moving face.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: depositing pigment on human skin. Transfer is limited — the design is a digital linework file applied to a flat, stabilized body area, whereas scars/aging/illness makeup requires 3D appliance placement, edge dissolution and freehand blending on a mobile face.

sources.developer: Grupo Boticário with CESAR Innovation Hub

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of cosmetic product to a human face. It marks the ceiling of demonstrated capability (single product, lips only, prototype) and therefore does not substantiate special-effects or prosthetic work.

sources.title: Gemma Robotics (company site)
sources.claim: Gemma Robotics is developing a touchless airbrush machine intended to apply foundation, contour, eye and lip makeup; as of mid-2026 the product is pre-launch with a public waitlist and company-stated performance, with no verified deployment or independent demonstration, and no capability for prosthetic attachment or effects makeup.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cosmetic application to a face. Cited only to show the frontier; autonomy and real-world performance are unverified and the stated scope (everyday airbrush makeup) excludes prostheses and special features.

tasks.label: Cleanse and tone the skin to prepare it for makeup application.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Film/TV production makeup trailer or studio makeup room: performer seated in a makeup chair at call time; artist assesses skin type, removes any residual product with micellar water/cleanser on cotton pads or sponges, works around closed eyes, hairline, nostrils and lips, blots, applies toner and primer/moisturizer before base makeup; tight schedule, conscious and talking performer.

Theater/opera/dance dressing room before a performance: a run of performers processed in sequence at mirrored stations; quick cleanse of oily or sweaty skin, removal of prior show makeup residue, toning, sometimes with the performer half-costumed; communal, cramped, time-pressured.

On-location shoot taken as found (outdoor set, street, field, hotel room, tent): performer in a folding chair with a portable kit; cleanse and tone in wind, dust, heat or cold, poor light, no running water; also re-cleansing between setups.

Photo studio or fashion-show backstage: rapid prep of many models by several artists working shoulder to shoulder; brief cleanse-and-tone pass on each face, varied skin tones and sensitivities, models moving between hair and wardrobe stations.

Special-effects/prosthetics prep in a makeup shop or lab: thorough cleansing and degreasing of face, scalp, neck (and sometimes chest/arms) with cleanser plus alcohol or astringent so adhesives and prosthetic pieces will bond; bald-cap and hairline prep; performer must be left dry and residue-free.

sources.system: SkinGrip (soft manipulator on a mobile manipulator, CMU)
sources.title: SkinGrip: An Adaptive Soft Robotic Manipulator with Capacitive Sensing for Whole-Limb Bed Bathing Assistance
sources.claim: SkinGrip, a soft robotic manipulator with capacitive sensing, autonomously wiped shaving cream from the limbs of 12 human participants in a lab bed-bathing study — the closest demonstrated robotic cleaning of live human skin, but on arms/legs, not the face, and as a research prototype.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted bed bathing (wiping a soiling substance off human skin). It shares compliant contact with live skin, but the objects and precision differ from facial cleansing and toning around eyes, nose and lips, and the system was evaluated only on limbs in a laboratory.

sources.title: Equinox | The World's Most Advanced Massage
sources.claim: Aescape's two-armed robotic table gives fully automated massages to paying customers at Equinox spas and hotels, showing commercially reliable force-controlled contact with a human body inside a structured facility — but on the back, glutes and legs through fabric, not on the face, and it applies no cleansing or skincare products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated massage. It substantiates autonomous, safe, force-regulated physical contact with a paying human client in a commercial spa, but treatment is limited to the back, glutes and legs and involves no product application, wiping or work near the eyes.

sources.system: Panasonic head-care / hair-washing robot (24 robotic fingers)
sources.title: High Tech Robot With 24 Fingers Washes Hair of Elderly At Hospitals
sources.claim: Panasonic's head-care (hair-washing) robot 3D-scans the head and washes and rinses the scalp with robotic fingers, shampoo and water while the user reclines in a fixtured salon chair over a basin; trialled in Japanese hospitals and care facilities, never a facial-skin cleansing or toning system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated scalp washing with liquid product in a purpose-built basin fixture. It is the nearest analogue to 'cleansing' but works on hair and scalp, wets and rinses the head, and does not clean facial skin, avoid the eye/nose/mouth region, or apply toner with a pad.

sources.system: Vision-guided robotic skin photo-rejuvenation prototype (Q-switched Nd:YAG)

sources.claim: A vision-guided robotic prototype performed automated laser photo-rejuvenation passes over the faces of human volunteers in a clinical study, showing 3D facial scanning and end-effector path following over facial contours — but the treatment is non-contact laser delivery, not cleansing, wiping or toning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered facial aesthetic treatment. It shows a robot can map a live human face and move an end effector over it, but the end effector never touches the skin, applies no product, and removes nothing, so it does not carry over to cleansing and toning.

sources.system: Autonomous beard-shaving assistive robot (adaptive force-tracking impedance control)
sources.developer: Ajani & Assal (Egypt-Japan University of Science and Technology)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous tool contact on the human face (shaving). Evidence is simulation-only, so it cannot support a positive judgment; it is recorded to show the state of face-contact robotics.

sources.title: Chinese company unveils autonomous robotic arm for precise beard shaving
sources.claim: An unnamed Shanghai company's robotic arm is reported to shave a man's beard with force sensing, but the system is not named and autonomy is only asserted in a stock-video description, so it cannot substantiate completion of face-contact work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: face-contact grooming. Treated as non-supporting: no named system, no technical documentation, and autonomy cannot be established from the video listing.

tasks.label: Provide performers with makeup removal assistance after performances have been completed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Theater dressing room right after curtain: artist helps actors take off standard stage makeup (foundation, greasepaint, eyeliner, lipstick, contour) using cleansing balm/oil, pads and cloths, working quickly on several performers in a crowded shared room, avoiding eyes and costumes.

Film/TV makeup trailer or studio makeup room: removal of prosthetic appliances (silicone/foam latex pieces, bald caps) glued with Pros-Aide/spirit gum, using solvents applied on brushes and swabs, gently lifting edges without tearing skin or the appliance, then cleaning adhesive residue and applying skin aftercare.

Body makeup removal at a wash/shower station in the venue: airbrushed body paint, tattoo cover-up, or full-body color on arms, chest, back and legs removed with remover, sponges and scrubbing before the performer showers, with the artist finishing missed areas.

Post-shoot cleanup of hair-related and effects materials in a studio makeup room: lace-front wig and bald-cap adhesive taken off the hairline, fake blood, gore, sweat/dirt effects and setting sprays cleaned off face, neck and hands.

On-location field conditions (outdoor set, tent, cramped location holding area, backstage of a touring venue): partial or full makeup removal between setups or at wrap, with variable lighting, no fixed station, limited water, and performers standing or seated wherever space allows.

Assisting a performer who removes most of their own makeup: supplying the right remover/wipes for their skin, spot-cleaning missed areas around eyes and hairline, checking skin for irritation, and applying moisturizer or aftercare.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: RABBIT is a research robot that autonomously washes, rinses and dries a person's limbs in a bed-bathing setup, using RGB/thermal sensing and a compliant 'Scrubby' end-effector; it was evaluated in a lab with 12 human participants. It is the closest demonstrated case of a robot wiping product off human skin, but it works on arms and legs in a lab, not on faces, and it does not remove cosmetics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-assisted bed bathing, i.e., wiping substances off human skin with a compliant tool. It shows safe force-controlled contact with a person, but only on large limb surfaces of a supine person in a lab; it does not demonstrate cleansing a face, working around eyes, lips and lashes, or judging when makeup is fully removed, so it does not transfer to makeup removal.

sources.title: Aescape Secures $83M to Scale AI-Powered Robotic Massage Technology – AlleyWatch
sources.claim: Aescape's robotic massage table autonomously delivers table massage to clients and is being rolled out commercially to about 60 Equinox gym locations, showing sustained safe robot contact with human bodies inside a structured commercial facility — but it works on the back and legs of a client lying on a purpose-built table and performs no cleaning, cosmetics or face work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hands-on bodywork on a human client in a commercial facility. It substantiates safe, autonomous physical contact with people, but the contact is broad pressure through a table interface, not fine tool work on a face with cleansers and solvents, so it does not substantiate makeup removal.

sources.title: LUUM Launches Next-Gen AI-Powered Lash Robot
sources.claim: LUUM's AI lash robot autonomously applies eyelash extensions to a reclining client's eye area in commercial shop-in-shop studios inside Ulta Beauty and Nordstrom stores, with human lash artists overseeing the service. It demonstrates precise robotic work at the human eye, but it adds extensions with adhesive and does not cleanse skin or remove makeup, adhesives or prosthetics.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precision robotic beauty service performed on a client's eye area in a beauty studio. It shows the hardware and safety case for face-adjacent robotic work, but the motion is placing individual fibers on a still client, not wiping, dissolving and verifying removal of cosmetics across a whole face, so it does not transfer to makeup removal.

sources.title: Panasonic Testing Head Care Robot At Salon - SlashGear
sources.claim: Panasonic's Head Care Robot scanned a customer's head and then autonomously shampooed and rinsed the scalp; it was trialled in a Japanese salon in 2012 for hospital and care-facility use. It is the closest case of a machine cleaning a human head, but it cleans hair inside a purpose-built basin and never worked on facial cosmetics; the product never became a commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated washing of a human head with water and product in a fixtured station. It shows head-contact cleaning is mechanically possible, but only on hair/scalp with the head clamped in a basin; it demonstrates nothing about wiping cosmetics from eyelids, lashes and lips or removing adhesives, so it does not transfer.

sources.title: Japan Human washing machine cleans head to toe in 15 mins
sources.claim: Japan's 'human washing machine' pod (Mirai Ningen Sentakuki) went on sale in late 2025 as an automated bathing capsule that washes and dries a seated person; even this purpose-built human-washing machine performs a general body wash and does not remove cosmetics, body paint or prosthetic adhesives, and reporting describes it as essentially a prototype for future ... bathing facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated washing of a whole human body in a purpose-built enclosure. Cited only to show that even the most machine-centric human-washing hardware performs a generic rinse, not the targeted cleansing and residue checking that stage-makeup removal requires.

tasks.label: Design rubber or plastic prostheses that can be used to change performers' appearances.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Feature film / episodic TV creature or character appliance designed in a special-makeup-effects shop: lifecast the performer's head or limb in alginate/plaster, sculpt the character in oil clay over the positive, make the stone/fiberglass mold, run foam latex or silicone, then fit-test on the performer and revise sculpt/edges for expression and camera.

Digital-hybrid design in a shop with a 3D pipeline: 3D scan of the performer, digital sculpt of the appliance to a director/designer brief, 3D-printed or CNC-milled mold shells and corrected core, silicone appliance cast and seamed, followed by a fitting and revision round.

Single small appliance (scar, wound, nose, chin, brow, ears, aging pieces) designed for a TV episode, indie film, or theatre production in a small studio or backstage workroom: sculpt on a generic or life-cast form, make a two-part stone mold, cast in gelatin, silicone, or foam latex, and check fit.

Theatrical, opera, or theme-park/haunt production: design a set of prosthetic pieces in the makeup/costume shop that read at viewing distance, survive repeated nightly wear and sweat, and can be applied fast; sculpt, mold, run multiples, and adjust after a stage/lighting test.

Re-design/re-engineering after a camera test or on-location fitting: in a makeup trailer or location fitting room, alter the appliance design (thin the edges, re-blend to the performer's anatomy, change material or thickness for heat, motion, or adhesion) and produce the revised piece in time for the shoot day.

sources.system: Formlabs Form 3L SLA 3D printer used for prosthetic makeup molds (Raised by Wolves S2)
sources.title: The Future of Props and Make-Up Effects: 3D Printing Large Props and Molds With the Form 3L for "Raised by Wolves" Season 2
sources.claim: State-of-the-art prosthetic-makeup pipelines in film use 3D scanning of the actor, human digital sculpting, and 3D-printed mold shells with hand silicone casting; the printer automates only mold fabrication, not the design or the appliance run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine fabrication of prosthetic molds. It shows the automated portion of prosthesis design is limited to printing a mold from a human-made digital sculpt; scanning, sculpting, casting, seaming and fitting remain human, so it cannot substantiate whole-instance completion.

sources.system: Artec Leo / Space Spider handheld 3D scanners in Kazu Hiro's prosthetic makeup workflow
sources.title: Kazu Hiro's breathtaking special effects makeup with Artec 3D scanners
sources.claim: Award-winning prosthetic makeup design with 3D scanners still relies on the artist for scanning decisions, sculpting, monitoring and on-set adjustment of the prostheses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: digital capture for prosthetic design. The scanner is hand-carried and only captures geometry; the design judgment and fitting adjustments stay with the artist, so it does not substantiate autonomous completion.

sources.title: robot chisel in italy carves detailed marble sculptures like a real artist
sources.claim: Robotic arms can autonomously carve sculptural forms in a purpose-built robotic workshop, but only by executing a digital model supplied by a human artist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic sculpting. It shows a machine can cut a form from a given 3D model inside a fenced robotic cell, but it neither conceives the character design nor produces a soft, skin-fitting rubber appliance for a live performer, so it cannot carry the whole instance.

sources.system: Automated non-contact facial topography mapping, 3D printing and silicone casting of orbital prosthesis
sources.developer: Academic clinical research team (single-center institutional study)
sources.title: Automated Non-contact Facial Topography Mapping, 3-Dimensional Printing and Silicone Casting of Orbital Prosthesis
sources.claim: The most automated facial-prosthesis workflow demonstrated is a medical, mirroring-based pipeline: non-contact scan, digitally designed 3D-printed mold, and silicone casting - still a human-directed, proof-of-principle lab process rather than autonomous design.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: custom facial prosthesis design and fabrication. Geometry is derived by mirroring the intact side rather than designed to a character brief, and mold assembly, casting and coloring remain manual, so it does not substantiate robotic completion of theatrical prosthesis design.

tasks.label: Create character drawings or models, based upon independent research, to augment period production files.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Regional/community theater period play: the makeup artist researches the era's hairstyles, cosmetics and facial conventions in books and online image archives, then draws character renderings (face charts) for each principal role and files them in the production book for the run.

Film or streaming period drama: the makeup designer builds research boards from paintings, photographs and museum references and produces annotated character sketches/plates per character (and per story day) that are added to the department's design and continuity file for approval by the director/designer.

Character/effects design for a historical or aged character: researching a real historical figure or period 'type' and creating a concept model — a sculpted maquette, a digital 3D head model, or a photographic composite — plus drawings documenting the prosthetic and makeup plan, filed with the production paperwork.

Opera, ballet, pageant or themed live show: producing standardized face-chart drawings on printed head templates for ensemble/chorus 'looks' derived from period research, filed with wardrobe and run paperwork so any crew member can reproduce the look.

Updating an existing period production file: after tests, fittings or a director's notes, revising the character drawings, adding annotated reference images, product/color keys and continuity photos so the file stays accurate for the remainder of the production.

tasks.label: Demonstrate products to clients, and provide instruction in makeup application.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Backstage in a theater dressing room before or during a run: the artist shows a cast member the products in their character kit (base, shading, aging stipple, powder), demonstrates the strokes on one side of the performer's face, then coaches the performer through replicating it in the mirror and corrects blending for stage lighting, under curtain-time pressure.

Film/TV production makeup trailer or studio room: the key artist demonstrates the specific products used on a performer (setting spray, powder, concealer, tattoo cover) and instructs the performer or a set assistant how to touch up continuity between takes, matching what the camera already recorded.

One-on-one private lesson or bridal trial in the client's home or hotel suite: the artist works from the client's own kit at an improvised vanity, swatches and applies half the face to demonstrate shade, texture and finish, then guides the client's hand through repeating it, adapting to the client's skill, features and lighting, and recommending purchases.

Retail beauty counter, pop-up, or trade-show/convention booth: the artist demonstrates cosmetic and character products to walk-up customers (swatching on hand or face, quick partial applications such as a lip, brow or airbrush pass), explaining technique, tools and shade choice while handling questions and hygiene between customers.

Group class or workshop for a school/community-theater cast, dance company, or cosplay panel: the artist demonstrates theatrical techniques (old-age, bruising, prosthetic adhesive, corrective base) step by step on a live model in front of the group, then circulates to inspect and correct each participant's own application.

sources.system: 10Beauty robotic manicure machine (incl. acquired Clockwork nail-painting robot)
sources.title: The First Five-step Robotic Manicure Is Coming to Ulta Beauty
sources.claim: 10Beauty/Clockwork's AI robotic manicure machine performs a multi-step nail service on a customer's hands in retail stores, showing autonomous cosmetic application to a human body part in a structured retail setting; it delivers a service rather than a product demonstration or makeup lesson and does not work on the face.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = robotic nail polish application in a store. It shares the retail setting and contact with a client's body, but the objects (nails vs. face), the shade-matching and blending precision, and above all the instructional purpose of this task (teaching the client to apply makeup themselves) are absent, so capability does not carry over.

sources.transferJustification: Related task = automated makeup application to a face. Even taken at face value it substitutes for applying makeup, not for demonstrating products to a client and teaching technique; autonomy and worker-quality output are unverified, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Wash and reset wigs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Regional, community, or educational theater: between performances the wig crew washes several synthetic and human-hair wigs in a backstage wig-room sink, blots them, pins each to a canvas block, sets it with rollers/pin curls and setting lotion, dries under a hooded dryer, then combs out and dresses the wig to the show's period style for the next call.

Broadway/major opera or resident company wig room: hand-tied lace-front human-hair wigs are cleaned (including removing adhesive and residue from delicate lace), conditioned in a sink with cool water, pinned to a block sized to the performer's head, wrapped in a precise roller/pin-curl pattern, dried in a wig dryer, and dressed back into an exact period look matched to a design photo, without damaging the lace or knots.

Film/TV production: at wrap the hair/wig artist washes and resets wigs in the hair trailer or base-camp workspace, matching continuity from the day's footage — same parting, wave pattern, and dressing — with wigs on blocks, set, dried and ready for the next call time.

Theme park, cruise ship, or Las Vegas production show wig shop: high volume of stock synthetic wigs washed in batches in a dedicated shop with sinks and wig dryers, then reset on blocks to a standardized show look and racked for the next cast rotation.

Freelance artist or small dance/drag/variety gig: wigs washed in a home kitchen sink, bathtub, or a client's bathroom, then air-dried on stands or set with rollers on a block on a table, with no dedicated wig-room equipment and varied wig types and conditions.

sources.title: DYMO-Hair: Generalizable Volumetric Dynamics Modeling for Robot Hair Manipulation (arXiv:2510.06199)
sources.claim: DYMO-Hair (CMU) is an autonomous model-based robot hair-manipulation system whose real-world tests consist of a robot arm repositioning hair on two physical wigs mounted on a head form in a lab, toward a goal hairstyle image. It does not wash, block, roller-set, dry, or dress a wig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic hair styling on wigs. It is the closest published capability to 'reset a wig' and marks the ceiling of the art — coarse strand repositioning with a single tool on a fixed mannequin — far short of washing, pinning to a block, roller/pin-curl setting, drying, and dressing to a period style.

sources.developer: MIT CSAIL and Harvard Soft Math Lab

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic detangling/brushing of wigs, a sub-step of combing out a wig after washing. It covers only brushing on a fixtured head form and provides no washing, blocking, setting, or drying capability.

sources.title: Hair care gets a high-tech upgrade with AI-powered washers | EYESHENZHEN

It washes hair attached to a living person's head in a fixed basin; it does not handle a detached wig or set/style it afterward.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine washing of hair. It substantiates only the shampoo/rinse sub-step performed on a person's head held in a purpose-built basin; it cannot pick up, wash, block, set, dry, or dress a detached theatrical wig.

tasks.label: Clean and sanitize tools and work environment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-client reprocessing of reusable metal implements (nippers, cuticle pushers, tweezers, metal files) at a nail salon station or back sink: pick used tools off the station, scrub with soap and brush under running water, rinse, fully immerse in EPA-registered hospital-grade disinfectant for the labeled contact time, remove, dry, and store in a clean covered container; log if the state board requires.

Between-client cleaning and disinfection of a pedicure foot spa: drain the basin, remove visible debris, remove filter screen/inlet jets and other removable parts, scrub bowl and parts with soap or disinfectant, refill with water plus disinfectant and circulate it through the jets for the required contact time, drain, rinse and wipe dry.

Station turnover between clients on a busy salon floor: discard used single-use items (files, buffers, orangewood sticks, toe separators, liners), wipe and disinfect table top, hand rest/armrest, lamp, drawer pulls and client chair, replace the towel/liner, and tidy polish bottles, brushes and supplies - done in a few minutes with other clients seated nearby.
End-of-shift floor care in the salon: sweep or vacuum nail clippings, acrylic dust and debris around manicure tables, pedicure chairs and the reception area, then damp-mop the hard floor.

End-of-day / weekly deep clean: empty trash and dispose of chemical-soaked waste, clean and disinfect sinks, counters and restroom, wash and dry salon towels, wipe down pedicure chairs and upholstery, clean dust-collector or ventilation filters, refill disinfectant jars and restock supplies.

sources.system: STERIS ATLAS Workflow Automation Vehicle with AMSCO washer-disinfectors

sources.claim: STERIS ATLAS ('Bella'), an autonomously navigating workflow vehicle in a hospital sterile processing department, picks up racks of used instruments and loads them into automated washer-disinfectors that run the validated cleaning/disinfection cycle.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reprocessing small stainless-steel hand instruments. Nail implements (nippers, pushers, tweezers) are the same class of object with a lighter soil load and a comparable requirement - clean, then disinfect for a validated contact time - so racked machine washing with robotic rack handling transfers.

Salon implements and a detachable spa basin are comparable objects - hard, non-fragile items needing scrubbing plus a sanitizing step - so the machine-side capability transfers when the work is presented to it.

tasks.label: Apply undercoat and clear or colored polish onto nails with brush.

instances.label: Salon manicure table, regular lacquer on natural fingernails: tech applies undercoat/base, two coats of a single cream color and a clear top coat to ten fingernails, keeping polish off cuticles and sidewalls and capping the free edge; client's hands rest on a towel and are repositioned by the tech; finish must be clean enough to send the client out without touch-ups.

Salon gel (soak-off) manicure on fingernails: thin gel base coat, one to two gel color coats and gel top coat, each flash-cured under an LED lamp between coats, with meticulous cuticle-line placement (gel on skin causes lifting) and free-edge capping.

Pedicure station: tech applies undercoat, color and clear top coat to ten toenails while the client sits in a pedicure chair with feet on a footrest, using toe separators; nails are small, curved, sometimes thickened or discolored, and the tech works at an awkward angle while holding and spreading the toes.

Polish work on enhancements or with detail: base and color coats over acrylic/gel-X extensions or long artificial nails, French tips, two-tone or ombre bases, plus hand-painted art or accent nails over the color, finished with clear top coat.

Mobile/on-location service: house call, bridal party, or nursing-home visit where the tech carries a kit and applies undercoat, color and clear top coat to a client's fingernails wherever the client is seated (kitchen table, hotel room, bedside).

tasks.label: Shape and smooth ends of nails, using scissors, files, or emery boards.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Nail salon / salon-service area of a retail store: a cooperative adult client's ten natural fingernails, short-to-medium length, bare or with polish already removed. Tech files the free edge to a requested round/square/oval shape with an emery board or file and smooths the edges before buffing and polish.

Pedicure at a salon or day spa: client's ten toenails in a pedicure chair/footbath. Tech clips length with toenail nippers/scissors, then files the thicker, often ridged or discolored free edges straight and smooths the corners; feet are wet, positioned by the client, and nail thickness varies widely.

Acrylic, hard-gel or Gel-X enhancement full set or two-week fill in a salon: tech files/shapes the artificial free edge (square, coffin, almond, stiletto) and refines length and sidewalls with a hand file and an electric e-file, removing substantial product from a hard extension without damaging the natural nail or skin.

Mobile / on-site service in a client's home, assisted-living apartment or nursing-home room: elderly or homebound client, hands and feet presented in a chair or bed, thick, brittle, fungal or ridged nails, tremor or arthritis, variable lighting and no fixed station. Tech clips and files nails to a safe smooth edge.

Salon service on atypical or damaged natural nails: very long nails needing substantial length removal with clippers/scissors before filing, bitten or torn nails, splits and hangnail-prone edges, children's or men's short nails, clients who move or are ticklish. Requires judgment about how much to remove and careful blade work.

tasks.label: Prepare nail cuticles with water and oil, using cuticle knives to push back cuticles and scissors or nippers to trim cuticles.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard salon manicure for a healthy adult client at a manicure table: soak fingertips in warm soapy water or apply cuticle remover/oil, push back the eponychium on all ten nails with a metal pusher/cuticle knife, scrape residue off the nail plate, then nip hangnails and excess cuticle with nippers without drawing blood; performed on a live, moving hand.

Salon pedicure with the client's feet in a spa tub: oil/soften toenail cuticles, push them back on ten toes at awkward angles, clean lateral nail folds, and nip dead skin, hangnails and overgrown cuticle around thick, ridged or ingrown-prone toenails while the client sits reclined.

Cuticle prep preceding a gel or acrylic enhancement: dry or lightly oiled prep in which the cuticle must be lifted and cleaned right to the nail wall (pusher or e-file bit), non-living tissue nipped off cleanly, and the plate left free of pterygium so product does not lift; tight sidewalls and short nail beds are common.

Client with problem cuticles or fragile tissue: ragged torn hangnails, badly overgrown or dry split cuticles, bitten nails, elderly clients with thin skin, or a diabetic/blood-thinner client where the tech must judge what may be trimmed, work gently, respond to flinching, and stop short of live tissue.

Mobile/off-site service in a private home, hotel room or care-facility bedside (bridal party, homebound or elderly client): the tech brings a bowl of water, oil, pusher and nippers, works on a sofa, bed or kitchen table with variable lighting and posture, and performs the same soften-push-trim sequence.

sources.title: The First Five-step Robotic Manicure Is Coming to Ulta Beauty (WWD)
sources.claim: 10Beauty's robotic manicure machine, deployed commercially at Ulta Beauty stores, performs an autonomous five-step manicure whose cuticle step is a softening solution plus a brush; it files without blades and does not cut cuticles.
sources.transferJustification: Same task domain (nail service on a client's hand); cited to show the scope of the only deployed nail-care robot — cuticle care limited to a softening serum and brush, with no knife or nipper work.

tasks.label: Prepare customers' nails in soapy water, using swabs, files, and orange sticks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Classic manicure prep at a nail-salon table: cooperative adult client with healthy natural nails soaks fingertips in a bowl of warm soapy water, tech dries the hand, pushes back and cleans the cuticles with an orange stick, files and shapes each nail to the requested shape, swabs under the free edge, and readies the nails for polish.

Pedicure prep in a salon: client's feet soaking in a soapy whirlpool foot bath, tech works one foot at a time out of the water — clipping/filing thick toenails to shape, pushing back and cleaning toe cuticles with an orange stick, swabbing under the nail plates, on feet that vary widely in size, callus and nail condition.

Pedicure prep as half of a mani-pedi combo in a busy salon under time pressure: soapy foot soak, toenail shaping, cuticle work and swabbing, while the client sits reclined in a pedicure spa chair and the tech kneels/sits at the footbath.

Salon prep on difficult nails: soak-off/removal of gel, dip or acrylic enhancements, bitten or peeling nails, deep ridges, overgrown or torn cuticles, hangnails and stained nails — soapy-water softening plus extensive orange-stick, file and swab work, with judgment about how much to remove and when to refer out.

Mobile service to a homebound or care-facility client (private home, assisted-living room, hospital bedside): portable basin of soapy water on a towel, elderly client with thick, brittle, curved nails, tremor or limited hand/foot mobility; tech positions the limb, softens, files and cleans nails with swabs and orange sticks.

Convenience on-location manicure prep for a healthy adult client (bridal party at a home or hotel room, corporate/event pop-up): portable soapy soak bowl, standard file/orange-stick/swab prep on natural fingernails before polish.

sources.title: The First Robotic Manicure System Launches at Ulta Beauty | NewBeauty

tasks.label: Remove previously applied nail polish, using liquid remover and swabs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Salon manicure appointment: client arrives with one- to two-week-old regular lacquer on ten fingernails. Tech saturates a cotton pad/swab with acetone remover, presses and wipes each nail, and cleans residue from sidewalls and the cuticle line at a manicure table on a busy salon floor.

Salon soak-off of gel/shellac (or dip/acrylic overlay) on fingernails: buff the topcoat, wrap each finger in acetone-soaked cotton and foil, wait 10-15 minutes, then scrape softened product off with a pusher, re-soak stubborn nails, without gouging the natural plate.

Pedicure: client seated in a spa pedicure chair, feet over the footbath. Tech removes old regular lacquer from ten toenails with acetone-soaked pads/swabs, working around thick, curved, ridged or discolored nails and surrounding calloused skin, bending over the footrest.
Pedicure gel removal: gel or gel-overlay toenail polish soaked off with foil wraps and/or e-file thinning, then scraped clean, on toes of varying shape and condition in the pedicure chair.

Mobile / on-location service: house call, nursing-home resident at bedside or in a wheelchair, or hospital pre-op removal. Tech works from a portable kit on a lap or tray table with variable lighting and seating; usually regular lacquer, often on frail or arthritic hands.

instances.label: Standard manicure at a walk-in nail salon: technician takes the client's hands across a small table, visually and by touch assesses nail and skin condition (dryness, hangnails, ragged/dead cuticle, calluses, discoloration), soaks and towels the hands, pushes back and nips dead cuticle skin, buffs off rough dead skin at fingertips, then applies lotion and gives a 2-5 minute hand and forearm massage before polish.

Spa/deluxe manicure in a salon or day spa: exfoliating sugar or salt scrub worked over hands and forearms and rinsed off, dead-skin sloughing at knuckles and cuticles, warm towel or paraffin dip, followed by an extended (5-10 minute) pressure-point hand, finger-joint and forearm massage with oil or cream on a live, freely-moving client.

Client with problem hands: heavy calluses or corns on palms/fingers, deeply cracked dry skin, torn hangnails, arthritic or fragile elderly skin, bitten nails or scar tissue; technician must judge how much dead tissue can safely be removed, avoid drawing blood, adjust massage pressure, and recognize conditions (fungal, warts, inflammation, open wounds) that require declining service or referral.

Mobile/at-home service: manicurist travels to a client's home, an assisted-living resident's bedside, or a bridal party in a hotel room; works on a kitchen table, sofa arm, or wheelchair tray with variable lighting and no fixed station, assessing hand condition, removing dead skin and massaging hands in a setting taken as found.

Express/high-volume service (gel fill, polish change, mall or airport nail bar): quick look at the hands and cuticles, brief buffing away of dead cuticle skin, quick lotion application and a short 60-90 second hand rub, done under time pressure between back-to-back clients.

tasks.label: Roughen surfaces of fingernails, using abrasive wheel.

instances.label: Nail salon, gel-polish service on natural nails: the tech runs a fine sanding band on an electric file (or a 180/240-grit buffer) over the whole nail plate of all ten fingers, out to the sidewalls and eponychium, to remove shine so the gel base coat bonds; must not thin the plate, cut skin, or leave shiny spots that cause lifting. The client's hand rests loose on a towel and moves.

Nail salon, full set of acrylic / hard gel / Gel-X extensions: tech etches the entire natural nail plate with a carbide or sanding-band bit on a 20,000-35,000 rpm e-file, feathering to the cuticle line and sidewalls, then dusts and dehydrates before tips/forms are applied. Over-filing thins or burns the plate; under-filing makes the enhancement pop off.

Nail salon, two- to three-week fill/rebalance of an existing acrylic or gel enhancement: the abrasive wheel files down the grown-out product, blends the ledge, and roughens both the remaining product and the exposed natural regrowth around the cuticle before new product is applied.

Nail salon, basic manicure with regular polish or a natural finish: a light pass of a fine abrasive buffer/wheel across the nail plate to smooth ridges, dull the shine and give polish something to grip; purely cosmetic acceptance standard, no adhesion-critical bond and no work tight to the cuticle.

Off-site service - client's home, hotel room, assisted-living resident's room or bridal/event party: the tech works with a portable drill or buffer on a kitchen table or bedside tray, variable lighting and seating, often elderly or brittle/ridged nails, roughening the plate before gel or an enhancement.

instances.label: Nail salon manicure station: client arrives with one split or cracked natural nail; the tech preps and dehydrates the nail plate, cuts a silk or fiberglass patch to the crack's shape with scissors/tweezers, seats it with brush-on resin, sprays activator, then files, buffs and blends the repair flush with the surrounding nail before polish. Live hand that moves slightly; skin must not be glued or resin-flooded into sidewalls.

Salon: full set of ten silk/fiberglass wrap overlays on thin, peeling natural nails for strength. Each nail is shaped and dehydrated, a precut wrap trimmed to that nail's curve, adhered, resined in two to three thin layers with activator between, then filed to a smooth, even, apex-correct overlay across all ten nails.

Salon: two-to-three-week maintenance/fill on existing wraps. Tech assesses lifting, files down old resin, removes loose fabric, applies a fresh wrap strip over the regrowth zone at the cuticle line, re-resins, rebalances the whole nail and buffs to a seamless surface.

Pedicure station: repair of a cracked or split toenail (or reinforcing a wrapped tip) with silk wrap and resin on a foot in a spa chair/footrest, with poorer access and lighting, sometimes over a thickened or damaged nail plate.

Mobile/on-location service: wrap repair performed in a client's home, an assisted-living room, a hotel room, or a bridal suite, using a portable kit with improvised seating and lighting and no fixed station.

tasks.label: Extend nails using powder, solvent, and paper forms attached to tips of customers' fingers to support and shape artificial nails.

instances.label: Standard full set of sculpted acrylic extensions at a walk-in nail salon: tech preps and dehydrates the natural nails, slides a paper/mylar form under each free edge and pinches it to the finger contour, picks up monomer-and-polymer beads with a sable brush, places apex/smile-line/free-edge beads, sculpts length and C-curve, waits for cure, removes forms, then files, shapes and buffs ten nails and finishes with color. ~90-120 minutes on a living, moving hand of varying nail bed shape.

Two-to-three-week fill/rebalance at a salon: existing enhancement is drilled down and rebalanced, and one or two nails that have lifted or snapped off are re-sculpted from scratch on a paper form back to matching length, apex and shape so the set looks uniform. Requires blending old and new product invisibly.

Long or dramatic sculpted sets at a nail studio: extreme-length stiletto, coffin or duck-tip nails built on forms, often with encapsulated glitter, ombre smile lines, or 3D acrylic detail, for a special-occasion or regular long-nail client. Heavy freehand sculpting judgment, custom form placement, and structural strength requirements.

Single-nail emergency repair/reconstruction at a salon: a client arrives with one broken enhancement or a torn natural nail; the tech fits a form to that one finger, sculpts a replacement extension to match the other nine in length and curve, files it in and re-polishes just that nail, usually squeezed between booked appointments.

Mobile/freelance work: a nail tech sculpts acrylic extensions on forms at a client's home, a bridal suite, a dorm room, or backstage/on set - a folding table, variable lighting and ventilation, pets and children present, layout different at every site.

tasks.label: Whiten underside of nails with white paste or pencils.

instances.label: Nail salon manicure table: after shaping and buffing natural fingernails, the tech dampens a white whitening pencil (or dabs white paste) and draws it along the underside of each free edge, tilting the client's hand and fingers to reach beneath the nail, wiping excess off the skin, to create a natural French-tip effect on a seated, moving client.

Salon pedicure station: after soaking, clipping and filing toenails, the tech whitens the undersides of the toenail free edges with a white pencil or paste, working on the client's foot in a footbath/footrest, spreading toes and reaching the small, often short and curved free edges of the lesser toes.

Salon client with stained or discolored nails (from dark polish, smoking, or dirt): the tech first cleans beneath the free edge with a brush or orangewood stick, then applies white paste under the edges of irregular, short, or bitten nails, blending so the whitening looks even across ten mismatched nails.

Mobile/on-location service: manicurist visits a client's home, a nursing home room, or a bridal party suite with a portable kit and whitens the undersides of the client's nails while seated wherever space allows, with variable lighting, seating, and a client who may have limited hand mobility.

High-end spa, pageant, or photo-shoot prep: whitening under the free edge must produce a crisp, uniformly bright line on all ten nails to camera-ready standard, often combined with a sheer pink overlay, under time pressure before the shoot or event.

tasks.label: Sterilize equipment and clean work areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Between-client turnover of a treatment room in a day spa or salon: strip used sheets, blanket cover, headband and towels into the hamper, remake the vinyl treatment bed with fresh linens/table paper, spray-and-wipe the bed, headrest, trolley, mag lamp and steamer arm with disinfectant, discard used cotton, gauze, wax sticks and gloves, wipe the sink and counter, and reset supplies — all inside a 10-15 minute gap before the next client.

Reprocessing reusable metal implements after treatments (tweezers, comedone extractors, lancet holders, scissors, electrolysis forceps and tips): rinse and scrub off debris, run the ultrasonic cleaner, dry, pouch and heat-seal, load and run the tabletop steam autoclave, verify/record the indicator and cycle log, and store the sterile pouches in the closed dispensary cabinet.

Cleaning and servicing treatment equipment in the room: scrape and wipe out the wax pot and its collar, empty/descale and refill the facial steamer with distilled water, alcohol-wipe high-frequency electrodes and the laser/IPL handpiece and cooling window, clean microdermabrasion handpiece and diamond tips, flush hydrafacial tubing, and wipe LED panel and magnifying lens.

End-of-day floor care in the spa after the last client: vacuum or sweep the treatment room and the adjoining corridor/reception floor and damp-mop the hard floors, working around the bed, stool, trolley and cords in a fixed-layout, institution-controlled facility.

End-of-day linen, waste and restock round: sort soiled towels and sheets, load the washer, transfer to the dryer, fold and restock the linen shelves; empty the treatment-room trash and the covered/biohazard container and sharps box into the back-of-house waste, and refill product, gloves and disposables.

Mobile or in-home work: an esthetician working in a client's home or a small rented studio breaks down and sanitizes the portable treatment table, wipes the improvised work surface (dining table, bathroom counter), bags soiled linens, and disinfects tools using a kitchen or bathroom sink, with layout and conditions differing at every site.

Body-treatment cleansing during a spa scrub, wrap or back facial: spreading cleanser/lotion over back, arms and legs and removing the product with warm towels, mitts or a rinse (Vichy shower) while the client lies draped on a wet or dry treatment table.

instances.label: Classic European/relaxation facial in a day spa or salon treatment room: client reclined and draped on a facial bed, skin analysis under a mag lamp, double cleanse, steam, enzyme or scrub exfoliation, light extractions, facial/neck/décolleté massage, a setting or clay/gel mask applied with fan brush and removed with warm towels, then toner, serum, moisturizer and SPF. 50-75 minutes, product choices adjusted to skin type and client feedback.

Superficial chemical peel (glycolic, lactic, salicylic or Jessner) in a medspa or dermatology practice: intake and contraindication screening, degreasing the skin, applying acid with gauze/brush in a set order while watching for frosting, erythema and client discomfort, timing and neutralizing or removing, then applying post-peel balm and SPF and giving home-care instructions.

Acne/congested-skin treatment facial in a salon or clinic: steam or softening solution, manual extractions of comedones and pustules with gloved fingers and a loop tool around the nose, chin and forehead, high-frequency or LED, then a sulfur/clay mask, removal, and calming finishing products on inflamed, uneven skin.

Contact device-based facial in a spa or medspa: hydradermabrasion (e.g., HydraFacial), microdermabrasion or ultrasonic treatment where the specialist presses and glides a handpiece over the contours of the face with controlled pressure and suction, changes tips, infuses serums, follows with a mask and finishing products, adapting passes to sensitive areas.

Light- or laser-based facial rejuvenation session in a medspa or dermatology clinic: cleanse and degrease, place eye shields, then deliver non-ablative laser toning / IPL photofacial / LED passes over the whole face with the handpiece held at a set distance and overlap, monitoring skin temperature and reaction, then apply post-treatment soothing product and SPF.

Mobile or event facial performed off-premises: esthetician travels to a client's home, hotel room, or a bridal/corporate event, sets up a portable table or works with the client in a kitchen chair, and performs a cleanse-exfoliate-mask-moisturize facial with limited water access, variable lighting and no fixed layout.

instances.label: New-client consultation in a day-spa/salon treatment room: client reclines on a draped table, esthetician cleanses the face, swings a 5x magnifying lamp (sometimes a Wood's lamp or skin scanner) over the skin, and evaluates skin type, pore congestion, dehydration, sensitivity/redness, pigmentation and fine lines; findings are documented and drive the treatment plan.

Quick pre-service check in a spa/salon treatment room before a facial, chemical peel, microdermabrasion or wax: a brief look, usually under the magnifying lamp after cleansing, for active acne, open lesions, cold sores, sunburn, rash or irritation, to confirm the service and adjust product strength.

Med-spa or laser hair-removal clinic assessment before a laser/IPL session: examine the treatment area under bright light/magnification to judge Fitzpatrick type and recent tanning, note moles, tattoos, folliculitis, scarring or hyperpigmentation, and record findings that set laser parameters.

Body-area examination for back facials, body treatments or electrolysis: client draped prone/supine on a table, esthetician moves the magnifying lamp over back, chest, arms, legs or bikini area to assess ingrown hairs, folliculitis, keratosis pilaris, congestion and moles.

Short skin assessment at a cosmetics counter, beauty-retail store or brand event: client seated in an open retail area under mixed lighting, 3-5 minute look with a handheld magnifier or counter-top scanner to characterize skin type and concerns and steer product choice.

Mobile/in-home esthetician visit: examine the client's skin in the client's living room or bedroom with a portable magnifying lamp on an improvised setup, variable lighting, pets and furniture, before performing a facial.

tasks.label: Perform simple extractions to remove blackheads.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Standard facial in a day spa or salon treatment room: after cleansing and steam, the esthetician stretches the skin with gloved fingers wrapped in gauze (or a comedone loop) and expresses blackheads from the nose, chin and forehead of a reclined client, judging by sight and touch which pores will release and stopping before bruising, then sanitizing the area.

Acne/congestion facial in a med-spa or dermatology practice: extensive extraction of open comedones over cheeks, nose and chin on oily, congested skin, sometimes after enzyme or chemical exfoliation and with a sterile lancet to open tight follicles; client gives continuous pain feedback and the practice's clinical standards apply.

Extractions on sensitive, reactive, rosacea-prone, or richly pigmented skin in a spa/clinic room: minimal, carefully limited pressure on a handful of comedones, abandoning any that resist, to avoid capillary damage, bruising or post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation.

Back/chest/shoulder ('bacne') extractions during a body facial: client prone or seated, larger area of thicker skin with dilated pores, extraction over curved, hair-bearing surfaces after steam or hot towels.

Express add-on extraction at a high-volume facial chain: 5-10 minutes of targeted nose/chin extraction inside a fixed 30-50 minute service, under time pressure and with room turnover and sanitation between clients.

Mobile/at-home esthetician: extractions performed in a client's living room or bedroom on a portable table, with improvised lighting, a handheld steamer or hot towels, and no fixed layout or facility standards.

sources.system: LUUM Precision Lash / Beauty Experience Automation

sources.claim: LUUM's 'Beauty Experience Automation' robot applies eyelash extensions to a client's eyes in commercial retail studios (Ulta Beauty, Nordstrom), with human lash artists prepping, advising and evaluating rather than performing the application. It is the closest deployed robot performing a precision beauty service on a client's face, but it bonds extensions to lashes and never applies compressive force to skin or expresses pore contents.
sources.transferJustification: Related task = eyelash extension application on the human face. It shares the client-on-a-table setting and sub-millimeter visual targeting, but the manipulation is adhesive placement onto hair fibers, not force-controlled compression of soft tissue to expel a sebum plug, and it involves no tactile judgment of skin resistance or lesion selection. It therefore does not substantiate blackhead extraction.

Transfer fails for extraction: Aescape works only on the back and posterior legs of a prone client through a table interface, with force resolution suited to muscle groups, not the millimeter-scale pinch pressure around individual facial pores, and it performs no lesion detection or sebum expression.

tasks.label: Apply chemical peels to reduce fine lines and age spots.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Superficial peel (glycolic, lactic, salicylic or light Jessner) in a day-spa/salon treatment room as part of a facial: skin intake and contraindication check, cleanse and degrease, occlusive barrier at eye corners/nasal folds/lips, apply acid with fan brush or gauze section by section on the reclined client's face, watch for erythema and ask about stinging while fanning, time the contact, neutralize or rinse at the shampoo bowl, then apply calming serum, moisturizer and SPF.

Peel in a medical spa or dermatology/plastic surgery office under physician protocol (TCA, Jessner, or layered combination to a medium depth): prep with acetone/alcohol, apply layer by layer while judging the frosting endpoint on each facial zone, manage patient discomfort with fans and cold compresses, stop or spot-treat as the endpoint appears, then post-care occlusive and written aftercare.

Peel applied to body areas for age spots and hyperpigmentation - dorsal hands, forearms, decolletage, upper back - with draping and repositioning of the client, larger surface coverage with gauze or brush, uneven and often sun-damaged skin, then neutralization and post-care.

Peel on a higher-risk client: Fitzpatrick IV-VI skin, melasma, rosacea-prone or active acne, or a first-time client. Requires patch test review, conservative acid choice and shortened contact time, continuous monitoring for early frosting or excessive reaction, and aborting/neutralizing early if the skin responds unexpectedly.

Mobile or on-location esthetician performing a light peel in a client's home or a hotel/bridal suite: improvised setup on a portable table, variable lighting and water access, supplies carried in, same cleanse-apply-monitor-neutralize-post-care sequence.

Cited to show the frontier and its limits, not to support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Remove body and facial hair by applying wax.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Facial waxing in a salon/wax-center treatment room: eyebrow shaping, upper lip, chin, sides of face. Client reclined on a treatment table; esthetician heats hard wax to correct temperature, tests it, spreads a thin layer along hair growth on a curved, mobile face within millimeters of the eye, holds skin taut, flicks the set wax off against growth, tweezes strays, applies post-care and checks symmetry against the client's requested brow shape.

Bikini line / Brazilian waxing in a salon treatment room: intimate, highly sensitive, folded and deformable skin; client is repositioned several times (knees up, side-lying, all-fours); hard wax applied in small sections at controlled temperature, skin pulled taut with the free hand, fast strip pull, tweezing, hygiene protocols (no double-dipping, drape management), continuous verbal reassurance and pain management.

Large-area limb waxing (full/half leg, arms) in a salon room: soft wax spread with a spatula or roll-on over broad curved surfaces, muslin strips laid, pressed and pulled section by section around knees, ankles and shins, avoiding moles, varicose veins, bruises and irritated skin; strays tweezed and lotion applied.

Underarm waxing in a salon room: small concave area with hair growing in several directions, requiring the arm to be lifted and the skin stretched flat, hard wax in two or three passes with reapplication over stubborn areas, and careful checking for lifted skin.

Men's body waxing (back, chest, shoulders) in a salon room: dense, coarse hair over a large curved torso, client prone or supine, multiple soft-wax passes with strips, higher pull force, ingrown-hair and skin-lift risk, plus trimming before waxing.

Mobile / in-home waxing appointment: esthetician travels to the client's home or hotel room, sets up a portable wax warmer and folding table (or works with the client on a bed or couch), variable lighting, pets, furniture and no standard layout, then performs brow, leg or bikini waxing.

sources.title: AI and Robotic Massage, Delivered On-Demand - ASME
sources.claim: Aescape's robotic massage table performs autonomous, force-controlled contact treatment on a client lying on a table, and is commercially deployed in gyms, hotel spas and Massage Envy locations. It is the closest deployed system that physically treats a human body in a salon-type room, but it delivers pressure through fixed end effectors and does not handle heated wax, assess hair growth direction, or strip hair from skin.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic massage of a clothed client on a treatment table in a spa (E2). Transfer to waxing is NOT supported: waxing requires temperature-controlled viscous material handling, thin-film spreading along hair growth on deformable contours, bimanual skin-tensioning and a fast, angle-critical strip pull with bruise/skin-lift risk — none of which Aescape's pressure-applying arms demonstrate.
