sources.claim: A robotic prototype delivered Q-switched Nd:YAG laser skin rejuvenation to one side of subjects' faces in a dermatology clinic study, i.e., robotic aesthetic treatment of human faces exists only for non-contact energy delivery, not for wax depilation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic laser treatment of facial skin in a clinic. Transfer to waxing is NOT supported: the robot scans and aims a laser at a standoff distance with no contact forces, no material application and no epilation by traction; waxing's core physical demands are absent.

sources.system: Rocozyer robotic laser hair removal machine
sources.title: The Newest & Latest Laser Hair Removal Machine in 2025: World's first #1 AI Robot for Laser Hair Removal
sources.claim: Vendor-marketed 'robotic' laser hair removal machines (e.g., Rocozyer) use robotic arms to aim laser handpieces at skin; these are hair-removal devices, not wax application, and their degree of autonomy is not documented in independent sources.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laser epilation. Even taken at face value it addresses a different modality (light-based follicle destruction) with no wax heating, spreading, setting or stripping; autonomy is unverified, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

tasks.label: Tint eyelashes and eyebrows.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Eyebrow tint in a salon or day-spa treatment room, alone or added to a brow wax/shape: consult and match dye color, verify patch test, cleanse the brow, apply barrier cream to surrounding skin, mix dye with developer, brush it through the brow hairs following the mapped shape, time 3-10 minutes, wipe off with damp cotton and clear skin staining, check symmetry.

Eyelash tint in a salon: client supine with eyes closed, protective pads placed under lower lashes, barrier cream on lids, dye mixed and applied to upper and lower lashes with a micro-applicator without contacting the cornea or lid skin, timed, then fully removed with damp cotton pads while the eye stays closed; safety-critical chemical work near the eye.

Combined brow and lash tint bundled with adjacent chemical services (lash lift, brow lamination, henna brows) as a 45-75 minute multi-step service: separate solutions, timed steps, rinsing/blotting between stages, and final shaping and grooming of the brows.

Difficult cases in a salon: sparse, gray, coarse or very fair brow/lash hair needing custom color mixing and longer or repeated processing, sensitive or reactive skin, an anxious client who blinks or fidgets, or corrective work over a previous over-dark tint.

Mobile or on-location tinting (client's home, bridal suite, hotel room) with a portable kit: improvised seating and lighting, no treatment bed, dye mixed and applied and removed in a setting the esthetician does not control.

sources.title: Luum Precision Lash: the 200 Best Inventions of 2024 (TIME)
sources.claim: LUUM's Precision Lash robot applies individual eyelash extensions to a reclining client's natural lashes in commercial salon studios using computer vision and soft-tipped tools; it is the closest existing system operating on human eyelashes, but it applies extensions, not dye, and does not do tinting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic eyelash extension application. Same objects (a client's individual eyelashes), same salon environment and reclined posture, finer precision than tinting requires. Transfer is only partial: the robot places dry fibers dipped in adhesive and never applies a liquid dye over the whole lash line, never times a chemical process, and never removes product from the lids, so it does not substantiate completion of a tint.

sources.title: I Got Eyelash Extensions From An AI Robot And I'm Hooked (Marie Claire)
sources.claim: At a LUUM appointment a human lash artist performs the consultation, cleanses the lashes and places the barcoded eye pads; the robot then performs only the extension-application step, and LUUM states its robots require lash artists to run them.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (robotic lash extensions). Shows the prep and finishing steps around the eye — cleansing, barrier/pad placement, product handling on the lids — are still done by a human, which are exactly the steps a tint requires in addition to application.

sources.title: Nail Painting Robot Debuts in Beverly Hills (Nails Magazine)
sources.claim: Clockwork's MiNiCURE is a fully autonomous robot that applies liquid nail polish to a customer's fingernails in retail stores and airport spa locations, showing autonomous liquid cosmetic application on a human body part — but on nails presented in a fixture, not on the face or eye area, and without prep or removal steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous application of a liquid cosmetic to a client's body. Environment (retail/salon) matches, but the workpiece is a rigid nail plate inserted into the machine, precision requirements and the consequences of error are far below dye work millimeters from the cornea, and the machine performs no removal or skin-staining cleanup.

sources.title: I Tried Aescape, the High-Tech Robot Massage—Here's My Review (Parade)
sources.claim: Aescape's robotic massage system delivers autonomous table-based massage to clients at roughly 100 gym, hotel and spa locations, demonstrating force-controlled robotic contact with a human body in commercial wellness settings — but on the clothed back and legs, not the face, and with no cosmetic product application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous robotic body treatment on a client lying on a table in a spa. Establishes safe compliant robot-human contact in an E2 beauty/wellness facility, but the contact is broad-area pressure through fabric, not sub-millimeter dye work on brow and lash hairs, so it cannot substantiate tinting.

sources.title: Blackdot's AI Tattoo Machine is Essentially a Robot That Inks Your Skin (TechEBlog)
sources.claim: Blackdot's automatic tattooing device autonomously deposits ink into human skin at dedicated studios, showing machine-controlled precision marking of a living person's skin — demonstrated on limbs with the device docked to the skin, not on the face or eye area.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous pigment application to human skin in a commercial studio. Precision on skin is comparable, but the work area is a flat, immobilized limb held in a docking apparatus; no demonstration exists on the face, around the eye, or with a rinse-and-remove chemical process.

sources.title: new l'oreal applicator uses AR to print up the perfect eyebrow look in seconds (designboom)
sources.claim: L'Oreal's Brow Magic, the main automated eyebrow-makeup device to reach market, is a handheld printer that the user brushes with primer and then sweeps across the brow by hand — a human-guided applicator rather than a robot that performs the service.
sources.transferJustification: Directly adjacent task (automated brow coloring), but the device is moved by a human hand and deposits washable makeup rather than performing a timed oxidative tint, so it is not a robotic system completing the task.

tasks.label: Collaborate with plastic surgeons and dermatologists to provide patients with preoperative and postoperative skin care.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-operative skin conditioning in a plastic surgery practice or affiliated medspa: over several weeks the esthetician performs the surgeon-ordered prep protocol on a client in a treatment room chair/table - cleansing, dermaplaning, light chemical peels, extractions - and starts the client on a topical regimen (retinoid, hydroquinone, sunscreen), adjusting for skin type, sensitivity and reaction.

Post-operative facial care after facelift, blepharoplasty, rhinoplasty or ablative resurfacing: gentle cleansing of crusting and dried blood around fresh incisions, applying occlusive ointment, calming masks or LED, avoiding sutures, drains and grafts, watching for infection or dehiscence and reporting findings back to the surgeon.

Post-procedure care in a dermatology office after lasers, injectables, or Mohs closure: cooling and soothing the treated area, applying barrier products, applying post-surgical camouflage makeup, and teaching home wound care while the physician moves to the next room.

Post-surgical manual lymphatic drainage and scar mobilization after body contouring (liposuction, abdominoplasty, breast surgery): very light directional strokes on bruised, swollen, sometimes drain-bearing tissue in the surgeon's office, working around compression garments and adapting pressure to patient pain and healing stage.

Consultation and care coordination: reviewing the surgeon's or dermatologist's orders and the chart, assessing the patient's skin (Fitzpatrick type, actives in use, contraindications), agreeing a pre/post regimen with the clinician, documenting in the EMR, and handing off products with hands-on application demonstration.

sources.title: Equinox Locations Add Aescape, a Fully Automated Massage Bed - Athletech News
sources.claim: Aescape's fully automated robotic massage table, with two robotic arms and 3D body scanning, is commercially deployed in spas inside Equinox fitness clubs and gives wellness massages to reclining clients without a therapist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bodywork on a reclining human client in a structured commercial facility. It is the closest deployed analogue to hands-on esthetic bodywork, but it treats healthy backs, arms and legs with a fixed set of strokes; it does not touch faces, healing incisions, drains or compression garments, and does not apply products or assess wounds, so it does not carry over to post-operative skin care.

sources.title: Lash Extensions From An AI Robot: Is This The Future Of Beauty? (Forbes)
sources.claim: LUUM's AI-powered lash robot autonomously applies eyelash extensions to clients' natural lashes in a commercial lash salon, using computer vision to work with sub-millimeter precision around the eye.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precise robotic beauty service performed on a client's face inside a salon. It shows face-adjacent dexterity, but it executes one narrowly specified, repeatable attachment operation on healthy lashes; it does not cleanse or treat healing skin, apply topical products over surgical sites, judge contraindications, or coordinate a regimen with a surgeon.

sources.title: Luum launches next-generation AI eyelash extension robot with faster application and national rollout
sources.claim: Luum's next-generation lash robot works on both eyes at once and shortens a full-set appointment to about 33 minutes, with a national rollout planned.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as the Forbes item (robotic lash extension on a client's face in a salon); cited to establish the current, most advanced state of commercial face-adjacent beauty robotics as of late 2025, which remains a single specialized cosmetic operation rather than pre/post-operative skin care.

sources.system: ARTAS iX / iXi Robotic Hair Restoration System
sources.title: ARTAS Robotic Hair Transplant | Venus Treatments USA
sources.claim: The ARTAS iX robotic hair restoration system operates on human scalp skin in a clinic, but it is a physician-directed surgical assistant for harvesting, site creation and implantation rather than an autonomous provider of skin care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic intervention on human skin in an aesthetic clinic. It is the most mature clinical skin-contact robot, yet it is physician-operated and limited to follicular unit harvesting/implantation on a fixtured scalp, so it substantiates no part of preoperative or postoperative esthetic skin care.

sources.developer: Carnegie Mellon University (Robotic Caregiving and Human Interaction Lab)
sources.title: SkinGrip: An Adaptive Soft Robotic Manipulator with Capacitive Sensing for Whole-Limb Bed Bathing Assistance (arXiv)
sources.claim: Research robots can autonomously wipe and clean a human limb for bed bathing, but performance is reported as partial cleaning effectiveness in a laboratory setting rather than clinical-quality skin care.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic cleansing of human skin with controlled contact force. It is the nearest research analogue to gentle post-operative cleansing, but it is a lab demonstration on healthy limbs with sub-worker cleaning rates and no handling of incisions, sutures, ointments or facial anatomy.

sources.system: Robotic wound redressing research platform (autonomous tape handling)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing (arXiv)
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic wound redressing, including handling tape and dressings on a wound, is still an open research problem addressed only in early-stage academic work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic care of a healing wound. The paper's framing as 'towards' autonomous tape handling shows that even the sub-step of removing and replacing a dressing is pre-deployment research, so post-operative skin care around fresh incisions is not substantiated at any environment tier.

sources.title: XpresSpa debuts Clockwork robotic manicures at MIA
sources.claim: Clockwork's fully autonomous manicure robot applies nail polish to customers in airport spa and retail locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cosmetic service applied to a human body part in a structured commercial facility. It marks the commercial frontier of beauty robotics, but it applies one product to rigid, presented fingernails and cannot substantiate treatment of living, healing facial skin or clinical coordination.

roles.title: Baggage Porters and Bellhops
roles.description: Handle baggage for travelers at transportation terminals or for guests at hotels or similar establishments.

tasks.label: Receive and mark baggage by completing and attaching claim checks.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel bell/luggage desk, standard case: a guest arriving early or checked out leaves one or two ordinary rolling suitcases for a few hours. The porter takes custody at the desk, completes a numbered claim tag (name/room/flight time), attaches it to the bag handle, hands the guest the matching stub, and moves the bag into the storage room.

Hotel bell desk, awkward/bulk case: a family or tour group leaves 6-12 mixed items at once - garment bags, golf clubs, cartons, strollers, backpacks, oversized cases. The porter writes and attaches a claim tag to each item, groups them under one stub or room number, and stacks them on carts in the storage room.

Hotel porte-cochere/driveway: bellhop meets an arriving taxi or car, lifts bags out of the trunk and back seat, tags each piece for room delivery or for storage while the guest checks in, gives the guest the stub, and loads the cart.

Airport curbside check-in (skycap): passenger pulls up at the terminal curb; the porter verifies reservation and ID at the curbside podium, weighs the bag, prints the IATA bag tag, loops and seals it around the bag handle, sticks the claim stub on the passenger's boarding pass receipt, and puts the bag on the induction belt - in traffic, weather and time pressure.

Other transportation terminals: cruise terminal curbside porters attaching cabin/sailing tags to bags before they go into cages; Amtrak/intercity bus checked-baggage counters completing and attaching destination checks; gate-check tagging of strollers and oversize carry-ons at the jet bridge.

sources.system: YOBOT (ABB IRB 6640 luggage storage robot, YOTEL New York)
sources.developer: ABB Robotics / Yotel (integrator Brooks Automation-style install reported by A3)
sources.title: News: An ABB Industrial Robot Provides Automated Luggage Storage and Retrieval at New Yotel in Manhattan
sources.claim: YOBOT, an ABB IRB 6640 industrial arm installed in the lobby of YOTEL New York, autonomously takes guests' luggage into custody in a bin, stores it in one of 117 lockers, and issues the guest a barcoded claim receipt used for retrieval - the hotel luggage-storage receive-and-claim-check function performed by a machine.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated guest luggage check-in/storage. It substitutes for the bell-desk act of receiving a bag and issuing a matched claim check; the claim identifier is a barcoded receipt tied to the stored bag rather than a tag looped on the handle.

sources.title: Luggage robot Yobot | horecatrends.com
sources.claim: In routine operation guests deposit their own bag into the bin at the YOBOT kiosk and receive a barcode receipt; the robot then handles storage and retrieval unattended in the hotel lobby.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (hotel luggage check-in/storage); shows the guest-facing intake step and issuance of the claim credential in a normal hotel lobby.

sources.system: Henn na Hotel cloakroom robotic arm (Yaskawa-type industrial arm)
sources.title: Henn na Hotel (変なホテル): Japan's Robot-Staffed Hotels
sources.claim: Henn na Hotel properties in Japan operate a lobby cloakroom robotic arm that stores guest items placed in a baggage handling door, but only within strict size limits (about 42 x 72 cm), i.e. small and medium items only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hotel cloakroom bag intake and storage; supports the same receive-and-claim function as a bell desk, and documents the size restriction that excludes bulky or oversized items.

sources.title: Robot bag drop being trialled at Geneva Airport's Terminal 1
sources.claim: SITA's Leo, the most advanced curbside baggage-check robot trialled at an airport (Geneva, 2016), navigates autonomously and prints bag tags, but passengers themselves load the bags and attach the printed tags; the robot performs no tag attachment.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the airport instance (curbside bag check-in). Cited as context for the negative judgment: even this purpose-built curbside robot leaves the receiving lift and the tag attachment to the passenger.

sources.system: Asiana Airlines Self Bag Drop (self-service bag drop units)
sources.title: Self Bag Drop | Asiana Airlines
sources.claim: Deployed airport self-service bag drop units automate scanning and belt induction but explicitly require the traveller to attach the baggage tag; no fielded machine loops and seals the tag onto the bag.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the airport tagging step. Used only as negative context: the state of the art in deployed airport baggage automation still assigns tag attachment to a human.

tasks.label: Greet incoming guests and escort them to their rooms.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Upscale full-service city hotel, single arriving party with 2-4 bags: porter greets guest at the curb/lobby door, takes bags off the vehicle onto a bell cart, walks the guest through the lobby, shares the elevator, proceeds down the corridor, opens the room door with the guest's key, sets bags on racks and briefly orients the guest before leaving.

Select-service, boutique or airport hotel: after check-in a bell/front-desk attendant welcomes the guest and walks them to their room with little or no luggage, pointing out the elevator, ice machine and breakfast area on the way, and handing off at the room door.

Convention/group arrival rush: a tour bus or conference wave arrives, crowded lobby and elevator queues, several parties greeted and escorted to rooms in quick succession with loaded luggage carts, room assignments coordinated with the front desk.

Resort or casino property with long or partly outdoor routes: greeting at the porte-cochere, luggage loaded, guest escorted along garden walkways or driven by golf cart to a villa/casita or distant tower, with property orientation conversation en route.

Guest needing extra assistance: elderly or mobility-impaired guest, wheelchair or walker, or a family with small children and a stroller; slow adapted pace, help through doors and elevators, escort to an accessible room.

sources.title: LG Airport Robots Take over Korea's Largest Airport
sources.claim: LG's Airport Guide Robot, deployed at Incheon International Airport, scans a passenger's boarding pass and autonomously escorts the traveler to their departure gate inside the terminal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting a person to a destination inside a large institution-controlled building. Same core capability as walking a hotel guest from the lobby to their room - person-paced leading, wayfinding and crowd avoidance among the public.

sources.title: New Room Service Robot Butler Robot for Hotels - Relay Delivery Robots
sources.claim: Relay (Botlr) service robots deployed in hotels navigate lobbies and corridors and ride the hotel elevator between floors on their own to reach a specific guest room door.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point travel from a hotel lobby to a named guest room, the exact route an escort must cover, including elevator use; it establishes hotel-route navigation but not guest-side greeting or luggage handling.

sources.title: Keenon Humanoid Robot Joins Hotel Workforce, Pioneering World's First General-Purpose + Special-Purpose Robot Collaboration Model
sources.claim: A Keenon XMAN-R1 humanoid deployed at the Shangri-La Traders Hotel, Shanghai Hongqiao Airport, autonomously greets arriving guests, answers questions and hands each guest a welcome gift, driven by the company's KOM2.0 vision-language-action model.

sources.title: Pudu Robotics and Shenzhen CTID Co. Ltd Launch the World's First Full-Scenario Robot-Serviced Hotel Project
sources.claim: At a hotel-project showcase, the PUDU T300 autonomously transported heavy luggage and operated elevators by itself, carrying up to 300 kg; Pudu plans it to move guests' luggage from the foyer to hotel rooms.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a guest's bags from the lobby to a guest floor. Covers the luggage-hauling half of a bellhop escort when bags are loaded onto the robot's deck, as a purpose-built setting would present them.

sources.title: A hotel robot that will give humans a 'Run' for their money
sources.claim: Yunji Technology's 'Run' hotel service robot, sold into Chinese chain hotels, delivers items to guest rooms and can lead guests who have lost their way to their rooms.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading people on foot through a busy public terminal, matching their pace - the walking-escort component of greeting and escorting hotel guests in a crowded lobby.

sources.title: FlashBot Max | Pudu Robotics' AI-enabled Multi-floor Delivery Robot for Semi-outdoor Hospitality
sources.claim: Pudu's FlashBot Max delivery robot is built for semi-outdoor hotel routes such as garden corridors, fitness zones and poolside areas in addition to indoor room service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous travel over a resort's semi-outdoor paths between the lobby and guest accommodation - the route an escort to a villa or casita must cover.

sources.claim: Negative evidence: the porter robots at Japan's Henn na Hotel, a property purpose-designed around robots, could not reach most guest rooms and the chain culled more than half its robot workforce.

sources.claim: Incheon International Airport operates a standing fleet of AirStar guide robots giving directions in multiple languages, AirPorter luggage-handling robots and autonomous AirRide shuttles that carry passengers needing assistance through the terminal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving a mobility-limited traveler and their bags to a destination within an institution-controlled building - the assistance component of escorting a guest who needs extra help.

tasks.label: Transport guests about premises and local areas, or arrange for transportation.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rooming an arriving hotel guest: bellhop meets the guest at the front desk, leads them across the lobby, calls and rides the elevator with them, walks the corridor and brings them to their room door (bags follow on a bell cart handled under the separate baggage task). Indoor, mapped, crowded at peak check-in.

Driving the property's courtesy shuttle/van: collect guests at the airport terminal curb or hotel porte-cochere, put their bags aboard, drive 5-20 minutes in mixed public-road traffic (signals, curbside queues, weather), and set them down at the other end.

Moving guests around a large resort/campus in a golf cart, tram or van: from lobby to a distant villa, pool, convention wing or parking area, on private drives and paths shared with pedestrians, on demand or on a fixed loop.

Transporting a guest or passenger with limited mobility in a wheelchair through a terminal or hotel: from check-in/lobby to the gate, room, restaurant or curb, at walking pace among other people, then returning the chair.

Departure handling: guest asks bell/door staff to arrange transportation (taxi, rideshare, town car, off-site shuttle); staff summons the vehicle by phone or app, tells the guest when it is at the door, walks them out to the porte-cochere/terminal curb and sees them and their bags into the vehicle.

tasks.label: Maintain clean lobbies or entrance areas for travelers or guests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Tidy-up round of a hotel lobby / terminal waiting area during operating hours: collect cups, bottles, newspapers and food wrappers left on side tables, sofas and window ledges; straighten chairs, cushions and magazines; empty the lobby and bell-desk waste bins (and the exterior ash urn) and replace liners; re-stage luggage carts. Guests and bags are present throughout.

Scheduled floor care of the lobby and entrance interior at a hotel or terminal: vacuuming carpet and entrance runners, dust-mopping or scrubbing marble/tile, usually during low-traffic hours, to a standard the front-office manager inspects.

On-demand spot clean of a soiled patch of hard lobby/entry floor after being alerted or spotting it: tracked-in rain water, slush, grit or dropped food/drink; mop or wet-vac the area and dry it while guests continue to walk through.

Difficult one-off incidents: broken glass or a dropped bottle near the entrance, a drink spilled into lobby carpet or upholstery, chewing gum, mud smeared over an area rug, or a sick guest's mess — requiring careful pickup, extraction or blotting, and moving furniture.

Wiping and polishing lobby surfaces: fingerprints and smudges on glass entrance doors and handles, dusting the bell desk, ledges, planters and lamp tables, wiping down luggage carts and the concierge counter, polishing brass rails and door hardware.

Policing the exterior entrance apron and porte-cochère of a hotel or the curbside frontage of a terminal: sweeping litter, cigarette butts, leaves and grit from the paving and gutter line, removing loose debris around planters, occasional hosing, with vehicles and guests arriving.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: sweeping paved facility surfaces for loose debris, comparable to sweeping a hotel entrance apron; same debris types and no fine manipulation required.

sources.title: Robots now wipe tables, sort trash, open doors at Google offices
sources.claim: Alphabet's Everyday Robots operated a prototype fleet in Google offices doing sub-steps of tidying — sorting trash, wiping tables, grasping cups — but as research prototypes; the program was shut down in 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: clearing cups/trash and wiping surfaces in an occupied office building — the nearest analogue to a lobby tidy round, but demonstrated only as prototype sub-steps, not whole-instance work at worker quality.

sources.title: Figure's Humanoid Robots Tidy a Bedroom, Hinting at Bigger Home Automation Leap
sources.claim: Humanoid tidying of rooms (picking up clutter, resetting a space) exists only as staged company demonstrations as of mid-2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking up loose objects and resetting a room; would transfer to lobby tidying if reliable, but it is a company demo in a staged room, with no evidence of sustained worker-quality performance.

sources.title: Gatsby makes US history with first humanoid robot home cleaning job
sources.claim: Gatsby dispatched a humanoid to clean a San Francisco apartment in May 2026, billed as the first US residential humanoid cleaning job; full autonomy is a company claim from a single event and is not independently established.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general cleaning/tidying of an occupied space; autonomy unverified and a single event, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic sells an autonomous restroom-cleaning robot service for office buildings; the robot cleans fixtures and floors and picks up trash during normal facility operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous surface cleaning and trash pickup inside an occupied human facility; transfer to lobby glass/furniture wiping is weak because the method is a no-touch power-wash-and-vacuum cycle in mapped, uniform, water-tolerant restrooms.

tasks.label: Transfer luggage, trunks, and packages to and from rooms, loading areas, vehicles, or transportation terminals, by hand or using baggage carts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel arrival: guest pulls up under the porte-cochere in a car, taxi or rideshare; the bellhop lifts 2-4 assorted suitcases, garment bags and backpacks out of the trunk or back seat, stacks them on a bell cart, wheels the cart through a busy lobby, rides the guest elevator, and carries the bags into the guest room, setting them on luggage racks or where the guest points.

Hotel departure and short-term bag storage: bellhop collects bags from a guest room or takes them from a guest at the bell desk, tags them, wheels them to the luggage storage room and stacks them, then later retrieves the right bags on presentation of a claim tag and loads them into a waiting taxi or shuttle trunk at the curb.

Group, tour or conference movement: 30-60 bags unloaded by hand from a motorcoach hold or van at the hotel entrance, sorted by room number onto several bell carts, staged in a holding room and then delivered room by room across multiple floors, and the reverse for departures, loading the coach hold.

Airport skycap at the terminal curb: takes checked bags from arriving vehicles, weighs and tags them, loads them onto a cart or the airline's curbside belt and moves them inside to the check-in or bag-drop conveyor; also helps arriving passengers move bags from the baggage claim carousel out to the curb or shuttle.

Back-of-house and terminal odd-freight transfers: trunks, boxes, sports equipment, strollers and packages moved with hand trucks and carts between loading docks, storage rooms, freight elevators, cruise or rail terminal staging areas and guest rooms or waiting vehicles; heavy, irregular items, often stacked and restacked.

sources.developer: Vanderlande Industries with Grenzebach Automation, Amsterdam Airport Schiphol
sources.title: Integrated Robot Loading Implemented by Vanderlande Industries at Amsterdam Airport Schiphol Wins interTERMINAL Award 2011 - Airport Technology
sources.claim: Robotic loading cells in Schiphol's baggage hall autonomously take buffered checked bags and load them into ramp-carts and ULD containers, replacing manual lifting, in a purpose-built fenced baggage handling facility.
sources.transferJustification: Same physical act as the porter's transfer of luggage to loading areas and carts - lifting individual passenger bags of mixed size and weight from a presentation point and placing them into a cart or container - with the work brought to the machine.

sources.title: Automated Baggage Loading - Airport Technology
sources.claim: Grenzebach supplies a field-proven fully automated bag handling system that grips a bag, moves it to a pre-calculated position in a container or ramp cart and sets it down accurately.
sources.transferJustification: Comparable objects (checked suitcases) and placement precision to a porter loading bags onto carts; establishes machine handling of individual bags in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: ABB articulated-arm industrial robot serves as automated luggage-storage and -retrieval system
sources.claim: An ABB industrial arm in a glass-enclosed cell in the Yotel New York lobby autonomously takes guests' luggage from a handover point and stores it in one of 117 lockers, returning it against a bar-coded receipt.

sources.title: Sheraton Los Angeles San Gabriel Hotel creates 'Jetsons'-style experience | Hotel Management
sources.claim: Aethon TUG autonomous mobile robots at the Sheraton Los Angeles San Gabriel navigate hotel corridors, call and ride service elevators and deliver items including luggage to guest rooms; staff load and guests unload the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Shows autonomous point-to-point transport of luggage inside a hotel (E2), but loading and unloading of the bags is done by staff and guests, so it covers only the transport leg of this task.

sources.title: Dexterity partners with FedEx to debut trailer loading robots - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Dexterity's DexR/Mech robot autonomously drives to a trailer and, fed by a powered conveyor, loads randomly sized and weighted boxes into the trailer at FedEx parcel hubs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: loading mixed, randomly sized heavy items presented by conveyor into a vehicle hold - the same physical act as a porter loading a coach hold or cart, at comparable weights, in a conveyor-fed purpose-built setting.

sources.title: Robot Handles Every Bag in Airports | The Road to Autonomy
sources.claim: Azalea Robotics' ARC One is a mobile, ... manipulator that picks, scans and places passenger bags onto carts inside airport ...; launched January 2026 with unedited autonomous operation shown.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects (passenger suitcases) and same act (pick from a presented stream, place onto a baggage cart) as the terminal side of the porter task; pilot-stage, so it supports capability with fixtured presentation rather than facility-grade deployment.

sources.developer: Aurrigo International with Changi Airport Group
sources.date: January 2024 trial; May 2024 four-vehicle fleet; further phases 2025-2026
sources.title: Changi Airport Group Collaborates with Aurrigo to Trial New Autonomous Baggage Handling Vehicle | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: Aurrigo's Auto-DollyTug autonomously drives across the airport apron and uses on-board robotic arms to load and unload baggage containers from itself; trialled at Changi Airport with a four-vehicle fleet agreed after Phase 2A.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous movement of baggage between loading areas at a transportation terminal; it moves whole containers rather than individual passenger bags, so it does not cover the porter's hand-loading.

tasks.label: Assist travelers and guests with disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Airport secure concourse: a passenger who requested wheelchair assistance and can transfer themselves (WCHR-type) is met after the security checkpoint; the porter seats them, stows their carry-on, and moves them along the concourse to the departure gate, then reports the handoff to the gate agent.

Airport full-service wheelchair assist: porter meets a non-ambulatory or heavy-assist passenger at curbside or check-in, handles their checked bags to the counter, pushes them through the TSA checkpoint (pat-down staging, reassembling belongings), waits at the gate, then pre-boards them down the jet bridge with an aisle chair, physically transferring the passenger into the aircraft seat.

Airport arrival or tight connection: porter meets the passenger with a wheelchair at the aircraft door, transfers them from the aisle chair, transports them through the terminal to a connecting gate or down to baggage claim, pulls their checked bags off the carousel, and escorts them to the curb, loading bags into a vehicle or shuttle.

Airport: escorting a traveler with a sensory or cognitive disability (blind/low-vision, Deaf, or a frail unaccompanied elderly traveler) - sighted-guide contact, verbal orientation, carrying and checking their bags, getting them through the checkpoint, restroom/food stops, and handing them off to the gate agent.

Hotel: bellhop meets a guest who uses a wheelchair, walker or scooter at the porte-cochere or lobby, moves their luggage to the accessible room, holds/props doors and works the elevator, places bags on the rack and items within reach, and shows the guest the roll-in shower, grab bars and controls.

Hotel errand for a guest with a disability: the guest phones the bell desk for a needed or forgotten item (towels, luggage cart, package, charger, item from storage); the bellhop collects it and brings it to the guest room so the guest need not leave the room.

sources.developer: WHILL, Inc. (with Unifi Aviation / Wayne County Airport Authority)
sources.title: Unifi Aviation Launches WHILL Autonomous Wheelchair Service at Detroit Metro Airport
sources.claim: WHILL's autonomous power wheelchair carries passengers with reduced mobility from a designated post-security comfort station to their departure gate under its own navigation, then returns to base autonomously; deployed commercially at Detroit Metro with Unifi/Delta and at LAX, MIA, SEA, AMS and Winnipeg.

sources.title: WHILL transforms accessibility for passengers with reduced mobility at Heathrow Airport
sources.claim: As of mid-2026 the WHILL autonomous mobility service runs at 26 airports and facilities worldwide (including a July 2026 Heathrow launch) with more than one million autonomous rides delivered, moving PRM passengers through terminals to their gates.

sources.title: Robotic Airport Wheelchairs Make Getting to Your Gate a Breeze
sources.claim: First-hand account of the autonomous airport wheelchairs at Miami and Los Angeles: the chairs drive themselves among other travelers using cameras and sensors while a remote representative monitors them; the passenger keeps their own carry-on and walks the jet bridge to board.

sources.title: How Autonomous Wheelchairs Work
sources.claim: Trade-press explainer: the service uses pre-mapped routes fitted to existing terminal layouts and is scoped to passengers who can travel to the gate on their own, explicitly leaving human staff to handle passengers with significant mobility challenges.

sources.developer: CAAMP consortium (Miraikan, Omron, IBM Japan, Alps Alpine, Shimizu)
sources.title: Autonomous Guidance Robot for the Visually Impaired "AI Suitcase" Demonstration at Expo 2025 Osaka, Kansai, Japan
sources.claim: The AI Suitcase is an ... physically guides blind and low-vision users through indoor spaces; it runs daily at the Miraikan museum and has been trialled in shopping malls and at New Chitose Airport. It guides walking only - it does not check bags or clear screening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting a blind traveler on foot through a terminal. Transfer holds only for the walking-guidance portion; the porter's instance also includes carrying and checking baggage and clearing the security checkpoint, which the robot does not do.

sources.title: Relay Robotics Releases New Hotel Delivery Robot That Offers Double the Capacity of Its Predecessor
sources.claim: Relay hotel delivery robots navigate hotel corridors and ride elevators autonomously to bring staff-loaded items from the front desk or ... to a guest's room door, where the guest takes the item from the bin; the fleet has completed more than a million deliveries.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bell-desk errand delivery to a guest room. Same building, corridors and elevators, and the same class of small guest items as the errand a bellhop runs for a guest with a disability.

sources.system: Hotel luggage delivery robots (Sheraton San Gabriel)
sources.title: Robots Take Over Luggage Duties at New Hotel
sources.claim: Hotel luggage robots at a Sheraton carried guests' bags to their rooms, but a human bell person loads the bags and the guest must take them off at the door; the robot does not escort the guest, open the room, or place bags inside.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bellhop luggage delivery to a guest room; cited to show the limit - autonomous transport only, with human loading and guest unloading, so a mobility-impaired guest is not served end to end.

tasks.label: Deliver messages and room service orders, and run errands for guests.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Room-service food/beverage order picked up at the kitchen or bar and delivered to a guest room in a mid-scale/upscale hotel: covered plates, coffee pot or drinks carried on a tray, knock/phone the room, hand the order to the guest at the door, charge posted to the room.

Amenity and forgotten-item runs from the front desk or housekeeping closet to a guest room: towels, toiletries, phone charger, iron, extra pillows, bottled water, a package that arrived for the guest; corridor and elevator travel, knock, hand over at the door, sometimes step inside to set the item down.

Delivering messages, envelopes, faxes, documents, flowers, dry cleaning and third-party deliveries to guests either at their room door or to a guest located in the lobby, restaurant, pool deck or a meeting room, where the guest must be found and the item handed over.

Full in-room service at an upscale/luxury property: wheel the linen-covered room-service cart into the guest room, position and set up the table, uncover plates, pour or uncork wine, present the check for signature, and return later to clear the tray/cart.

Off-property errands for guests: walk or drive to a nearby pharmacy/convenience store to buy a requested item, pick up event tickets, mail or drop off a package at a courier office, take clothing to a tailor, or fetch something from the guest's car in an off-site lot; involves streets, shops, payment and receipts.

sources.developer: Savioke / Relay Robotics (deployed by MGM Resorts at Vdara)
sources.title: Vdara employs a pair of robots to deliver room service — VEGAS INC
sources.claim: Two Relay (Savioke) autonomous robots at Vdara Hotel & Spa, Las Vegas deliver snacks, sundries, spa products and food-and-beverage items from the ground-floor cafe to guest suites, riding the elevators and corridors of the 1,490-room resort.

sources.system: Keenon W3 ButlerBot with Otis Integrated Dispatch
sources.title: Otis Elevators Integrate With Delivery Robot at Polish Hotel — Elevator World
sources.claim: At the Imperiall Resort & MediSpa in Poland a Keenon W3 delivery robot autonomously calls, enters and exits the hotel's Otis elevators and delivers restaurant orders and items such as fresh towels to guest rooms.

sources.title: BayCare Expands Autonomous Hospital Delivery with New Relay Robots at Winter Haven Hospitals
sources.claim: Relay robots — the same platform sold to hotels — run item deliveries in hospitals without human intervention, riding elevators and passing badge-access doors, with a reported 99.8% delivery success rate in a 2025 pilot of 50 deliveries/day.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-to-point delivery of small items in enclosed bins along corridors and elevators of a hospital. Same robot model used in hotels, same object class (small consumables, meals, supplies), same corridor/elevator environment and handoff at a door, so the demonstrated autonomy and >99% reliability carry over to hotel message/amenity/room-service runs.

sources.title: Robotic Butler Delivers Amenities to Guests at Detroit's Aloft Hotel — DBusiness Magazine
sources.claim: Aloft Hotels deployed the Relay 'Botlr' robot butler, which autonomously transports toothbrushes, snacks, towels and phone chargers from the lobby to guest rooms.

sources.title: Hotel Robots Running at a Loss After Burning Through Billions and Slashing Prices by Over 90% — 36Kr
sources.claim: Yunji's hotel delivery robots (the 'RUN' family), which autonomously map hotels, ride elevators and phone guest rooms to hand over items, are in commercial service across more than 34,000 hotels of large chains; the company listed in Hong Kong in October 2025.

sources.title: Bear Robotics Brings Physical AI, Service Robots and Autonomous Cleaning to Restaurants and Hotels — Restaurant Technology News
sources.claim: Bear Robotics' Servi autonomous food-running robots, which carry plates and drinks from the kitchen ... specific tables and bus dishes back, have shipped more than 16,000 units into commercial service including restaurants and hotels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running plated food and drinks from a kitchen to a designated guest location in a hotel/restaurant dining room. Same objects (trays, plates, glasses), same spill-and-timing precision, and the same institution-controlled floor as delivering an item to a guest seated in a hotel lobby, restaurant or pool deck.

tasks.label: Pick up and return items for laundry and valet service.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Guest phones the bell desk for valet laundry pickup; the porter rides the elevator to the guest floor, knocks, and the guest hands over a filled laundry bag or two with the completed list, which the porter carries back through corridors and elevators to the valet/laundry room and hands to the attendant.

Finished wash-and-fold order (folded shirts/underwear in a laundry box or bag) is collected from the valet room and delivered to the guest room; the porter knocks, the guest opens the door and takes the order.

Dry-cleaned and pressed garments on hangers under plastic are carried from the valet room to the guest room and either handed to the guest, hung on the door hook, or hung in the room closet without wrinkling them.

Guest is out: the porter uses a key/access card to enter the room, collects the laundry bag left on the closet floor or bed, or places the returned pressed order in the closet/on the bed and leaves the ticket, then secures the door.

Back-of-house bulk movement: several bagged valet orders or a rolling rack of returned dry cleaning are moved by cart between the loading dock, valet/laundry room and floor pantries at shift-change or when the outside cleaner's delivery arrives.

Guest drops garments at the bell/front desk or hands them over at checkout for express pressing; the porter takes the items, tags and logs the order, and later returns the finished garments to the guest in the lobby against the ticket.

sources.title: Hotel Tech-in: The robot butlers taking over hotel deliveries | Hotel Dive
sources.claim: Relay delivery robots run autonomous guest-room delivery routes in hundreds of US hotels (Marriott, Hilton, IHG, Wyndham brands), riding elevators and meeting guests at their doors with items in a lockable 10-gallon bin; over one million deliveries completed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: room delivery of towels/amenities. Same corridors, elevators and guest-door handoff as returning a bagged laundry order; payload (towels, linens, packages) is comparable in size, weight and softness to a hotel laundry bundle.

sources.title: Hotel Tech-in: The robot lightening the load for housekeepers | Hotel Dive
sources.claim: TechForce's TIM-E autonomous logistics robot is installed at a Homewood Suites hotel where it moves laundry: it takes collection bins to guest-room floors and returns the filled bins to the laundry room, with elevator and door integration and minimal human input.

sources.title: Robots Haul Waste, Deliver Linens at Froedtert Hospital
sources.claim: A fleet of five Aethon TUG robots at Froedtert Hospital autonomously picks up, transports and drops off heavy carts of soiled linen and waste across a 2.5 million sq ft, 13-story campus, completing more than 78,000 deliveries in 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soiled-linen cart logistics in a large institutional building. Physically the same as bulk movement of bagged valet/laundry orders between floors, service corridors and the laundry room in a hotel.

sources.title: BayCare Expands Autonomous Hospital Delivery with New Relay Robots at Winter Haven Hospitals
sources.claim: Relay robots deployed at BayCare hospitals run two-way transport routes: an authorized person badges in and loads the lockable bin, the robot autonomously navigates and rides elevators to the destination, where the item is removed (e.g., specimens from urgent care to the lab).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pickup-and-deliver runs where a person loads the robot at origin and another removes the item at destination — the same workflow as collecting a guest's laundry bag at the door and depositing it at the valet room.

sources.system: Piece Assembly automatic garment assembly conveyor
sources.title: Assembly Conveyor: Simultaneous Unloading and Loading - Metalprogetti
sources.claim: Automatic dry-cleaning assembly conveyors receive garments at a load point and then mechanically transport, group and unload hanging garments by customer order, handling over 4,000 items per 8-hour shift in a purpose-built plant installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine handling and routing of hanging garments by order in a dry-cleaning plant. Shows that with work presented to the machine as a purpose-built setting would present it, garments on hangers reach the correct destination point without a human carrier.

sources.system: Automated 24/7 dry-cleaning drop-off and pickup kiosk
sources.developer: Four Seasons Cleaners (kiosk installation, State Street, Santa Barbara)
sources.title: Automated kiosk gives dry cleaning customers 24/7 access | Kiosk Marketplace
sources.claim: A California dry cleaner has a fully automated 24/7 drop-off and pickup kiosk in commercial operation: customers deposit soiled garments and later collect the cleaned order themselves via QR code, with the machine storing and releasing the garments without staff involvement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended intake and return of laundry/valet orders to a customer. Covers the same start-to-accepted-output loop (receive garments, hold, return the finished order) the porter performs, inside a purpose-built machine enclosure.

sources.title: Robots Are Coming To A Hotel Near You, But Are Consumers Ready? (Forbes)
sources.claim: An ABB IRB 6640 industrial robot ('YOBOT') behind a glass enclosure in the Yotel New York lobby takes guests' bags, stores them in one of 117 lockers and retrieves them against a bar-coded receipt; it handles more than 30,000 pieces ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: accepting an item from a hotel guest at a lobby station, storing it, and returning it against a claim code — the same custody-transfer function as bell-desk valet intake and return, performed in a purpose-built robotic cell.

sources.title: Watch A New Humanoid Robot Clean A Hotel Room Like It Owns The Place (Forbes)
sources.claim: Zerith H1, a wheeled humanoid aimed at hotel housekeeping, is shown in a vendor video picking up towels and clothes and tidying a hotel room; the company was founded in 2025 and says the robot still needs more training to adapt to diverse environments.
sources.transferJustification: Cited only to show the state of in-room garment manipulation: a vendor demonstration video with no fielded deployment, so it cannot substantiate worker-quality completion of an in-room valet pickup.

tasks.label: Act as part of the security team at transportation terminals, hotels, or similar establishments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Hotel bell stand / lobby-entrance watch: bellhop holds a visible post at the door and bell stand during a shift, observing arrivals and departures, spotting loiterers, solicitors, non-guests and unattended bags in the lobby and porte-cochere, and radioing security or the front desk about anything suspicious while remaining a deterrent presence.

Security rounds of the property: walking corridors, guest floors, luggage storage room, back-of-house doors, loading dock, parking garage and grounds; confirming doors and storage rooms are locked, noting propped doors, hazards, or people who do not belong; logging the round and reporting anomalies to the security office.

Transportation terminal watch (skycap/porter at curbside, ticket lobby, baggage claim): keeping eyes on baggage staged on carts and carousels, spotting unattended or abandoned bags, watching for luggage theft or people entering bag-handling areas, and alerting airport police or terminal security.

Access and credential control at fixed points: watching guest-floor elevators and restricted/back-of-house doors, checking room keys, badges or boarding documents before allowing entry, responding to a door alarm or propped-door alert, and challenging or reporting an unauthorized person.

Hands-on incident response as part of the security team: responding to a disturbance, intoxicated or aggressive guest, theft in progress, medical emergency or fire alarm; de-escalating, escorting the person out or the guest to safety, directing crowds during an evacuation, guarding a suspicious item, and standing by for police.

sources.title: M Resort Spa Casino Deploys Knightscope K5 Security Robot | Hospitality Technology
sources.claim: A Knightscope K5 autonomous security ... is deployed at the M Resort Spa Casino (a Las Vegas hotel-casino), patrolling parking lots and the garage and serving explicitly as extra eyes and ears for the property's human security team.
sources.transferJustification: Same task: functioning as an added member of a hotel property's security team (patrol, observation, deterrence, two-way communication, alerting human officers).

sources.title: Knightscope Deploys Security Robots at Casino and International Airport - Silicon UK
sources.claim: San Antonio International Airport deployed a Knightscope K5 to work inside the terminal's secure non-public areas, monitoring strictly controlled access points and responding to door alarms as an added security resource.

sources.system: Cobalt Robot (Robot-as-a-Service with Cobalt Command Center)
sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: The Cobalt security robot performs autonomous indoor patrols of corporate campuses and offices, riding elevators for multi-floor rounds, opening doors, reading badges and ..., backed by a remote command center that intervenes on events.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (indoor guard patrol and access control in an office building) transfers to hotel/terminal security rounds and access points: same indoor human-occupied premises, same observe-verify-report duties, no manipulation beyond doors and badge checks.

sources.title: Ally Financial Plans to Deploy More Systems From Cobalt Robotics to Provide Security and Safety - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Ally Financial expanded its deployment of Cobalt security robots across its facilities, with its physical-security director stating the robot costs a fraction of a security officer, indicating paid operational use as part of a security program.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (corporate facility guarding) transfers: the robot is accepted by the employer in place of part of a human security team's watch and patrol duties.

sources.title: Cobalt - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: Independent robotics reference describes the Cobalt robot as an indoor security guard robot ... checks badges and identifies security or environmental threats, navigating autonomously with optional human operator supervision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (indoor guard duty with credential checking) transfers to hotel/terminal access-point watch: same environment type and same verify-and-report output.

sources.developer: Secom Co., Ltd. / Kansai Airports (VINCI Airports)
sources.title: Security Robots Heading to Japanese Airport and Rail Station - HSToday
sources.claim: Kansai International Airport deployed the Secom Robot X2 to perform security and monitoring patrols in Terminal 2 and the airport railway station zones, joining the human security team; the robot navigates its patrol routes autonomously using laser localization and cameras.

sources.title: Relay Robotics Announces New Line of Delivery Robots for Hotels and Hospitals
sources.claim: Relay hotel service robots navigate hotel hallways, ride elevators and move among guests fully autonomously, and have been operating in hotels commercially for years.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous hotel corridor/elevator delivery rounds) transfers the mobility half of security rounds: identical corridors, elevators, guest traffic and lighting conditions that a patrol robot must traverse.

sources.title: Ascento Guard 2.0 is ready for security duty at large facilities - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Ascento Guard wheel-legged robots autonomously patrol outdoor grounds and parking areas at customer sites and, per an early customer at Swiss Securitas, have been rolled out beyond pilots and integrated into day-to-day security operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (outdoor night patrol and parking-area security) transfers to a porter's exterior rounds of hotel grounds, drives and garages: same open-air institution-controlled premises and same observe-and-alert output.

tasks.label: Set up conference rooms, display tables, racks, or shelves, and arrange merchandise displays for sales personnel.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Set up a hotel meeting/conference room from stored furniture: roll out and unfold folding banquet tables, unstack and align chairs in classroom, theater or U-shape per the banquet event order, add linens/skirting, water pitchers, pads and pens, position lectern and easels; done on a deadline between events.

Flip or tear down a function room between events: remove used tables and chairs, fold and cart them to storage, restack chairs, reposition remaining furniture to the next layout, clear debris in a 30-60 minute window.

Set up display tables, racks, easels, pipe-and-drape and signage in a prefunction area, lobby or exhibit hall for a vendor or sales event: fetch equipment from storage on carts, assemble/erect racks and shelving, skirt and drape tables, place signs where the sales staff want them.

Arrange merchandise and collateral on the display tables/racks for sales personnel: unpack cartons of product samples, brochures, giveaways and apparel, and place, hang or fold them into an attractive arrangement per the salesperson's direction, replenishing during the event.
Stock and face packaged goods on a hotel gift-shop, sundry-shop or grab-and-go display shelf or cooler: place bottles, snacks and sundries into their shelf slots and pull product forward.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA robot restocks beverage display shelves in the cold cases of 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, running autonomously under its GORDON AI during routine operation with remote teleoperated recovery only when an error occurs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf restocking. It is the same physical act as the gift-shop/display-stocking instance here - placing packaged consumer goods into designated positions on standard store display shelving in an institution-controlled retail space.

sources.title: The Worldfolio: Telexistence: Revolutionizing robotics
sources.claim: Telexistence reports TX SCARA completes restocking without human intervention 96% of ..., with remote operators handling the small remainder.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above; the autonomy figure establishes that shelf stocking there is autonomous with only occasional remote assistance, not continuous teleoperation.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Staples has deployed RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking arms across its North American fulfillment centers, where the arms grip items of varied shape, size, weight and packaging presented in totes and place them into target containers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order-fulfillment piece picking. Transfers to arranging merchandise on a display when the display is fixtured and stock is presented in totes: comparable objects (packaged consumer goods) and comparable placement precision, in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid has moved more than 100,000 ... live GXO warehouse workflow, picking totes on and off mobile robots, loading conveyors and stacking containers at floor locations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: facility material handling. It marks the current ceiling for humanoid handling of bulky objects in human work facilities - rigid standard totes moved between fixed stations - and does not extend to unfolding banquet tables or laying out furniture.

sources.title: US: BMW deploys Figure 03 humanoid at smart factory for logistics
sources.claim: BMW's Spartanburg plant, after an 11-month Figure 02 deployment, is putting Figure 03 humanoids on logistics sequencing: picking unsorted components from containers and organizing them into sequencing trolleys.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting mixed parts into a prescribed arrangement on a fixtured trolley, inside a plant logistics station - comparable to placing presented merchandise into prescribed positions on a fixtured display rack.

tasks.label: Inspect guests' rooms to ensure that they are adequately stocked, orderly, and comfortable.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Rooming an arriving guest: bell attendant escorts the guest with luggage to an assigned room, opens the door with the keycard, sets bags on the rack, and while in the room verifies with the guest that towels/toiletries/coffee/water and ice are present, that the bed and furnishings are in order, that lights, TV and HVAC work and the temperature is comfortable, adjusts curtains/thermostat, and reports or fetches anything missing.

Pre-arrival / VIP room check of an unoccupied, freshly serviced standard guest room: walk the assigned rooms, confirm linens, towels, toiletries, coffee/tea, glassware, stationery and minibar are stocked to brand standard, straighten furniture and bedding, set thermostat and lighting, test TV/phone, place a welcome amenity, and report deficiencies to housekeeping/front desk.

Delivering a requested item to an occupied room (extra towels, pillows, iron, crib, package) and, while inside, checking that the room is adequately stocked and orderly around the guest's belongings, replacing missing supplies from the cart and noting problems.

Mid-stay response to a guest complaint or front-desk request: go to the occupied room, verify the reported condition (room too warm/cold, missing supplies, TV or lamp not working, room not made up), correct what can be corrected on the spot, and escalate the rest to engineering or housekeeping.

Check of an unoccupied suite, resort villa/cabin or extended-stay unit between guests: multiple rooms plus kitchenette and patio, wider inventory (dishware, glassware, robes, kitchen supplies, outdoor furniture), non-standard layout varying unit to unit, verify stock and order and comfort, then report.

sources.title: Watch A New Humanoid Robot Clean A Hotel Room Like It Owns The Place
sources.claim: Zerith H1, a wheeled humanoid built for hotel housekeeping, is reported to autonomously clean floors, restock amenities ... scrub fixtures inside guest rooms; company video shows it tossing towels into a hamper, replenishing toiletries and tidying a bathroom counter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-room housekeeping): replenishing toiletries and tidying a guest room covers the 'adequately stocked and orderly' content of this inspection task, with the same objects, room and precision.

sources.title: Zerith H1: China's humanoid robot cleans and restocks hotel rooms
sources.claim: Company footage of Zerith H1 shows it moving through a hotel room and vacuuming and disposing of waste without human assistance, adapting to varying room layouts and narrow corridors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-room cleaning): establishes autonomous mobility and manipulation inside a hotel guest room, the environment in which this inspection task occurs.

sources.title: The Housekeeping Robots Driving Hospitality Industry Innovation
sources.claim: Industry review of hospitality housekeeping robots as of 2026 characterises Zerith H1 as an early-stage pilot limited mainly to repeated bathroom routines, with human staff retaining the quality checks and guest-facing judgment.

sources.title: Is 2025 the year for robots in Hotels?
sources.claim: Tailos' Rosie autonomous vacuum operates inside hotel guest rooms and has been deployed at scale across hotels, but its function is floor cleaning, not verifying amenities or room readiness.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (guest-room vacuuming): shows commercially deployed autonomous operation inside the same guest rooms, bounding what deployed hotel robots actually do there (floor cleaning only).

sources.title: Orbit 5.0 adds features to Boston Dynamics' Spot quadruped robot
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with Orbit 5.0 autonomously patrols facilities on set routes and uses vision-language prompts to flag anomalies such as spills or missing fire extinguishers and report them, a commercially released industrial inspection capability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous facility inspection rounds): the perceptual core matches this task - traverse a known layout, check whether specified items are present and the space is orderly, and report deficiencies - though Spot cannot open keycarded guest doors or restock amenities.

sources.title: How Hotel Robots Enhance The Art of Hospitality
sources.claim: Deployed hotel service robots such as Relay autonomously ride elevators and travel corridors to bring towels, toiletries and snacks to a guest room, but the handoff occurs at the door - the guest opens the lid and takes the item; the robot does not enter or inspect the room.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (in-hotel item delivery): defines the reach of deployed hotel delivery robots - door-side handoff without entering the occupied room, so no in-room stock or comfort check is performed.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot autonomously cleans fixtures, floors and picks ... and opens doors in hospitals and airports as a commercial service, illustrating the current ceiling of autonomous in-facility mobile manipulation (cleaning, not inventory verification or restocking).
sources.transferJustification: Related task (autonomous restroom cleaning in occupied facilities): comparable indoor human-facility mobile manipulation, but the accepted output is cleanliness, not verification that a room is stocked, orderly and comfortable.

tasks.label: Arrange for shipments of baggage, express mail, and parcels by providing weighing and billing services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Airport curbside/lobby skycap check-in of standard checked suitcases: greet the traveler at the curb or check-in hall, verify the reservation, lift each bag onto the scale, read the weight, print and affix the bag tag, hand over the claim receipt, collect any per-bag checked-baggage charge, and place the bag on the induction belt.

Airport check-in area, overweight or extra bag: bag weighs over the allowance, so the porter/agent weighs it, quotes and collects the excess-baggage or extra-piece fee by card, applies a heavy tag, and inducts the bag; traveler may repack between bags to get under the limit.

Airport terminal, oversize/odd-size items: skis, golf bags, bicycles, boxed goods, strollers, musical instruments. Porter weighs and measures the item, prices it against the special-item tariff, takes payment, tags it (often with straps or tubs), and walks it to the out-of-gauge belt.

Hotel bell desk: guest wants a suitcase or a carton shipped home or ahead by FedEx/UPS. Bellhop boxes or straps the item if needed, weighs it on the bell-desk scale, completes the courier airbill (addresses, declared value, service level), affixes the label, posts the charge plus handling fee to the guest folio, and stages the item for the courier pickup.

Hotel/resort business center or bell desk, express mail and small parcels: guest or conference group hands over envelopes, document packs and small boxes; worker weighs each, meters or prints the label, logs the shipment in the outbound register, and bills the room or the group master account.

Rail/bus/in-town terminal or cruise pier: checked baggage and express parcels accepted from passengers — weigh each piece, apply the tariff for extra/heavy pieces, issue the claim check or receipt, tag and load onto carts or into the baggage room for the departure.

instances.label: Hotel concierge takes a guest request and delivers a small item to the guest room: forgotten toothbrush/charger, extra towels, a welcome amenity, or a third-party food/parcel delivery left at the front desk. Route runs lobby → elevator → corridor → knock/hand-off at the door.

Apartment/condo concierge receives couriered parcels, food orders and dry-cleaning at the lobby desk, logs them, and carries them up to the resident's unit door (or the resident's designated spot), notifying the resident.

Off-property errand for a guest: walk or drive to a nearby pharmacy, shop, florist, box office or dry cleaner; identify oneself, pay or present a confirmation, collect or select the goods, and bring them back to the guest. Public streets, ordinary retail counters.

In-building pickup and hand-off of a stored or back-of-house item: retrieve a specific suitcase from bell storage, a returned dry-cleaning bag from the rack, or a left-behind item from lost and found, and bring it to the guest in the lobby, restaurant or room.
Office-building concierge delivers mail, documents, courier packets or catering to tenant suites on upper floors and picks up outgoing shipments from tenant reception desks.

sources.claim: Moxi mobile manipulators have completed over 1 million deliveries and 125,000 autonomous elevator rides across 31 hospitals, fetching and delivering supplies, specimens and medications between departments and staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital fetch-and-deliver runs. Same class of work as concierge item delivery — small parcels and packets moved between a pickup point and a named recipient inside a people-filled multi-floor building, using elevators and hand-off to a person.

instances.label: Hotel bell stand/front desk: receive luggage from arriving or departed guests (roller bags, duffels, backpacks, sometimes 5-8 pieces per party), tag each piece with a claim ticket, wheel it into the luggage storage room, stack it, then retrieve the right pieces later against the ticket and hand them back at the lobby.

Hotel: take a guest's bags at the curb or lobby after check-in, load a bell cart, ride the guest elevator, walk the corridor, and place the bags inside the guest room (or collect them from the room at departure and bring them down to a waiting car).

Residential apartment/condo concierge desk: receive a courier's daily drop of parcels (UPS/FedEx/Amazon, envelopes to large boxes), scan or log each into the package-tracking system, shelve them in the package room by resident, and hand them over when residents come to the desk.

Deliver parcels, mail, dry cleaning or small items from the lobby/package room to individual apartment units or office suites: load a cart, ride the elevator, find the door, hand to the occupant or leave it at the door with a notification.
Office-building concierge/reception: receive and sign for incoming mail and courier deliveries, sort into tenant mailboxes/pigeonholes or bins, and release items to tenant staff who come to the desk.

Irregular, high-touch items held for guests/residents: garment bags, golf bags and skis, strollers, flower arrangements, dry cleaning on hangers, oversized or fragile gift boxes and perishables — received, stored appropriately, and returned or delivered intact.

sources.claim: YOBOT at YOTEL New York is an ABB industrial robot arm in a glass-enclosed lobby cell that accepts a guest's bag, stores it in one of 117 lockers, and returns it against a bar-coded receipt — i.e., autonomous receipt, storage and retrieval of hotel luggage in a purpose-built machine enclosure.

sources.title: About YOTEL New York Times Square – YOTEL Help Center

sources.transferJustification: Related task: airport checked-baggage acceptance, storage and retrieval. Same objects (mixed suitcases and duffels), same operation (take in a tagged bag, buffer it in a rack, retrieve the right bag on demand) as a concierge's luggage store, performed in a machine-built hall.

sources.system: ABLE robotic baggage loading system with SICK Visionary-T Mini 3D camera

sources.claim: Robots at Schiphol load passenger baggage from conveyors into ULD containers in production using 3D vision, showing autonomous grasping and stacking of varied suitcases in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic handling/stacking of checked bags. Demonstrates that arbitrary suitcases can be grasped, moved and stacked autonomously — the physical core of receiving and storing guest luggage — inside a machine-built cell.

sources.title: Cleveron 402 – Cleveron
sources.claim: The Cleveron 402 robotic parcel locker takes parcels inserted by couriers one after another, shelves and rearranges them autonomously, and dispenses the right parcel to a customer in about ten seconds on presentation of a code — receipt, storage and hand-out of parcels without staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail click-and-collect parcel storage and pickup. Objects (parcels and envelopes), the log-in/store/retrieve-on-code workflow and the accuracy standard match an apartment package room's receive-store-hand-out cycle.

sources.system: Berkshire Grey Robotic Product Sortation with Identification (BG RPSi)
sources.title: Learn How FedEx Uses Berkshire Grey Robotic Sortation to Speed Up Customer Deliveries
sources.claim: FedEx Ground uses Berkshire Grey robotic product sortation ... at its Queens, NY station to pick, identify and sort thousands of individual small parcels daily into destination containers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parcel/mail sortation in a carrier station. Same objects (envelopes, polybags, small boxes) and same operation (read the label, place the item in the correct destination bin) as a mailroom sorting incoming mail into tenant slots.

sources.title: InnVest Hotels Partners with Relay Robotics to Become Canada's Largest User of Hotel Delivery Robots
sources.claim: Relay delivery robots are deployed in hundreds of hotels worldwide and have completed over a million autonomous deliveries of items from the front desk to guest room doors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering amenities, room-service items and guest packages from the lobby to a room door. Same corridors, elevators, doors and item sizes as delivering mail and small parcels to units or suites.

sources.title: Relay2 delivery robot offers 2x payload, new elevator integration
sources.claim: Relay2 autonomously carries lobby drop-offs (e.g., delivery cartons) up to a hotel room, with integrated elevator control, so multi-floor door delivery inside a building runs without staff escorting the item.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lobby-to-room transport of third-party deliveries. Identical to a concierge carrying a parcel or mail from the desk to a resident's door within the same building type.

sources.title: Bringing Robotics into Everyday Living: Samsung C&T Expands Autonomous Delivery Services
sources.claim: Autonomous delivery robots operate in Samsung C&T's Raemian apartment complexes in Seoul, navigating outdoor paths, elevators and residential hallways to bring orders directly to residents' apartment doors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: last-metre delivery to apartment doors in a managed residential building. Same route (lobby, elevator, corridor, unit door) and comparable payloads to delivering parcels or mail to residents.

sources.title: Pudu Robotics and Shenzhen CTID Co. Ltd Launch the World's First Full-Scenario Robot-Serviced Hotel Project
sources.claim: Pudu's T300 was shown transporting luggage and operating elevators autonomously at a hotel-project launch event, but only as a demonstration of a transport platform that staff load and guests unload; no deployed hotel system takes bags from a guest and places them in a room.

sources.claim: The Henn na Hotel's porter robots, the best-known attempt at robotic bellhop service in guest corridors, could not serve most rooms and were among the robots retired in 2019 after staff spent their time rescuing them.
