instances.label: Hotel/office-building concierge handles a guest print, copy or scan request at the business center or front desk: receives a file by email or USB (or a stack of loose originals such as a passport, contract or itinerary), prints/copies, collates and staples the set, and hands it to the guest at the desk or delivers it to the room. Timeframe is minutes; small volumes; originals must be returned undamaged.

Residential/office concierge receives inbound parcels and mail from FedEx/UPS/Amazon couriers at the desk, signs for them, scans/logs each into the package-tracking system, stores them in the package room or behind the desk, notifies the resident/guest, and releases the parcel on request after verifying identity (or delivers it to the unit door).

Concierge ships an outbound parcel for a guest: takes the item (documents, a forgotten laptop, purchases, a gift), selects and assembles a box or envelope, adds void fill and tape, weighs it, completes the FedEx/UPS airbill or prints the label from the guest's account, affixes it, and stages the parcel for courier pickup.

Concierge sends or receives a fax or scan-to-email for a guest: feeds loose pages (sometimes mixed sizes, contracts with signatures) into the machine, dials/addresses, confirms transmission, retrieves the confirmation and originals; for inbound faxes, collects the pages, puts them in an envelope and holds them at the desk or delivers them to the guest's room.

Concierge assists a guest with business-center equipment and non-routine requests: connecting the guest's own laptop or phone to the printer, clearing a paper jam, replacing toner or paper, resolving a failed print/format problem, or improvising a workaround (e.g., emailing a document to a nearby FedEx Office) when the on-site equipment can't do the job.

sources.title: Cleveron 402 - Cleveron
sources.claim: Cleveron 402 is a commercially deployed robotic parcel locker whose internal robotics accept parcels in bulk through a loading port, store and rearrange them on shelves, and dispense the correct parcel to a customer who scans an order code, in about 10 seconds.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail order pickup. It covers the same physical operations as concierge package handling — take in parcels, store them in a known location, and release the right parcel to a verified recipient — with comparable object sizes and precision, but only when parcels are presented at the machine's loading port.

sources.title: Cleveron Robotic parcel locker is now in the iconic Zara Corso Vittorio Emanuele Milan store
sources.claim: The Cleveron robotic parcel locker is installed in retail flagship stores, where the customer scans a code at the machine and the machine hands over the parcel within seconds without a store associate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store order handover. The verified release of a stored parcel to a named recipient is the same accepted output as a concierge releasing a resident's package, though the robot works only inside its own purpose-built cabinet.

sources.title: CVP Impack | Packsize
sources.claim: The CVP Impack automated packaging machine takes an item on an inline conveyor and measures, constructs, tapes, weighs and ... a right-sized box every seven seconds; multiple units are installed in commercial fulfillment operations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: e-commerce order packing. It performs exactly the physical steps of a concierge shipping a guest's item — box selection/creation, closing, weighing and label application — at equal or better precision, provided the item is presented on the machine's induction belt.

sources.title: Amazon's robot arms break ground in safety and technology - Amazon Science
sources.claim: Amazon's Robin robotic arms autonomously pick individual parcels and mailers off a conveyor, rotate them to read the shipping label, and sort them onto drive robots; they are deployed at scale across Amazon facilities and divert damaged or unreadable parcels.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parcel induction and sortation. Reading a shipping label and routing the parcel to the right destination is the machine equivalent of a concierge logging an inbound package and shelving it by recipient; objects and label-reading precision are the same.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch robot autonomously unloads mixed cases and parcels from trailers and containers in DHL warehouses, identifying boxes with computer vision without pre-programming; ten units were in commercial service across three countries by mid-2025.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unloading incoming freight. Handling unlabelled, mixed-size cartons off a truck is the closest deployed analogue to a concierge taking in a courier's load of parcels; it works in a dock area laid out for the robot.

sources.title: Automatic Book Scanner | Treventus
sources.claim: The Treventus ScanRobot 2.0 MDS is a commercial automatic book scanner that turns pages by itself using air flow and captures up to 2,500 pages per ...; it is used for mass digitization in libraries and archives.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: document digitization. Separating and handling individual sheets of paper without damaging them, then capturing each page, is the physical core of copying, scanning and faxing documents for a guest; it requires the paper to be presented in the machine's cradle.

sources.title: The Rise of Robotics: Automating Wide Format Print Production - FESPA
sources.claim: Durst's P5 Robotics uses two KUKA robot arms in commercial wide-format print production to pick sheets from a stack, register them, and place them precisely on the printer, handling media as thin as foil paper.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: press loading/unloading in print production. Picking single sheets from a stack and placing them accurately is the manipulation a concierge performs when loading originals and collecting printed output, demonstrated in a purpose-built print cell.

sources.title: Room Service and Delivery Robots: Logistics Automation in Hospitality
sources.claim: Relay autonomous delivery robots operate in hotel corridors and elevators at major hotel brands, carrying items from staff workstations to guest room doors, but they are loaded by staff at the desk or kitchen.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-hotel item delivery. It shows the transport leg of delivering a fax, printout or parcel to a guest room is automated at E2, but the robot has no manipulator, so retrieving pages from a machine or a parcel from a shelf still requires a person.

Deliver a beverage or food item (welcome amenity, bottled water, coffee, snack, guest's food-delivery order or room-service style tray) from the lobby up to a guest room door, using corridors and elevators, and hand it to the guest.
Hotel lobby lounge: take drink orders from seated guests, collect the drinks from the bar, place them on guests' tables, then clear empty glassware and napkins afterward.

Club/executive lounge concierge: set out and continuously replenish the breakfast/evening buffet (chafing dishes, pastries, fruit, coffee urns, juice, wine), clear guests' used dishes and glasses from tables, and wipe tables between guests.

Office or apartment building concierge: set up coffee, water, and catered food in a conference room or lobby for a meeting or resident event (arrange urns, cups, platters on the table), then clear and tidy afterward.

sources.title: Blendid expands robotic smoothie kiosk presence on California college campuses

tasks.label: Clean and tidy hotel lounge.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-shift tidy pass of the lounge seating area with guests coming and going: plump and square up cushions and throw pillows, push chairs and pull side tables back to their layout positions, align magazines, newspapers and brochure racks, pick up stray items left behind and take them to lost-and-found.

Clearing guests' used coffee cups, glasses, water bottles, small plates, napkins and litter off lounge coffee tables and side tables into a tray or bus tub and carrying it back of house; fragile glassware, cluttered tabletops, must avoid removing items still in use by a seated guest.

Wiping and spot-cleaning after guests: coffee rings and drink spills on wood/stone tabletops, the side counter and window ledges, using a damp cloth and spray bottle; occasional spot-treating a spill on carpet or upholstery.
Running a vacuum or sweeper over the lounge carpet and hard floor off-peak (early morning or after an event), picking up crumbs, sugar packets and general debris around seating clusters.
Restocking and neatening the lounge coffee/water station and brochure rack: refill cups, lids, stirrers, sugar, napkins and the water pitcher from a supply caddy, straighten the display, wipe drips.
Emptying the lounge's small waste bins: pull the liner, tie it off, replace it with a fresh liner and carry the bag to the back-of-house trash room.

sources.title: Hotel Cleaning Robot | SoftBank Robotics America
sources.claim: SoftBank Robotics' Whiz autonomous vacuum is deployed commercially in hotels to vacuum public areas and guest floors, replacing manual vacuuming by hotel staff (Marriott Denver Tech Center).

sources.system: Kärcher KIRA B 50 (also Avidbots Neo, Tennant T7AMR cited in same article)
sources.title: The Housekeeping Robots Driving Hospitality Industry Innovation
sources.claim: Commercial autonomous floor-cleaning robots such as Kärcher KIRA B 50 are sold and used for hotel lobbies, corridors and pre-function areas — the exact space and floor-cleaning work in this task.

sources.title: Pudu CC1 Pro — AI Commercial Cleaning Robot for Hotels, Multifamily & Schools | RobotLAB
sources.claim: Pudu's CC1 Pro multi-function cleaning robot is sold and used in hotels for sweeping, scrubbing, vacuuming and mopping public floors.

sources.title: π0: Our First Generalist Policy
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0 policy autonomously buses a table: picking dishes, cups, cutlery and trash off a table into a bussing bin and a trash bin, run by a fixed UR5e arm pair at a laboratory table with bins placed alongside.
sources.transferJustification: Same act as clearing a lounge table: picking assorted used tableware and litter from a tabletop into a bus tub, including thin glassware.

sources.title: π₀: A Vision-Language-Action Flow Model for General Robot Control (arXiv HTML)
sources.claim: The π0 paper reports the bussing evaluation uses novel objects in cluttered scenes, including delicate glasses and large plates, with reported scores of 0.971 (easy) and 0.875 (hard) on the fixed-arm bussing benchmark.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that the fixtured bussing demonstration handles unseen cups, plates and glasses, the object variety a lounge table presents.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (π0.5)
sources.claim: π0.5 drives a mobile manipulator to tidy and clean kitchens and bedrooms in homes not seen in training, but does not reliably succeed on the first attempt.
sources.transferJustification: Tidying loose items into their places in an unseen room is the same act as a lounge tidy pass; cited to show it is demonstrated but not at reliable worker quality.

sources.developer: Epoch AI (assessment of Physical Intelligence et al.)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: Independent 2026 assessment places bedroom tidying (placing loose items where they belong, repositioning pillows, making beds) at 'validated in lab' — demonstrated with transfer but with imperfect first-try reliability and demos run 2-10x slower than humans; not deployed.
sources.transferJustification: Bedroom tidying is the closest assessed analogue to tidying a lounge seating area; used to bound reliability claims.

sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: Figure 03 has been shown tidying a sofa area ... a laptop and toys and repositioning a pillow — in a controlled environment with no shown transfer to new locations.
sources.transferJustification: A sofa-area tidy with cushions and loose items is the seating-area tidy of this task, demonstrated in a controlled, machine-friendly setting.

sources.system: household robots surveyed (PI, Figure, Loki, others)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 | Epoch AI
sources.claim: As of 2026, no robot has been shown handling a trash bag end-to-end: closing and carrying the bag remain unattempted components of the take-out-the-trash task.
sources.transferJustification: Emptying and re-lining a lounge waste bin is the same bag-handling problem the assessment finds unattempted.

sources.title: Moravec's Paradox and the Robot Olympics
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence reports its π0.6 model solving 'robot olympics' wet-cleaning tasks — wiping a countertop and washing a greasy pan with a sponge — at fixed arm stations in its lab kitchen; the challenge requires the robot to run autonomously in uncut video.
sources.transferJustification: Wiping a countertop with a sponge is the same manipulation as wiping a lounge tabletop or spill: flat surface, cloth, low precision.

sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization (arXiv HTML)
sources.claim: π0.5 was commanded to clean an unseen kitchen with subtasks including wiping a spill and putting dishes in the sink, using a mobile manipulator.
sources.transferJustification: Wiping a spill and clearing dishes to a receptacle are the manipulation content of clearing and wiping lounge tables.

sources.title: A VLA that Learns from Experience (π*0.6)
sources.claim: π*0.6 ran autonomously for a full day at a fixed espresso station making drinks, and folded novel laundry in a new home for ... uninterrupted, with reported failure rates cut by 2x or more.
sources.transferJustification: Sustained autonomous work at a fixed beverage station (cups, supplies, machine) is the counterpart of restocking and tending a lounge coffee station with supplies presented at the station.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's bathroom cleaning robot is deployed in hospitals and airports, where its arm cleans fixtures and floors and picks up trash during facility operating hours.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed surface-wiping/trash-picking manipulator in a human facility; its surfaces are mapped restroom fixtures in rooms closed during cleaning, not open lounge furniture.

roles.title: Tour Guides and Escorts
aliases: VIP Tour Guide (Very Important Person Tour Guide)
roles.description: Escort individuals or groups on sightseeing tours or through places of interest, such as industrial establishments, public buildings, and art galleries.

tasks.label: Describe tour points of interest to group members, and respond to questions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Escort individuals or groups on cruises, sightseeing tours, or through places of interest, such as industrial establishments, public buildings, or art galleries.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Docent-led gallery tour in a museum or art gallery: guide meets a group of 8-25 visitors at a fixed start point, leads them along a set route through galleries, stops at works/artifacts to narrate, answers visitor questions, keeps the group together and away from objects, and returns them to the lobby on schedule.

Interior tour of a public building or historic site (state capitol, courthouse, historic house, cathedral, university landmark building): fixed route through corridors, chambers and stairways controlled by the operating institution, scripted narration plus Q&A, security/ropes and crowd-flow rules, group of 10-30.

Tour of an industrial establishment or corporate visitor facility (brewery, food plant, power station, automotive assembly plant, company showroom/exhibition hall): safety briefing and PPE, fixed visitor walkway or gallery route past operating equipment, narration of the process, escorting the group in and out of controlled areas.

Outdoor walking sightseeing tour of a city district or historic quarter: guide leads 10-20 people along public sidewalks, crosses streets, stops at landmarks amid pedestrians, traffic, street noise, weather and construction, counts heads, and delivers narration while shepherding stragglers.

Vehicle-based sightseeing tour (motorcoach, trolley, open-top bus, harbor/river cruise boat): guide narrates landmarks over a PA while the vehicle follows a route, then escorts passengers on and off at photo stops and handles boarding, seating and timing.

Cruise/multi-day tour escort: accompanying a group through embarkation, shore excursions in port towns, coach and airport transfers, hotels and meal stops; mustering the group, headcounts, ticket/manifest handling, and resolving problems (late arrivals, lost members, medical or weather disruptions) across unfamiliar sites.

tasks.label: Provide for physical safety of groups, performing such activities as providing first aid or directing emergency evacuations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor museum, art gallery, aquarium or public-building tour: guide keeps a group of 15-30 visitors together and clear of hazards (stairs, barriers, artifacts), watches for a visitor who faints or feels ill, renders basic first aid (seats them, water, bandage, summons house medic/EMS), and on a fire alarm counts heads and leads the group along the posted route to the assembly point.

Industrial or infrastructure facility tour (brewery, factory floor, power plant, mine, dam): guide issues and enforces PPE, keeps visitors behind painted lines and off catwalk edges, monitors for slips and machinery hazards, and on an alarm directs the group through the plant's evacuation route to a muster point and reports the headcount.

City walking or food tour on public sidewalks: guide manages street crossings and traffic, keeps the group out of bike lanes and off uneven pavement, watches for pickpockets and heat/cold exposure, and responds to a member who trips and scrapes a knee or becomes faint - first aid from a belt kit, shade/water, calling 911 while keeping the rest of the group safe.

Outdoor adventure/nature tour (hiking, kayaking, caving, ski, wildlife, horseback): guide sets spacing and pace on trail, assesses weather and terrain, and treats an injured client on scene - sprain wrapping, bleeding control, hypothermia or altitude response - then organizes carry-out or coordinates a rescue evacuation of the group.

Motorcoach or excursion-boat escort: safety briefing, headcounts at each stop, physically steadying elderly or mobility-impaired passengers on steps and gangways, and responding to an onboard medical incident or directing an orderly evacuation of the vehicle/vessel.

sources.title: Drone-delivered defibrillator helps save cardiac arrest patient in Sweden - Aviation24.be
sources.claim: Everdrone's autonomous drone system is operationally dispatched to suspected cardiac arrests and delivers an AED to the scene, but the life-saving care itself is administered by bystanders/paramedics; the machine delivers equipment rather than providing first aid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: emergency medical response. It is the closest deployed autonomous system to 'providing first aid', and it establishes the limit - the robot transports an AED outdoors to a location, while a human performs the actual assessment and treatment on the casualty.

sources.system: Emergency Guide Robot (Georgia Tech overtrust study)
sources.title: Overtrust of Robots in Emergency Evacuation Scenarios (PDF)
sources.claim: The best-known robot 'emergency guide' that led people out of a building during a simulated fire was remote-controlled by a hidden researcher, so it does not establish autonomous evacuation direction.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the related task of directing an emergency evacuation of people in a building; it is teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Multi-Robot-Assisted Human Crowd Evacuation using Navigation Velocity Fields
sources.claim: Robot-guided crowd evacuation remains a research topic framed in the conditional - robots 'may be able to ...' guide people - with results from modeling, simulation and lab studies rather than fielded systems responsible for group safety.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: directing emergency evacuations of crowds. The literature is at the modeling/simulation stage, confirming no fielded system performs this duty at worker quality.

sources.system: Airstar guide robot (Incheon International Airport); LG CLOi GuideBot
sources.title: Innovation in Incheon: From robot guides to robot food delivery | Delta News Hub
sources.claim: Autonomous guide robots are deployed in structured human facilities such as Incheon International Airport, where they self-navigate among the public and escort travellers to locations - but their function is wayfinding and information, with no first-aid or emergency-safety responsibility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting/guiding people through a facility. Capability transfers only to leading people along routes; it provides no evidence of hazard intervention, casualty care, or taking charge of a group in an emergency.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling for robotic wound redressing (dual Franka Emika Panda arms)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: Robotic wound dressing - a narrow sub-step of first aid - is at laboratory stage, evaluated on anatomical surface models rather than on live casualties in the field.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a dressing, a component of first aid. It shows even this narrow sub-step is confined to fixtured lab benches with phantoms, far from treating a real casualty on a tour.

sources.title: Knightscope Autonomous Security Robot (ASR)-E Privacy Impact Assessment (VA)
sources.claim: Deployed autonomous security robots patrol institution-controlled premises (hospitals, campuses, parking areas) and monitor for anomalies, but their output is detection, deterrence and alerting for human officers - not physical protection of a group, casualty care, or evacuation command.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: safety patrol of premises occupied by the public. It establishes autonomous mobility among people in E2 facilities, but the accepted output is monitoring and alerting humans, not the guide's safety and first-aid duties.

tasks.label: Assemble and check the required supplies and equipment prior to departure.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Walking/city/food tour guide at the tour company's office or storeroom before a departure: draws whisper-radio receivers and earpieces plus a transmitter from a charging rack, counts them against the booking list, checks charge/pairing, and adds flag or sign, printed tickets/vouchers, brochures, water bottles and a small first-aid pouch into a rolling case staged at the meeting point.

Motorcoach/step-on guide at a depot or staging lot: loads cooler, cases of bottled water and snacks, first-aid kit, spare umbrellas and paperwork/manifests into the coach's luggage bay, and tests the coach PA microphone and any on-board equipment before passengers board.

Adventure/outfitter guide (raft, kayak, bike, zipline, snorkel) at the outfitter's base or yard: counts and inspects PFDs, helmets, wetsuits, paddles, ropes/harnesses, throw bags, repair and first-aid kits; checks bikes for brakes, tire pressure and drivetrain or checks e-bike battery charge; loads boats/boards/bikes onto trailer or van.

Museum, gallery, brewery or industrial-plant tour guide at a visitor center: pulls audio-guide units and headsets from charging racks, verifies charge, content version and cleanliness, and assembles hard hats, safety glasses, hi-vis vests, hearing protection and visitor badges in the right sizes/quantities for the booked group.

Cave, historic-house, ghost or attraction guide at a small ranger office or ticket booth: checks out flashlights/lanterns and spare batteries, gate and door keys, two-way radio, counting caps and props, and confirms each lamp and radio actually works before leading the group out.

sources.date: 2023-11 (page); RightPick 4 launched 2024; Apotea logistics-center deployment operating 2025
sources.title: RightHand Robotics | Pharmaceutical
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick piece-picking system is a commercially deployed robotic cell that autonomously picks and places a very wide range of individual products, including items it has never seen ... downstream manual consolidation - the core 'assemble a required set of supplies' operation in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic order/piece picking in fulfilment and pharmacy operations. Transfer: assembling a tour kit is item-level order picking of comparable small consumer objects (bottles, headsets, packets, printed matter) into a container, at similar precision, when the goods are presented to the machine as in an E1 cell.

sources.system: Danfoss Drives kitting cell with Roboception rc_viscore 3D vision
sources.title: Robot Vision Optimizes Automated Kitting Cell - Roboception
sources.claim: A production kitting cell at Danfoss Drives uses a robot with 3D stereo vision to compile an assortment of different parts ... supplier pallets into differing trays, with sub-millimetre detection and cycle times of ~25 s - a deployed example of autonomously assembling a specified, mixed kit in a purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial kitting. Transfer: 'assemble the required supplies' is kitting - selecting a defined list of distinct items from stock and placing them in a tray/case; the vision system also verifies part identity and placement, matching the 'check' element when the stock is presented to the machine.

sources.date: 2025-11 (Henry Ford Health deployment announcement); product line in commercial use for years
sources.title: BD Rowa - store & pick medications automatically
sources.claim: BD Rowa's pharmacy robots automatically store and pick packaged goods and the automated input system includes expiry-date recognition, i.e. machine verification of stock condition/validity; BD Rowa Vmax units are commercially installed in retail and hospital-based pharmacies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated pharmacy storage, retrieval and stock verification. Transfer: shows a machine reliably retrieving specified items on demand and checking item identity/expiry - the counting-and-checking half of assembling supplies - inside an enclosed purpose-built unit.

sources.system: Averna end-of-line automated test systems (Mecademic/FANUC/Stäubli/Epson robots + test benches)
sources.title: End-of-Line (EOL) Testing Solutions | Averna
sources.claim: Averna builds and deploys end-of-line functional test cells that combine industrial robots with vision systems, precision fixtures and test benches to automatically run functional, safety and audio tests on manufactured units - the machine equivalent of verifying that equipment (radios, headsets, microphones, lamps) actually works.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic end-of-line functional testing of consumer electronics (including audio test). Transfer: checking that a tour headset, receiver, radio or PA microphone functions is a functional test of a small electronic device; in an E1 setting the unit is docked in a fixture exactly as EOL test cells present units.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics - Automated Warehouse
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch performs autonomous case handling in commercial logistics: DHL had ten units unloading cases across three countries as of June 2025 (~700 cases/hour) and signed an MOU for 1,000+ more, showing robotic handling and loading of cased supplies into and out of vehicles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic case unloading/loading at dock height inside trailers. Transfer: loading cases of water, coolers and supply boxes into a coach luggage bay is comparable box-sized, similar-weight case handling with the vehicle brought to a fixed bay.

sources.title: How Diligent's Robots Are Making a Difference in Texas Hospitals - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi is the closest deployed E2 mobile manipulator: it works in hospital corridors and supply rooms, autonomously picking supplies out of supply ..., with a fleet of roughly 100 robots and over a million autonomous deliveries - but it fetches and transports predefined items and does not count out, functionally test, or stage heterogeneous equipment kits.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous hospital supply fetch-and-deliver in a structured human facility. Cited to bound the E2 judgment: the manipulation is limited to grasping and transporting known, pre-staged items, so it does not substantiate assembling and functionally checking a full pre-departure kit at E2.

tasks.label: Greet and register visitors, and issue any required identification badges or safety devices.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Museum, gallery, zoo or historic-site visitor center: guide/greeter welcomes arriving individuals and small parties at an indoor welcome desk, verifies tickets or timed-entry reservations, logs them into the visit register, hands out sticker badges or entry wristbands and audio-guide headsets/receivers, and gives house rules before the tour starts.

Corporate HQ, government building, broadcast studio or campus tour: greeter at the lobby security desk meets pre-registered visitors, checks photo ID against the day's list, has them sign an NDA/waiver, prints and issues a photo visitor badge with access rights, and notifies the host before the tour group assembles.

Industrial establishment tour (factory, brewery, power plant, water treatment, distribution center): greeter registers each visitor at the plant reception, records ID and emergency contact, runs a safety orientation/waiver, then issues a visitor badge plus PPE - hard hat, safety glasses, hearing protection, hi-vis vest - to each person before the group enters the floor.

Adventure/outdoor outfitter (raft, kayak, zipline, caving, bike, snorkel): guide greets clients at the launch site, trailhead or riverside base, checks the reservation list and signed waivers, then sizes, hands out and physically fits safety devices - helmets, PFDs, harnesses, wetsuits - adjusting straps and confirming fit on each person, including children.

Meeting-point check-in for walking tours, coach/bus tours and cruise shore excursions: guide waits at a street corner, plaza, hotel entrance or pier curb, greets guests as they arrive, matches names to a paper or tablet manifest, scans phone vouchers, and hands out sticker badges/lanyards and whisper-radio receivers with earpieces, in weather and street noise.

sources.title: ALICE Virtual Receptionist: Visitor Management System
sources.claim: Commercial self-service visitor-management kiosks deployed in building lobbies register walk-in visitors, verify ID, and physically print and issue a visitor badge, notifying the host - the same greet/register/issue-badge sequence as the task.

sources.title: Visitor Management Kiosks - FacilityOS (VisitorOS)
sources.claim: iLobby/FacilityOS VisitorOS self-service check-in kiosks are deployed in manufacturing plants and high-security facilities, handling visitor registration, ID scanning, badge printing and enforced safety-briefing completion at check-in.

sources.title: PPE Vending Machines: Smart Safety Equipment Distribution
sources.claim: Industrial PPE dispensing machines installed inside plants automatically issue hard hats, safety glasses and hearing protection to identified individuals, controlled by badge/PIN authentication - the physical 'issue safety devices' step of a plant tour check-in.

sources.system: Fastenal FAST 5000 industrial vending machines and lockers
sources.title: Vending Case Study - Machinery Manufacturing (Fastenal)
sources.claim: Fastenal's FAST 5000 vending machines ... lockers are installed in manufacturing facilities to distribute and account for PPE at the point of use, showing this dispensing is deployed at scale in real plants.

sources.system: Incheon Airport autonomous self check-in robot (plus guide/patrol and docent robots)
sources.title: World's first autonomous self check-in robot at Incheon Airport
sources.claim: Incheon International Airport has put 31 autonomous mobile robots into operation, including a self check-in robot that proactively approaches passengers in the terminal and performs the check-in transaction normally done at a kiosk or counter.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: passenger self check-in. Same act of meeting an arriving member of the public in an institution-controlled concourse, registering them against a booking and issuing their travel credential.

sources.title: How Robotics Are Changing Airport Operations
sources.claim: Trade press confirms robots are being used for passenger check-in at Incheon Airport, corroborating the deployment rather than an announcement of intent.

instances.label: City sightseeing driver-guide: drives a 6–14 passenger van/minibus on congested metropolitan streets between landmarks, museums and neighborhoods, pulling into curbside loading zones, waiting for the group at each stop, coping with traffic, pedestrians, double-parked vehicles and construction detours.

Transfer/shuttle runs: picks up visitors at a hotel, airport terminal curb, cruise pier or convention center and drives them (city arterials plus freeway) to an establishment, attraction or the tour start point, including luggage handling and curbside drop-off.

Out-of-town excursion: drives a large van or motorcoach several hours on interstates and rural two-lane roads to wineries, national/state parks, caverns, battlefields or small historic towns, parking in unpaved or tight lots at each site, in weather and after dark.

On-premises visitor transport: drives a tram, trolley, shuttle bus or cart on the operator's own controlled property — zoo, resort, theme park, university campus, industrial plant, ranch, park loop road — on a fixed route between visitor stops with guests boarding and alighting.

Adventure/backcountry tour: drives a 4x4 Jeep, open-air safari truck, dune buggy or snowcoach over unpaved trails, sand, rock ledges, forest roads or snow-covered routes, choosing lines over rough terrain and stopping at scenic/wildlife points.

Rock climbing / via ferrata / canyoning / caving guide at an outdoor natural site: teaches technique, ties and shows knots, demonstrates harness, helmet, belay and rappel devices, then fits and safety-checks each client's gear on uneven rock in variable weather and light.

Segway, e-bike, ATV, snowmobile or jet-ski tour orientation on the operator's staging lot or practice area: demonstrates controls, throttle and brakes, helmet fitting, mounting and dismounting, then supervises a practice loop and corrects each rider before departure.

instances.label: Walking, food, bike or ghost tour: guide meets 10-25 people at a street corner, plaza or park meeting point over a 15-minute window, matches each arrival to the booking manifest from a phone screen or printed voucher, takes cash or card from walk-ups, makes change, and hands out wristbands/headsets, amid pedestrian traffic and weather.

Motorcoach or day-trip boarding: guide stands at the coach door at a hotel curb, terminal bay or coach park and collects or scans each passenger's ticket or voucher as they board, sells or collects cash fares from walk-ups, and counts heads against the manifest.

Museum, gallery, aquarium or historic-house guided tour: guide or tour desk inside the visitor center collects admission tickets and timed-entry passes, scans member cards, and takes card or cash payment for tour add-ons before the group enters.

Industrial plant, brewery, distillery, utility or public-building tour: visitors check in at a lobby reception desk, the guide verifies the reservation, collects the tour fee (card or cash), collects the signed waiver and issues a badge or wristband.

Outdoor gated attraction - harbor cruise dock, ferry pier, cavern, ski or zipline base area, park entrance station: staff/guide collect fees and validate passes at a controlled entry point outdoors before the group boards or enters.

instances.label: Mobility assistance on the move: helping an elderly participant or wheelchair/walker user step down from the motorcoach, negotiate curbs, stairs, cobblestones and uneven ground at attractions, folding and stowing the wheelchair or walker in the coach bay, and carrying their bags so they keep pace with the group.

Escorting a slow-moving, mobility-limited or vision-impaired participant across a large indoor venue kept to a working standard — airport or cruise terminal, museum, convention hotel — from the group's drop-off point to the gate, exhibit or meeting point, arriving before the group moves on.

Meal-time special needs at a restaurant or hotel dining room: confirming a participant's allergy or dietary restriction with kitchen staff, checking the plate that arrives, getting it to the right person, cutting or adapting food, fetching water for medication and prompting a participant about medication timing.

Health incident on tour: a participant faints in the heat, sprains an ankle on a trail, suffers altitude sickness or a diabetic episode in a hotel room; the guide assesses, gives first aid, stays with the person and arranges transport to a clinic while managing the rest of the group.
Hotel-stay errands for a participant with special needs: bringing bottled water, an extra blanket, an amenity or medication left at reception up to the participant's guest room during the stay.

Sensory, cognitive and emotional support: describing surroundings and warning a blind participant of hazards, repositioning or repeating narration for a hard-of-hearing participant, calming an anxious flyer, and keeping a confused or memory-impaired participant with the group.

tasks.label: Administer first aid to injured group participants.

instances.label: Small cut or abrasion on a participant's hand/forearm during a walking, bus, or sightseeing tour: guide stops, inspects the wound, cleans/disinfects it and applies an adhesive dressing from the kit, then checks on the person later.

Other minor complaints on a tour route (sidewalk, trailhead, park, coach aisle): blisters needing moleskin/taping, insect stings, splinters, nosebleeds, sunburn, minor burns, motion sickness - varied body locations, patient standing or seated on the ground, bystanders and traffic around.

Injury on a backcountry/adventure segment (hiking, trekking, rafting, cycling, ski touring): sprained ankle, deep bleeding laceration, or suspected fracture - direct pressure and wound packing, wrapping/splinting, ice, assisting the person off uneven terrain, deciding on evacuation, in weather and away from roads.

Non-traumatic medical episode in the group: fainting, heat exhaustion/dehydration, hypoglycemia, altitude sickness - position and cool/shade the person, monitor pulse and breathing, give fluids or oxygen, manage the rest of the group until recovery or handoff to EMS.

Life-threatening emergency: cardiac arrest (CPR and AED), anaphylaxis (epinephrine auto-injector), or severe arterial bleeding (tourniquet) on a trail, tour bus, or street, sustained until professional responders arrive.

Minor first aid delivered inside a controlled indoor facility on the itinerary - hotel lobby, cruise-ship lounge, museum or visitor center - stocked first-aid kit, staff present, level floor, patient seated in a chair.

sources.title: Aletta - Vitestro
sources.claim: Aletta is a CE-marked medical robot that autonomously performs the full venipuncture procedure on a human arm placed in its fixture, including skin-site targeting and placing the adhesive bandage afterwards; one human supervises up to three devices.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: phlebotomy. Transfer to first aid covers only the manipulation core of dressing a small wound - locating a target on human skin, applying antiseptic prep, and placing an adhesive bandage on a human forearm - with comparable objects (human skin, adhesive dressings) and far finer precision than a plaster requires. It occurs only with the arm held in a purpose-built armrest under supervision.

sources.system: Aletta Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device (ADOPT trial, NCT05878483)
sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial
sources.claim: Multicenter clinical trial in Dutch outpatient phlebotomy departments reports the autonomous device achieved 94.5% first-stick success in routine use with 0.6% mild adverse events - human-comparable quality, but only for its narrow procedure in a supervised fixtured workstation, with failures referred to a human phlebotomist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outpatient phlebotomy. Establishes that autonomous robotic contact with a human limb at worker-quality reliability exists only in a supervised, fixtured workstation for one stereotyped procedure; it does not cover injury assessment or care of unfixtured patients.

sources.system: Autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing
sources.developer: University of California San Diego (Yip lab)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing (arXiv:2510.06127)
sources.claim: State of the art in autonomous robotic wound care is individual subtasks - detaching and re-securing adhesive tape, dressing removal - demonstrated at bench scale; whole wound redressing is still performed exclusively by trained clinicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: chronic wound redressing. It is the closest published work to robotic first aid on a wound and shows capability stops at laboratory subtasks, supporting negative judgments for whole-instance first aid.

sources.title: DARPA launches search for robot medics to treat battlefield casualties
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic treatment of casualties in the field (self-deploying wound assessment and hemorrhage control) is a DARPA solicitation issued in 2026 for capability that does not yet exist, so no fielded or demonstrated system performs field first aid autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: field trauma care. Cited only as context for negative judgments - it is a request for capability not yet built, and cannot support any positive judgment.

Guide drives a fixed-route, low-speed shuttle or tram inside a controlled property — resort campus, ranch, winery, theme attraction, park village, ski base area — between a small set of standard stops with staff-managed loading.

Guide pilots a small aircraft — mostly scenic/sightseeing flights or short hops from an established airfield or floatplane base to an activity site — including preflight, passenger briefing, takeoff, the sightseeing route, and landing.

tasks.label: Verify amounts and quality of equipment prior to expeditions or tours.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whitewater/sea-kayak outfitter: in the boathouse or gear warehouse the morning of a trip, the guide counts PFDs, helmets, paddles, throw bags, dry bags and spray skirts against the trip manifest, tugs straps and works every buckle, checks foam and webbing for rot/tears, verifies raft/inflatable pressure and that the pump, patch kit and first-aid kit are complete.

Mountaineering, trekking or backcountry-ski guide service base or hut: before departure the guide runs ropes hand-over-hand feeling for core shots and glazing, inspects harnesses, slings and crampon straps by sight and touch, counts ice screws/carabiners against the rack list, function-tests avalanche transceivers (send/search) and checks probes, shovels and the group first-aid kit.

Multi-day camping/overland or expedition-cruise tour: at the operator's depot or warehouse the guide checks the packing list for the trip - tents, sleeping bags/pads, camp stoves and fuel, cook kit, water jugs, coolers, food boxes, spare parts - confirming quantities are right and that packaging/items are intact and serviceable before loading the vehicle or trailer.

Day-tour hardware check at a shop or garage: bike/e-bike tour guide squeezes brakes, spins wheels, checks tire pressure, shifting and quick-releases on each bike and counts helmets and repair kits; equivalent checks for snorkel sets, wetsuits, or audio-guide headsets (power on, charge level, count in the case).

Field check in the open before launch: at a remote trailhead, riverbank, airstrip or base camp the guide unloads duffels and dry boxes, recounts gear against the manifest after transport, inspects for transit damage or missing items, and re-packs - on uneven ground, in wind, dust, rain or snow, with clients and porters milling around.

tasks.label: Instruct novices in climbing techniques, mountaineering, and wilderness survival, and demonstrate use of hunting, fishing, and climbing equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Outdoor rock-climbing instruction at a natural crag on a guided trip: the guide sizes and fits harnesses and helmets on novice clients, demonstrates figure-eight and clove-hitch knots with the rope, shows belay-device threading, checks every client's knot/harness/carabiner before each climb, demonstrates footwork and body position on the rock, then coaches and belays each novice up the route. Uneven ground, wind, mixed client ability, life-safety consequences.

Mountaineering skills session on a snowfield or glacier: demonstrating crampon technique and step-kicking, ice-axe self-arrest on a slope (repeated demo plus hands-on correction of each novice's attempts), rope-team spacing and coiling, and basic crevasse-rescue anchor/pulley setups, in cold, glare, and changing snow conditions.

Fishing instruction on a riverbank, lake shore, or from a guide boat: demonstrating knots and rigging, fly/lure selection, the casting stroke and mending, hook set, then physically correcting each novice's grip and timing, and demonstrating netting, handling, and release of a fish.

Wilderness survival instruction at a backcountry camp: demonstrating fire starting with ferro rod and natural tinder, tarp/shelter construction and knots, water treatment, stove operation, map-and-compass navigation, and improvised first aid, then supervising and correcting novices' own attempts in variable weather and terrain.

Hunting equipment demonstration and safety instruction in the field or at an outfitter's informal outdoor range: showing safe firearm or bow handling and carry, loading/unloading, sight-in and shot placement, glassing with optics, plus demonstration of field-dressing tools on rough ground with live novices present.

Pre-trip gear orientation indoors at a lodge, base camp, or outfitter shop: guide gathers clients in a fixed briefing room, demonstrates avalanche transceiver search, harness and crampon fitting, pack loading, stove lighting, and layering, sizing and adjusting each client's equipment on their body and confirming they can operate it.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous locomotion over natural trails, a prerequisite for any field instruction. Cited to show the ceiling: the result is simulation-only, so it cannot substantiate completion of outdoor guiding or demonstration work on real terrain.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous rope manipulation, the closest analogue to demonstrating climbing knots. Transfer fails: it is a tabletop workpiece with a fixed camera, one rope type, no client harness fitting, no safety checking, and 84% success is unacceptable for belay-system instruction.

tasks.label: Set up camps, and prepare meals for tour group members.

instances.label: Backcountry trekking/backpacking camp: guide arrives at a wilderness site with a group of 6-12, scouts tent pads, pitches and stakes several tents on uneven, rocky or root-crossed ground in wind or rain, rigs a tarp/kitchen area, sets up water treatment and a latrine, and strikes and packs the camp the next morning.

Vehicle- or raft-supported camp setup: overland/van tour or river trip pulls into a designated campground site or a river sandbar, guide unloads trailer/dry boxes, erects large canvas tents, canopy, tables, propane stove kitchen, hand-wash and toilet systems, then breaks it all down and reloads next day.

Cooking and serving the main evening meal at camp for 8-16 guests: guide works from coolers and dry boxes on a folding camp kitchen, uses two-burner propane stoves, a grill or dutch ovens over coals, prepares a multi-component menu with dietary substitutions, serves buffet style, and cleans up in wash basins.

Breakfast and trail-lunch preparation at an already-standing camp: hot drinks, eggs/pancakes/oatmeal for the group at dawn, then assembling and packing sandwiches, wraps, cut fruit and snacks into boxes or panniers for the day's travel.

Meal service at a semi-permanent tented safari/expedition base camp run by the outfitter: fixed kitchen tent or hut with pantry, gas range, refrigeration and staff, guide plans and prepares plated multi-course meals for guests on a set schedule and keeps the mess tent stocked.

tasks.label: Maintain a safe play environment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Childcare center classroom, free-play block with 8-16 infants/toddlers/preschoolers present: worker positions herself for sightlines, continuously scans the room, and physically intervenes as hazards arise — fishing a bead or bottle cap out of a toddler's mouth, blocking a child climbing a shelf, catching an unsteady walker, separating a biting/pushing conflict, moving a tipped chair or spilled water out of the traffic path.

Fenced outdoor playground at a center or school: pre-use walk-through (broken glass, litter, animal waste, standing water, insect nests, loose hardware, worn fall-zone mulch, hot metal slide), gate/latch check, then supervising 10-25 running, climbing and swinging children — repositioning, spotting climbers, clearing the swing arc, ending unsafe play.

Play room hazard-proofing and reset with no children present: sort and wash/sanitize mouthed toys, discard cracked or broken toys and missing-part sets, sweep floor for small parts and choking hazards, secure furniture, cords, blind pulls and outlet covers, verify latches and gates, re-arrange centers so pathways are clear.

After-hours cleaning of the emptied classroom/play room as a health-and-safety routine: vacuum or scrub the floor and mats and disinfect the open room surfaces so the space is sanitary for the next morning.

Nanny or family childcare provider in a private home: childproofing a house taken as found (stair gates, cabinet latches, cords, small objects, pet bowls, unstable furniture), then supervising play indoors and in the back yard, removing hazards as children move through rooms.

Off-site outing — public park playground, splash pad, library story time, or a walk to a field-trip site: scan an uncontrolled setting for hazards (broken glass, water, traffic, dogs, strangers), keep the group within bounds, and intervene physically when a child heads for a street or climbs beyond ability.

sources.title: Figure's Humanoid Robot Picks Up Toys, Wipes Surfaces in New Demo
sources.claim: Figure's Figure 03 humanoid, running Helix 02, was shown in a March 2026 demo autonomously tidying a staged living room — collecting scattered toys and blocks into containers, repositioning cushions, and spraying and wiping a surface — without step-by-step human control.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying. Picking up toys and wiping surfaces overlaps with resetting a play room, but the demo is a staged room with no children present, no reported reliability, and no safety judgment (identifying a cracked toy, a choking-size part, an unanchored shelf).

sources.title: Figure humanoid robot cleans cluttered living room in new video demo
sources.claim: A second outlet independently describes the same Figure 03 demonstration as autonomous tidying of a cluttered living room, confirming it is a company video demo rather than a deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying; same transfer and same limits as the eWeek item — a mock living room, single demo, no evidence of worker-quality hazard removal in an occupied childcare room.

sources.title: Brain Corp: School Cleaning Services Get a Boost From Robots
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile floor-cleaning robots (BrainOS-powered scrubbers, SoftBank Whiz vacuums) are commercially deployed in K-12 school buildings, navigating classrooms, hallways and gyms autonomously alongside students and staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: custodial floor cleaning in an education facility. It transfers to the after-hours cleaning instance because the surface, layout and standard (institution-maintained classroom floors) are the same; it does not transfer to hazard judgment or supervision.
