Transfers to the after-hours sanitizing of an emptied play room (same room type, institution-controlled, no occupants); it cannot run with children present and does not wash mouthed toys or remove physical hazards.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: The leading consumer home humanoid ships with human teleoperators handling tasks its autonomy cannot, and no humanoid has been shown completing a full household chore end to end.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household work in private homes. Bears directly on the nanny instance: the only home-deployed humanoid relies on remote human operators, so it cannot support autonomous childproofing or supervision in a home.

sources.system: Socially assistive robot in free-play study
sources.developer: University research (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.title: Influence of a Socially Assistive Robot on Physical Activity, Social Play Behavior, and Toy-Use Behaviors of Children in a Free Play Environment
sources.claim: In the published study placing a socially assistive robot into a children's free-play area, the robot was teleoperated and its role was to offer lights, sounds and bubbles — not to detect or remove hazards or intervene physically.
sources.transferJustification: Direct-setting evidence: robots actually placed among playing young children operate under continuous human control and perform social, not safety-maintenance, functions.

sources.system: Mobile service robots with foundation models (survey)
sources.title: Embodied AI with Foundation Models for Mobile Service Robots: A Systematic Review
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of embodied AI for mobile service robots lists childcare — including monitoring young children and detecting risks such as toddlers approaching stairs or handling small objects — as an open research direction rather than a demonstrated capability.
sources.transferJustification: Survey evidence framing child monitoring and hazard detection as a prospective research problem, supporting the negative judgments for the supervision instances.

tasks.label: Observe and monitor children's play activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Indoor free-play period in a licensed childcare center classroom: 8-16 toddlers/preschoolers spread across block, dramatic-play, art and sensory centers. Worker positions herself for sightlines, scans and counts continuously, watches for choking hazards, climbing on furniture, biting and toy conflicts, and moves in to redirect or physically separate children.

Outdoor gross-motor time on a fenced center or school playground: 15-25 children on climbers, swings, slides and wheeled toys, spread over a large area in sun/wind/cold. Worker circulates, keeps every child in sight, counts heads, spots risky climbing or rough play, and steps in to catch, redirect or remove a child.

Nanny or babysitter supervising play in a private home, back yard, or neighborhood park: 1-3 children of mixed ages, household hazards (stairs, pets, cords, pools, kitchen), toys and layout that differ house to house, and unscheduled transitions between rooms and outdoors.

Before/after-school or summer-camp program in a school gym, cafeteria or multipurpose room: 20-30 school-age children in active games, board games and free choice, high noise, boisterous physical play; worker monitors for injuries, exclusion/bullying and children leaving the area.

Infant and young-toddler room floor play: 4-8 crawlers/new walkers on mats with soft toys; near-constant proximity required, watching for small objects going in mouths, pulling up on shelving, and one child crawling over another, with licensing 'sight and sound' supervision at all times.

sources.title: Promobot Announces the First-Ever Childcare Robot | PROMOBOT
sources.claim: The only widely publicized robot 'implemented' in a daycare setting is an autonomous service/greeter robot that entertains and teaches children about technology; it does not supervise play, watch for hazards, or intervene between children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interactive companion/education in a childcare center. Transfer to observing and monitoring play does NOT hold - the robot converses and demonstrates technology from a fixed interaction position; it does not track a group of moving children, judge developmental or safety risk, or intervene physically.

sources.title: Autonomous public safety robots on patrol, connected by Verizon
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile robots can patrol and monitor large structured facilities (campuses, malls, parking lots, schools) unattended, streaming video and raising alerts, but they detect security anomalies rather than supervising people, and they take no physical action.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous patrol and anomaly monitoring in an institution-controlled facility (E2). Transfer to monitoring children's play does not hold: the objects of attention are unpredictable small humans, the required output is anticipation of behavioral and injury risk plus immediate physical redirection, and the robot can only alert a remote human.

sources.title: Enabot EBO X review: Live in the future with this incredible Alexa robot
sources.claim: The best commercially available home 'guardian' robot autonomously cruises a house, follows a child on command and pushes alerts on baby crying or a person falling; it is a mobile camera that notifies an adult rather than a caregiver that supervises play.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-home mobile monitoring of a child. Transfer to the childcare task does not hold: coverage is one room and one subject at a time, detection is limited to crying or falls already in progress, there is no hazard anticipation or conflict judgment, and no ability to intervene - a remote adult must act.

tasks.label: Communicate with children's parents or guardians about daily activities, behaviors, and related issues.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Support children's emotional and social development, encouraging understanding of others and positive self-concepts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Care for children in institutional setting, such as group homes, nursery schools, private businesses, or schools for people with disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Infant/toddler room of a licensed childcare center or nursery school: worker diapers and toilet-trains, prepares and gives bottles and solid food, lifts and carries, soothes crying children, dresses them for outdoors, puts them down for naps and watches them breathe, sanitizes surfaces, and keeps continuous line-of-sight supervision at state ratios (1:4).

Preschool/nursery classroom, ages 3-5: worker sets up and oversees free play and centers, helps with toileting and handwashing, serves and supervises snacks and meals, resolves conflicts and injuries, dresses children for and supervises outdoor playground time, does head counts and transitions, and reports to parents at pickup.

Before/after-school program or drop-in childcare run by a private business, church, gym or school: worker signs school-age children in and out, supervises homework, crafts, gym and free play, serves snacks, enforces rules and behavior expectations, handles minor first aid, and manages arrival/departure with authorized adults.

School or day program for children with disabilities: worker assists a child or small group with feeding (including special diets and adaptive utensils), toileting and diapering, mobility transfers and positioning, communication device setup, sensory/behavioral de-escalation, and one-to-one shadowing during class and recess.

Residential group home evening/weekend routine: worker bathes and dresses children, prepares and shares meals, does laundry and chores with the children, supervises homework and recreation, manages bedtime and overnight checks, and documents incidents.

sources.developer: Global Bridge Holdings with Gunma University
sources.title: Day care facilities test robots as high-tech solution to alleviate staffing shortages - The Japan Times
sources.claim: Vevo, a bear-shaped robot deployed in Japanese nursery schools run by Global Bridge Holdings, greets and identifies children and records body temperatures; cot sensors monitor children during naps and alert human teachers. Its role is monitoring and record-keeping support, not physical care or supervisory responsibility.
sources.transferJustification: Closest deployed robot in an institutional childcare setting (nursery school). Cited to show that the demonstrated scope in that environment is greeting, identification and vital-sign monitoring — no feeding, diapering, dressing, or responsibility for supervising children.

sources.title: Special Education · RobotLAB
sources.claim: NAO humanoid robots are sold to and used in special-education classrooms to run social-skills and ABA-style sessions alongside teachers; the robot delivers prompts and gestures, it does not attend to children's personal care or safety.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated instruction/therapy for children with disabilities in a school. Nearest deployed capability to 'schools for people with disabilities'; it covers only seated verbal/gestural interaction with a teacher present, not feeding, toileting, transfers or supervision.

sources.system: Social robots for child safeguarding (expert review of NAO/Pepper-class systems)
sources.developer: Academic review presented at ACM HRI
sources.title: Expert Insights on Robots for Safeguarding Children: How (not) and Why (not)?
sources.claim: Expert review of robots for child safeguarding finds current perception and speech capabilities insufficient to reliably monitor or protect children in real time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous monitoring and safeguarding of children. Supervisory responsibility for children's safety is the core of institutional childcare, and the review indicates robots cannot perform it reliably.

sources.title: NEO humanoid designed for household use, available for preorder - The Robot Report
sources.claim: 1X's NEO, the most advanced general-purpose home humanoid shipping in 2026, performs only simple pre-programmed tasks autonomously; anything more complex is executed by a human teleoperator driving the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general manipulation and chores in people-occupied settings. Establishes that even state-of-the-art humanoids rely on teleoperation for non-trivial tasks, so they cannot substantiate autonomous physical caregiving.

sources.system: Bimanual robotic dressing assistance scheme (IEEE T-RO 2024); SkinGrip bed-bathing manipulator
sources.developer: University of York / Delft and other academic groups
sources.title: New dressing robot can 'mimic' the actions of care workers
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing and bed-bathing remain laboratory research: bimanual systems dress a cooperative adult's arm in a controlled lab using motions learned from human demonstrations; no deployed system dresses or bathes children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physically assisting a person with dressing/washing. Closest research analogue to dressing and bathing children; it is a single-garment sub-step with a cooperative, still adult in a lab, so it does not transfer to squirming toddlers or whole-shift care.

sources.system: Social robot in an inclusive daycare (HRI 2026 field study)
sources.title: Long-Term Integration of a Robot in an Inclusive Daycare: An Ethnographic Study Focused on Children and Caregivers
sources.claim: A long-term ethnographic study of a social robot placed in an inclusive daycare frames the robot as engaging children while supporting caregivers, with practical integration still an open research question.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot presence in a daycare group room. Most recent field evidence that robots in childcare institutions act as engagement aids under caregiver oversight, not as substitutes for the caregiver.

tasks.label: Sanitize toys and play equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Licensed center infant/toddler room: toys mouthed by babies are dropped into a 'dirty' bin through the day; at closing the worker washes each item (rattles, teethers, stacking rings, plastic figures) with detergent in a sink or dishwasher, rinses, immerses/sprays with bleach sanitizer, air-dries, and returns them to open shelves before morning.

Preschool/school-age classroom at a center: weekly (or after illness) sanitizing of hard toys — blocks, manipulatives, dramatic-play dishes, cars, puzzle pieces — sorted into bins, run through a sanitizing dishwasher cycle or scrubbed and soaked in sanitizer, dried, and restocked to labeled bins.

Large or fixed play equipment at a center, sanitized in place: indoor climbers, slides, playhouses, activity/water-sensory tables, riding toys, cots and gross-motor mats, plus the outdoor play structure — sprayed or wiped with detergent then sanitizer, working around varied shapes, textiles, and crevices.

Soft goods at a center: plush toys, dress-up clothes, fabric books, puppets, and nap blankets collected and laundered in a hot-water washer/dryer cycle, then sorted and returned to the dramatic-play area.

Private household (nanny) or family childcare home: wiping toys with disinfectant wipes, running plastic toys and teethers through the home dishwasher or sink, cleaning bath toys and high-chair toys, amid a home layout with pets, furniture, and mixed household items.

sources.system: IWT/Tecniplast ARES and PEGASUS robotic cage-wash cells
sources.date: 2016 (brochure); product line still marketed with VOYAGER AGV additions as of 2024-2025
sources.title: BOTTLE & CAGE AUTOMATION (IWT/Tecniplast automation brochure, PDF)
sources.claim: IWT/Tecniplast sells robotic cage-wash cells (ARES, PEGASUS) in which industrial robots load and unload plastic rodent cages, lids, bottles and accessories on the dirty and clean sides of tunnel/rack washers; over 100 robots are installed in vivaria worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical washing/disinfection of hard plastic housewares (cages, lids, bottles, feeders) in a purpose-built wash cell. The objects are the same class as hard childcare toys — moulded plastic, hand-sized to bin-sized, soiled with organic matter — and the robot handles loading, presentation and unloading, which is exactly the handling a toy-wash cell would need at E1.

sources.title: Getinge Vivus Tunnel Washer | Cage, Rack & Bottle Tunnel Washer
sources.claim: Vivarium tunnel washers (e.g., Getinge Vivus) run fully automatic multi-phase cycles that continuously sanitize and dry plastic cages and bottles at high throughput.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated wash-rinse-sanitize-dry of hard plastic items presented in racks/conveyors — the same wash/sanitize/dry sequence childcare licensing requires for toys, at a validated sanitation level.

sources.developer: study of standard vivarium tunnel washers
sources.title: Mechanical Washing Prevents Transmission of Bacterial, Viral, and Protozoal Murine Pathogens from Cages (PMC)
sources.claim: Peer-reviewed testing shows mechanical tunnel-washing of soiled plastic cages at >=82 C eliminated transmission of multiple bacterial, viral and protozoal pathogens, i.e. the automated wash achieves genuine sanitation of soiled plastic items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: validation that the automated wash cycle used in the robotic wash cell actually sanitizes soiled plastic surfaces — the outcome standard a childcare employer requires for sanitized toys.

sources.title: Dishcraft Robotics raises funding to help caterers, cafeterias reopen (The Robot Report)
sources.claim: Dishcraft Robotics operated purpose-built robotic dishwashing machines that autonomously scrubbed and sanitized food- and mouth-soiled dishware at commercial scale for Bay Area cafeterias and caterers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic washing and sanitizing of saliva- and food-soiled hard tableware (plates, bowls, cups) — materially and dimensionally comparable to dramatic-play dishes and hard plastic toys, and held to health-code sanitation standards.

sources.title: Lights out, system on: The Dark Factory (Laundry and Cleaning Today)
sources.claim: JENSEN's Dark Factory laundry automation runs the soil-side sorting, storage and feeding of an industrial laundry overnight with no staff present, so soiled textiles are processed and washed without human handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated sorting and hot-wash laundering of soiled textiles in a purpose-built plant — the same process used for plush toys, dress-up clothes and nap blankets, which childcare staff sanitize by machine laundering.

sources.title: UVD Robots Deploys Largest Fleet of Autonomous Disinfection Robots to a U.S. School District
sources.claim: Autonomous UV-C disinfection robots are deployed at scale in US school buildings, disinfecting room surfaces without staff driving them; they provide only line-of-sight surface disinfection and do not remove soil or handle objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: whole-room surface disinfection in an institutional building. It is the closest deployed in-facility system, but it neither cleans visible soil nor reaches shadowed toy surfaces or items in bins, so it cannot deliver the wash-then-sanitize output childcare requires.

sources.title: 1X's $20,000 NEO Humanoid Robot Launches With A Catch: It Needs Humans To Do Your Chores
sources.claim: Consumer humanoid robots marketed for household chores such as loading the dishwasher and tidying still rely on remote human operators rather than autonomy.

tasks.label: Dress children and change diapers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Licensed childcare center infant/toddler room: worker changes diapers on a wall-mounted changing table on a posted schedule and on demand - lifts a squirming 8-30 lb child onto the table, unfastens clothing and tabs, wipes the perineal area (sometimes heavy soiling), applies barrier cream, fastens a clean diaper, redresses, sanitizes the surface and washes hands, and logs the change, while keeping a hand on the child at all times.

Childcare center / preschool: dressing a group of 2-5 year olds for outdoor play or departure - coats, zippers and snaps, hats, mittens, boots/shoes with laces or Velcro - plus changing a child fully after a toileting accident or spill, often with children who resist, wiggle, or insist on doing it themselves.

Private household nanny: morning/after-nap dressing of an infant or toddler in the family's home - pulling onesies, shirts, tights and pants over a mobile, uncooperative child on a bed, floor or lap; matching parent-specified outfits; handling snaps, buttons and diaper covers.

Private household nanny/babysitter: diaper change wherever the child is - floor changing pad, couch, or a diaper bag on an outing - including cloth diapers, blowouts requiring a full clothing change or wipe-down bath, and children who roll, kick, or crawl away mid-change.

Infant room, center or home: dressing a newborn/young infant - supporting the head and neck, threading floppy limbs through sleeves, snapping a onesie, swaddling or zipping a sleep sack before nap, on a changing table or crib mattress.

sources.developer: Fan Zhang and Yiannis Demiris, Imperial College London
sources.title: Learning garment manipulation policies toward robot-assisted dressing | Science Robotics
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous robot dressing is validated on an immobile medical training manikin, dressing a loose hospital gown onto an adult-sized body in a lab setup - no live, mobile human subject and no child.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dressing a person in a garment. It does not transfer to dressing children - the subject is a rigid manikin held still, the garment is a loose open-back gown, and there is no head/limb support, no resistance or sudden movement, and no diaper handling.

sources.system: Close-fitting dressing assistance system with semantic visual attention and tactile sensing
sources.developer: Tsukakoshi, Miyake, Ogata, Sugano et al., Waseda University
sources.title: Close-Fitting Dressing Assistance Based on State Estimation of Feet and Garments with Semantic-based Visual Attention (arXiv:2505.03400)
sources.claim: Dressing close-fitting garments (socks) on a human limb is still an open research problem in 2025; the demonstrated system works on a seated, cooperative adult foot in a laboratory rig.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting a close-fitting garment on a body part. The authors state it is not yet solved even for a still adult foot, so it cannot support putting tights, onesies or shoes on a moving toddler.

sources.title: Self-Wearing Adaptive Garments via Soft Robotic Unfurling (arXiv:2507.07221)
sources.claim: The most recent 'autonomous dressing' result is a garment that wraps itself around a stationary adult wearer via soft actuators; it is a wearable device, not a robot that dresses another person or handles diapering.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: getting a garment onto a person. It requires a cooperative, still wearer and a purpose-built powered garment; it provides no capability for undressing a child, cleaning, diaper fastening, or restraining a squirming infant.

sources.system: Infant washer and diaper-changer apparatus (patent concept)
sources.date: 2017 filing, granted 2018; no deployment found as of 2026
sources.title: US20170143168A1 - Infant washer and diaper-changer apparatus and method - Google Patents
sources.claim: Automated infant diaper changing exists only as a patent-stage concept apparatus (an 'infant washer and diaper-changer'), with no evidence of a built, tested, or deployed system operating on real infants.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (diaper changing) but only a paper design; no demonstration of autonomous operation on a real infant, so it cannot substantiate completion at any tier.

tasks.label: Keep records on individual children, including daily observations and information about activities, meals served, and medications administered.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Identify signs of emotional or developmental problems in children and bring them to parents' or guardians' attention.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Instruct children in health and personal habits, such as eating, resting, and toilet habits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Toilet-habit coaching in a licensed childcare center: worker watches a 2-3 year old for cues, walks the child to the child-height toilet, coaches and physically helps with pulling down clothing, sitting, wiping, flushing and handwashing, praises success, and handles accidents and soiled clothing while other toddlers are present.

Mealtime habit instruction at a center: worker seats toddlers/preschoolers at low tables, models and hand-over-hand guides spoon/fork/cup use, coaches trying new foods, chewing, not sharing food, staying seated, wiping face and hands, and clearing the plate to the cart.

Naptime/rest routine instruction: worker sets out cots, guides children to their mats, coaches quiet-body rest routines (shoes off, blanket, lying down), rubs backs or pats to settle resistant children, quiets talkers, and manages non-sleepers with quiet activities.

Hygiene routine instruction through the day at a center: worker prompts and escorts children to sinks before meals, after toileting and after outdoor play, lifts or steps up small children, coaches soap/scrub/rinse/dry sequence, and teaches nose-blowing, tissue use and coughing into the elbow.

Group health lesson at circle time in a preschool room: worker leads 10-18 three-to-five-year-olds through a song, book or prop-based lesson on healthy foods, germs, teeth brushing or bedtime, calling on individual children, managing wiggly behavior, and checking understanding.

Nanny or family childcare provider in a private home: same eating, resting and toilet-habit instruction for one to four children, in a house whose bathroom, kitchen and nap spaces vary, following the family's routines and rules amid pets, siblings and household clutter.

sources.title: WallBo: A Social Robot for Fostering Hand Hygiene For Children | Proceedings of the Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference
sources.claim: WallBo is a low-cost wall-mounted social robot that teaches WHO handwashing technique to children; its 2026 iteration is presented as a conference demonstration with fully autonomous operation intended for school washrooms, providing verbal scaffolding and AR gamification.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coaching children through the handwashing sequence. It is the closest published analogue to a childcare worker's hygiene-habit instruction, but covers only sink-side technique coaching for children who already wash independently.

sources.title: Handwashing robot makes a splash at Glasgow primary schools - University of Glasgow news
sources.claim: WallBo's school pilots in Glasgow primary schools were run with a human controlling the robot; autonomy was still a goal at that stage.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task (handwashing coaching); establishes that the field deployments with children relied on teleoperation.

sources.title: Enhancing Hand Hygiene Practices Through a Social Robot-Assisted Intervention in a Rural School in India
sources.claim: A WallBo pilot deployment in a rural school in ... measured handwashing compliance and knowledge gains among children, again as a research pilot rather than a staffed-role replacement.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hygiene-habit promotion with school children; shows measured effect on one habit only, with no physical assistance and no management of the surrounding routine.

sources.system: Avatar robots (CommU/Sota-type) in elementary classroom field trial
sources.developer: Osaka University / Hiroshi Ishiguro Laboratory and collaborators
sources.title: Encouraging classroom activities for children using avatar robots: a field trial (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robots supporting whole classroom activities with children are avatar robots driven by rotating teams of remote human operators, not autonomous systems.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sustained robot participation in classroom routines with children; demonstrates that continuous human teleoperation is still required for open-ended child group interaction.

sources.title: Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens (Phys.org / AFP)
sources.claim: Commercially sold kindergarten robots in China (Keeko, iPal) act as teaching assistants delivering stories, puzzles and screen-based lessons; they have no manipulators and do not carry out children's care routines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led activities for preschool-age children in a kindergarten. Shows the deployed capability is scripted story/puzzle delivery under teacher supervision, not habit instruction or physical guidance.

sources.system: NAO-based 'Hero the Sleep Professor' sleep-hygiene education robot
sources.developer: Princess Máxima Center / Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam / TNO
sources.title: Interactive Education on Sleep Hygiene with a Social Robot at a Pediatric Oncology Outpatient Clinic
sources.claim: Social-robot health-habit education for children has been trialled as short one-to-one scripted question-and-answer sessions with school-age patients in a hospital outpatient clinic.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instructing children in a health habit (sleep). Transfer is limited: participants were 8-12 year olds able to follow a scripted dialogue, and the robot neither ran a rest routine nor handled younger children.

sources.system: Global Bridge Holdings nursery robot and cot sensor system
sources.title: Japan company testing robots to counter childcare shortage - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Technology introduced into Japanese nursery schools to address childcare staffing addresses monitoring during naps, with cot sensors alerting human caretakers, rather than instructing children in rest routines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: naptime support in a childcare facility. It substantiates only passive monitoring with human caretakers alerted, so it cannot support completion of rest-habit instruction.

tasks.label: Organize and store toys and materials to ensure order in activity areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Cleanup transition in a licensed child care center / preschool classroom: after free play, the worker (with children helping) gathers blocks, dolls, dress-up clothes, puzzle pieces, small manipulatives and vehicles from the floor, tables and under furniture and returns each to its labeled bin, shelf or cubby within a few minutes, while continuing to supervise mobile children.

Nanny or in-home childcare worker tidying a family's playroom/living room: toys of every kind scattered across rugs, sofas and under furniture; items returned to household-specific storage spots (toy chest, closet shelves, bedroom bins) whose layout differs from home to home; books and craft items collected too.

Art, craft and sensory materials in a center classroom: after a project the worker collects markers, crayons, scissors, glue sticks and paper scraps from tables and floor, caps and sorts them into caddies, returns paint, playdough and sensory-bin materials to labeled cabinet shelves, and throws away scraps.

Center playground / outdoor play area: after outdoor time the worker collects balls, jump ropes, sand and water toys, chalk and ride-on trikes from grass, sand and pavement and stores them in a shed, bin cart or storage bench, in sun, wind or wet conditions.

Weekly / end-of-day deep reset in a center: bins are emptied and re-sorted, puzzle and game pieces matched to their sets, broken or incomplete toys culled, toy sets rotated in and out of a storage room, and shelves restocked so the room meets licensing tidiness standards.

Before/after-school or camp program in a shared multipurpose space (school gym, cafeteria, church hall) that must be fully cleared each day: board games, sports equipment, craft supplies and mats packed into rolling carts and locked closets after the session.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics reveals RightPick 3 item-handling robot
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick piece-picking stations autonomously grasp diverse, previously unseen items presented in totes by an AS/RS or conveyor and place them into designated outbound totes or cartons; the systems are commercially deployed in warehouses worldwide.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse piece picking. If toys and craft supplies were presented at a fixtured station the way totes are presented here, sorting mixed small objects into designated containers is the same grasp-and-place problem with comparable object variety and placement precision.

sources.title: AMP's Horowitz on Bringing AI to the Recycling World
sources.claim: AMP Robotics' AMP Cortex robots autonomously identify and sort mixed streams of objects on a moving conveyor into separate category bins, at up to 99% purity and 80-120 picks per minute, with 125+ units deployed in recycling facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated recycling sortation. Culling broken items and re-sorting a mixed pile of toys and materials into category bins is the same visual classification plus pick-and-place operation, at higher speed and accuracy than a ... sorter, when the material is presented on a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Introducing Vulcan: Amazon's first robot with a sense of touch
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robots autonomously pick and stow individual items into tightly packed fabric storage-pod compartments in operating fulfillment centers in Spokane and Hamburg, using force feedback.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic stowing into shelf compartments. Placing supplies onto designated shelf/bin locations in a storage rack is the same contact-rich insertion into a crowded compartment that storing toys and materials on labeled shelves requires, when items are presented at a fixed station.

sources.developer: Princeton / Stanford / Google (Wu, Antonova, Bohg, Song et al.)
sources.title: Personalized Robot Assistance with TidyBot
sources.claim: TidyBot, a mobile manipulator, autonomously picks objects off the floor of real rooms and puts each away in the correct receptacle, but succeeds with only ~85% of objects and takes roughly 15-20 seconds per object.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (π0.5 blog)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 controls a mobile manipulator to clean ... kitchens and bedrooms in homes that were not in its training data, including picking items off the floor and moving objects into drawers; performance is reported as success rate averaged over subtasks, i.e. a research evaluation rather than a deployed service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household cleanup. Picking scattered items off a bedroom floor and placing them in bins/drawers is the closest published analogue to gathering toys into their storage places in a home playroom.

sources.title: Figure's Humanoid Robot Picks Up Toys, Wipes Surfaces in New Demo
sources.claim: Figure released a March 2026 demonstration of its Figure 03 humanoid, running Helix 02, autonomously tidying a cluttered living room: picking ... toys and other items, sorting them, and wiping surfaces. It is a company demonstration video, not a deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Same class of task (picking up toys and putting them away) in a home living room; cited to assess whether home/classroom tidying has reached worker-quality reliability.

sources.title: Figure 03 Is The Robot in Your Kitchen (TIME)
sources.claim: Independent reporting on Figure's robots in April 2026 documents repeated failures in household manipulation during an in-person visit, indicating that home tidying demonstrations are not yet at reliable worker quality.
sources.transferJustification: Same developer and hardware family as the living-room tidying demo; used to bound the reliability claim for picking scattered objects off floors.

sources.title: Alphabet's X has 'Everyday Robots' test fleet that autonomously performs office maintenance tasks
sources.claim: Alphabet's Everyday Robots ran a fleet of more than ... mobile manipulators autonomously performing office cleanup tasks such as sorting waste into recycling/compost/landfill bins and wiping tables in Google offices; the program was shut down by Alphabet in early 2023.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: sorting loose items into the correct receptacle inside a human work facility (E2). Closest institutional-setting analogue to putting toys into labeled bins, though it operated at fixed waste stations with small light objects and no longer exists.

tasks.label: Perform general administrative tasks, such as taking attendance, editing internal paperwork, and making phone calls.

instances.label: Nanny or family-childcare provider in a private home does the children's laundry end to end: gathers clothes from hampers and bedroom floors, sorts and pretreats stains, runs the household washer and dryer, folds, and puts items away in dressers and closets.

In a private home, the worker cleans up after children's meals and snacks: scrapes and rinses plates, loads/unloads the household dishwasher, hand-washes bottles, nipples, sippy cups and pump parts, dries and puts them away.
In a private home, routine floor care in play areas, kitchen and children's bedrooms: vacuum carpet and rugs, sweep and mop hard floors after crumbs, tracked-in dirt and dropped food.

In a private home, the worker picks up toys, books and art supplies into bins, wipes the table, high-chair tray and counters, makes the children's beds and strips and changes crib and bed linens (including after nap-time accidents).

Childcare center classroom and hallway floor care: sweep and vacuum after activities and meals, damp-mop hard floors, in a licensed center with fixed layout, standard furniture and staff-controlled access.

Childcare center non-floor housekeeping: wash and sanitize bottles, sippy cups, plates and mouthed toys; launder cot sheets, bibs, towels and blankets and remake cots; sanitize tables and high chairs after meals.

sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0 model drove a robot to autonomously take laundry out of a dryer and fold garments neatly on a table, recovering from disturbances.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element (laundry folding); the garments (shirts, shorts, towels) are the same class of deformable items a childcare worker folds.

sources.system: DYNA-1 robot foundation model on fixed dual-arm station
sources.title: Dyna Robotics Unveils DYNA-1: The First Commercial-Ready Robot Foundation Model Offering Fully Autonomous, Round-the-Clock Dexterity

sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial linen/napkin folding at a dedicated station. Cot sheets, bibs and towels are the same class of flat textiles handled at a fixtured station; the company reports transfer to laundry folding.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing
sources.claim: Armstrong's dishwashing robots have run live in restaurant dish rooms for about 18 months, operating 24 hours a day and washing over a million dishes a ... autonomously, working with standard commercial dish machines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial dish washing. Plates, cups, glasses and utensils presented at a dish station are the same objects and soils as children's dishes; the reported millimetre-accuracy dish perception matches the precision needed.

sources.claim: SoftBank's Whiz autonomous vacuum has been deployed in K-12 schools, autonomously vacuuming classrooms, libraries and lunchrooms over millions of square feet since deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: custodial floor vacuuming in school classrooms. A childcare classroom is the same class of institution-controlled room with standard furniture; debris and coverage requirements are comparable.

sources.title: Avidbots releases floor-scrubbing robot for industrial spaces
sources.claim: Avidbots' Neo autonomous floor scrubber ... a commercial product with over 1,000 units deployed, used in schools, airports, hospitals and malls to scrub hard floors without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wet scrubbing/mopping of hard floors in institutional buildings including schools, the same operation a center worker performs on classroom and hallway floors.

sources.title: Figure AI's Helix-02 Robots Complete Full 8-Hour Autonomous Shifts as Humanoid Race Intensifies
sources.claim: Figure's Helix-02 drove a humanoid through a full dishwasher cycle in a kitchen - unloading, putting dishes in cabinets, reloading and starting the machine - autonomously, as a staged company demonstration.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element (loading/unloading a dishwasher), but in a staged company kitchen and only four minutes long, so it evidences capability rather than sustained worker-quality service in an as-found home.

sources.title: Figure AI's Helix-02 Robots Complete Full 8-Hour Autonomous Shifts as Humanoid Race Intensifies
sources.claim: Two Figure humanoids autonomously reset a staged bedroom in under two minutes, including hanging clothes, taking out trash and cooperatively making a bed; this is a company demonstration, not a deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tidying a room and making a bed - the closest evidence to changing linens - but it is bed-making in a staged room, not stripping and remaking soiled crib/cot linens, and no reliability data is reported.

sources.title: 1X Neo is a $20,000 home robot that will learn chores via teleoperation
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading shipping home chore robot, relies on human teleoperators to perform household tasks it cannot do autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers the household chores in this task (tidying, linens, surfaces) in real homes; because it is teleoperated it cannot support a positive judgment at E3.

sources.title: Isaac 0 - Weave Robotics
sources.claim: Weave's Isaac 0, a stationary home laundry-folding robot shipping to California customers in 2026, folds household laundry using a mix of autonomy and human teleoperation.
sources.transferJustification: Same task element (folding household laundry in a home), but the vendor states teleoperation is in the loop and the machine only folds - it does not gather, wash, dry or put away.

sources.title: Peanut Robotics | Home
sources.claim: Peanut Robotics fields a commercially deployed mobile manipulator that autonomously cleans and wipes hotel bathroom surfaces around the clock in hotels and corporate buildings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping/disinfecting fixed surfaces in an institution-controlled room. It is the nearest analogue to sanitizing classroom tables, but it targets mapped bathroom fixtures, not food-soiled tables, high chairs and toys.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 controls a mobile manipulator to clean ... homes never seen in training, including wiping a spill and placing dishes in the sink, while still making frequent mistakes.
sources.transferJustification: Directly covers home tidying, spill wiping and dish placement, but the developers state it is far from perfect, so it does not meet the worker-quality bar for these instances.

instances.label: Circle-time read-aloud in a childcare center/preschool room: worker gathers 8-15 toddlers/preschoolers on a rug, holds a picture book up and turns pages so all can see, reads with expression, asks and fields spontaneous questions, redirects children who wander or poke each other, and closes with a transition.

Art/craft activity at a childcare center: worker sets out paint, brushes, paper, glue sticks, crayons and scraps at child-height tables, demonstrates the day's simple project (handprint art, collage, seasonal craft), moves between 6-12 children helping them hold brushes/scissors, prevents paint from going on clothes and walls, labels work and cleans up.

Music/song time at a center: worker leads familiar songs, fingerplays and movement games (e.g., 'Wheels on the Bus'), models the gestures, hands out shakers/rhythm sticks, and gets a group of toddlers/preschoolers to sing and move along.

One-on-one or two-child story session at a center or before/after-school program: a child brings a specific book or the worker picks one, they sit together in a quiet corner, the worker reads it, points at pictures and answers the child's questions.

Nanny or family childcare home: reading stories one-on-one to a child at home during quiet time or bedtime, with the child choosing arbitrary books from the household shelf, sitting in the worker's lap, turning pages and interrupting with questions.

Nanny or family childcare home: drawing/craft time at a kitchen table with one to three children — getting out playdough, markers, safety scissors and glue, showing the child how to make the item, guiding small hands, and clearing the table afterward.

tasks.label: Assist in preparing food and serving meals and refreshments to children.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Licensed childcare center, toddler/preschool classroom (ages 2-5): worker sets low tables, portions family-style lunch or snack from serving bowls onto each child's plate, pours milk/water into small cups, hands plates to seated children, cuts food into safe-sized pieces, gives refills, tracks allergy plates, wipes spills and faces during the meal.

Center kitchen assist: worker helps the center cook on a schedule - washing and cutting fruit and vegetables, spreading/assembling simple items, portioning hot food from pans into serving dishes or individual plates, filling cups, loading classroom carts for delivery.

Infant room: preparing bottles from parent-labeled formula or breast milk (measuring, mixing, warming, testing temperature), preparing pureed/soft foods, spoon-feeding infants in high chairs, burping and cleaning up after each feeding.

Nanny / in-home childcare: preparing a simple lunch or snack in the family's own kitchen (sandwich, pasta, reheated leftovers, cut fruit) using whatever ingredients and equipment the household has, serving it to one or two young children at the kitchen table, helping them eat and cleaning up.

Before/after-school program in a school cafeteria or classroom (ages 5-11): portioning bulk or packaged snacks into cups/napkins, pouring juice or water, distributing to children at tables, opening containers and cartons for them, collecting trash and wiping tables.

sources.claim: Chef Robotics' robots track trays in real time and also place discrete produce items such as oranges, apples ... containers on high-volume lines.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated meal/produce packing. Comparable objects (fruit pieces, scooped foods) and precision to plating children's portions, but only in a purpose-built line environment.

sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline dispenses ingredients into bowls at up to 500 bowls per hour in operating restaurants, but does not do prep work ... finishing touches, which employees still perform.

sources.claim: Figure's Helix 02 completed a four-minute end-to-end autonomous task in a full-sized ... (unloading a dishwasher, stacking items in cabinets, reloading and starting it) with no human intervention.

tasks.label: Regulate children's rest periods.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Licensed childcare center infant room (6 weeks–15 months): worker follows each infant's individual sleep schedule, swaddles/soothes and places each infant on its back in a safety-approved crib, dims lights, performs required visual/physical safety checks every 10–15 minutes with written logs, re-settles infants who stir, and lifts each infant out and re-dresses on waking.

Center toddler/preschool room (~18 months–5 years): after lunch the worker sets out 10–20 cots/mats with each child's sheet and comfort item, dims lights, starts quiet music, walks children through toileting and lying down, rubs/pats backs, keeps non-sleepers quietly on cots with books, wakes the group at the scheduled time, and stacks cots and bedding.

Mid-rest disruptions in a center room: a child cries out or has a nightmare, wets the cot, coughs/vomits or feels feverish, a non-sleeper wanders off the mat or disturbs others; worker responds quietly, changes bedding/clothing, comforts the child, and maintains required staff:child supervision and ratios throughout the rest period.

Nanny or babysitter in a private household with 1–3 children: carries out the family's own nap/bedtime routine in rooms as found (bottle or snack, story, darkened room, sleep sack, crib or toddler bed), stays within earshot, resettles as needed, and wakes the child at the time the parents requested so the schedule holds.

Family childcare home (provider's own residence, mixed ages): infants napping in pack-and-plays or cribs in a converted bedroom/living area while toddlers nap on mats and school-agers do quiet activities nearby, with the provider alone covering all groups and household variability (pets, siblings, deliveries).

School-age or kindergarten quiet/rest period (before-and-after-school program, Head Start, or school aide): 5–20 older children on mats or at desks for a short mandated quiet period; worker enforces quiet, redirects children who will not rest, and transitions the group back to activity.

sources.title: How SNOO Automatically Responds to Your Baby's Cries
sources.claim: SNOO is a motorized, sensor-driven bassinet that autonomously detects an infant's fussing and responds with graduated rocking and white noise to settle the baby back to sleep; it is a commercial product also used in hospital nurseries and NICUs.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: soothing/settling an infant during a rest period is a component of regulating rest periods; cited to show the frontier covers only in-crib rocking and sound, not placement, checks, or group management.

sources.title: How SNOO Automatically Responds to Your Baby's Cries
sources.claim: SNOO's automation is explicitly bounded: when it cannot settle the infant it shuts off and signals that a human caregiver must intervene for feeding, a diaper change, or ... — the machine cannot carry the rest period to completion on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Same task component (settling an infant to rest); establishes the handoff to a human that prevents whole-instance completion.

sources.title: This AI smart crib gently bounces waking babies back to sleep
sources.claim: Cradlewise is a commercially sold smart bassinet/crib that senses early wake-up signs and automatically bounces the infant back to sleep; like SNOO it acts only on an infant already placed inside it, in private homes.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related sub-capability (keeping an infant asleep through a rest period); shows the commercial frontier is a fixed appliance, not a caregiver substitute.

sources.system: Vevo nursery robot / cot sensor system
sources.developer: Global Bridge Holdings with Gunma University
sources.title: Day care facilities test robots as high-tech solution to alleviate staffing shortages
sources.claim: The most advanced reported robot deployment in a nursery school setting (Japan, Global Bridge Holdings/Gunma University) is a greeter robot that identifies children and takes temperatures; naptime safety is handled by passive cot sensors, not by any robot performing the rest-period work.
sources.transferJustification: Closest existing robot presence in the exact setting (nursery naptime); demonstrates that no robot performs the physical rest-period work even in a purpose-fitted nursery.

sources.title: The strong robot with the gentle touch
sources.claim: Robotic lifting and transfer of a human body remains an experimental laboratory prototype (ROBEAR, RIKEN/Sumitomo Riko), sized for adult patients and never commercialized; no fielded robot lifts a child into or out of a crib or cot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and transferring a person to/from a bed, the physical analogue of placing a child in a crib or onto a cot. It does not transfer: ROBEAR is a caregiver-operated lab prototype sized for cooperative adults, not autonomous handling of infants.

sources.system: Toyota HSR and Fetch bed-making system (Berkeley AUTOLAB)
sources.title: Deep Transfer Learning of Pick Points on Fabric for Robot Bed-Making
sources.claim: Autonomous robotic manipulation of bedding (grasping and pulling a blanket to cover a bed) has been demonstrated only in laboratory experiments with mobile manipulators on a fixed bed frame, with coverage-based success metrics far below caregiver standards.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: laying out sheets/blankets, the closest published analogue to setting out and making up nap cots. It does not transfer: the experiments are single-bed lab setups with no children present, no cot transport or stacking, and no supervision component.

tasks.label: Organize and participate in recreational activities and outings, such as games and field trips.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Childcare center classroom: worker sets out materials and leads a structured indoor recreational activity (circle-time game, music/movement, board or card game, craft) for a group of roughly 8-15 preschoolers, keeping all engaged, mediating turn-taking disputes, adapting the game when it falls flat, then leading cleanup.

Center's fenced outdoor playground or gym: worker organizes and joins gross-motor play (tag, ball games, obstacle course), pushes swings, retrieves equipment, scans continuously for hazards, intervenes in rough play, comforts and treats scraped knees, and lines children up to return indoors.

Off-site outing: worker walks a group to a neighborhood park or library, or rides a bus to a zoo/museum, handling headcounts, street crossings, restroom stops, keeping children with partners in public crowds, and running the activity at the destination.

Nanny in a private home: worker plans and runs the day's play for one to three children (indoor games, backyard water play, crafts), takes them to a nearby playground or playdate, supervises continuously, and manages snacks, conflicts, and cleanup.

Before/after-school or day-camp program in a school gym, cafeteria, or multipurpose room: worker organizes team games and rotating activity stations for a mixed-age group of school-age children, sets rules, referees, and keeps non-participants occupied.

sources.title: Toddlers show increased physical activity with a robot playmate moving around the room
sources.claim: GoBot, a low-cost mobile play robot, engaged toddlers in keep-away play in a university play room; one experimental condition ran an autonomous routine that raised children's activity levels about as much as direct teleoperation, with adults present throughout.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-toddler active play. It shows a robot can autonomously sustain a simple chase game with a single child in a controlled play room, but not organize an activity for a group, handle materials and cleanup, or carry safety-supervision responsibility, so it does not transfer to whole-instance completion.

sources.system: Social robots in education (206 deployments, 43 models incl. NAO, Pepper)
sources.title: Social robots for education: a global analysis of deployments in real scenarios
sources.claim: A global review of 206 real-world social-robot deployments in kindergartens and schools found their roles are edutainment and entertainment segments used as tools alongside teaching staff, not independent leadership or supervision of children's activity time.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led educational play in classrooms. Even in institution-controlled kindergartens, deployed robots run discrete game or story segments with staff present; none is documented running and supervising a group recreational period end to end.

sources.developer: Global Bridge Holdings with Gunma University
sources.title: Japan company testing robots to counter childcare shortage
sources.claim: Childcare-specific robots actually placed in nursery schools perform greeting, child identification, and health monitoring rather than organizing or leading recreational activities.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: The leading consumer home humanoid relies on remote human operators for anything beyond narrow routines; trade press reports no humanoid has been shown completing an ordinary household task end to end autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household work by a home humanoid. It bounds what a mobile robot can do unsupervised in a private home, the setting of the nanny instance; if simple object-handling chores still need teleoperation, running and supervising children's play there is not substantiated.

sources.title: Using the Humanoid Robot KASPAR to Autonomously Play Triadic Games and Facilitate Collaborative Play Among Children With Autism
sources.claim: The KASPAR humanoid has been used in schools for short turn-taking and imitation game sessions with small numbers of children, always as an adult-facilitated intervention tool.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-mediated turn-taking games with children in schools. Sessions are brief, involve one or two children with an adult facilitator, and do not include setup, group management, or safety supervision, so they do not carry over to leading a group activity period.

tasks.label: Sterilize bottles and prepare formulas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Licensed childcare center infant room: at each feeding the worker takes the child's parent-supplied formula (powder, concentrate, or ready-to-feed) and a clean bottle, measures water and scoops per the parent's written instruction, mixes, warms to feeding temperature, checks it, and labels the bottle with the child's name and time. Several infants, different formulas and volumes, on demand, at a small prep counter.

Center-based end-of-use bottle care: collecting used bottles, disassembling nipples, rings, caps and anti-colic valves, rinsing and brush-washing at a sink or running them through a dishwasher/sanitize cycle, air-drying on a rack, reassembling and returning each set to the right child's cubby or bag, per state licensing sanitation rules.

Nanny in a private home: sterilizing bottles, nipples and pump parts (electric steam sterilizer, boiling water, or dishwasher sanitize cycle), then preparing a day's worth of formula bottles with the family's chosen water, refrigerating them, and warming one at feed time in a home kitchen shared with family activity.

Family childcare provider working out of her own home with two or three infants: mixing formula for each child to different recipes in an ordinary kitchen while supervising other children, washing bottles between feeds at the household sink, storing them in the family refrigerator.

Special-instruction preparation: newborn/preemie or medically directed feeds requiring exact measurement, added cereal/thickener or supplements, boiled-and-cooled water, or sterilizing every part before each use, prepared to a pediatrician's written directions in a center or a home.
