sources.developer: Erasmus MC, Erasmus University Rotterdam and RoboHouse (TU Delft)
sources.title: Breast milk robot aims to free up nurses' time | ICT&health
sources.claim: A milk-preparation robot at Erasmus MC Sophia Children's Hospital automatically processes prescribed feed quantities, adds fortifiers, and prepares individual feeds for neonatal patients; the third prototype under test prepares feeds for ten patients over 48 hours.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing prescribed infant feeds (expressed milk plus fortifier) in a hospital milk room. Same objects (infant bottles/syringes, powdered supplements) and tighter dosing tolerance than childcare formula mixing; it is an enclosed purpose-built machine and still a tested prototype, not in service.

sources.title: Armstrong Robotics wants to create general purpose kitchen robots, starting with dishwashing - The Robot Report
sources.claim: An autonomous dishwashing robot works in restaurant dish rooms, picking dirty plates, cups and silverware from bus tubs, loading racks and running the dish machine around the clock without on-site babysitting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: commercial dishwashing in a human kitchen. It marks the E2 frontier but covers only plates, cups, silverware and racks; no evidence of disassembling bottles into nipples, rings and valves, verifying sanitation, or measuring and mixing per-child formula, so it cannot complete this task's whole instance.

sources.system: π0.5 on a mobile bimanual manipulator
sources.title: π0.5: a Vision-Language-Action Model with Open-World Generalization (arXiv:2504.16054)
sources.claim: A vision-language-action model drives a mobile manipulator to clean ... homes not seen in training, performing multi-stage manipulation such as clearing dishes into a sink.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying and dish clearing in unstructured homes. It marks the E3 frontier: research-grade success on coarse tidying, well short of the reliability and food-safety precision needed to sterilize bottles and mix an infant's formula unattended.

tasks.label: Help children with homework and school work.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Provide care for children with physical, developmental, or mental health disabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Licensed childcare center / preschool classroom: a childcare worker includes a 3-5 year old with autism or global developmental delay in the daily routine - shadowing during free play and circle time, running a visual schedule and picture/AAC communication, redirecting hitting or elopement, de-escalating a sensory meltdown, and keeping the child and peers safe while the rest of the group continues.

Center or school-based personal care for a child with a physical disability (cerebral palsy, spina bifida): diapering/toileting on a changing table, undressing and redressing over braces, lifting and transferring between wheelchair, floor mat, stander and toilet, repositioning for comfort, and managing skin and hygiene while adapting to the child's tone, spasms and resistance.

Mealtime and health-procedure support in the center: positioning a child who cannot self-feed, spoon-feeding pureed food and thickened liquids, watching for choking or aspiration, wiping face and hands, giving prescribed medication or a rescue plan step per the child's health care plan, and documenting intake for the family.

In-home care (nanny or family childcare provider) for a child with disabilities across a full day in a private house: play and comfort, meals, toileting, running therapist-assigned home-program exercises with adaptive equipment, handling siblings, pets, clutter and unplanned events such as a seizure or a behavioral crisis.

Outdoor and community settings: supervising a child with a disability on the playground, on neighborhood walks and field trips, loading and securing a wheelchair on a bus, pushing an adaptive stroller over uneven ground, and preventing elopement into traffic or crowds.

One-on-one structured skill session at a table in a quiet room of the center, implementing the plan written by a speech therapist or behavior analyst: turn-taking, emotion recognition, requesting practice, with prompting, reinforcement and data collection, plus handling the child's toileting or regulation needs that interrupt the session.

sources.title: Robots4Autism + STEM: Milo, Veda, and Carver from RoboKind
sources.claim: RoboKind's Milo is a commercially deployed social robot used in US special-education classrooms for autism social-skills lessons, but it functions as an extra instructional tool used by an educator or therapist who remains with the student; it performs no caregiving.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered social-skills instruction for children with developmental disabilities. It is the closest deployed system to this task, but it covers only a lesson-delivery sub-step and runs with an adult facilitator present, so it does not transfer to whole-instance care.

sources.developer: Multiple (academic review, ACM Transactions on Human-Robot Interaction)
sources.title: Utilizing Human-Robot Interaction in Autism Therapy to Enhance Children's Social Skills: Literature Review
sources.claim: A 2026 peer-reviewed review of robot-assisted autism therapy reports that robots in these interactions are commonly remote-controlled by a human (Wizard of Oz) to simulate autonomy, and that therapists need interfaces to control the robot during sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: therapeutic/social interaction with children with developmental disabilities. Establishes that the state of the art in this closest area is human-operated rather than autonomous, so it cannot substantiate autonomous completion of care instances.

sources.title: QTrobot for special needs education - LuxAI S.A.
sources.claim: QTrobot is a commercial humanoid sold for special-needs education and autism therapy; it delivers curriculum content but is explicitly a tool operated by parents, teachers or therapists rather than an autonomous caregiver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: structured skill teaching for children with developmental disabilities. Shows the deployed capability is adult-operated lesson delivery, not the supervision, physical care and safety responsibility the childcare task requires.

sources.title: Obi Robotic Feeding Device | School Health
sources.claim: Obi, a commercially sold robotic feeding device used by children and adults with disabilities at home and school, moves a spoon to the user's mouth only on the user's switch commands, and a caregiver still loads the bowls, positions the device and assists during the meal.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisted feeding of a person who cannot self-feed. It substitutes for the spoon-to-mouth motion only, requires the child to operate switches, and does not cover positioning, drinks, choking monitoring, cleanup or documentation, so it does not complete the mealtime instance.

sources.system: Wheelchair-mounted robot-assisted feeding system (Cornell EmPRISE and collaborators)
sources.developer: Cornell University EmPRISE Lab and collaborators
sources.title: Lessons Learned from Designing and Evaluating a Robot-assisted Feeding System for Out-of-lab Use
sources.claim: Research robot-assisted feeding systems evaluated out-of-lab with adults with motor impairments still rely on user-in-the-loop bite selection and caregiver setup, and long-term real-world deployment of physical caregiving robots remains unachieved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: feeding a person who cannot self-feed. Demonstrated with cooperative adults choosing their own bites; it does not transfer to feeding an uncooperative or medically fragile young child with aspiration risk.

sources.title: RABBIT: A Robot-Assisted Bed Bathing System with Multimodal Perception and Integrated Compliance
sources.claim: The most advanced robotic personal-hygiene demonstration is a laboratory system that autonomously washed, rinsed and dried a single forearm of an adult with mobility limitations; nothing comparable exists for diapering, dressing or bathing a moving child.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot performing an intimate personal-care ADL. Shows the frontier is a single limb of a stationary consenting adult in a lab, far short of toileting, dressing and transferring a squirming child.

sources.title: Japan's teddy bear nurse robot gets a softer touch | PCWorld
sources.claim: Robear, the best-known patient-lifting caregiving robot, was a research prototype for transferring adults between bed and wheelchair and was never deployed in care settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting and transferring a dependent person. Even for cooperative adults it remained a lab prototype, so it cannot substantiate transferring or repositioning a child with cerebral palsy.

sources.title: 1X's $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the 'Creepy' Factor
sources.claim: The first general-purpose humanoid aimed at private homes, 1X's NEO, began shipping to US households in 2026 with its first wave partly run by human teleoperators rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household physical work in a private home, the setting of the in-home childcare instance. Teleoperated operation cannot support a positive judgment, and no child-supervision capability is claimed.

sources.title: Mobility challenges in kiddos can be addressed with Trexo Plus
sources.claim: Trexo Plus is a commercial pediatric robotic gait trainer used in clinics, schools and homes that powers a child's legs through a walking pattern, but an adult must fit the child into the device and supervise the session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: physical mobility support for children with disabilities. It is a wearable device the caregiver straps the child into and steers; it automates leg motion only and performs no supervisory or personal-care step of the instance.

tasks.label: Perform general personnel functions, such as supervision, training, and scheduling.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Accompany children to and from school, on outings, and to medical appointments.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Walking a small group of preschool/school-age children between a childcare center or home and the school or a nearby park: lining them up, holding hands or a walking rope, crossing streets, keeping headcounts, managing a child who bolts, lags, or melts down, in rain, cold, or heat on public sidewalks.

Driving children by car or center van to school, after-school activities, or an appointment: buckling toddlers into car seats and older children into boosters, loading bags/strollers, driving public streets, unloading at curbside, and walking each child to the door and handing off to an authorized adult.

Accompanying one child to a medical or dental appointment: travel to the clinic, checking in at the front desk, waiting-room supervision, staying with the child during the exam, comforting/holding a frightened child, then returning the child and reporting to the parent.

Chaperoning an outing or field trip (bus or walking trip to a zoo, museum, library, or park): keeping an assigned group together in crowds, restroom trips, snacks and spills, first aid for scrapes, and repeated headcounts before boarding back.

Escorting children within institutional premises: walking a class from classroom to gym/cafeteria, taking children out to the school bus loading zone or the pickup line at a childcare center, and releasing each child only to a verified adult.

sources.title: Waymo teen accounts offer peace of mind for Phoenix families
sources.claim: Waymo's fully driverless ride-hailing service added teen accounts (ages 14-17) in Metro Phoenix, letting teens ride alone with remote human Rider Support; it conveys teens but provides no in-vehicle caregiver, no car-seat securing, and no door-to-door escort or supervision of young children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous passenger transport. It covers only the driving leg for teenagers; the childcare task requires an accompanying caregiver who secures young children in car seats, walks them in, and supervises them, none of which the vehicle performs, so it does not substantiate completion of any instance.

sources.system: Autonomous vehicles used for student commutes (Waymo)
sources.title: Autonomous Vehicles Aren't Built for Student Transportation [Op-Ed] | School Bus Fleet
sources.claim: Trade press (Feb 2026) reviewing parents' use of driverless cars for school commutes states that most states bar minors from riding in AVs ... and that AV technology lacks the human judgment student transportation requires — i.e., no deployed AV performs the accompaniment/duty-of-care role.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driving students to school. Establishes that the closest commercial autonomous systems provide conveyance only and are not accepted as substitutes for a supervising adult, so the driving instance is not completed at worker quality.

sources.system: Incheon International Airport guide robots (LG CLOi GuideBot)
sources.title: Airports of the Future Will Be Run By Robots and AI - Newsweek
sources.claim: Autonomous guide robots deployed in airports escort passengers to gates or restaurants inside a controlled terminal — the nearest deployed 'escorting a person through a facility' capability, but for self-directed adults, with no physical care, restraint, or responsibility for a child's safety.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting a person through a structured facility. It does not transfer: guiding a compliant adult who follows the robot differs from accompanying young children, who require hand-holding, physical intervention when they bolt, comforting, toileting, and verified handoff to an authorized adult.

sources.system: Social robot in inclusive daycare (long-term ethnographic study)
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology / Ulm University research groups (Rixen et al.)
sources.title: Long-Term Integration of a Robot in an Inclusive Daycare: An Ethnographic Study Focused on Children and Caregivers (ACM/IEEE HRI)
sources.claim: Robots studied in daycare settings are social/interaction robots evaluated in ethnographic and HRI studies; the literature describes mediating interaction with children, not taking custody of children or escorting them off premises.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robots operating among young children in a childcare facility. Research-stage social robots mediate interaction under caregiver presence; they do not supervise or transport children, so they cannot substantiate completion of the accompaniment task.

roles.title: Nannies
roles.description: Care for children in private households and provide support and expertise to parents in satisfying children's physical, emotional, intellectual, and social needs. Duties may include meal planning and preparation, laundry and clothing care, organization of play activities and outings, discipline, intellectual stimulation, language activities, and transportation.

tasks.label: Instruct children in safe behavior, such as seeking adult assistance when crossing the street and avoiding contact with unsafe objects.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Remove hazards and develop appropriate boundaries and rules to create a safe environment for children.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ongoing hazard sweep of the family's living and play areas while children are awake and mobile: scanning rooms as the child moves, picking up coins, beads, small toy parts, button batteries and plastic bags off floors and low tables, moving hot drinks, knives, purses and cleaning bottles out of reach, closing doors, latching stair gates. Private home, layout and contents differ family to family, children and pets present.

Hazard control embedded in kitchen, bath and sleep routines: turning pot handles inward and keeping hot liquids and cords back from counter edges while cooking with a toddler underfoot, testing bath water temperature and never leaving the child unattended in the tub, clearing the crib of blankets and soft toys, keeping medications and vitamins secured. Private home.

Periodic childproofing setup as the child develops or the family moves: installing safety gates at stairs, cabinet and drawer latches, outlet covers and toilet locks; anchoring dressers and TVs to walls; tying up blind cords; checking smoke/CO alarms; reporting remaining hazards to parents. Requires tools, drilling and fitting to the particular house.

Outings and outdoor play: inspecting the yard or neighborhood playground before play for broken glass, dog waste, standing water, an unlatched pool or yard gate, tools or a hot grill; setting physical boundaries at the park; correctly buckling car seats; keeping children clear of streets and driveways. Public and semi-public outdoor settings taken as found.

Setting, communicating and enforcing rules and boundaries with the children: stating no-go zones and safety rules at the child's level, redirecting a toddler climbing on furniture or reaching for a stove, physically intercepting a child heading toward a street or pool, applying consistent consequences, and coordinating the rules with parents. Private home and outings.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (pi0.5)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 VLA autonomously drove mobile manipulators to tidy kitchens and bedrooms (dishes in the sink, clothes in a basket, items off the bedroom floor) in real homes not seen in training, but the developers report frequent semantic and motor errors; it is a research demonstration, not a deployed product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: household tidying and putting objects away in unstructured homes. It is the closest demonstrated analogue to clearing floor and surface hazards in a private home, so its error rate and absence of any child-hazard judgment bound what is achievable on this task at E3.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading consumer household robot, relies on human teleoperators ('Expert Mode') for chores it cannot do; trade press reports no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore end to end autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household chores in private homes. Establishes that the best-funded home humanoid still needs continuous human control for home manipulation, so it cannot support autonomous hazard removal in a home.

sources.title: Figure 03 Is The Robot in Your Kitchen
sources.claim: Figure's home humanoid, Figure 03 with Helix, is marketed for household tasks but as of April 2026 was going only to selected partners for testing, with the CEO stating full autonomous home operation has not been achieved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous household manipulation. Shows that home-directed humanoids remain in partner testing rather than delivering worker-quality household work.

sources.title: iRobot Roomba j7+ review: Tops in obstacle avoidance, cleaning power
sources.claim: The most widely deployed autonomous home robots, camera-equipped robot vacuums, are designed to identify and steer around floor objects such as cords, socks, shoes and pet waste rather than pick them up; the user must clear objects first.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation on home floors. Demonstrates that mass-deployed home robots avoid, rather than remove, exactly the small objects that constitute child hazards.

sources.title: AI-Powered Robot by Boston Dynamics and Toyota Research Institute Takes a Key Step Towards General-Purpose Humanoids
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous humanoid whole-body manipulation (Atlas with a Large Behavior Model) was demonstrated on structured part-sequencing work with known parts and bins, not on open-ended safety work around people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mobile manipulation of varied objects. Marks the frontier of humanoid autonomy and shows it is demonstrated in structured, staged industrial settings with known parts, not in child-occupied living space.

tasks.label: Perform first aid or cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) when required.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Minor wound care in the private home: a toddler or young child falls and gets a scraped knee, small cut, or grazed palm. The nanny comforts the crying, squirming child, inspects the wound, rinses it, applies antiseptic and an adhesive bandage from the family's supplies, and monitors afterward. Household layout, supplies and child cooperation vary.

Bumps, bruises, minor burns and head knocks at home: child bangs head on furniture or touches a hot pan; nanny assesses for concussion or serious burn signs, runs cool water or applies a wrapped ice pack, holds it on a resisting child, soothes, reports to parents, and escalates if red-flag signs appear.

First aid away from the home - playground, park, sidewalk, pool, car: splinter, bee sting, nosebleed, scraped elbow on pavement, grit in a wound. Improvised supplies from a diaper bag, other children present, weather and bystanders uncontrolled, child upset and mobile.

Acute non-arrest emergency: infant or toddler choking (back blows and chest thrusts, or abdominal thrusts for an older child), anaphylaxis requiring an epinephrine auto-injector to the thigh, an asthma attack requiring inhaler and spacer, or a febrile seizure requiring positioning and protection - while calling 911 and the parents.

Full pediatric CPR: nanny finds an infant or child unresponsive and not breathing normally (drowning, progressed choking, cardiac event), checks responsiveness and breathing, calls 911 on speaker, opens the airway, gives rescue breaths and two-finger or one-hand compressions on a firm surface until EMS arrives.

sources.title: LUCAS 3, v3.1 chest compression system Instructor guidebook
sources.claim: The LUCAS 3 mechanical chest compression system delivers automated external compressions in EMS and hospital settings, but it is manually carried, positioned and started by a trained rescuer and is indicated only for adult patients in cardiac arrest, not infants or children.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical CPR on adults. It does not transfer to the nanny CPR instance - the device is indicated only for adults, must be carried and placed on the patient by a human rescuer, and performs no assessment, airway management or rescue breathing.

sources.developer: Seoul National University Hospital research group (Kim, Suh et al.)
sources.title: Development of artificial intelligence-driven biosignal-sensitive cardiopulmonary resuscitation robot - PubMed
sources.claim: An AI-driven, biosignal-guided CPR robot has been shown feasible only as a laboratory proof of concept in anesthetized pigs, benchmarked against a LUCAS 3, with the device set up on the instrumented animal by researchers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated chest compressions. Does not transfer: the subject is an anesthetized, instrumented adult-sized pig in a laboratory, the robot is positioned by humans, and no pediatric patient, arrest recognition or ventilation is involved.

sources.system: Autonomous tape-handling framework for robotic wound redressing
sources.developer: UC San Diego (Yip lab) with Cornell
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing (arXiv:2510.06127)
sources.claim: State-of-the-art robotic wound-care automation is at the level of autonomous tape detachment and placement sub-steps evaluated on phantoms and anatomical models; clinical wound care itself remains a manual clinician task.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying adhesive dressings to skin, the closest analogue to bandaging a child's scrape. It does not substantiate the instance: only tape sub-steps on static phantoms and models, with no wound assessment, no cleaning, and no moving, distressed child.

sources.system: 6-DoF anthropomorphic robot arm bandaging system with force feedback
sources.title: Force Feedback Algorithm for Robot Arm to Bandage A Swaying Arm - IEEE Xplore
sources.claim: Robotic bandaging of a human limb remains a laboratory control-research problem: a force-control method was proposed for a 6-DoF anthropomorphic arm to follow a swaying injured arm while bandaging.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wrapping a bandage on a human limb. It is a control-algorithm study of a compliant arm-following sub-problem, not a demonstrated end-to-end first-aid episode at caregiver quality.

sources.system: Teleoperated humanoid robots performing medical tasks (mannequin experiments)
sources.developer: academic groups, as reported in arXiv paper on humanoids in surgery
sources.title: Humanoid Robots as First Assistants in Endoscopic Surgery (arXiv:2602.24156)
sources.claim: Humanoid robot demonstrations of emergency medical interventions such as bag-valve-mask ventilation and physical examination have been performed on mannequins under teleoperation rather than autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-delivered emergency care. It shows the closest humanoid emergency-care demonstrations are teleoperated on mannequins, so they cannot support autonomous completion of first aid on a child at any tier.

tasks.label: Instruct and assist children in the development of health and personal habits, such as eating, resting, and toilet behavior.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Toileting in a private home: changing a squirming toddler's diaper on a changing table or floor, or taking a potty-training 2-3 year old to the bathroom, pulling down clothing, seating them, wiping, flushing, re-dressing, washing hands, praising, and cleaning up accidents on the child, clothing, and floor.

Mealtime in a private home: strapping an infant/toddler into a high chair or booster, serving age-appropriate portions, spoon-feeding a moving infant, coaching cup and utensil use, encouraging a reluctant eater to try foods, watching for choking, wiping face and hands, and cleaning the tray/floor.

Nap and bedtime routine in a private home: recognizing sleep cues, changing diaper and pajamas/sleep sack, swaddling or rocking an infant, carrying and laying the child in a crib or bed, story and lights, monitoring, and re-settling mid-nap wakeups.

Grooming and hygiene in a private home: bathing a young child, brushing teeth, wiping noses, combing hair, dressing/undressing, teaching handwashing steps at the sink, while keeping the child safe around water and steps.

Coaching a largely self-sufficient school-age child in a private home: verbal reminders and routines for handwashing before meals, toothbrushing, drinking water, healthy snack choices, quiet rest time and bedtime, using charts, praise, and follow-up checks for compliance.

Away from home (playground, playdate, store, restaurant, car): taking a child to an unfamiliar public restroom, managing a snack away from home, hand sanitizing, and getting a tired child to rest in a stroller or car seat.

sources.system: ADA / robot-assisted feeding system (University of Washington Personal Robotics Lab, with Cornell EmPRISE)
sources.title: Real-World Trials: UW's Assistive Feeding Robot Tested Beyond the Lab
sources.claim: Research assistive feeding arms can autonomously acquire and deliver a bite of food to an adult with motor impairments after the user selects the bite through an interface; tested outside the lab with care recipients.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assisted eating. It does NOT transfer to this task: the system serves a cooperative adult who holds still and directs each bite through an assistive interface on a wheelchair-mounted arm, whereas a nanny must seat and restrain a moving infant/toddler, judge portions and choking risk, coach utensil use, respond to refusal, and clean up.

sources.developer: Waseda University (Shigeki Sugano lab) and partners
sources.title: Japan tests AIREC robot to roll patients, easing caregiving challenges
sources.claim: A humanoid care robot in Japan is in testing and has demonstrated rolling a lying adult onto his side, a precursor motion for diaper changing; it is not deployed in care work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: personal-care body handling (repositioning for diaper change). It does not substantiate the nanny instance: the demonstration is a single assisted motion on a cooperative, stationary adult in a lab test, not autonomous diapering, wiping, or toilet-training a mobile toddler.

sources.title: Happiest Baby SNOO Smart Sleeper Bassinet + Reviews | Crate & Kids
sources.claim: A commercially sold responsive bassinet autonomously detects infant fussing and responds with rocking and white noise to keep the baby asleep in private homes, but does not handle, swaddle, lift, or place the infant.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soothing an infant during rest. It covers only the in-crib soothing sub-step of the nap instance and only for infants 0-6 months; it cannot change the child, carry or lay the child down, or manage an older child's rest routine.

sources.developer: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham (AmmachiLabs) with University of Glasgow
sources.title: Enhancing Hand Hygiene Practices Through a Social Robot-Assisted Intervention in a Rural School in India
sources.claim: Social robots that promote children's handwashing habits have been piloted in schools, but the deployments are research pilots and the earlier robot sessions were Wizard-of-Oz controlled; only perception components have been made autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instructing children in a health habit. Instruction is only part of this task, which also requires physically assisting the child; the robot does not assist at the sink, and the pilots are Wizard-of-Oz research interventions rather than autonomous, worker-quality supervision.

sources.developer: Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham / University of Glasgow researchers
sources.title: Handwashing Action Detection System for an Autonomous Social Robot
sources.claim: Work on an autonomous social robot for handwashing coaching reports a perception module for recognizing handwashing steps; earlier behavioral results came from Wizard-of-Oz (human-controlled) robot studies.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hygiene coaching for children. Only a vision component is autonomous; no end-to-end autonomous system is shown assisting or supervising children's hygiene routines.

sources.title: 1X NEO Home Robot Review: Price, Features & Capabilities 2026
sources.claim: The leading consumer home humanoid shipping to US homes relies on scheduled human teleoperation for anything beyond a small set of simple tasks, so household caregiving-style work is not autonomous.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household assistance in private homes. Teleoperated operation cannot support a positive judgment, and 1X does not offer child personal-care as a capability.

sources.title: Xiaoban (Smart Toilet Robot) - Baidu Baike
sources.claim: A self-driving toilet robot for disabled and semi-disabled adults debuted at a Chinese aged-care expo in 2026; it is an adult continence-care device with no confirmed release outside China.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: toileting assistance. It does not transfer: the device serves a cooperative adult transferring onto a self-cleaning commode, not the diapering, wiping, dressing, coaching, and accident cleanup a nanny performs with a toddler.

tasks.label: Regulate children's rest periods and nap schedules.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Young infant (0-6 months) nap in the family home: nanny reads wake-window/sleep cues, does the pre-nap routine (diaper, feed, swaddle/sleep sack), carries the baby to the nursery, lays them in the crib or bassinet, soothes to sleep, monitors, resettles brief wakings, then ends the nap on schedule and lifts the baby out.

Older infant/toddler (6 months-3 years) nap in the home: transition the child out of play, pre-nap routine (books, cup, diaper, sleep sack), place in crib or toddler bed, manage protest, stalling or climbing out, keep the room quiet, monitor, then wake/retrieve and re-orient a groggy child.

Preschool/school-age (3-6+ years) quiet rest time at home after lunch or after school: settle the child on a bed, mat or couch, read or play soft music, enforce quiet without a forced sleep, keep siblings from disrupting, and end rest at the right time to protect bedtime.

Nap away from the nursery: child falls asleep in a stroller, carrier or car seat during errands, a park visit or a playgroup; nanny protects the sleep (shade, noise, timing the route), decides when to head home, and transfers the sleeping child indoors to a bed without waking them.

Two or more children with staggered or shifting schedules, plus disruptions (teething, illness, travel, dropping from two naps to one): nanny adjusts the day's timing, settles whichever child needs it while supervising the other, and logs/reports naps to parents.

sources.title: How SNOO Automatically Responds to Your Baby's Cries
sources.claim: SNOO is a commercially sold responsive bassinet whose onboard microphones detect infant fussing and autonomously escalate rocking motion and white noise to calm the baby back to sleep, without a caregiver intervening.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: soothing an infant to sleep and maintaining the nap. This is the core physical act of the nanny's infant rest-period instance once the baby is in the crib — same object (a swaddled infant), same required output (a settled, sleeping baby), same fixed sleep surface.

sources.title: SNOO in Hospitals and Healthcare - Happiest Baby
sources.claim: SNOO responsive bassinets are deployed in hundreds of US hospitals (postpartum units and NICUs), where clinicians report the device handles infant soothing and saves roughly 2 hours of staff time per shift.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: institutional infant sleep soothing. It shows the responsive-bassinet function is accepted as substituting for caregiver soothing at professional quality, but nurses still swaddle, place and remove each infant.

sources.title: This AI smart crib gently bounces waking babies back to sleep - Engadget
sources.claim: The Cradlewise smart crib learns an individual child's sleep patterns, senses the onset of waking from its built-in monitor, and automatically bounces to return the child to sleep, stopping when the child settles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: extending and protecting an infant's nap. Pattern learning plus pre-emptive soothing is the schedule-regulating portion of the nanny's infant nap instance, performed on the same fixed crib surface.

sources.title: 1X NEO Home Robot Review: Price, Features & Capabilities 2026
sources.claim: The only humanoid robot marketed for private homes as of 2026, 1X's NEO, performs only basic navigation, door opening and object retrieval autonomously; multi-step household tasks are executed by a remote human teleoperator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general in-home mobile manipulation. It bounds what any home robot can do autonomously — no cited system carries, places, or physically settles a child — so it cannot support positive judgments for the mobile, child-handling instances.

tasks.label: Teach and perform age-appropriate activities, such as lap play, reading, and arts and crafts, to encourage intellectual development of children.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Infant/young-toddler lap play in the family home: nanny holds the baby on her lap or floor mat, does peekaboo, songs with hand motions, tummy time, rattles, stacking cups and cloth/board books, positioning and steadying the child, responding to fussing, and keeping the child safe through a 20-40 minute play block.

Reading aloud to a toddler or preschooler in the home: nanny picks books off a shelf, sits the child on her lap or beside her, holds and turns pages, points to pictures, asks dialogic questions, re-reads on demand, and manages a wriggling child, snacks and interruptions before transitioning to the next activity.

Arts and crafts at the kitchen table or playroom floor: nanny fetches and sets out paper, crayons, paint, glue, safety scissors, playdough or seasonal craft kits, demonstrates the technique, hands materials over, guides small hands, keeps paint off furniture and out of mouths, praises the work, then cleans up child, table and floor.

Manipulative educational play with a preschool/early-elementary child at home: puzzles, block and magnet-tile building, letter and number cards, sorting and counting games, simple kitchen science experiments, reading practice — nanny sets out and handles the physical materials, models the activity, corrects, and adapts difficulty to the child.

Purely verbal enrichment session with a school-age child (no materials the adult must handle): make-up storytelling turn-taking, word and rhyming games, twenty questions, quizzing vocabulary or times tables while the child sits at a table, roughly 10-20 minutes.

Educational outing away from the home: library storytime, children's museum exhibit, nature walk in a park or zoo trip — nanny explains exhibits, asks questions, runs a scavenger hunt or leaf-collecting activity, carries the gear, and supervises the child among strangers, traffic and crowds.

sources.system: Furhat robot with fine-tuned GPT-3 storytelling models (CreativeBot)

sources.title: Fostering children's creativity through LLM-driven storytelling with a social robot (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led collaborative storytelling / verbal creativity activity with children. It transfers only to the purely verbal enrichment slice of the nanny task — same age group, same turn-taking story activity — and not to instances requiring handling books, craft materials or the child, which this head-and-torso robot cannot do.

sources.title: Robot teachers invade Chinese kindergartens (Phys.org / AFP)
sources.claim: The Keeko robot, a small autonomous wheeled robot, was deployed in Chinese kindergartens telling stories and posing logic problems to children alongside human teachers; it is armless and manipulates nothing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: delivering story and logic-game activities to young children in an institutional childcare facility (E2). It substantiates verbal activity delivery only; being armless, it cannot perform lap play, book handling, crafts or manipulative play, and teachers remain present for care and safety.

sources.title: Maker of AI robots for kids abruptly shutters (Axios)
sources.claim: Moxie, the main commercially sold home social robot that ran daily reading exercises and guided conversations with children aged 5-10, stopped functioning when Embodied shut down in December 2024; even in service it had only rudimentary arms and manipulated no objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-home child enrichment activities. Cited to establish that the frontier of home child-activity robots is a screen-faced conversational device performing no physical manipulation, and that even that product is no longer operable.

sources.title: 1X's $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the 'Creepy' Factor (eWeek)
sources.claim: The leading humanoid intended for private homes, 1X NEO, began shipping to US households in 2026 with its first wave partly controlled by human teleoperators rather than acting autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household manipulation in private homes. Cited to show that the only home humanoid that could in principle handle books or craft materials operates under teleoperation, so it cannot support a positive judgment for craft setup, page turning or child-directed play.

tasks.label: Help prepare and serve nutritionally balanced meals and snacks for children.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-afternoon snack in the family's own kitchen: nanny checks what's on hand, washes and cuts fruit, adds crackers/cheese/yogurt, pours water or milk into the child's cup, works around the family's allergy rules and preferences, carries it to the table or counter, and wipes up afterward.

Simple lunch or supper for one to three children: grilled cheese, quesadilla, pasta, or reheated leftovers plus a fruit and a vegetable side, cooked on the family's stove/microwave, cut into child-safe pieces, portioned onto the children's plates and served at the kitchen table.

Cooking a fuller dinner from scratch in the employer's kitchen, often per parents' instructions or a family meal plan: multiple components (protein, starch, vegetable) with oven and stovetop timing, using whatever is in the fridge and pantry, then plating and serving to children and sometimes the returning parents.

Infant/toddler feeding: preparing and warming formula bottles or expressed milk, making or warming purees and soft finger foods, cutting to safe sizes, feeding the baby by bottle or spoon in arms or a high chair, then washing and sterilizing bottles and feeding gear.

Packing food to go: assembling a school or daycare lunchbox and outing snacks in the home kitchen — sandwich, cut produce, containers, ice pack, drink bottle — matching the school's allergy/nut policy and the child's likes.

sources.title: Introducing Chef+: Chef's Most Advanced Meal Assembly Robot Yet
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' AI-driven meal-assembly robots portion and assemble complete meal trays (protein, starch, vegetables) to spec on food-production lines, with over 80 million servings produced in commercial production.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial meal assembly. Transfer: the objects (cooked proteins, grains, cut vegetables) and the output (a portioned, nutritionally specified plated meal) match a nanny's plating step, but only when ingredients are presented in fixed hoppers on a line.

sources.title: AI robots automate tray assembly for fresh produce packing
sources.claim: Chef Robotics models also assemble snack-style packs, placing whole fruits into clamshells and snack boxes and portioning ... items into trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: produce/snack-box packing. Transfer: same objects (whole and cut fruit, scoopable sides) and same output (a filled snack container), which is the packing step of a lunchbox, but only on a fixtured line.

sources.title: Blendid teams with Jamba on robotic smoothie maker in Walmart store

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated fresh snack/beverage preparation and hand-off. Transfer: fruit and dairy ingredients, portioning to a recipe, and serving the finished item to the consumer mirror a nanny's snack-and-drink instance, inside a purpose-built enclosure.

sources.title: Sweetgreen's automated makeline shows robots and humans can coexist
sources.claim: Sweetgreen's Infinite Kitchen automated makeline moves bowls along a conveyor while dispensers add exact portions of greens, toppings and dressing and mix them; deployed in a growing number of stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated bowl assembly for guests. Transfer: portioning multiple fresh components into an individual serving and presenting it for pickup is the assemble-and-serve core of a simple child's meal, when work is conveyed to fixed dispensers.

sources.title: Miso Robotics Unveils AI-Powered Flippy 2 Robot, Gets Put to Work at White Castle as a Fry Cook
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy 2 autonomously runs an entire fry station — filling, shaking, emptying and returning baskets — in White Castle restaurant kitchens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hot-food cooking at a station. Transfer: thermal cooking of portioned foods to a doneness standard matches the cooking step of a child's hot lunch, but only at a purpose-built fixtured fry station.

sources.title: This $1,500 Kitchen Robot Does The Cooking For You
sources.claim: Posha is a shipping countertop cooking robot that, once a human loads washed and chopped ingredients into its designated containers, autonomously dispenses, stirs, seasons and controls heat to cook a dish using computer vision; it does not shop, chop, plate or clean.

sources.title: BONAPITA Adds Robotic Sous-Chef Alfred from Dexai Robotics
sources.claim: Dexai's Alfred robotic sous-chef was installed in working institutional and restaurant kitchens (Travis Air Force Base dining facility; a Boston restaurant) to prepare salads and bowls with standard utensils and ingredient pans.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order-driven bowl assembly in a human kitchen. Transfer: scooping portions from standard pans is the plating step of a child's meal, but Alfred works only at its own fixtured station and does not fetch, cook or deliver.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading home-deployed humanoid, relies on human teleoperators for household chores, and reviewers report no humanoid has been shown completing a household chore start to finish.

instances.label: Indoor play session in the family's home with a toddler or preschooler: nanny picks an age-appropriate activity, gets out blocks/puzzles/board game/dress-up materials, plays along on the floor, redirects and mediates, keeps the child physically safe (stairs, small parts), and tidies the toys away afterward.

Arts and crafts at the kitchen table in a private home: nanny gathers paper, paint, glue, scissors, dough or seasonal craft kit, covers the surface, demonstrates and physically assists the child (cutting, gluing, hand-over-hand), manages spills and mess, then washes up hands, brushes and table.

Walk or park/playground outing: dressing children for weather, loading stroller, walking public sidewalks and crossing streets with a toddler and infant, supervising climbing structures, swings and slides at a neighborhood playground, handling falls, other children, dogs, and the return trip home.

Active/sports play outdoors in the backyard or a park: throwing and kicking balls, tag and chase games, riding scooters or bikes with the nanny running alongside, sprinkler or backyard pool water play, with continuous safety supervision of a 3-8 year old.

Arranging and hosting a play date: coordinating with another caregiver, preparing the home or meeting at a park, setting up shared activities for two or more children, mediating sharing conflicts, serving a snack, supervising the group and cleaning up afterward.

Taking children to an organized community activity (library story time, toddler gym or music class, children's museum, indoor play centre): transporting and signing in, keeping children with the group, participating in and reinforcing the activity, managing transitions and departures.

sources.system: NAO 6 socially assistive robot (KIT daycare deployment)
sources.developer: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (Rixen, Gerling, Bruno); robot by Aldebaran/SoftBank Robotics
sources.title: Long-Term Integration of a Robot in an Inclusive Daycare: An Ethnographic Study Focused on Children and Caregivers
sources.claim: A NAO 6 socially assistive robot was deployed for four months in an inclusive daycare as a social mediator; it required a researcher to set it up each morning and to intervene on malfunctions, and children's activities continued to be structured by human caregivers rather than by the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Closest available analogue to a caregiver conducting play activities with young children; it shows that even in a structured childcare facility a state-of-the-art social robot supplements caregiver-led activities, needs daily human setup and repair, and cannot organize or run activity sessions itself.

sources.title: Miko 3 AI Robot for Kids - official product page
sources.claim: Miko 3 is a commercially sold tabletop child companion robot used autonomously in homes that runs games, dances, jokes and stories with children aged roughly 5-10; it is a screen-and-wheels device with no arms, so it cannot handle play or craft materials or supervise a child.

sources.title: Families face heartbreak as Moxie robots stop working after company shutdown
sources.claim: The Moxie child companion robot, an autonomous conversational home robot offering games and activities for children aged 5-10, was withdrawn when its maker ceased operations, illustrating that no home child-companion robot has reached durable caregiver-substitute deployment.

sources.title: 1X's $20K Robot Targets US Homes in 2026, Aims to Reduce the 'Creepy' Factor

sources.transferJustification: Best-case robotic 'plays a game with a person' capability; it is limited to a single fixtured sport against an able adult player and provides no child supervision, so it does not carry over to conducting recreational play with young children.

sources.title: Expert Insights on Robots for Safeguarding Children: How (not) and Why (not)?

sources.transferJustification: Child supervision/safeguarding is inseparable from conducting recreational activities with children; this expert consensus supports the negative judgment on whole-instance completion.

tasks.label: Observe children's behavior for irregularities, take temperature, transport children to doctor, or administer medications, as directed, to maintain children's health.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Ongoing, contextual observation of a child through the day in the family's home: noticing that a toddler is unusually clingy, off her food, sleeping oddly, breathing fast, scratching, or that a school-age child's mood or coordination has changed; judging it against that child's baseline and reporting to parents.

Discrete hands-on health inspection at a set moment (start of shift, after nap, before an outing): looking the child over for rash, red or crusty eyes, sore throat, blisters, head lice, bruises; feeling the forehead; deciding whether something is abnormal and flagging it.

Taking a temperature when illness is suspected: retrieving and readying a thermometer, using it on a squirming 1-4 year old (temporal, tympanic, axillary), getting a reliable reading, repeating it later, logging it and texting the result and recommendation to the parents.

Administering medication exactly as directed by parents/physician: measuring liquid antibiotic or fever reducer into an oral syringe, coaxing a resisting toddler to swallow it, or giving an inhaler with spacer, eye drops, allergy meds, topical cream; confirming the dose was actually taken and recording it.

Transporting a child to a pediatrician, dentist, or therapy appointment: dressing and readying the child, buckling into a car seat/booster, driving on public roads, parking, walking the child into the clinic, supervising in the waiting room, and relaying the visit's outcome to parents.

Caring for an acutely sick child at home: comforting and monitoring symptoms over hours, pushing fluids, cleaning up vomit or diarrhea and changing bedding, watching for red-flag signs, and deciding when to call the parents, the nurse line, or 911.

sources.title: Robots are used to carry out daily health inspections at schools across China - Digital Trends
sources.claim: Walklake health-screening robots installed at more than 2,000 Chinese preschools autonomously inspect 2-6 year olds each morning — cameras and an infrared thermometer check eyes, throat, hands and body temperature in about three seconds, generate a report, and alert teachers or the school nurse to abnormal results.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: daily preschool health inspection. It covers the same objects (young children), the same checks named in this task (looking for irregularities, taking temperature) and the same accepted output (a flagged abnormality reported to a responsible adult), so performance transfers to the nanny's inspection and temperature-taking instances — but only at a fixed station inside an institution.

sources.title: Robots safeguard students' health - Chinadaily.com.cn
sources.claim: The same preschool screening robot is a commercial product sold to schools and exported; it measures body temperature and examines eyes, hands and mouth with medical-grade sensors in seconds, with pupils presenting themselves to the device at the kindergarten.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: institutional daily health screening of children. Confirms the screening robot is a fielded commercial product performing temperature measurement and visual health checks on the same population, supporting the temperature instance at E2.

sources.title: Waymo teen accounts | Independence for teens, free time for parents
sources.claim: Waymo operates driverless robotaxis on public roads commercially, but its rider policy bars children 13 and under from riding without an adult and limits 14-17 year olds to guardian-linked teen accounts; riders are responsible for their own car seats.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous point-to-point driving. The driving leg transfers, but the instance also requires securing a young child in a car seat, escorting the child into and through the appointment, and supervising them — none of which the Waymo Driver performs, and children of nanny age may not ride unaccompanied.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: 1X's NEO home humanoid, the leading consumer household robot shipping to private homes, relies on human teleoperators for complex multi-step household tasks; only basic navigation, door opening and simple object retrieval run autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general household work in private homes. Establishes that the only fielded home humanoid cannot autonomously complete open-ended in-home caregiving chores, so it cannot substantiate the home-based observation, medication or sick-care instances.

sources.system: Robot-assisted feeding system with inside-mouth bite transfer (EMPRISE lab)
sources.title: Using machine learning, robotic feeding system empowers users with mobility issues - Advanced Science News
sources.claim: Cornell's robot-assisted feeding system performs autonomous inside-mouth bite transfer for adult users with severe motor impairments, evaluated with end users in real-world settings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bringing a utensil into a person's mouth. It is the closest robotic analogue to giving oral medicine, but the recipients are cooperating adults who open their mouths on cue, and the system does not measure a prescribed dose, handle a resisting toddler, or verify ingestion.

sources.title: Lio -- A Personal Robot Assistant for Human-Robot Interaction and Care Applications (arXiv)
sources.claim: The Lio personal care robot with a manipulator arm is deployed in several healthcare facilities where it operates autonomously assisting staff and patients daily, performing fetch-and-carry and interaction tasks rather than administering medication.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: personal-care assistance in institutional care settings. Shows the state of fielded autonomous care manipulators — item delivery and interaction in structured facilities — and that even these do not administer medications to patients, supporting a negative judgment on the medication instance.

Tidying and putting away children's belongings: gathering toys, blocks, puzzle pieces, books, art supplies, shoes and stuffed animals scattered across a playroom, living room and bedroom floors and returning each to its bin, shelf or closet at the end of play or the day.

Routine floor cleaning in children's areas: vacuuming or sweeping crumbs under the high chair and table, dust and cracker debris in the play area and bedroom rugs, and damp-mopping hard floors after meals and play.

Children's laundry: gathering soiled clothes and bibs, pretreating stains, sorting, running the household washer and dryer, then folding small garments and putting them away in labeled drawers and closets.

Bath and bathroom cleanup: rinsing and wiping the tub after bath time, mopping splashed water, cleaning the sink, toilet or training potty, sanitizing bath toys and hanging wet towels in a family bathroom.

Bedding and soft-surface care: stripping and changing crib sheets and mattress pads after leaks or illness, remaking the bed, and spot-cleaning spills, spit-up or potty accidents on carpet, sofa and car seat fabric.

instances.label: Morning/afternoon school or daycare run in the family car: nanny gets one to three young children (infant/toddler/preschool, in rear- or forward-facing car seats or boosters) out of the house, buckles and checks each restraint, drives neighborhood streets and arterials, queues in the school drop-off line or parks and walks the child in, signs the child in/out with staff, and returns home.
