automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Weekly/biweekly main grocery run for the household: nanny drives to a supermarket, pushes a cart through public aisles, selects 40-60 items including fresh produce, dairy, meat and packaged goods (checking dates, ripeness, brands and prices against family preferences and allergies), goes through checkout, loads the car, drives home, carries bags in and puts everything away.

Quick top-up errand for child-care essentials - diapers, wipes, formula, OTC children's medicine, sunscreen - at a pharmacy, convenience or big-box store, often squeezed between school runs and frequently with a toddler or infant along in the cart.

Children's clothing and shoe shopping at a mall or department store: judging current sizes, trying garments/shoes on the child, checking fit, fabric and seasonal need, staying within the parents' budget and taste, and handling returns/exchanges.

Online/app ordering of groceries and child supplies followed by curbside pickup at the store or receipt of a home delivery: loading the order into the car or taking it at the door, then unpacking and stowing perishables and supplies in the household's fridge, pantry and closets.
Trip to a big-box or specialty store for school supplies, craft and activity materials, toys, books or birthday gifts from a teacher's or parent's list, comparing options and quantities on the shelf.

Fresh-food specialty errand: farmers market, bakery, butcher or ethnic grocer for perishables, judging quality/ripeness at the stall or counter, sometimes paying cash and carrying the goods home on foot or by transit.

sources.title: The technology Re:Imagining online grocery
sources.claim: Ocado's On-Grid Robotic Pick (OGRP) autonomously picks and packs individual grocery items into customer orders inside automated customer fulfilment centres; it is rolled out at 14 CFCs, with the Luton site picking about half of total order volume robotically across a 45,000-SKU grocery range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a customer's grocery order from a 45,000-SKU range is the selection-and-collection core of a nanny's shopping trip - same objects (packaged and fresh grocery items), same care required against damage, with goods brought to the machine as an E1 setting would present them.

sources.title: Ocado's AI-powered robotic arms: Levelling efficiency
sources.claim: Ocado states OGRP is a robust autonomous machine-learning system, not a rigidly scripted one, developed specifically for the variability and fragility of grocery items; it picked over 30 million items in 2024.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes autonomy (not teleoperation or scripting) for the grocery order-assembly evidence used to judge shopping instances at E1.

sources.title: Amazon's Sparrow is leaving the nest: Trailblazing warehouse robot is ready for a wider rollout
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks individual consumer products (about 65% of a 100-million-item inventory, including drugstore-type consumables, toys and general merchandise) out of mixed totes in fulfillment centres, identifying each product and checking it for damage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order picking of diverse retail goods. The objects a nanny buys (diapers, wipes, formula, medicines, craft supplies, toys) are the same catalogue items Sparrow singulates, so item selection carries over when the goods are presented to the machine.

sources.title: Stow: Robotic Packing of Items into Fabric Pods (arXiv:2505.04572)
sources.claim: Amazon Robotics' Stow system autonomously places diverse purchased items into densely packed fabric storage pods at human-level packing density and speed, with more than 500,000 stows performed in a working fulfillment centre.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stowing arriving goods into storage. This is the put-away half of a shopping errand (unpacking an order onto fridge/pantry/closet shelving), with comparable objects and placement precision, executed where goods are brought to the machine.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: Home humanoids marketed for household errands such as carrying groceries are not autonomous: 1X's NEO relies on remote human teleoperators for such tasks as of late 2025/2026.
sources.transferJustification: Supports the negative finding that no cited system performs shopping errands or home put-away autonomously in E3 settings.

sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: Autonomous mobile manipulation inside working supermarkets remains a research prototype; published work targets shelf stocking and names human traffic, tight aisles and product variety as open challenges.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store handling of retail goods by a mobile manipulator. Shows E2 store-floor item handling is at prototype stage, not worker-quality shopping.

roles.title: Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors
roles.description: Instruct or coach groups or individuals in exercise activities for the primary purpose of personal fitness. Demonstrate techniques and form, observe participants, and explain to them corrective measures necessary to improve their skills. Develop and implement individualized approaches to exercise.

tasks.label: Observe participants and inform them of corrective measures necessary for skill improvement.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Offer alternatives during classes to accommodate different levels of fitness.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mainstream group strength/HIIT/bootcamp class in a gym studio: 12-30 participants of mixed ability on mats and with dumbbells; instructor performs each movement at the front while continuously scanning the room and offering scaled options (knee push-up instead of full, step-back instead of jump, lighter load), demonstrating the easier version in real time and sometimes swapping a participant's weight mid-set.

Yoga, Pilates or barre class in a studio: instructor demonstrates a pose from the mat or floor, verbally offers a modification (bent knees, hand on shin, block under hip), physically shows the modified shape, walks the room, hands props to individuals and occasionally gives a hands-on adjustment.

Indoor cycling, treadmill or rowing class: instructor works on their own bike/deck, calls intensity alternatives (stay seated, take a half-turn of resistance, walk instead of run), demonstrates seated vs standing options, and adjusts an individual rider's setup or console when they cannot hold the prescribed effort.

Seated/gentle exercise class for older adults at a senior center, community center or long-term care home: 6-20 participants in chairs, narrow repertoire of arm, neck, trunk and leg movements; instructor demonstrates a standing and a seated version, cuts range of motion or reps for frailer participants, and hands out light bands or weights.

Small-group training session (3-6 clients) on the gym floor: trainer substitutes an easier variation mid-circuit for one client (goblet squat to box squat), changes the machine pin or seat, swaps to lighter dumbbells or a band, and spots while the rest of the group continues.

Outdoor bootcamp class in a park, parking lot or beach: uneven ground, weather, mixed abilities and portable equipment; instructor demonstrates lower-impact alternatives on the grass or sand (march instead of sprint, incline push-up on a bench) and redirects individuals during the circuit.

sources.developer: Ngee Ann Polytechnic / Infocomm Development Authority of Singapore
sources.title: Singapore turns to robots to get seniors moving | CNN
sources.claim: RoboCoach Xian, a robotic exercise trainer developed by Ngee Ann Polytechnic, was deployed to Singapore senior activity centres where it leads seated exercise classes for groups of seniors, demonstrating movements and showing instructions on a chest screen.
sources.transferJustification: Leading a class and demonstrating exercise options for a mixed-ability senior group is the same delivery mode as offering alternatives, though the repertoire is limited to gentle seated arm exercises.

sources.title: Assistive Technology and Robotics In Healthcare - Smart Nation Singapore
sources.claim: Singapore's national Smart Nation programme describes RoboCoach Xian as a robotic trainer that teaches exercise routines to seniors individually or in groups and provides personalised, gentle routines.

sources.system: Pepper exercise facilitation system (ASBLab, University of Toronto)
sources.developer: Shao, Pham-Hung, Alves, Snyder, Eshaghi, Benhabib & Nejat (U. Toronto), SoftBank Pepper platform
sources.title: Long-Term Exercise Assistance: Group and One-on-One Interactions between a Social Robot and Seniors (Robotics 12(1):9)
sources.claim: A Pepper robot autonomously facilitated group and one-on-one upper-body exercise sessions with residents over a long-term study at the Yee Hong Centre ..., adapting its assistive behaviours to users and monitoring heart rate to avoid overexertion.

sources.title: Long-Term Exercise Assistance: Group and One-on-One Interactions between a Social Robot and Seniors (Robotics 12(1):9)
sources.claim: The same Pepper system adapts its assistive behaviour to each user's affect, tracks progress against individual exercise goals across sessions and monitors heart rate to prevent overexertion during the class.
sources.transferJustification: Per-participant dose adjustment (rest prompts, overexertion limits, goal-scaled progression) is the seated-class form of offering easier options to lower-fitness participants.

sources.title: News on Aging | ILC-Japan
sources.claim: The PALRO humanoid robot has been adopted in roughly 900 Japanese nursing care facilities, where it leads the exercise portion of group rehabilitation/recreation programmes with a library of different exercises rotated over time.

sources.developer: Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (Levy-Tzedek lab)
sources.title: "Gymmy": Designing and Testing a Robot for Physical and Cognitive Training of Older Adults (ResearchGate record, Applied Sciences 11(14):6431)
sources.claim: Gymmy, a humanoid-robot training system, demonstrates upper-body exercises to older adults while an RGB-D camera measures their performance and the robot gives verbal and visual feedback; tested in lab studies with older adults.
sources.transferJustification: Robot demonstration of exercises with camera-based performance monitoring is the perception-plus-demonstration loop required to notice a struggling participant and show a different option.

sources.system: SAR cognitive-motor training platform for Parkinson's disease
sources.developer: Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (Raz, Shapiro, Levy-Tzedek et al.)
sources.title: A novel socially assistive robotic platform for cognitive-motor exercises for individuals with Parkinson's Disease (Frontiers in Robotics and AI)
sources.claim: A socially assistive robotic platform for Parkinson's disease cognitive-motor training uses two custom mobile robots whose exercise difficulty level is adapted automatically during a session based on the patient's performance; feasibility tested in-lab with end users.
sources.transferJustification: Automatic within-session difficulty adjustment to a participant's ability is the mechanism behind offering an easier or harder option, but shown only for single-user reaching/stepping games in a lab.

sources.title: Will People Enjoy a Robot Trainer? A Case Study with Snoopie the Pacerbot (arXiv:2604.18331)
sources.claim: SNOOPIE is an autonomous quadruped pacing robot that runs interval-training workouts scaled to an individual runner's ability on a running track, outperforming a wearable coach on pace adherence in a user study.
sources.transferJustification: Tailoring workout intensity to one user's fitness level is the closest robotic analogue to offering alternatives, but it covers only pacing for a single runner on a track, with no movement demonstration or option-giving to a class.

sources.system: Robotic system for physical training of older adults
sources.title: Robotic System for Physical Training of Older Adults (International Journal of Social Robotics)
sources.claim: A Kinect-based robotic physical-training system for older adults delivered eight strength exercises, but its authors state that making difficulty levels adaptive to each user's performance and level remains future work.
sources.transferJustification: Documents that even purpose-built robot exercise trainers largely run fixed routines rather than selecting per-participant alternatives.

sources.developer: University of the West of England / Bristol Robotics Laboratory
sources.title: World's first robotic personal trainer guides gym-goers through exercise programme | UWE Bristol
sources.claim: Bristol Robotics Laboratory reported a socially intelligent robot fitness coach that guides a single gym user through a treadmill exercise programme with support personalised to heart rate, speed, mood and personality; no evidence found that it runs autonomously without researcher control.

tasks.label: Monitor participants' progress and adapt programs as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Plan routines, choose appropriate music, and choose different movements for each set of muscles, depending on participants' capabilities and limitations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Evaluate individuals' abilities, needs, and physical conditions, and develop suitable training programs to meet any special requirements.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Initial intake/consultation with a new personal-training client at a commercial gym: reviewing a health-history and PAR-Q form, interviewing the client about goals, injuries, medications and schedule, watching a few movement patterns (squat, hinge, overhead reach), noting baseline numbers (weight, resting heart rate, self-reported activity), then writing a 4-8 week individualized program in the club's software.

Periodic reassessment of an existing client: reviewing training logs and adherence, retesting a few benchmarks (push-up count, plank hold, treadmill or step test, girth measures), discussing what has and has not worked, and revising sets/reps/loads/progressions for the next training block.

Pre-class screening and planning for a group fitness class (spin, HIIT, yoga, bootcamp): collecting injury/pregnancy/limitation disclosures from participants at sign-in or at the top of class, gauging the mixed ability level of the room, and planning regressions, progressions and substitute movements into the class plan.

Special-population client (older adult, post-physical-therapy, pregnant, or with a chronic condition such as hypertension, diabetes, or joint replacement): reading physician clearance or PT discharge notes, running functional tests (30-second chair stand, gait/balance, range-of-motion checks), and building a modified, contraindication-aware program, sometimes documented back to the referring clinician.

Remote/online client onboarding: intake questionnaire and video call, client-submitted movement-screen videos and photos, wearable and app data review, then writing and loading an individualized program into a coaching app with periodic written check-ins and adjustments.

tasks.label: Instruct participants in maintaining exertion levels to maximize benefits from exercise routines.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Teach and demonstrate use of gymnastic and training equipment, such as trampolines and weights.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: One-on-one personal training session on a commercial gym floor: trainer loads plates, sets machine seats/pins, physically demonstrates barbell and dumbbell lifts (squat, press, row) with correct human biomechanics, then watches the client's reps, cues and hands-on corrects form, and spots the working set.

Group fitness class in a studio (bootcamp/strength/HIIT): instructor demonstrates use of kettlebells, dumbbells, resistance bands, steps and plyo boxes at the front of the ..., scans 10-25 participants while they work, and calls or walks over to correct unsafe form mid-class.

New-member equipment orientation on the gym floor: walking a member through cardio machines and selectorized/cable machines, showing start-up, settings, safety stops and clips, demonstrating a rep on each, then watching the member try it and correcting.

Gymnastics/trampoline instruction in a gymnastics gym or trampoline park: demonstrating skills and progressions on trampoline, mats and apparatus, and physically spotting learners through jumps, flips and landings.

Older-adult or rehab-oriented session in a senior living facility or community center: demonstrating light hand weights, resistance bands, chairs and balance equipment, with hands-on assistance and close monitoring of frail clients.

In-home or outdoor personal training: client's living room, garage gym or a park, using portable equipment (dumbbells, bands, TRX, mini-trampoline) in a layout that differs at every site, demonstrating each movement and correcting the client.

sources.system: Pepper robot fitness coach (Bristol Robotics Laboratory / UWE Bristol)
sources.developer: Bristol Robotics Laboratory, University of the West of England
sources.title: World's first robotic personal trainer guides gym-goers through exercise programme | UWE Bristol
sources.claim: A Pepper humanoid was developed by Bristol Robotics Laboratory as a 'socially intelligent' fitness coach that coaches a runner on a treadmill with voice prompts and gestures, personalized to heart rate and mood; it does not handle or demonstrate use of weights or other training equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: verbal/gestural coaching of a treadmill runner. Cited as the closest robotic analogue to instructing gym users; it does not transfer to demonstrating use of weights or gymnastic apparatus because the robot never grasps, loads or operates equipment.

sources.developer: Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (Avioz-Sarig, Olatunji, Sarne-Fleischmann, Edan)
sources.title: Robotic System for Physical Training of Older Adults | International Journal of Social Robotics
sources.claim: A NAO/Poppy robotic coach system autonomously instructs older adults, demonstrates bodyweight exercises with its own body, and gives real-time corrective feedback using an RGB-D camera; the exercises involve no weights or gymnastic apparatus.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led demonstration and correction of bodyweight exercise. It shows demonstration-plus-correction is feasible for small, unloaded arm/leg movements, but does not transfer to this task, whose objects are barbells, dumbbells, machines and trampolines that these small robots cannot lift, load or safely spot.

sources.system: NAO socially assistive exercise coach (Fasola & Mataric)
sources.developer: University of Southern California Interaction Lab
sources.title: A socially assistive robot exercise coach for the elderly | Journal of Human-Robot Interaction
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid acted as an autonomous exercise instructor for groups at a senior living community, leading warm-up and exercise routines; the routines are gesture-based movements with no training equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading a group exercise session. Establishes that robots can autonomously lead unloaded group calisthenics in a care facility, but not that they can teach or demonstrate the use of weights, machines or trampolines, which the platform cannot physically manipulate.

sources.system: NAO and Pepper in nursing home (University of Minnesota Duluth project)
sources.developer: SoftBank Robotics / University of Minnesota Duluth researchers
sources.title: Robots are now helping nursing home residents in Minnesota - Bring Me The News
sources.claim: NAO and Pepper robots were placed in a Minnesota nursing home, with NAO programmed to lead residents in group ... - a real facility deployment of robot-led, equipment-free exercise sessions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robot-led group exercise in an institutional facility. Shows deployment feasibility for equipment-free movement sessions only; there is no handling of weights or gymnastic equipment, so it does not substantiate this task.

sources.title: Humanoid robot Digit deadlifts 65 lbs with advanced coordination
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid was shown deadlifting 65 lbs in a laboratory test of whole-body coordination - a strength/manipulation demonstration, not instruction of a human learner.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: lifting a loaded barbell-like object. Cited as near-miss context: it shows a humanoid can move weight in a lab, but the demonstration is a lab strength test with no human learner, no human-form modeling, no observation/correction and no spotting, so it does not carry over to teaching equipment use.

sources.system: ddrobotec robotic personal trainer (robotic leg press)
sources.title: Robotic Personal Trainer | Swiss Made by ddrobotec
sources.claim: ddrobotec markets a commercial robotic strength-training machine (a robot-controlled leg press) that guides a user's movement with programmed force; the robot is the exercise equipment and does not demonstrate or teach the use of free weights or gymnastic apparatus.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: machine-guided resistance exercise. Cited as near-miss context: the device constrains a user's motion on one fixed machine rather than teaching and demonstrating how to use gym equipment, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

tasks.label: Explain and enforce safety rules and regulations governing sports, recreational activities, and the use of exercise equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Teach proper breathing techniques used during physical exertion.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Group fitness class (indoor cycling, HIIT, bootcamp) in a health club studio: the instructor cues breathing rhythm over a microphone during work intervals — when to exhale on effort, how to recover breath between sets — while participants of mixed fitness levels follow along.

One-on-one personal training session on a gym floor: the trainer teaches bracing and exhale-on-exertion for squats, presses and deadlifts, explaining the technique, demonstrating it, watching the client's ribcage and abdomen, and correcting breath-holding verbally (sometimes with a light hand cue on the client's abdomen or ribs).

Mind-body class (yoga, Pilates, stretch/recovery) in a studio: the instructor explains and demonstrates diaphragmatic, ujjayi, or lateral-costal breathing, counts breath timing to movement, and gives individual verbal corrections while walking the room.

Client onboarding, fitness assessment, or virtual/remote session: the trainer explains breathing mechanics and technique verbally (in person or over video), answers questions, and assigns practice drills for the client to do on their own.

Special-population coaching (older adults, cardiac/pulmonary rehab-style classes, prenatal, beginners) in a community center or clinic-affiliated gym: the instructor teaches pursed-lip or paced breathing, warns against Valsalva breath-holding, and monitors perceived exertion while cueing breath.

tasks.label: Maintain fitness equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Wiping down and sanitizing equipment during/after use on a busy commercial gym floor: spraying and wiping benches, cardio console panels, handlebars, grips, upholstered pads and machine frames with a bottle and towel, with members moving around the floor.

Re-racking and putting away free weights and accessories after client sessions and classes: returning 5-100 lb dumbbells to the correct rack slot, stripping plates from barbells to the tree, collecting kettlebells, medicine balls, bands, foam rollers and mats scattered on the floor into their storage positions.

Routine safety/preventive-maintenance rounds on the floor: checking cable and pulley wear, selector pins, seat and bolt tightness, testing that treadmills, bikes and ellipticals run correctly, lubricating treadmill decks, adjusting belt tracking/tension, logging findings and tagging out defective units.

Minor repairs and part replacement on a machine in the facility: swapping a frayed cable or worn pedal strap, tightening a wobbly bench or loose handle, replacing a console battery or torn upholstery pad, then testing the machine before returning it to service.

Group-fitness studio set-up and breakdown: laying out steps, mats, dumbbell sets and risers in a per-participant grid, adjusting and wiping spin bikes, then collecting and re-stacking everything into the storage racks after class.

Caring for portable gear used away from a facility (in-home personal training, outdoor bootcamp): loading/unloading kettlebells, TRX straps, bands, mats and cones from a vehicle, wiping them down in a client's living room or a park, inspecting straps and stitching for wear, and stowing the kit.

sources.title: This robot will clean toilets for $1,000 a month | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is a commercially leased autonomous mobile manipulator that sprays, wipes, disinfects and dries fixtures and surfaces in commercial restrooms in offices, airports and casinos during normal facility operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping/disinfecting fixed sanitary fixtures. Transfer to gym-equipment wipe-down: both are fixed, standard-model objects at mapped locations in an institution-controlled indoor facility, cleaned by spray-and-wipe contact to a visual/sanitary standard rather than to tight tolerance.

sources.title: Autonomous SOMATIC Robot Demonstrates its Bathroom Cleaning Skills - TechEBlog
sources.claim: Somatic's robot is taught a given room once through a VR interface and thereafter cleans fixtures, floors and trash autonomously using onboard LiDAR and sensors, without an operator in the loop.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that operation is autonomous (teaching is offline, per-site programming), not continuous teleoperation, for the cleaning transfer above.

sources.title: Everyday Robots Moves Out of Alphabet X, Reports Progress Toward General Purpose Robot - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Everyday Robots ran a fleet of over 100 mobile manipulators that autonomously wiped tables and tidied in Google's Bay Area offices and cafes, showing autonomous spray/squeegee surface wiping inside an occupied human work facility (program ended in 2023).
sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping cafe tables. Transfer to wiping gym machine surfaces: same spray/wipe contact motion on waist-height surfaces, same acceptance standard (visibly clean), same class of mapped, institution-controlled indoor facility.

sources.title: Ecoppia's Advanced Robotic Technology Now Powers Automated Solar Panel Cleaning at AES California Site | Business Wire
sources.claim: Ecoppia's T4/E4 robots autonomously clean the surfaces of fixed equipment (PV modules) nightly at commercial solar plants, riding purpose-built rails and docking stations installed on the equipment rows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine cleaning of equipment surfaces. Transfer to equipment wipe-down at E1: the machine is presented in a fixed, known pose in an installation engineered around the robot, and the acceptance standard is a clean surface.

sources.title: Robotic Palletizing Systems | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC M-410iC palletizing robots operate in fenced end-of-line cells, autonomously picking 50 lb items presented by a conveyor and placing them in defined positions, including diverting rejects to designated stations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: heavy-item pick-and-place into defined stack positions. Transfer to re-racking dumbbells/plates and laying out class equipment at E1: comparable object weights (25-50 lb class), comparable placement precision (slot/stack position), and the same fenced cell with items presented in known pose.

sources.title: ACF-K ACTIVE CONTACT FLANGE KIT (datasheet)
sources.claim: FerRobotics Active Contact Flange kits are commercially sold end-effectors that let industrial robots and cobots perform force-controlled contact surface work - including cleaning, brushing, stripping and polishing - on fixtured workpieces in robot cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: force-controlled surface cleaning/finishing of fixtured parts. Transfer to wiping down gear presented at a cleaning station: same contact-force control over curved metal/plastic surfaces, same purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot performs scheduled autonomous inspection rounds in factories and other industrial facilities, capturing thermal, visual and acoustic data for predictive maintenance; it is operating at hundreds of sites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous preventive-maintenance inspection rounds in a facility. Covers only the sensing sub-step of a trainer's PM round; no cited system performs the hands-on servicing (lubricating decks, tightening hardware, adjusting belts, tagging out).

sources.system: Gym cleaning robots (autonomous floor scrubbers, e.g. Whiz / Scrubber 50 fleet)
sources.title: Gym Robots for Fitness Center Automation | RobotLAB
sources.claim: Robots marketed and deployed into US gyms and fitness studios are autonomous floor scrubbers/vacuums that clean floors around the machines; the vendor states equipment sanitization remains staff work.
sources.transferJustification: Shows the actual state of robot deployment inside fitness facilities: floor cleaning only, with equipment maintenance and sanitization still done by staff; supports negative judgments on in-gym equipment servicing.

tasks.label: Provide students with information and resources regarding nutrition, weight control, and lifestyle issues.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

tasks.label: Administer emergency first aid, wrap injuries, treat minor chronic disabilities, or refer injured persons to physicians.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Acute minor musculoskeletal complaint mid-session on a commercial gym floor or studio: a client tweaks a shoulder, low back or hamstring during a lift or class. The trainer stops the set, asks about mechanism and pain, looks at and palpates the area, retrieves an ice pack or cold spray from the front desk kit, applies it with light compression and elevation, has the client rest, and logs the incident.

Wrapping or bracing at the gym: applying an elastic compression wrap, athletic tape or kinesiology tape to an ankle, knee or wrist, or fitting a support sleeve, for a mild sprain or a known chronic joint problem, with correct tension, anchoring and circulation check, before or after activity.

Minor wound care in the facility: a barbell scrape, treadmill mat burn, torn callus, blister or small laceration. The trainer gloves up, cleans the wound, applies antiseptic and an adhesive dressing, controls minor bleeding, and cleans blood off equipment per the club's bloodborne-pathogen protocol.

Assessment and referral at the gym: a client reports persistent or worsening pain (knee, shoulder, low back). The trainer screens the movement, applies simple hands-on checks, decides the issue exceeds scope of practice, modifies or stops the program, documents the incident, and refers the client to a physician or physical therapist.

Medical emergency in the club or group-fitness studio: a participant collapses, faints, has a cardiac arrest, hypoglycemic episode or heat illness. The instructor clears the area, checks responsiveness and breathing, directs someone to call 911, begins CPR and applies the wall-mounted AED, or places the person in recovery position, until EMS arrives.

First aid away from the club: outdoor bootcamp in a park, run-club route, or in-home personal training session. A client rolls an ankle on uneven grass or scrapes a knee; the trainer works from a small portable kit on varied terrain, with no facility supplies, fixed layout, or staff backup.

sources.title: Massage Envy Introduces Aescape Robotic Massage at Select Franchised Locations
sources.claim: Aescape's fully automated robotic massage tables are commercially deployed in roughly 100 gym, hotel and spa locations (Equinox, Massage Envy, hotels), performing autonomous soft-tissue bodywork on a clothed client lying on a table, with no human therapist present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic soft-tissue bodywork on a human in a fitness facility. It is the closest deployed system making controlled physical contact with a client's body in a gym, so it bounds what exists today. It does not assess an injury, apply ice or compression, clean or dress a wound, wrap a joint, or make referral decisions; the client selects the routine on a touchscreen, so it does not substitute for the trainer's injury-management judgment.

sources.system: Autonomous tape handling for robotic wound redressing (UCSD, Yip lab)
sources.title: Towards Autonomous Tape Handling for Robotic Wound Redressing
sources.claim: First autonomous approach to medical tape manipulation for wound redressing; evaluated in a laboratory robot workspace on anatomical surface models (leg, hip, heel phantoms), not on live patients, and covering only tape peeling and re-securing sub-steps.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying adhesive dressing/tape to a body surface, the manipulation core of bandaging a cut or blister. Transfer fails for this task: the work is on rigid anatomical phantoms in a lab cell, addresses only two sub-steps (initiating detachment, re-securing tape), and no cleaning, assessment, or complete dressing of a live person's wound is shown.

sources.developer: Korean academic research team (published in the resuscitation literature)
sources.title: Development of artificial intelligence-driven biosignal-sensitive cardiopulmonary resuscitation robot
sources.claim: An AI-driven chest-compression robot autonomously adapted compression using predicted carotid blood flow, but was demonstrated only in an anesthetized porcine cardiac-arrest laboratory model with the device positioned on the animal by researchers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mechanical chest compressions during cardiac arrest, the core motor act of CPR. Transfer fails: the robot only controls compressions once humans have exposed the chest and mounted the device on an anesthetized pig; it does not detect collapse, check responsiveness, position itself on a person, ventilate, or apply an AED.

sources.title: Sensor-guided robots could boost lifesaving combat casualty care | DARPA
sources.claim: DARPA in September 2025 launched the Medics Autonomously Stopping Hemorrhage (MASH) program to develop, over three years, robots that can find and stop bleeding, indicating autonomous robotic hemorrhage control does not yet exist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous emergency treatment of an injured human (bleeding control). Cited as a bound on the state of the art, not as capability: it is an announcement of intent with the autonomy still to be developed.

sources.system: Hybrid control robot-assisted dressing (Franka Emika Panda)
sources.title: Hybrid Control Strategies for Safe and Adaptive Robot-Assisted Dressing
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing, the closest demonstrated manipulation of fabric around a live human limb, remains a laboratory activity: experiments used a Franka Emika Panda arm with two healthy participants in a university human-robot interaction lab.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pulling compliant fabric onto a human arm, mechanically similar to wrapping an elastic bandage around a limb. Transfer fails: garment sleeving tolerates loose fit with slow, seated, cooperative lab subjects, whereas a compression wrap requires graded tension, figure-eight patterning and secure anchoring on a painful joint, which has not been demonstrated.

sources.system: Medical Swarm Robotics / robot medic solicitation
sources.title: DARPA launches search for robot medics to treat battlefield casualties
sources.claim: As of May 2026 DARPA was still soliciting robot medics able to perform battlefield interventions such as hemorrhage control and fracture stabilization, with the first phase permitting demonstrations only in a laboratory or on manikins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous first aid on injured humans. Cited only as a bound on the state of the art as of mid-2026: the capability is being sought, and even the first milestone is a manikin demonstration rather than treatment of a real casualty.

tasks.label: Maintain equipment inventories, and select, store, or issue equipment as needed.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Group fitness class setup and teardown in a health-club studio: before class the instructor pulls mats, steps, dumbbell pairs, bands and bosus from the studio closet and stages a station for each of 15-30 participants; after class collects, wipes and re-shelves everything in ~10 minutes before the next class.

Weight-room floor duty at a commercial gym: gathering dumbbells, plates, kettlebells and medicine balls members left on the floor and benches and returning each to its correct rack slot by weight and size, among members who are training; pulling damaged items out of service.

Personal-training session on the gym floor: selecting the equipment the client's program calls for (kettlebells, TRX, bands, plyo boxes, cable attachments), carrying and staging it at the training area, swapping items between sets, and returning it all to storage at the end.

Periodic inventory audit and stock control: walking the floor and storage room counting and logging equipment (dumbbell sets, mats, bands, spin shoes, towels, cleaning supplies), checking items for wear or damage, updating the inventory sheet, flagging reorders and putting away deliveries.

Boutique studio or corporate wellness room: issuing personal gear at check-in (spin shoes, heart-rate straps, boxing gloves, mats), then collecting, sanitizing and returning each item to its labeled bin or hook in a shared closet and restocking for the next session.

Mobile trainer working in clients' homes or a public park: loading kettlebells, bands, mats, cones and an agility ladder into a vehicle, carrying them into a living room or onto grass, laying them out for the session, then repacking and re-inventorying the kit.

sources.date: 2025-11 (product page; series in production for decades)
sources.title: M-410 Series Palletizing Robot | FANUC America
sources.claim: FANUC M-410 series four-axis palletizing robots are a widely installed commercial product that repeatedly picks heavy rigid loads (boxes, bags, slabs) presented at a fixed infeed and places them in precise defined positions inside a fenced end-of-line cell, running unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: end-of-line palletizing. Storing/issuing gym equipment at E1 reduces to picking heavy rigid objects (dumbbells, plates, kettlebells, weighted balls) from a presented position and placing them in a defined slot pattern; payload and placement precision far exceed what dumbbell racking requires.

sources.date: 2025-05 (announced; fleet scaled at Spokane FC through 2026)
sources.title: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force sensing to stow items - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously picks and stows a wide variety of items of differing weight and fragility into individual compartments of storage pods in fulfillment centres, at human-comparable speed, escalating to a human only for rare exception items.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stowing mixed goods into shelf compartments. That is the same act as putting varied pieces of equipment away in designated storage locations, with comparable object variety and placement precision, when the inventory is presented to a fixed arm as a purpose-built cell would present it.

sources.date: 2025-10-28 (vendor documentation; systems in production for years)
sources.title: How AutoStore Works - Everything You Need to Know - Kardex
sources.claim: AutoStore cube storage systems (integrated by Kardex, Dematic and others) use fleets of autonomous grid robots to store items away and retrieve the requested bin on demand, delivering it to a port; the systems are in commercial production use at scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage and retrieval of stock. 'Select, store or issue equipment as needed' is store/retrieve-on-demand; in a purpose-built setting the gear lives in grid bins and the machine issues and re-stores it while holding a running count of what is on hand.

sources.title: Harmons Deploys Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot In Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally robot autonomously navigates grocery store aisles among shoppers multiple times a day, scanning shelves to count stock, detect missing items and verify placement and pricing; it is deployed across 17 Harmons stores after a pilot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retail shelf inventory audit. Maintaining an equipment inventory is the same act - a mobile robot traverses an institution-controlled facility, images racks, counts items and reports shortfalls into a stock record; gym racks hold far fewer and more distinguishable item types than a grocery planogram.

sources.system: Amazon Vulcan / Physical Intelligence π0.5 (capability assessment)
sources.title: Where Autonomy Works: Evaluating Robot Capabilities in 2026 - Epoch AI
sources.claim: Independent 2026 assessment of autonomous robot capability: mixed-weight pick-and-place is in production deployment, but the deployed picker works in a zone without people and with very limited mobility, while whole-room tidying of loose objects is only 'validated in lab'.
sources.transferJustification: Same capability family (mixed-object pick/place and room tidying). Establishes the environment boundary: the production-grade putting-away system requires a purpose-built, humanless workspace, while free-roaming tidying of loose objects remains lab-stage.

sources.title: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid passes 100,000-tote milestone in live GXO implementation
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid works autonomously in a live GXO warehouse alongside staff, moving standardised totes between AMRs, conveyors and floor stacking locations, passing 100,000 totes moved in commercial operation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile manipulation of stored goods inside a human work facility (E2). Cited as the boundary case - it handles one standardised tote at engineered pick/place stations, not mixed heavy free weights, mats and bands scattered across a gym floor, so it does not transfer to the gym instances.

sources.system: π0.5 vision-language-action model on a mobile manipulator
sources.title: π0.5: a VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 controls a mobile manipulator to tidy kitchens and bedrooms in homes never seen in training, placing loose objects into their proper locations, but first-try reliability is imperfect and the demonstrations are slow and lab-run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting loose objects away in an unstructured home (E3). Closest evidence for the mobile-trainer instance, but it handles light household clutter at sub-worker reliability, not a full weighted training kit.

tasks.label: Conduct therapeutic, recreational, or athletic activities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Lead a scheduled group fitness class (HIIT, step/aerobics, indoor cycling, bootcamp-style strength, power yoga) in a gym or rec-center studio for 10-30 adults: demonstrate each movement full-body to music tempo, cue transitions, scan the room, correct or modify for individuals mid-class, manage equipment (mats, weights, bikes) and class flow for 45-60 minutes.

Take a member through a prescribed machine-based strength/cardio circuit session in a health club (onboarding or beginner program): set each machine's load and range of motion for the person, pace the reps and rest, keep them moving through the sequence, and log the session.

Conduct a therapeutic/adaptive exercise session for older adults or clients with limited mobility in a senior activity center, adult day program, or long-term care facility: seated and standing low-impact routines, range-of-motion, balance and strength work, verbal cueing, encouragement, watching for fatigue or overexertion.

Conduct a one-on-one or small-group personal training session on the gym floor: demonstrate free-weight and functional movements, load plates and adjust benches/racks, spot barbell and dumbbell lifts, give hands-on tactile form cues, and finish with assisted (partner) stretching.

Lead a recreational or athletic activity on a court, field, gym floor, or public park: sports drills and games, youth or team conditioning, obstacle/boot-camp circuits — setting out cones and equipment, participating/demonstrating, officiating play, and keeping participants safe in variable outdoor conditions.

Conduct an aquatic exercise class (water aerobics, aqua therapy, adaptive swim conditioning) at a facility pool: demonstrate movements from the deck and in the water, cue against ambient noise, distribute flotation equipment, and physically assist participants entering, positioning in, and exiting the water.

sources.title: News on Aging — The Future of the Robot-led Nursing Care | ILC-Japan
sources.claim: The humanoid robot PALRO is used as the exercise instructor at an ARFIT adult day-care/functional-training facility in Yokohama, leading the group warm-up exercise block and a later oral-motor exercise block for attending elders each morning.

sources.developer: Ngee Ann Polytechnic with IDA Singapore
sources.title: In Singapore, robots are now leading workouts for the elderly (Yahoo Finance / Tech in Asia)
sources.claim: RoboCoach, a sensor-equipped robotic exercise instructor, was deployed to Singapore senior activity centres to lead exercise classes for elderly participants, demonstrating routines and checking that seniors perform them correctly.

sources.system: Pepper-based autonomous exercise facilitation robot (Autonomous Systems and Biomechatronics Lab, Univ. of Toronto)
sources.developer: Goldie Nejat lab, University of Toronto
sources.title: Long-Term Exercise Assistance: Group and One-on-One Interactions between a Social Robot and Seniors (Robotics, MDPI)
sources.claim: An autonomous socially assistive Pepper robot facilitated repeated one-on-one and group upper-body exercise sessions with older adults over a long-term study inside a long-term care facility, adapting to affect, tracking goal attainment and monitoring heart rate to prevent ....

sources.system: Socially intelligent robot fitness coach (Pepper), Bristol Robotics Laboratory
sources.title: World's first robotic personal trainer guides gym-goers through exercise programme | UWE Bristol
sources.claim: A Pepper robot coached gym users through repeated treadmill running sessions of the NHS Couch-to-5k programme in a university gym, personalising motivational prompts from heart rate, speed and mood after learning behaviours from a human fitness instructor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conducting a supervised cardio training session. Transfer is limited to sessions where the client is already positioned on one purpose-built machine (treadmill); it shows autonomous session-long pacing, monitoring and motivation, the coaching content of a guided machine-based workout.

sources.date: 2026-07 (page retrieved); machines in service at named YMCA branches
sources.title: Welcome to EGYM | YMCA of Western North Carolina
sources.claim: EGYM Smart Strength machines are installed in US commercial gyms (YMCA branches) where each machine physically sets the resistance and range of motion for the identified member, guides tempo and form on-screen, and sequences the member through a complete strength circuit.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conducting a prescribed strength-training session. The computer-controlled machines physically perform what the trainer does in a machine circuit — setting load and ROM per person, pacing reps, and moving the client through the session — with the client fixtured in the machine.

sources.title: Use Dynamic Weight Modes to Transform Your Strength Training – Tonal
sources.claim: Tonal's motor-driven digital-weight trainer detects a failing repetition and automatically reduces the applied load, performing the spotting function within a guided strength session.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spotting and load management during resistance training. It substantiates only the machine-presented case: force is applied and withdrawn by the device itself, not by handling a free barbell in an open gym.

sources.system: Social robots for physical activity in older adults (NAO, Pepper and others, review)
sources.title: Artificial intelligence-powered social robots for promoting physical activity in older adults: A systematic review (ScienceDirect)
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review finds AI-powered social robots have motivated older adults to engage ... physical activity across settings, including encouraging correct joint flexion and improving exercise adherence.
sources.transferJustification: Corroborating context for robot-led exercise sessions with older adults; autonomy varies across the included studies, so it is treated as supporting rather than decisive.

tasks.label: Teach individual and team sports to participants through instruction and demonstration, using knowledge of sports techniques and of participants' physical capabilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: One-on-one lesson in an individual sport at a club, court or studio (tennis, pickleball, golf, boxing/pad work, swim stroke work): trainer physically demonstrates the stroke or strike, feeds balls or holds pads, watches the client's execution, and corrects grip, stance, footwork and timing, sometimes by hands-on repositioning, adapting to the client's fitness and injury history.

Beginner table-tennis / ping-pong instruction and rally practice at a club, rec center or corporate fitness facility: instructor rallies with the participant at a standard table, gauges skill level, varies pace and placement, and gives short tips on timing, placement and stroke.

Group sport-skills class inside a gym studio (kickboxing, boxing conditioning, martial-arts basics, sports-conditioning bootcamp) with 10-25 participants of mixed ability: instructor demonstrates combinations from the front, keeps the class in time, scans the room, calls individual corrections, scales moves for beginners and stops unsafe form.

Team-sport skills and drills on an indoor court at a gym, rec center or school (basketball, volleyball, indoor soccer): set up and run drills, demonstrate passing/shooting/serving, rotate players, referee a scrimmage, and adjust drills to participants' physical capabilities.

Outdoor session on a field, park or beach (adult-league soccer or flag-football practice, sand volleyball, sport-conditioning bootcamp): carry and lay out cones/balls, demonstrate skills on uneven turf in wind, sun or cold, keep a mixed group organized while the public passes through.

In-home or client-site individual sport instruction (client's home gym, driveway hoop, backyard golf net, apartment building fitness room): work in a small, cluttered, non-standard space with whatever equipment the client owns, demonstrating technique and correcting form.

sources.title: Video: The record breaking robot that teaches humans how to play table tennis | Guinness World Records
sources.claim: Omron's FORPHEUS is a table-tennis robot recognized by Guinness World Records as the first robot table tennis ...; it uses vision and motion sensors to judge a player's skill during play and is described as teaching humans to play the game.

sources.title: CES2020 | OMRON Global
sources.claim: Later FORPHEUS generations shown at CES adapt coaching to the individual player, reading facial expression and skeletal data and adjusting return speed to encourage improvement; the rig is a purpose-built cell with a six-axis arm and overhead camera array around one end of a table.

sources.title: Ping-Pong Robot to Control Motivation of a Human Player | OMRON TECHNICS
sources.claim: Omron's own technical publication describes FORPHEUS as a ping-pong robot that sustains rallies with a human and interacts to keep the player motivated, confirming closed-loop autonomous play rather than teleoperation.

sources.title: Robot Learns to Play Badminton Against Humans
sources.claim: ETH Zurich's ANYmal-D learned, via reinforcement learning with onboard stereo vision, to play badminton against humans on a court, sustaining rallies of up to about ten shots - the state of the art for a robot as an athletic practice partner, with no instructional or corrective coaching function.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: playing a racket sport with a human. It shows machines can act as practice partners in a marked court, but it neither demonstrates technique for a learner nor diagnoses and corrects a participant's form, so it does not carry over to teaching.

sources.title: BotBoxer | Smart Boxing Machine for Your Gym
sources.claim: BotBoxer is a commercially sold robotic sparring machine installed in gyms and boxing studios: a sensored bag on a moving mount that autonomously slips punches, sets drills on a touchscreen and reports punch force and speed, but it does not demonstrate technique or correct a student's stance and form.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: combat-sport training in a gym. It substantiates only reactive drill delivery and quantitative feedback from a fixed machine, not instruction and demonstration of technique, so it cannot substitute for a boxing lesson.

sources.title: World's first robotic personal trainer guides gym goers through exercise programme
sources.claim: The most advanced robot 'personal trainer' reported is a Pepper humanoid in a university gym study that gives motivational voice prompts and gestures to a runner on a treadmill; its role is encouragement during a running programme, not teaching sports skills.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: coaching a client through exercise in a gym. It shows verbal motivation and gesture only, with no physical demonstration of sport technique or individualized error correction, so it does not transfer to teaching a sport.

sources.system: Socially assistive exercise robots (NAO/Zora-class and similar)
sources.title: Artificial intelligence-powered social robots for promoting physical activity in older adults: A systematic review
sources.claim: A 2025 systematic review of social robots promoting physical activity in older adults finds studies in nursing homes, senior living and community centers where robots lead simple exercise routines and encourage correct joint flexion; the movements are basic calisthenics led from a fixed position, not sport instruction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading exercise sessions in a facility. Sessions are staff-initiated, scripted routines of simple seated/standing movements, far below the demonstration, diagnosis and correction of sport technique required here.

Organize and promote activities, such as arts and crafts, sports, games, music, dramatics, social recreation, camping, and hobbies, taking into account the needs and interests of individual members.

tasks.label: Organize, lead, and promote interest in recreational activities, such as arts, crafts, sports, games, camping, and hobbies.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Youth day camp or after-school program: a counselor plans and runs a 45-90 minute block for 10-25 children in a school gym, cafeteria or playground - sets out cones/balls/craft supplies, explains and demonstrates the game or craft, forms teams, keeps order and enthusiasm, adapts to ability and mood, and cleans up.

Municipal parks & recreation / community center staff: organizes and runs drop-in open gym, youth sports clinics and league play - hauls and sets up nets, goals, scoreboards and equipment, officiates or coaches, manages sign-ups, and recruits participants at the counter and on the floor.

Long-term care / assisted living activity aide: announces and runs a recurring seated group activity (bingo, trivia, sing-along, chair exercise) for roughly 6-20 residents in the facility activity room - calls the game, paces it, helps individuals track their cards, draws in quiet residents, and closes the session.

Senior center or care-home hands-on activities: arts and crafts, baking, gardening club, holiday parties and escorted community outings - procures and distributes materials, physically demonstrates and assists residents with tools and fine work, manages spills and mobility needs.

Resident or outdoor day camp counselor: leads hiking, nature crafts, campfire programs, canoeing/waterfront and cabin group activities in woods, fields and waterfront taken as found - carries gear, rigs equipment, supervises safety in variable weather and terrain.

Resort, cruise ship, hotel or community special-event recreation staff: runs poolside games, deck tournaments, family game nights and festival activity booths - sets up equipment and prizes, roams to recruit guests, hosts and scores the activity, and resets between rounds.

sources.developer: Autonomous Systems and Biomechatronics Lab, University of Toronto / Dr. Robot Inc.
sources.title: Robot-Delivered Cognitive Stimulation Games for Older Adults: Usability and Acceptability Evaluation
sources.claim: The socially assistive robot Tangy autonomously facilitated group bingo game sessions for older adults inside a long-term care facility, calling numbers, displaying them, and giving individual players assistance.
sources.transferJustification: Directly this task: facilitating a group recreational game for residents in a care facility.

sources.title: A User-Study with Tangy the Bingo Facilitating Robot and Long-Term Care Residents (IRIS 2016)
sources.claim: User study in which seven long-term care residents took part in six one-hour bingo sessions run by Tangy; the paper studied the robot's efficacy in autonomously facilitating the group recreational activity.

sources.system: NAO socially assistive exercise coach (Fasola & Mataric)
sources.title: An Autonomous Robot-to-Group Exercise Coach at a Senior Living Community: A Study in Human-Robot Interaction
sources.claim: A NAO humanoid was programmed as an autonomous exercise instructor ..., running a warm-up plus a guided physical exercise routine with a group of residents.
sources.transferJustification: Leading group chair exercise is one of the recreational activities recreation workers run in senior settings; same participants, same activity room, same session structure.

sources.developer: University of Georgia (Beer lab) et al.
sources.title: Facilitating Resident Interaction Through Robot-Delivered Trivia in Assisted Living Settings, Innovation in Aging
sources.claim: Pepper robots delivered structured trivia sessions (introduction, Q&A, discussion prompts, closing) to groups of 2-16 residents across two assisted living facilities; the report does not establish that the robot ran without operator control.

sources.system: SoftBank Pepper in nursing home recreation
sources.title: Inside Japan's long experiment in automating elder care, MIT Technology Review
sources.claim: A Japanese nursing home used Pepper to run daily afternoon recreation sessions, but a care worker had to boot the robot up, wheel it to the front of the room, and work to get residents to participate; the routine was prerecorded.

sources.title: Meet Abi, The Bubble-Blowing Startup Robot Bringing Fun To Senior Homes, Upstarts Media
sources.claim: Abi, a companion robot commercially deployed in aged care homes (104 tracked sessions Feb 2024-Dec 2025) for conversation and playful activities, is currently managed by staff from an internal app rather than running autonomously.

sources.title: Using the Humanoid Robot KASPAR to Autonomously Play Triadic Games and Facilitate Collaborative Play Among Children With Autism
sources.claim: The humanoid KASPAR autonomously played triadic turn-taking and imitation games with children with autism in primary schools - a supervised, seated interaction with one or two children rather than leading a full group recreation session.
sources.transferJustification: Closest evidence to leading games with children; cited to show its scope (one or two seated children, adult-supervised) falls short of running a camp or after-school activity block.

tasks.label: Manage the daily operations of recreational facilities.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Municipal community recreation center: the recreation worker runs the day — sets the daily staff assignment/shift coverage, checks the room and gym booking schedule against actual use, handles registrations and fee collection at the front desk, resolves patron complaints and scheduling conflicts, logs incidents and attendance, and reports issues (broken equipment, custodial needs) to maintenance. Decisions are made and communicated verbally, by phone, and in the facility's registration/scheduling software.

Aquatic center or indoor pool operation: recreation supervisor sets the lifeguard rotation and break schedule, reviews chemical and safety-check logs submitted by staff, decides on pool closures or capacity limits, coordinates swim-lesson and lap-swim block scheduling, tracks certifications, and files daily operations and incident reports with the parks department.

Summer day camp or after-school program site: the site director runs daily operations — counselor assignments and ratios, headcounts and sign-in/sign-out records, the day's activity rotation and rain-plan decisions, supply ordering and inventory requests, parent communication, and end-of-day reporting to the agency office.

Sports complex, athletic fields, or gymnasium under a park district: staff member manages field/court permits and rentals, adjusts league and tournament schedules, coordinates with officials and groundskeeping, approves weather-related cancellations, monitors facility use against reservations, and keeps usage and revenue records.

Senior center, resort/cruise activity office, or hospital-based therapeutic recreation unit: activity director plans and posts the daily activity calendar, assigns staff and volunteers to rooms and programs, orders supplies within a budget, coordinates transportation and outside entertainers, and maintains participation records and required documentation.

tasks.label: Administer first aid according to prescribed procedures and notify emergency medical personnel when necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Minor open wound at a day camp, playground or community-center program: a child falls and scrapes a knee/elbow or gets a small cut or splinter. Worker kneels to the child, calms them, inspects the wound, irrigates and wipes it with antiseptic, removes grit, selects and applies an adhesive bandage or gauze, checks for other injury, and writes an incident note.

Closed soft-tissue injury during a gym, sports or game program: jammed finger, rolled ankle, bumped head, bruise. Worker stops play, asks about pain/mechanism, checks range of motion and swelling, applies an instant cold pack, elevates or wraps the limb, holds the participant out of play, monitors for concussion signs, and phones the parent or supervisor.

Outdoor camp/park incident: nosebleed, insect sting, blister, sunburn, minor burn, or heat exhaustion on a field, trail or picnic area away from the first-aid room. Worker pinches the nose or removes the stinger, moves the person to shade, gives water, cools skin, watches for worsening symptoms, and radios base.

Medical emergency with a known condition: anaphylaxis, asthma attack, seizure or hypoglycemia in a program participant. Worker recognizes symptoms, retrieves the participant's epinephrine auto-injector or inhaler, assists with or administers the dose (through clothing, into the outer thigh), positions and protects the person, calls 911, and stays with them until EMS arrives.

Life-threatening emergency: unresponsive person with no normal breathing at a pool deck, gym or senior program (cardiac arrest, near-drowning). Worker checks responsiveness and breathing, directs a bystander to call 911 and bring the AED, gives chest compressions and rescue breaths, applies AED pads and follows prompts, manages the crowd, and hands off to paramedics.

Serious trauma at the site as found: fall from playground equipment or a collision producing a suspected fracture, head/neck injury or heavily bleeding wound. Worker keeps the person still, applies direct pressure with gloves and gauze, improvises support, prevents spinal movement, summons EMS and guides them in.

sources.title: Performance, Safety, and Patient Experience of an Autonomous Robotic Phlebotomy Device: A Multicenter Trial (Clinical Chemistry)
sources.claim: Vitestro's autonomous robotic phlebotomy device performs a full venipuncture on human patients in clinics and applies an adhesive bandage, but only with a cooperative adult placing an arm into the machine's fixture at one standard site.
sources.transferJustification: Closest demonstrated analog to applying a dressing to a person: an autonomous machine contacting live human skin and placing an adhesive bandage. Transfer to first aid fails because the site is fixed and known, the patient is a calm adult who fixtures their own arm, and the machine cannot search for, irrigate or size a dressing to an arbitrary wound.

sources.title: Robot performs autonomous needle-less injection (Robotics and Automation Magazine)
sources.claim: The Cobi platform performed an autonomous needle-free intramuscular injection into a standing, cooperative volunteer who checked in at the machine; a one-off university/startup demonstration, not a fielded emergency-medication system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous intramuscular injection, the mechanical core of giving an epinephrine auto-injector. Transfer fails: the demo needs a registered, still, cooperative patient at a kiosk, and excludes recognizing anaphylaxis, positioning a collapsing child, and post-dose monitoring.

sources.title: Robots Are Starting to Make Decisions in the Operating Room (IEEE Spectrum)
sources.claim: The most advanced autonomous soft-tissue robot, STAR, autonomously sutures tissue only in an operating room on anesthetized animals with fluorescent markers and under surgeon supervision; autonomous robots are not yet operating on people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous manipulation of living soft tissue (wound closure). It marks the frontier: even in a controlled OR with markers, an immobilized anesthetized subject and a supervising surgeon, autonomy covers one planned suturing step, far short of assessing and treating a conscious injured child.

sources.system: ROSCER remote-controlled automatic chest compression device
sources.developer: NT Robot Co. / Korean research group
sources.title: A remote-controlled automatic chest compression device capable of moving compression position during CPR: A pilot study in a mannequin and a swine model of cardiac arrest (PLOS One)
sources.claim: Automated chest-compression hardware for cardiac arrest is placed on the patient by a human rescuer, and the mobile research prototype is driven by a remote operator; no cited system autonomously reaches a collapsed person and performs CPR.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is mechanical CPR. Even this dedicated device is teleoperated and must be positioned on the chest by a person, so it cannot replace the worker who finds the victim, checks breathing, starts compressions and applies the AED.

sources.title: Underwater rescue robot - Fraunhofer IOSB-AST
sources.claim: An autonomous underwater rescue robot stationed in a swimming pool can locate a person in distress and bring them to the surface, but its function ends at retrieval; it provides no first aid.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is aquatic rescue at a pool, the step preceding first aid for a near-drowning. It does not substantiate this task: the robot performs no airway check, rescue breathing, compressions or AED use.

sources.system: Medical Swarm Robotics for Extraction and Life-Saving Interventions (MASH-related STTR)
sources.title: Medical Swarm Robotics for Extraction and Life-Saving Interventions: STTR | DARPA
sources.claim: As of 2026 DARPA is soliciting research to create autonomous robots that assess wounds and deliver trauma care, indicating the capability is a research goal rather than a fielded system.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (autonomous hemorrhage control and casualty care), but it is a solicitation of intent and so cannot support a positive judgment; cited only to show no such autonomous first-aid robot is fielded today.

tasks.label: Explain principles, techniques, and safety procedures to participants in recreational activities and demonstrate use of materials and equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Youth sports and active games at a rec-center gym, park ballfield, or day camp: the leader explains the rules and the safety points, physically demonstrates a skill with real equipment (dribble, batting stance, serve, stretch), then watches a group of 8-25 children try it and corrects individual form.

Arts, crafts, and hobby instruction in a community-center or senior-center craft room: the leader demonstrates tools and materials (scissors, hot glue gun, needle and thread, brushes, clay, beads), explains technique and tool safety, and shows individuals again when they get stuck.

Camp outdoor/waterfront activity instruction: archery range, canoe/kayak dock, climbing wall, or campfire - safety briefing and range/dock rules, fitting PFDs, harnesses and arm guards on participants, demonstrating the gear and the stroke/shot, then supervising the first attempts.

Group wellness and recreation session at a senior center, adult day-care, or long-term care facility: the leader explains and demonstrates seated exercise, tai chi, or dance movements, cues participants on safe range of motion, and runs games such as bingo or trivia with the group.

Structured indoor group-game or activity session for children/teens at a community center, after-school program, or camp classroom: explain the rules of the game or craft-free activity, demonstrate a round, answer questions, and keep a group of children engaged and on task.

Drop-in public program in an unstructured setting - park nature program, playground pop-up, beach or festival booth: explain the activity and demonstrate the equipment (fishing rod, nature kit, lawn game) to a walk-up, mixed-age crowd whose size and composition change minute to minute.

tasks.label: Direct special activities or events, such as aquatics, gymnastics, or performing arts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Directing aquatics programming at a community/YMCA indoor pool: running the swim-lesson block or water-aerobics session, positioning instructors and participants in lanes, demonstrating strokes from the deck and in the water, physically supporting or repositioning nervous swimmers and children, continuously scanning for distress and intervening, adjusting the plan for late arrivals, chemistry closures, or a crowded deck.

Directing a youth gymnastics/tumbling class in a rec-center gym: dragging out mats, wedges and beams and setting the circuit, demonstrating skills, hand-spotting children through rolls, handstands and back handsprings, keeping a line of 10-15 kids rotating safely, and handling behavior and minor injuries.

Directing a performing-arts activity at a rec/community center: running drama-club rehearsals or a talent show/dance recital, blocking and cueing performers, arranging chairs, props, mics and lighting, keeping a running order backstage, adapting live when a performer freezes, is late, or equipment fails.

Directing an outdoor special event at a park or camp: field day, holiday festival or youth sports tournament — setting up stations and equipment, briefing volunteers, starting heats, moving crowds between activities, handling weather changes, lost children and equipment breakdowns on ground taken as found.

Leading a seated group exercise / call-and-response recreation segment (chair exercises, stretching, quiz or sing-along) from the front of the room for residents at a senior center or adult day facility, with staff present in the room.

Directing a fuller activity session for seniors or special-population participants at a senior/community center: setting up tables and materials, distributing supplies, assisting participants with mobility or grip, adapting the activity individually, managing cognitive or behavioral issues and safety incidents through to clean-up.

Activity room at a senior center, care facility, or hospital rec program: puts up themed seasonal decorations, arranges chairs and tables for wheelchair access, sets out bingo cage/cards, craft supplies and prizes, and sets up a music player or TV, working around residents already in the room.

Running the entertainment during the event itself: operating the music/AV, cueing a performer or DJ, handing out props, prizes and craft materials, leading the group through games, and continuously adjusting decorations, tables and equipment as a crowd of participants moves through the space.

instances.label: Assisted living / skilled nursing facility outing: activity director loads 8-12 residents (walkers, wheelchairs, some with dementia) onto the facility bus, secures wheelchairs on the lift, drives to a restaurant, mall, or scenic drive, escorts residents inside, helps with seating, ordering, paying, and restrooms, watches for fatigue or medical incidents, does head counts, and returns everyone safely.

Group home or adult day program for people with intellectual/developmental disabilities: staff takes 3-6 clients by van or on foot to a grocery store, park, bowling alley, or movie; provides prompting and money-handling supervision, manages behavior in public, keeps the group together, and returns them home.

Parks-and-recreation or camp field trip: recreation worker accompanies 20-30 children on a chartered/agency bus to a zoo, pool, museum, or ballgame; counts heads, crosses streets with the group, escorts to restrooms, handles minor injuries and behavior, and returns all children to pickup.

Short walking outing from a senior residence: worker pushes one to three wheelchairs or walks alongside residents to a nearby park, coffee shop, or farmers market on public sidewalks, negotiating curb cuts, driveways, traffic crossings, weather, and rest stops.

Large special-event outing: casino trip, county fair, holiday-light tour, or professional sports game; coordinates tickets and venue accessibility, manages a larger group over several hours in dense crowds and unpredictable conditions, handles toileting, medication timing, and lost-participant contingencies.

sources.title: Waymo begins fully autonomous ops with 6th-gen Driver, targets 1M weekly rides
sources.claim: Waymo operates a fully driverless, commercially available ride-hailing service on public roads in multiple US cities, carrying millions of paid passenger trips per year, but the service only conveys passengers between points; it provides no boarding assistance, escorting at the destination, or supervision of a group.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: point-to-point passenger transport on public roads. It covers only the driving sub-step of a community outing; it does not cover wheelchair loading, escorting into venues, or duty-of-care supervision, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole instance.
