instances.label: Retail auto parts store (chain such as AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA/Advance): a DIY or pro customer asks for a part at the counter; the salesperson looks it up, walks the showroom aisles or back stock room, pulls a small boxed item (filter, brake pads, sensor, belt, wipers, spark plugs) off standard shelving, brings it to the register and hands it over; if not on hand, keys a same-day order to the hub/DC.

Franchise dealership parts department: filling ticket after ticket of OEM parts for service technicians, body shop and wholesale accounts from bin shelving and racks in the parts room, mostly small-to-medium boxed components, staged on the counter or in a bin for the tech; out-of-stock lines are special-ordered through the DMS to the OEM parts distribution center.

Orders that include heavy, bulky or oversized stock - batteries, brake rotors, exhaust and suspension assemblies, bumper covers, tires, ag/heavy-truck components - pulled from floor stock, pallet racks or the outside yard, moved with a cart, hand truck or forklift and loaded into the customer's vehicle or onto a delivery truck.

Wholesale parts distribution center / hub counter: batch-filling store, fleet and jobber orders in a parts warehouse - picking many line items to totes for delivery routes, then confirming and staging them for the driver; backorders placed with vendors.

Small independent parts store, specialty (marine, motorcycle, farm, industrial) counter or repair-shop parts room: stock held in a mix of bins, loose piles, mislabeled boxes, mezzanines and back rooms whose layout is idiosyncratic to the site; the counterperson finds the item, often verifying it against the old part, and orders anything not on hand.

tasks.label: Receive and fill telephone orders for parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail auto parts store (chain or independent): phone order from a DIY customer or a local repair shop for common small/medium boxed items (filters, brake pads, plugs, sensors, wipers, belts, quarts of oil). Counterperson looks up the SKU by year/make/model, walks the sales floor and back stockroom, picks the boxed part, and stages it at the will-call counter or bags it for the hotshot delivery driver.

Franchise dealership parts department: phone order from a wholesale body shop, fleet, or independent technician. Look up by VIN/part number in the DMS, pull small bin stock and boxed OE parts from shelving and mezzanine racking, verify part numbers against the pick ticket, and stage on the wholesale delivery shelf for the parts driver.

Heavy-duty truck / agricultural / industrial parts distributor: phone order for boxed but heavy items (brake drums, hubs, hydraulic pumps, cases of filters, pails of fluid) up to ~50 lb, picked from warehouse racking, sometimes in full-case or palletized quantities, and staged on the shipping dock.

Phone order for bulky, irregular, often unboxed inventory — tires and wheels, radiators, exhaust sections, bumper covers, batteries — that must be retrieved from floor stock or overhead racking and staged for pickup or the delivery truck.

Interpretive phone order: the caller describes a symptom or an old part rather than a part number. The salesperson questions the caller, checks interchange/fitment and superseded numbers, sometimes compares against stock on hand, selects the correct SKU (and any related items), then picks and stages it.

Requested part not in local stock: the salesperson sources it from the DC, hub store, or another branch, commits the order, and later receives the inbound shipment off the truck, checks it against the packing slip, labels it and stages it in the will-call/hold area for the customer.

sources.title: Brightpick Unlocks Lights-Out Fulfillment with Autopicker
sources.claim: Brightpick's Autopicker is a commercially deployed autonomous mobile manipulator that picks individual items out of totes and shelves into order containers at roughly human productivity, and now runs lights-out with no humans present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: e-commerce/wholesale order picking. Filling a phoned-in parts order is the same physical act — locate the SKU in stock, retrieve the boxed item, place it in an order container for staging — on comparable small-to-medium boxed goods at comparable precision.

sources.system: Brightpick goods-to-person robots (Retriever/Giraffe) at NAPA DCs
sources.title: Brightpick enters automotive market through strategic partnership with NAPA
sources.claim: NAPA, a major US automotive replacement-parts distributor, has been running Brightpick robotic fulfillment automation in its distribution centers since a 2025 pilot and contracted a further site with 100+ robots to serve its store network.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automotive aftermarket order fulfillment and store replenishment. The objects are exactly the parts a parts salesperson sells, and the output is a picked, staged order for a store or customer.

sources.system: AutoStore R5 robots / Kardex at Emil Frey Logistik
sources.title: Warehouse Automation Increases Storage Capacity 300% (Emil Frey case)
sources.claim: An automotive spare-parts logistics provider fills parts orders out of a robot-operated cube storage grid: robots autonomously retrieve, sort and deliver bins of spare parts to order-picking ports at two German distribution centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spare-parts storage and retrieval. It substantiates that automotive parts inventory can be held and presented to a picking station entirely by machine, i.e. the work brought to the machine in a purpose-built setting.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm, working inside a caged cell in fulfillment centers, autonomously detects and picks individual products of widely varying shape, size and weight from bins into order totes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level order picking. The physical act (identify a specific SKU among mixed inventory, grasp it, place it into the order tote) matches filling a parts order; SKU variety exceeds a parts store's catalogue.

sources.title: Amazon unveils Vulcan robot meant to reduce worker strain at fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously picks and stows items to and from densely packed storage pods in live fulfillment centers, handling roughly three quarters of stored product types.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving items from high and low shelf locations. Parts picking likewise requires reaching cluttered bin locations at varying heights; the demonstrated envelope covers the majority of small boxed goods.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch mobile robot autonomously handles boxed cases in warehouses at up to 700 cases per ..., deployed by DHL across multiple countries for trailer unloading and case handling.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: case handling and inbound trailer unloading. Heavy boxed parts and cases of filters/fluids are the same class of object, and receiving/staging an inbound special order is the same physical act performed on the same dock.

sources.title: Stronger MBR800+ robot - Cimcorp
sources.claim: Cimcorp's gantry robots pick individual tires and stacks autonomously and are used as the picking element of order-picking systems in tire distribution centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: tire order picking in distribution centers. Tires and wheels are the archetypal bulky, heavy, unboxed parts-store item; picking them individually to fill a customer order is the same physical act.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Piece-picking robots from RightHand Robotics are deployed across a major retailer's North American fulfillment centers, autonomously picking individual mixed items with manual intervention rates reported as low as 0.01%.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: item-level order fulfillment of general merchandise/office supplies — small boxed goods comparable to shelf-stock auto parts — performed in an enclosed robotic picking station.

sources.title: Sanctuary’s Humanoid Robot Is for General-Purpose Autonomy - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: The one humanoid retail-store deployment that performed store picking and packing of orders relied on teleoperation rather than autonomy, so no cited system autonomously fills orders from human retail shelving.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant negative: this is the closest instance of a robot picking and packing customer orders inside a working retail store, and it was teleoperated, so it cannot support an E2 judgment.

sources.title: Agility's ‘hardest working’ humanoid robot hits 100,000-tote milestone
sources.claim: Humanoid robots working in live, human-occupied warehouses are so far limited to moving totes and containers between conveyors, AMRs and floor locations — not to identifying and picking individual SKUs from stock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: material movement in a shared human facility. It shows what mobile robots reliably do in an E2-type facility (whole-tote handling), and by contrast that SKU-level order filling there is not yet substantiated.

tasks.label: Locate and label parts, and maintain inventory of stock.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain auto parts store or dealership parts room: the daily stock truck arrives with 100-400 boxed parts (filters, sensors, brake pads, belts, gaskets). Worker unpacks, scans each against the invoice, applies price/SKU labels, and puts each part in its bin location on back-room shelving, pegboard and floor gondolas, updating the POS/DMS on-hand record.

Locating a specific part from stock: worker reads the bin location from the system, walks the aisles, finds the right box among visually similar SKUs (including misplaced or overstock locations), verifies the part number, tags it with the customer name / repair-order ticket, and stages it on the will-call shelf or counter.

Routine inventory audit in the store or parts room: walking aisles to check on-hand versus system, spotting empty or short bins, wrong or missing shelf/bin tags, price discrepancies and obviously misplaced stock, and feeding the findings back into the ordering/inventory system.

Periodic full physical or cycle count: unit-level counting of parts stacked deep inside bins, drawers and overstock racks (including loose hardware and returned/opened boxes), reconciling counts against the system, correcting bin labels and consolidating stock into the right locations.

Bulky and heavy stock: batteries, tire and wheel stacks, cases of oil, exhaust and body panels, rotors and equipment parts received on pallets; worker moves them with hand truck, cart or forklift, labels them, racks them in the back room, mezzanine or fenced outdoor yard, and counts them periodically.

Unstructured settings: independent repair shop back room, off-site storage container or salvage/recycler yard, where legacy and used parts sit loose, unmarked or in reused boxes on ad hoc shelving; worker identifies the part by sight and fitment, hand-writes or prints a tag, and adds it to a rough inventory record.

sources.title: RBR50 Spotlight: Exotec Skypod system scales to serve automotive supplier's SKU volume
sources.claim: Exotec's Skypod ASRS is deployed at Lane Automotive, an aftermarket automotive parts distributor stocking over 100,000 SKUs, where robot fleets store, locate and retrieve boxed parts from high-density racks and deliver them to picking stations, with inventory tracking handled by the system.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated storage/retrieval of the same objects (boxed automotive parts, 100k+ SKUs). It substantiates the machine-side of 'locate parts and maintain inventory of stock': the robots hold every part in a known machine-readable location and the system keeps the on-hand record, which is what the parts salesperson's bin-location and stock-record work produces.

sources.title: Auto Parts Supplier Quadruples Storage Capacity | AutoStore
sources.claim: AutoStore grid systems with robots, storage bins and inbound conveyor ports are installed at automotive spare-parts distributors (Bertel O. Steen, Emil Frey Logistik) for high-density storage and order handling of small and medium parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is automated small-parts warehousing for an auto parts supplier; inbound ConveyorPorts and robot-managed bins mean parts are inducted, stored in machine-known locations and inventoried without a person walking bins, matching the storage/locating/inventory portion of this task with identical objects.

sources.title: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force sensing to stow items
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously stows items into and picks items from fabric storage pods ... fulfillment centers, handling roughly three-quarters of item types at human-comparable speed; it is in full operation in Spokane and Hamburg.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic stowing of mixed retail merchandise into bin storage. It transfers to parts put-away because the objects (small boxed/loose goods of varied shape), the precision (placing an item into a designated bin without damage) and the record-keeping (each stow updates the inventory location) are equivalent to shelving a part in its bin.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch is commercially deployed by DHL to unload cases from trailers and containers at rates up to 700 cases per ..., with an agreement for over 1,000 additional units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous handling of heavy cases arriving on a truck. It transfers to the bulky-stock instance because the objects (cases up to ~50 lb such as oil, batteries, boxed hardware) and the receiving-to-conveyor motion match the heavy receiving and staging step of parts stocking.

sources.system: Badger Technologies retail robot with Retail InForm
sources.title: McCoy's Building Supply Uses Badger Robots to Verify Availability, Pricing of Retail Hardware Products
sources.claim: Badger Technologies' autonomous multipurpose robots are deployed across McCoy's Building Supply hardware stores, performing daily store-wide inventory shelf scans that detect out-of-stock items and price/tag integrity problems, replacing up to 50 hours per ... of associate shelf inspection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is store-wide shelf inventory and price-tag auditing in a hardware retailer, whose SKU-dense boxed merchandise and aisle layout closely resemble an auto parts store; the delivered output (verified on-shelf availability, tag and stock discrepancies fed to the inventory system) is the same as the parts salesperson's routine inventory check.

sources.title: Simbe end user survey validates that Tally can transform inventory management
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally shelf-scanning robot autonomously traverses store aisles and extracts item SKUs and inventory counts; it is deployed in roughly a thousand stores across several retail verticals including wholesale clubs and home-improvement chains.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous in-store inventory verification. It transfers to the parts-store inventory check because it operates in the same kind of institution-controlled retail aisle on packaged, barcoded merchandise and produces the SKU-level on-shelf counts a parts salesperson gathers by walking the bins.

sources.title: Reducing Inventory Cycle Counting Time with a Drone-Powered Monitoring Solution
sources.claim: Gather AI's drones fly autonomously inside operating warehouses without infrastructure changes, scanning racking to produce cycle counts including inferred case counts; deployments include GEODIS, NFI Industries, Barrett Distribution and AAFES.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous cycle counting of stock in racking. It transfers to 'maintain inventory of stock' because the output is the same reconciled count of labeled stock against system records, though it reads pallet/case locations rather than counting loose units deep inside small-parts bins.

sources.system: K-Label labeling system (Kawasaki robot + REA print-and-apply)
sources.developer: Kawasaki Robotics with REA LABEL ES
sources.title: Automatic labeling: easier, faster, more reliable
sources.claim: A Kawasaki industrial robot combined with a print-and-apply labeling system (K-Label) automatically prints and applies logistics labels to outbound goods at GROHE, replacing manual label application.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is robotic print-and-apply labeling of goods in a logistics flow; it substantiates the 'label parts' step because the action (print the correct identifying label and place it accurately on a presented item/unit load) is identical, and such applicators are standard equipment on distribution-center conveyor lines.

sources.title: RightHand Robotics Introduces RightPick 4 System
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick 4 is a commercially sold autonomous piece-picking system that handles individual items across general merchandise, office supplies, apparel and pharmaceutical verticals in distribution centers, with increased item size and weight range.
sources.transferJustification: Related task is autonomous each-picking from presented bins. It transfers to locating/pulling a specific part because, once an ASRS presents the bin, isolating and transferring the correct individual boxed item to an outbound container is the same manipulation with the same class of small packaged goods.

tasks.label: Examine returned parts for defects, and exchange defective parts or refund money.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail auto parts store counter: a customer brings back an installed, used part (alternator, starter, battery, sensor, brake component) claiming it failed. The counterperson looks it over for signs of abuse, wrong installation, burn marks or cracked housings, often bench-tests it on the store's alternator/starter/battery tester, then either hands over a replacement off the shelf or refunds the purchase at the POS.

Retail counter: an unused part in original packaging is returned (wrong part, no longer needed). The worker verifies part number against the receipt, opens/inspects the box for completeness, missing hardware, grease marks, or scratched/installed condition, decides it is resalable, refunds the card or cash, and restocks it on the shelf.

Dealership or heavy-duty/industrial parts department: a technician or fleet shop returns parts ordered for a job, plus core returns. The parts specialist inspects each item for installation marks or damage, checks the core is the correct, complete unit, restocks into bins/racks, and issues a credit to the shop's account.

Disputed case: the returned part is clearly abused, cross-threaded, contaminated, modified, or was not sold by this store; or the failure cause is ambiguous. The worker must judge warranty eligibility, deny or grant the claim, explain the decision to an unhappy customer, and package the part for a supplier warranty claim.

Online/phone-order return received by mail at the store or parts distribution counter: open the shipping carton, verify the item matches the order, inspect its condition, issue the refund in the system, and restock or route the part back to the distribution center.

sources.title: Turn Your Old Phone Into Cash: Everything About ecoATM Recycling
sources.claim: ecoATM kiosks placed in US retail locations autonomously accept a used device from a member of the public into an evaluation chamber, scan it, test power-on, screen and buttons, assess physical condition, price it and pay cash on the spot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: buy-back of a used consumer device. It is the same inspect-a-returned-item-for-defects-then-pay-money loop, performed unattended, but only for a narrow catalog of small standardized electronics placed into a purpose-built chamber, not for arbitrary auto parts handed across a counter.

sources.title: Can You Sell a Broken Phone or Broken Tablet - ecoatm
sources.claim: The ecoATM network comprises over 5,000 automated kiosks in the US performing instant evaluation and payment for devices in any condition, including cracked or non-powering units.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: establishes scale and commercial maturity of unattended defect evaluation plus cash payout, for a single standardized product class.

sources.system: TOMRA Basic Line / B5 Combi, T9, R1 reverse vending machines
sources.title: TOMRA launches Basic Line reverse vending machines for retailers new to deposit return schemes
sources.claim: TOMRA reverse vending machines deployed in supermarkets autonomously recognize returned containers with 360-degree barcode scanning, camera, weight and metal sensors, reject ineligible items and pay an accurate deposit refund.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: accepting a returned container, verifying its identity and eligibility, rejecting damaged/ineligible items and issuing a refund. Same verify-then-refund loop with machine-vision identification, but only for one rigid, standardized object class fed into a purpose-built intake.

sources.system: GameStop automated mobile device grading robots
sources.title: A Look into GameStop's Automated Mobile Device Grading Program
sources.claim: GameStop runs a robotic grading system at its production facility that automatically inspects traded-in/returned mobile devices for cosmetic defects, identifying scratches, chips, cracks, dents and chassis damage and assigning a grade used for pricing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: grading returned merchandise for damage. It substantiates automated visual defect adjudication of customer-returned goods in a purpose-built cell, which is the examination half of this task; objects are standardized handhelds rather than greasy automotive components.

sources.title: AI robot grades, erases up to 55 phones an hour
sources.claim: Phonecheck launched a robot that automatically ... used device's cosmetic condition, runs functional diagnostics and erases data at up to 55 devices per hour, sold to electronics refurbishers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: combined cosmetic grading and functional testing of returned goods. Demonstrates a machine rendering the pass/grade verdict that a returns clerk would render, in a fixtured purpose-built enclosure.

sources.system: D&V Electronics ALT-198 / JBT-1 alternator and starter testers
sources.title: D&V Electronics Ltd. — product listing (Rematec)
sources.claim: D&V Electronics alternator/starter test stands run adjustable automated test profiles and produce customized pass/fail reports, and are marketed for warranty evaluation as well as end-of-line production testing; the JBT-1 countertop unit is designed for parts stores, warehouses and distribution centers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related: machine-controlled functional testing of the exact returned parts at issue (alternators, starters) to a pass/fail warranty verdict. The unit must be mounted into the bench by hand, which is precisely the fixtured presentation an E1 setting supplies.

sources.system: Cognex deep learning defect detection (ViDi / In-Sight)
sources.title: 4 Tools for Deep Learning Inspections | Cognex
sources.claim: Cognex AI/deep-learning machine vision systems are deployed on production lines to detect surface defects such as rust, dents, scratches and misalignments and to separate defective from acceptable parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated visual defect inspection of parts presented on a line. Same visual judgement (damage, corrosion, deformation) on comparable metal/plastic components; presentation is fixtured and lighting controlled, i.e., an E1 setting.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Staples deployed RightHand Robotics RightPick autonomous piece-picking arms across its North American fulfillment centers to handle items of varying shapes, sizes and weights, including items it has not seen before.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous handling of mixed retail SKUs in a caged picking cell. Supports the retrieve-replacement and restock/put-away steps of an exchange when the goods are presented to the machine in totes.

sources.title: FASTVend - Industrial Vending Solutions
sources.claim: Fastenal FASTVend industrial vending units autonomously dispense individual parts with verified-vend sensing and automate the check-out/return of items at customer facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended issue and return of parts against a user account. Supports the exchange/credit disposition step of this task for catalogued parts held in a machine-loaded cabinet.

sources.title: How Returns Kiosks Improve Retail Efficiency | BestKiosk
sources.claim: In-store self-service returns kiosks only scan the barcode and take the item into a locked bin; store staff subsequently open the unit and check which returned items are fit for refund and restocking.
sources.transferJustification: Negative context for the E2 counter setting: deployed retail return kiosks do not perform the defect examination, which remains a human step.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence TX SCARA robots were deployed to hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores, autonomously restocking about 1,000 standardized bottles and cans per day from a fixed overhead track with >98% success.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous item handling on the sales floor of a working store (E2). Shows what is demonstrated at E2 is restocking of one standardized product class on a fixed track, not inspection of arbitrary customer-returned merchandise.

sources.title: Vision guided robotic inspection for parts in manufacturing and remanufacturing industry
sources.claim: Visual inspection of returned used products (cores) in remanufacturing still relies heavily on manual work because of varying product condition, wide variant diversity and missing product information; flexible automated inspection remains a research problem.
sources.transferJustification: Negative context: the closest industrial analogue to adjudicating an arbitrary used automotive part returned in unknown condition is core inspection, which is documented as still manual and only at research stage for automation.

tasks.label: Manage shipments by researching shipping methods or costs and tracking packages.

tasks.label: Mark and store parts in stockrooms, according to prearranged systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain auto parts store (AutoZone/O'Reilly/NAPA type): the daily stock truck arrives; the counterperson checks totes/cartons of small-to-medium parts (filters, plugs, sensors, belts, wipers, brake pads) against the invoice, applies SKU/price/bin labels, and shelves each item in its assigned backroom bin or planogram location, updating overstock locations. Mixed packaging, some loose or blister-packed items, aisles shared with coworkers.

Same store, heavy/bulky/awkward stock: batteries, brake rotors, cases of oil and antifreeze, exhaust pipes and mufflers, body panels, tires. Items are marked with SKU/location tags and placed on floor racks, cantilever/bulk shelving or pallets, often moved with a hand truck or dolly.

Dealership or OEM parts department: a weekly stock order and daily emergency order are received, scanned into the DMS, bin-location labels printed and affixed, and parts put away into small-bin shelving, drawer cabinets and bulk racks according to the DMS-assigned bin scheme, including sheet metal and glass in the bulk area.

Returns, cores and put-backs: customer returns in opened or damaged boxes, greasy core units (alternators, calipers), and unsold parts pulled for orders that fell through. The worker inspects condition, decides restock vs. core/defective, re-marks the part or box, and returns it to the correct bin or core rack.

Heavy-duty truck, industrial or farm equipment parts operation with an attached warehouse: palletized and crated parts received at a dock, tagged with location/ID labels, and put away by forklift into pallet racking and bulk locations per the inventory system.

Small independent repair shop or mobile parts operation: parts kept in a cluttered, non-standard back room with improvised shelving; marking is by hand-written tag or marker on the box, and parts are stored wherever they fit within a loose personal system.

sources.title: Stow: Robotic Packing of Items into Fabric Pods (arXiv:2505.04572)
sources.claim: Amazon Robotics' Stow system autonomously places diverse individual items into densely packed fabric pod bins at a fulfillment-center stow station, having completed over 500,000 stows at human-level packing density and speed — the core act of putting a marked part into its assigned storage slot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: warehouse stowing. It is the same operation as stockroom putaway — placing a diverse mix of consumer-goods-sized items into a system-assigned compartment recorded by inventory software — at comparable object sizes and precision.

sources.title: How Amazon's Vulcan robots use touch to plan and execute motions - Amazon Science
sources.claim: Vulcan robots with force-sensing end effectors run in Amazon fulfillment centers in ..., WA and Hamburg, Germany, stowing items into and picking them from fabric pods that autonomous drive units carry to fixed stations — a work cell built around the machine.

sources.system: AutoStore cube AS/RS empowered by Kardex
sources.title: Case Study: Kardex AutoStore AS/RS deployed for MAHLE Aftermarket - Supply Chain 24/7
sources.claim: An AutoStore robotic cube AS/RS integrated with SAP WMS stores automotive aftermarket parts by system-assigned bin at MAHLE Aftermarket's Olive Branch, Mississippi distribution center, with 18 autonomous robots handling 42,000 bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage of automotive spare parts by assigned location. Same objects (aftermarket auto parts) and the same 'prearranged system' requirement — every unit tracked to a machine-assigned storage address.

sources.system: Weber Alpha HSM / LA6000 print-and-apply labeling systems
sources.title: License Plate Labels produced by Weber - Weber Labels UK
sources.claim: Commercial high-speed print-and-apply labelers automatically print and apply the WMS-generated barcode identity label to each handling unit (case, bin or pallet) as it is entered into the storage system, at up to 3,500 products per ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated marking of stock units. The 'mark' half of this task — printing and affixing an identifying/location barcode label to a part's box or handling unit — is exactly what these machines do in fixed labeling stations.

sources.title: Walmart plans to automate 25 distribution centers with Symbotic - Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Symbotic's system in Walmart regional distribution centers autonomously breaks down inbound pallets, stores goods at the case level in dense racking under algorithmic slotting, and retrieves them to build outbound pallets, at roughly 1,700 cases per hour per module.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated case-level receiving and putaway. Heavy cased goods (oil, batteries, rotors arrive cased) are handled and stored to machine-assigned rack locations, matching the weight and bulk of heavy parts-store stock.

sources.system: Daifuku Unit Load AS/RS / Mini Load AS/RS (MPM parts center)
sources.title: Revving up Efficiency in Automotive Spare Parts Centers | DAIFUKU
sources.claim: Automated unit-load AS/RS stacker cranes and mini-load systems are used in automotive spare parts centers to store large components such as bumpers, windshields ..., and a mini-load AS/RS deployment at parts distributor MPM handles 13,000 SKUs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated storage of bulky auto parts in a parts distribution center. Same objects (bumpers, windshields, exhausts) and the same requirement to place them in a system-recorded location.

sources.title: Automated Steel Storage System for SPS - Fabricating & Metalworking
sources.claim: A KASTO UNICOMPACT automated storage system at steel distributor Steel and Pipe Supply stores and retrieves long, heavy stock (bars, tubes) with digital inventory tracking of every location.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated racking of long goods. Exhaust pipes, tubing and long trim stored on cantilever racks in a parts stockroom are the same class of object, and the system assigns and records each storage location.

sources.system: Mobile-manipulator supermarket stocking system (From Pixels to Shelf)
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: The closest analogue to in-store shelf stocking by a mobile manipulator — an autonomous supermarket-stocking system — was validated in a laboratory replication of store conditions, and its authors report that current autonomous systems still fall short of human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stocking human shelving in a retail facility. It is the nearest evidence for an E2 judgment on stockroom putaway, and it shows the capability is not yet at worker quality outside purpose-built cells.

tasks.label: Maintain and clean work and inventory areas.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift floor cleaning of the retail parts-store sales floor: dust-mopping/sweeping and mopping or scrubbing the open aisles, entry mat area and checkout lane of a 5,000-10,000 sq ft store with fixed gondola shelving.

Floor upkeep of the stockroom/warehouse inventory area behind the counter: sweeping and scrubbing aisles between parts racking and the receiving area, clearing dust, packing peanuts and debris from around bins and the shipping bench.

Cleaning the parts counter and customer-facing displays: wiping the counter, POS terminal and keyboard, clearing catalogs/paperwork/loose parts, cleaning glass display cases, dusting merchandise shelves and straightening/facing product in the showroom.

Tidying and organizing the inventory area: returning stray and returned parts to their correct bins, removing empty cartons and packaging from shelves, breaking down cardboard for the baler, and hauling trash/recycling to the dumpster.

Cleaning the shop-side work area of a repair shop or dealership parts department: soaking up and sweeping oil, grease and coolant spills near the will-call window and service bays, degreasing shelving and benches, cleaning the receiving dock.
Cleaning the restroom and emptying trash receptacles in the store's back-of-house and customer restroom, including toilets/urinals, sinks, mirrors and restroom floors.

sources.title: Pudu CC1 At QT: How A 4-in-1 Floor Cleaning Robot Delivers Real ROI In Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Pudu CC1 autonomous 4-in-1 floor cleaning robots (sweep, scrub, vacuum, mop) have been rolled out across more than 1,200 QuikTrip convenience stores, replacing overnight manual scrubbing in small retail sales floors.
sources.transferJustification: A convenience-store sales floor is the same class of small retail floor (fixed gondola aisles, hard floor, merchandise displays) that a parts store's closing floor-cleaning duty covers.

sources.title: Walmart expands use of robotic floor scrubbers | Chain Store Age
sources.claim: Walmart is expanding its fleet of autonomous Tennant T7AMR floor scrubbers from about 300 stores to 1,500 additional store locations, automating in-store floor cleaning.

sources.title: Case Study: Robotic Scrubbers Help Albert Automate its Floor Cleaning - Brain Corp
sources.claim: A supermarket chain deployed a fleet of 40 BrainOS-powered Tennant T380AMR and ... across its national stores, operating alongside employees and customers.

sources.system: Brain Corp-powered autonomous floor scrubbers (with inventory scan towers)
sources.title: Robotic scrubbers scan inventory and clean floors at Sam's Club | Chain Store Age
sources.claim: Sam's Club runs autonomous floor-scrubbing robots chainwide in its warehouse-club stores, a racked, pallet-and-bulk-storage format comparable to a parts stockroom/back room.
sources.transferJustification: Warehouse-club aisles with steel racking, pallets and receiving areas are the closest deployed analog to sweeping/scrubbing the racked stockroom floor of a parts operation.

sources.title: Somatic - Autonomous Bathroom Cleaning Robots
sources.claim: Somatic's BCR is a commercially offered autonomous bathroom-cleaning mobile manipulator deployed in hospitals and airports that cleans toilets, urinals, fixtures and floors and picks up trash.

sources.title: Toilet-cleaning robot makes us feel better about all this AI business
sources.claim: Somatic's restroom robot runs autonomously in daily operation; only the initial site mapping/teaching is done by humans with a sensor kit and VR.

sources.title: Primech launches upgraded bathroom cleaning robot
sources.claim: Primech's HYTRON bathroom-cleaning mobile manipulator, launched in an upgraded version in 2025 and in commercial trials since 2023, autonomously navigates and performs multiple restroom cleaning tasks in airports, hospitals, malls and offices.

sources.system: Stäubli HE robots in washing/cleaning cells (user: Maschinenbau Silberhorn)
sources.title: Robotic solutions for washing-cleaning parts | Stäubli United States
sources.claim: Industrial robot arms are used in commercial fixtured cleaning cells for low- and high-pressure cleaning, degreasing, rinsing and drying of components in wet spray areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removing grease/oil/soil from surfaces presented to a robot in a fenced cell. With counters, shelving panels or greasy fixtures fixtured and presented as an E1 setting would present them, the wiping/degreasing motion and quality standard transfer directly.

sources.title: Fives' Smart Automation Solutions Division | RoboWash Robotic Industrial Parts Washer
sources.claim: Fives' RoboWash is a commercial robotic industrial washer in which a 6-axis robot manipulates parts through spray chambers to clear oil, chips, burrs and swarf contamination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: removal of oil and grease from work surfaces/hardware. In a purpose-built cell where the soiled item is presented to the machine, robotic wash cells achieve production-grade cleanliness, which is the E1 rendering of degreasing shop-area shelving and fixtures.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers | Supply Chain Dive
sources.claim: Staples deployed RightHand Robotics' autonomous RightPick piece-picking arms across its North American fulfillment centers, where the robots grip items of varying shapes, sizes, weights and packaging presented in totes and place them into destination bins.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting stray/returned parts back into their bins. Piece-picking cells grasp heterogeneous small SKUs presented in totes and place them into designated bin locations at commercial reliability — the E1 rendering of restoring order to an inventory area.

sources.title: Living Room Ready: Watch How Figure 03 Tackles Domestic Tidying with Helix 02 | Humanoids Daily
sources.claim: Figure demonstrated its Figure 03 humanoid, driven by the Helix 02 neural system, autonomously tidying a staged living room, including spraying and wiping a table surface and collecting and putting away loose objects.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: spray-and-wipe of a work surface plus clearing loose clutter, which is the manipulation core of cleaning a parts counter. It is a single staged demonstration with no reliability or throughput data, so it supports feasibility only in a highly structured, presented setting.

tasks.label: Place new merchandise on display.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain auto parts store sales floor: worker cuts open cartons on a stock cart and places small packaged parts (oil/air filters, spark plugs, wiper blades, bulbs, fuses, blister-pack accessories) onto gondola shelves and peg hooks per planogram, fronting/facing product and checking shelf label alignment, with customers moving through the aisle.

Heavy and bulky goods: cases of motor oil, gallon jugs of coolant/washer fluid, and batteries brought from receiving on a pallet jack or hand truck and stacked on bottom shelves, battery racks, and floor stack/pallet displays at the aisle ends.

Behind-the-counter and back-room stocking: newly received hard parts in mixed-size boxes (alternators, brake rotors, belts, sensors) placed into numbered bins, drawers, and back-wall racks in a parts store's counter area or a repair shop's parts room, in tight aisles with mixed box sizes.

Promotional/seasonal display build-out: assembling a cardboard shipper or POP floor display, positioning it on an endcap or front aisle, loading merchandise into it, and attaching signage and price cards per a corporate merchandising directive.

Small independent parts store or repair-shop parts counter with an ad hoc, cluttered layout and no planogram: worker finds space among existing stock, tools, and equipment, restacks and shifts items to make room, and places new merchandise on counters, wall shelves, and showcases.

sources.title: Amazon's Vulcan robot uses force sensing to stow items
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot autonomously stows individual retail-type items into shelf bins (fabric pods) in fulfillment centers, covering about 75% of item types at speeds comparable to human ...; it moved from pilot to beta and larger deployment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stowing new inventory into tightly packed shelf bins. It transfers to placing new merchandise on a store shelf/bin: comparable objects (small boxed and bagged consumer goods), comparable precision (force-controlled insertion into a constrained slot), in a purpose-built robotic station where the storage fixture is presented at a known pose.

sources.title: How Amazon's Vulcan robots use touch to plan and execute motions
sources.claim: Vulcan Stow plans the space needed for a new item in a shelf bin and uses a blade to push existing stock aside before inserting the item; six robots ran a pilot in Spokane, with a 30-robot beta and a larger German deployment following.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing storage bins with newly arrived merchandise. Making room among already-placed stock and inserting a new unit is the same manipulation as filling a partly full shelf or parts bin.

sources.system: FANUC SCARA / delta pick-and-place packaging cells
sources.title: Picking & Packing Industry's Most Trusted Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercially supplied industrial pick-and-place cells place consumer packaged goods, including blister packs, into retail trays and display groupings from conveyors under vision guidance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-speed placement of packaged retail goods into presented trays/cases. It matches the parts-store instance when the work is brought to the machine: items arrive singulated on a conveyor and the display fixture is presented at a fixed pose.

sources.title: From case unloading to picking and beyond with DHL and Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch performs autonomous case handling (truck/container unloading) at roughly 700 cases per hour and is in multi-site commercial deployment with DHL, which signed for 1,000 additional units.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: bulk case handling and stacking. Cases of motor oil and coolant jugs are the same class of heavy corrugated units; the demonstrated grasping, lifting, and stacking capability carries over when pallets and stack positions are presented as in a purpose-built cell.

sources.developer: Number1 / system integrator (reported by Packaging World)
sources.title: Robots assemble, pack, and stack grocery retail displays at 40/hr
sources.claim: An installed multi-robot line automatically builds, fills, and stacks cardboard box-pallet and tray displays used for retail grocery promotions, at about 40 displays per hour.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: erecting and loading promotional cardboard displays. This is the same physical output as a parts-store endcap shipper display, produced in a purpose-built cell where blanks and product are fed to the machine.

sources.title: Telexistence to Install AI Restocking Robots in 300 Convenience Stores Across Japan
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocks refrigerated beverage display shelves in about 300 FamilyMart convenience stores, running autonomously with remote human takeover only in rare error cases; TX Ghost now automates the majority of drink restocking with teleoperation retained for unpredictable errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing new merchandise on a retail display shelf inside a store. It is limited to uniform bottles and cans loaded from crates into one fixed, machine-adapted cooler, so it does not transfer to aisle-wide stocking of varied parts packaging.

sources.system: Hello Robot Stretch 3 + ROS2 autonomous stocking stack (KTH/Animum)
sources.developer: KTH Royal Institute of Technology / University of Padova / Animum AB
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: A mobile-manipulator shelf-stocking system achieved 98% pick-and-place success over 724 stocking events, but only in laboratory replications of supermarket conditions, and the authors report it remains inferior to human workers in performance and cost.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the same task (autonomous shelf stocking of retail merchandise); cited as the state of the art showing that in-store aisle stocking is not yet at worker quality.

tasks.label: Demonstrate equipment to customers, and explain functioning of equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail auto parts store, counter or aisle: a walk-in customer is considering a device (OBD-II code reader, jump pack, battery charger, digital torque wrench, brake bleeder). The counterperson takes the demo unit or opens the box, powers/connects it, runs it through its main functions, points out controls and readouts, and answers follow-up questions amid other shoppers.

Store parking lot / at the customer's own vehicle: the counterperson carries out the demonstration on the car itself - clamping a battery/charging-system tester to the terminals under the hood, plugging a scan tool into the OBD port under the dash, or showing how a wiper blade, bulb or filter clips into place on that specific vehicle, explaining the readings as they go. Varied vehicles, weather, curbside conditions.

Farm-equipment, outdoor-power-equipment or heavy-truck dealership parts department: demonstrating a powered item to a farmer or fleet mechanic - starting a chainsaw or generator, running a pressure washer or transfer pump, working a grease gun or hydraulic hose crimper - in the parts shop or on the lot, while explaining operation, adjustment and maintenance.

Industrial / hydraulic / bearing distributor branch with a demo bench: demonstrating equipment to a maintenance technician - crimping a hose sample, assembling a fitting or coupler, running an air tool, showing a bearing puller or press attachment - with the item set on the bench or in a vise, explaining how it functions and its limits.

At the customer's premises (farm shop, fleet garage, jobsite, independent repair shop): an outside/counter salesperson brings a new tool or piece of equipment and demonstrates it in situ on the customer's own machine or vehicle, explaining functioning and fit under whatever conditions the site presents.

sources.title: Video: GPT-enhanced humanoid speaks and reasons as it works (New Atlas)
sources.claim: Figure 01 autonomously manipulated everyday objects on a staged table while conversing with a person in real time - answering questions and explaining what it was doing as it acted; Figure's CEO stated the robot was not teleoperated.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: conversational object handling. It couples the two elements of this task - operating/handling an item presented in front of it and simultaneously explaining in natural language what it is doing - at a staged, purpose-built table.

sources.title: AI-powered humanoid robot can serve you food, stack the dishes - and have a conversation with you (Live Science)
sources.claim: Figure 01 learned to operate a consumer coffee machine end-to-end by watching human video, and executes the machine operation autonomously while able to speak with people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating a small appliance (loading a pod, closing the lid, pressing the button). Demonstrating a countertop device to a customer requires the same class of act - actuating the controls of a presented piece of equipment so it visibly works.

sources.developer: Figure AI (at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg)
sources.title: F.03 Arrives at BMW (Figure AI)
sources.claim: Figure 03 running the Helix 02 vision-language-action policy performs a parts-sequencing logistics workflow autonomously on BMW's plant floor, picking thin-walled individual parts from carts and bins that are not presented in fixed positions and placing them precisely into slots; the predecessor Figure 02 ran 10-hour shifts for months.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: industrial part handling and precise insertion. It substantiates reliable, non-scripted handling of hard parts and fittings at a workstation, the manipulation core of a bench-top equipment demonstration.

sources.system: Gemini Robotics / Gemini Robotics 1.5 (ALOHA and bi-arm Franka platforms)
sources.title: Introducing Gemini Robotics and Gemini Robotics-ER (Google DeepMind blog)
sources.claim: Gemini Robotics is a vision-language-action model that drives bi-arm robots through dexterous multi-step manipulation from spoken instructions in lab settings, generalizing to novel objects and instructions, and (in the 1.5 version) narrating its reasoning in natural language while acting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: instruction-following dexterous manipulation with language. Supports a robot at a demo station taking a spoken customer request, manipulating the presented item, and explaining the steps.

sources.title: Hilti Unveils BIM-Enabled Construction Jobsite Robot (PR Newswire)
sources.claim: The Hilti Jaibot is a commercial construction robot that operates a powered rotary hammer: an operator drives it into position, after which it drills the programmed holes automatically.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous operation of a powered hand tool. Shows a machine can trigger, feed and run a power tool to a usable result once positioned - the physical act at the centre of demonstrating powered equipment.

sources.title: Chery hands over first batch of humanoid robots to dealers (CarSifu)
sources.claim: Chery/AiMOGA's Mornine humanoid has been handed to dealers and works in showrooms giving vehicle walkaround explanations, guiding customers and serving drinks; its customer-facing role is speech, navigation and gesture rather than operating the product's controls, and vendor autonomy claims are not independently verified.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: showroom product presentation. Cited to characterise what customer-facing robots actually do inside structured retail facilities - narrated walkarounds, not hands-on operation of the equipment being sold.

sources.title: Watch: New humanoid robot helps Nestle sell coffee machines (CBS News)
sources.claim: SoftBank's Pepper was deployed by Nestle Japan across roughly 1,000 appliance stores to talk with shoppers and promote Nescafe coffee machines; Pepper converses and gestures but has no capability to operate the machines it sells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store product promotion. Shows the deployed state of retail sales robots on a real store floor: explanation only, with no hands-on demonstration of the equipment's functioning.

tasks.label: Measure parts, using precision measuring instruments, to determine whether similar parts may be machined to required sizes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Retail auto/truck parts store counter: a customer brings in a worn, greasy or broken component (bolt, bushing, bearing, pulley, hose fitting). The counterperson wipes it, measures OD/ID/length/thread pitch with a dial or digital caliper and thread gauge at the counter or back bench, and compares against catalog stock to decide whether a stocked part fits as-is or a larger stock part could be turned/bored to the required size. Customer waiting; part identity often unknown.

Repair-shop parts room / service bay: measuring brake rotors and drums with a micrometer or drum gauge against minimum machining (discard) thickness to tell whether they can be resurfaced, or measuring crankshaft journals, flywheels and valve seats to determine which oversize/undersize replacement or regrind is required. Shop bench, dirty used parts, micrometer-class precision (0.001 in).

Industrial / bearing & power-transmission distributor counter and back room: measuring shafts, sleeves, bushings, seals, sprockets and keyways with micrometers, bore gauges and calipers to spec a replacement, and judging whether an oversize stock blank or bushing can be bored/machined to the customer's dimension. Clean-ish bench, small to medium metal parts.

Heavy-duty truck, agricultural, mining or marine dealership parts department: measuring large or heavy components (hydraulic cylinder rods, gears, pins, brake drums, housings) on a bench, floor or hoist, sometimes partly assembled, to determine remachining/resleeving feasibility before ordering. Awkward handling, wide size range.

Outside/mobile parts salesperson at a customer site (fleet garage, farm shop, jobsite, vessel): measures a part or an in-place feature (shaft journal, bore, hose assembly, pin) with tape, caliper or micrometer where it sits, to spec a replacement or a machining job. Layout differs site to site, poor light, no fixed bench.

sources.system: Robotic measurement cell with Mitutoyo MiSTAR CMM and Engineering Data robot loading
sources.title: Meca-Precis optimises control processes using Mitutoyo solution - Instrumentation Monthly
sources.claim: A deployed robotic measurement cell (Mitutoyo MiSTAR CMM + Engineering Data robot/fixturing) at precision machining firm Meca-Precis autonomously loads palletised parts onto a clamped CMM table and runs full dimensional inspection programs unattended, including 100% inspection of aerospace parts.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated dimensional inspection of machined parts. Same class of precision instrument (CMM probing, micrometer-class accuracy) on the same class of metal parts, and the accept/reject-against-tolerance output is the same comparison a parts salesperson makes when deciding whether stock remains to machine a part to a required size. Requires palletised, clamped presentation of known part types.

sources.system: Q-Span Automated Small-Part Measurement Workstation (robotic digital calipers on UR3e)
sources.title: Q-Span Systems combine robotic digital calipers, part handling, and data logging to automate measurement inspection | New Scale Robotics
sources.claim: New Scale Robotics Q-Span is a commercially sold workstation in which a UR3e cobot fitted with gripper/digital-caliper tools picks small parts from trays, measures several dimensions with metrology fingertips, decides pass/fail or sorts by range, and places parts in output trays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automating the manual job of measuring parts with digital calipers in QC. The instrument (digital caliper), the objects (small machined metal parts) and the required precision match the parts-counter measuring task; only the decision rule differs (tolerance limit versus machining allowance).

sources.title: Q-Span Systems combine robotic digital calipers, part handling, and data logging to automate measurement inspection | New Scale Robotics
sources.claim: The same Q-Span system reaches micrometer-class metrology performance and requires part-specific fingertips, trays, fixtures and scripts, i.e. a purpose-built presentation of each part type.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes that robotic caliper measurement meets the 0.001 in precision a parts salesperson works to with hand micrometers and calipers, and that the capability is tied to fixtured, part-specific presentation (an E1 setting).

sources.system: CUBE-R robotic 3D scanning CMM (MetraSCAN 3D-R on robot arm in enclosed cell)
sources.title: Creaform Launches the CUBE-R, the Fastest and Truly Accurate Turnkey 3D Scanning Coordinate Measuring Machine for At-Line Inspection
sources.claim: Creaform CUBE-R is a commercially available turnkey robotic 3D-scanning coordinate measuring machine (robot-mounted MetraSCAN) performing automated dimensional measurement of parts from 1 to 3 m at metrology-grade accuracy in shop-floor conditions, extending automated measurement to large components.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated at-line dimensional inspection of large components. Same measurement output (full geometry versus required dimensions) on the large castings, housings and drums a heavy-duty parts salesperson would measure, but only inside an enclosed, fixtured robot cell.

tasks.label: Pick up and deliver parts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Scheduled commercial delivery route: counter staff stage boxed parts and invoices for several independent repair shops, dealerships and fleet garages; the parts person loads the store van/pickup, drives public streets, parks at a curb or crowded shop lot, carries 1-40 lb boxes into the shop's parts counter or service bay, gets a signature, and picks up cores, warranty returns and wrong-part returns to bring back.

Hot-shot urgent single run: a shop or DIY customer needs one part now; the parts person grabs it, drives across town (sometimes to a residential driveway or a disabled vehicle), hands it over, and returns. Time-critical, unfamiliar addresses, varied weather and traffic.

Inter-store / hub / supplier pickup run: drive to a hub store, distribution center will-call, machine shop or vendor, identify and receipt the part at their counter, load it, and bring it back to the store for the waiting customer.

In-store retrieval and hand-off: locate a specific SKU in the back stockroom, mezzanine racking, outside storage container or overhead bins, retrieve it, and bring it to the front counter or hand it to the waiting customer (including carrying a battery, rotors or a case of oil out to the customer's car in the lot).

Receiving the inbound stock delivery: meet the DC box truck at the store's back door or dock, unload cases, totes and loose bulky items (exhaust, bumpers, batteries), check them against the manifest, and move them into the stockroom staging area.

sources.title: Serve Robotics to Acquire Diligent Robotics, Expanding Physical AI Platform Beyond the Sidewalk
sources.claim: Diligent Robotics' Moxi mobile manipulator autonomously fetches and delivers supplies, medications and lab specimens point-to-point inside hospitals, at large deployed scale.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: intra-facility supply/specimen delivery. It is the same pick-up-and-deliver work — small boxed/bagged goods carried between a stocking point and a recipient who takes the item at hand-off — in a human-occupied facility with corridors, doors and elevators.

sources.title: Moxi reaches milestone of 100,000 autonomous elevator rides in hospitals
sources.claim: Moxi operates around the clock in existing hospital workflows and has logged over 100,000 autonomous elevator rides, i.e. multi-floor autonomous routing without an operator.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hospital supply delivery. Comparable objects (small parts-sized items), comparable precision (hand-off to a person at a counter/station), and an institution-controlled facility, which is the E2 counterfactual for a parts delivery run.

sources.title: Meet Moxi, the newest nurse assistant of Trinity Michigan medical team
sources.claim: Moxi carries an arm and gripper and fetches medications, equipment and lab specimens, delivering them in ... badge-access torso drawer while navigating hallways and doors on its own.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: fetch-and-deliver of small clinical items. Same physical demands as carrying a boxed part from a stocking location to a recipient inside a controlled facility.

sources.title: Amazon unveils latest warehouse robot as tech giants continue AI layoffs
sources.claim: Amazon's Proteus autonomous mobile robot transports carts and containers of goods through fulfillment centers shared with human workers and is in production use across 25 U.S. facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving loaded carts of packages between staging points. It substantiates autonomous pick-up (docking under a loaded cart), transport and drop-off of goods in a human-occupied structured facility.

sources.title: OTTO - ROBOTS: Your Guide to the World of Robotics
sources.claim: OTTO autonomous mobile robots transport materials and deliver parts to assembly cells inside manufacturing plants and warehouses.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-plant parts delivery. Same objects (bins/boxes of automotive parts), same job (bring the part from stock to the point of use) inside an institution-controlled facility.

sources.title: Automated Trailer Unloading | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously detects, grasps and places boxes of varying size when unloading trailers and containers at loading docks.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment
sources.claim: DHL has Stretch robots in live supply-chain operations unloading cases at rates up to 700 per hour and signed an MOU for large-scale further deployment.

sources.title: Factory Motor Parts - Case Study | KPI Solutions
sources.claim: An automotive parts distributor (Factory Motor Parts) runs an AutoStore goods-to-person system with 68 robots and 90,000 parts bins that retrieves stored auto parts and presents them at pick workstations.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving a specific auto part from storage and presenting it for the order. Identical objects and precision to a counterperson pulling a SKU from the stockroom, with the storage purpose-built around the machine (E1).

sources.title: How Automotive Parts Distributors Use AutoStore - Kardex
sources.claim: Robotic goods-to-person retrieval is standard in automotive parts distribution: robots retrieve inventory and deliver ... to workstations instead of operators walking the racks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: parts retrieval from storage. Same SKUs and same output (the right part presented for the customer's order) as the in-store stockroom pull.

sources.title: Staples deploys RightHand Robotics tech in its fulfillment centers
sources.claim: RightHand Robotics' RightPick autonomous piece-picking systems are deployed across Staples' North American fulfillment centers, picking individual items including ones never seen before.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: single-item (each) picking into an order tote. Mixed boxed hardgoods comparable in size and weight to counter-sold parts, in a fixtured pick cell (E1).

sources.title: Amazon's new warehouse robot has a 'sense of touch' that could see it replace human workers
sources.claim: Amazon's Vulcan robot, which picks and stows items from storage bins using force sensing, is operating in Spokane and Hamburg fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: retrieving a designated item from a cluttered storage bin. Supports E1 retrieval of a specific part when the storage is presented to the machine.

sources.title: Agility's 'hardest working' humanoid robot hits 100,000-tote milestone
sources.claim: Agility's Digit humanoid autonomously moves totes from mobile robots onto conveyors in GXO warehouses under a multi-year commercial agreement, passing 100,000 totes moved.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: transferring totes of goods between a mobile robot and a fixed station — the loading/unloading step of an in-facility parts delivery, in a human work facility.

sources.title: Nuro Goes Driverless in Three Cities, Advances Capabilities of the Nuro Driver
sources.claim: Nuro operates zero-occupant driverless delivery vehicles on public roads in three cities; goods are carried in locked compartments that the recipient opens at the curb, with no robotic loading or door-to-counter hand-off.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: driverless road delivery. Shows the driving leg is automatable on public roads, but not the loading of a multi-stop van, the carry into a repair shop, the signature, or the core pickup.

sources.title: Evri Unleashes Robot Dog Delivery in Industry-First UK Trial
sources.claim: RIVR's wheeled-legged robot in Evri's UK trial performs only the last-100-yard walk from a courier's van to the front door; the human courier still drives the route and loads the robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: last-yards parcel hand-off in unstructured streets. Cited as the state of the art at E3; it is a courier-assist pilot, so it does not complete a whole delivery run.

tasks.label: Repair parts or equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Curbside/parking-lot service on a customer's vehicle at an auto parts store: install a replacement battery (remove corroded terminal bolts and hold-down, lift out ~40 lb battery, fit and torque new one), replace wiper blades, swap a headlight bulb or fuse, clean corroded terminals. Arbitrary make/model, engine bay clutter, outdoors in whatever weather.

Back-shop machine work on a detached part with store equipment: mounting a brake rotor or drum on the lathe and resurfacing it to spec, pressing bearings, bushings or U-joints in the shop press, grinding/deburring or sharpening a mower blade or chainsaw chain, honing a cylinder. Part is dirty and worn but handled on a fixed machine at a bench.

Rebuilding or reconditioning a used component a customer brings to the counter: repacking a hydraulic cylinder, rebuilding a carburetor, water pump, starter or brake caliper — disassembly of a rusted/greasy assembly, cleaning, inspection, replacement of seals/brushes/gaskets, reassembly and test.

Making up or repairing an assembly to order at the counter: cutting hose or wire to length and crimping fittings/terminals for a hydraulic hose assembly or battery cable, making a chain or belt loop, repairing a trailer light pigtail, then pressure/continuity testing it.

Repairing a customer's small equipment brought into the store: mower, chainsaw, trimmer or power tool — replacing a pull cord, belt, spark plug, blade or switch, clearing a fuel system, diagnosing a no-start, on a unit of unknown history.

Repairing the store's own equipment and fixtures: broken shelving or display rack, jammed receipt printer or key-cutting machine, failed lighting, hand truck or forklift battery, minor fix on the delivery vehicle — in aisles and back rooms with customers and staff around.

sources.system: FANUC MT Series / LR Mate machine tending cells
sources.title: Machine Tending Robots | FANUC America
sources.claim: Commercial robotic machine-tending cells autonomously load and unload metal parts into CNC lathes, including transferring parts through wash/dry cycles, in fenced industrial cells.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: CNC lathe tending. Resurfacing a brake rotor or drum is the same operation class — load a heavy cast-iron disc onto a lathe fixture, run a programmed cut, unload — with comparable object size, weight and machining precision, in the same fenced cell.

sources.system: Waybo PartNR / CyberDrawers cells with KUKA robots
sources.title: Robotic Machine Tending Cells for CNC Automation | KUKA Canada
sources.claim: Pre-engineered robotic machine tending cells are sold for high-mix, low-volume shops and can load/unload existing lathes or mills, and also perform marking, inspection and washing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: high-mix machine tending. Shows the fixtured-cell approach handles varied part types with in-cell inspection, which is what turning an assortment of rotors/drums to spec requires.

sources.system: ESE Automation workcell with Promess EMAP 60 kN servo press
sources.title: Integrating Presses Into Assembly Systems | ASSEMBLY
sources.claim: Industrial workcells combine a six-axis robot with a servo press to press bushings into automotive components, with force and position monitoring verifying each installation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic press-fit of bushings. Pressing bearings, bushings or U-joints into a part at a parts-store press is the same press operation on the same class of automotive components, with force/position verification substituting for the counterman's feel.

sources.title: Sharpening tools overnight with Vollmer Automation | Cutting Tool Engineering
sources.claim: A CNC sharpening machine with automatic magazine loading reconditions circular saw blades unmanned overnight and through weekends at a commercial sharpening service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated tool sharpening. Sharpening a mower blade or saw chain at a parts counter is the same grind-to-geometry reconditioning of a worn cutting edge, done on a purpose-built machine with the workpiece fixtured.

sources.system: MESH Automation robotic grinding cell (FANUC M10iD/16S)
sources.title: Case Study: Robotic Grinding of Small Parts - MESH Automation
sources.claim: A guarded robotic cell performs belt and wheel grinding, deburring and reaming of small metal parts with a FANUC robot, running at over 90% OEE with 12–60 second cycles.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic abrasive finishing of small metal parts in a fenced cell — the same force-controlled grinding/deburring used when a parts store dresses, deburrs or sharpens a metal part on shop equipment.

sources.system: Komax automatic crimping machines (Alpha 550 G2, Gamma 450, CrX-44HD)
sources.title: Automatic Crimping | Komax
sources.claim: Fully automatic wire-processing machines cut wire to length, strip it and crimp terminals (including seals) in one machine, producing finished leads unattended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cut-strip-crimp lead making. Making up a battery cable or repairing a wiring pigtail at the parts counter is the same cut-to-length-and-crimp operation on comparable gauge wire and terminals, with crimp-force monitoring giving the quality check.

sources.title: Automated Tire decloaks with new autonomous tire-changing SmartBay - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Autonomous tire-changing bays are only now entering the field; the first-generation system still requires a technician supervising bays and does not fully automate mounting, airing and balancing. An earlier competitor deployed in tire stores went bankrupt.
sources.transferJustification: Nearest available evidence for automated service work on customer vehicles; it is confined to a purpose-built bay and to wheels on a standardized hub interface, so it does not transfer to under-hood battery, wiper or bulb replacement on arbitrary vehicles.

sources.system: Experimental robotic disassembly cell for EV battery modules
sources.title: An experimental robotic cell for the disassembly of electric vehicle battery modules | Journal of Remanufacturing
sources.claim: Robotic disassembly of used assemblies for remanufacturing remains at experimental prototype-cell stage in the research literature.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated teardown of used assemblies. It shows that even single-family, fixtured disassembly is prototype-stage, so rebuild of varied worn components (cylinders, carburetors, starters) is not substantiated.

tasks.label: Compute sales prices, total purchases, and receive and process cash or credit payment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel / soft-goods or general specialty store counter: customer brings 1-6 tagged items; salesperson keys or scans them, applies a promotion, loyalty discount or price adjustment, computes total with sales tax, takes a contactless/chip credit or debit card, and hands over the printed receipt. Indoor sales floor, standard POS terminal and card reader.

Cash tender at the register: customer pays a computed total with bills (sometimes with a paper coupon, gift card, or split cash/card tender); worker counts the cash, opens the drawer, makes and counts back change in bills and coins, and issues the receipt. Drawer must reconcile at end of shift.

Big-ticket furniture, mattress or appliance write-up: salesperson prices a multi-piece order, adds delivery/haul-away fees, protection plan, promotional discount and tax, quotes monthly payments under store financing, then collects a deposit or full amount on a credit card (occasionally check) and prints a sales order/contract for signature at the write-up desk.

Payment taken away from the fixed register: handheld/mobile POS used for line-busting on the sales floor, in an outdoor garden center or lumber lot, or at curbside pickup in the store lot; salesperson totals the items, takes a card tap/insert and emails or prints the receipt.

Vehicle or other high-value negotiated sale: salesperson computes the out-the-door figure (negotiated price, trade allowance, rebates, doc/registration fees, taxes), presents it to the customer, and receives and processes the down payment by credit card, cashier's check or cash in the dealership showroom/business office, issuing a receipt.

Off-premises selling: home show or fair booth, sidewalk/tent sale, or in-home flooring/furniture measure-and-quote visit; salesperson computes the price on a tablet or handheld reader and takes a card or check payment on the spot, with no fixed register and variable lighting/connectivity.

sources.claim: Payment kiosks are built and deployed for outdoor as well as indoor self-service payment workflows, covering card, contactless and cash tenders away from a fixed indoor register.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: taking payment outside the main checkout line. Same objects (cards, notes, receipts) and same precision, showing the payment-receipt hardware works in outlying and outdoor areas of a controlled site such as a garden center or curbside lane.

tasks.label: Prepare merchandise for purchase or rental.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/softlines counter prep with no security device: associate takes the customer's garments or soft goods at the wrap desk, refolds them, adds tissue or a garment bag, inserts the receipt and bags the order, working amid shoppers at the counter.

Apparel or hardlines counter prep on protected merchandise: associate detaches hard EAS tags, ink tags, cable/spider wraps or lanyards with a detacher or key, deactivates soft labels, then refolds/repacks the item and bags it at the register.

General-merchandise/hardlines prep: associate retrieves the boxed or loose item from the shelf, locked case or stockroom, checks contents and condition, removes shelf tags/packaging, installs batteries or activates a device where needed, then boxes or bags it with the receipt for the customer.

Big-ticket (furniture, appliance, TV, mattress, lumber) prep in the store's back room or attached warehouse: pull the correct carton from racking, inspect for damage, corner-pad or shrink-wrap it, attach the sold ticket/customer paperwork, and stage it on a pallet or cart at the pickup/delivery dock.

Custom in-store make-to-order prep at a machine or bench: duplicate a key, tint and shake a can of paint, cut fabric/blinds/chain/lumber to the customer's measurement, fill a propane tank, or assemble a bike or grill before handover.

Rental and vehicle delivery prep: clean/wash and vacuum the vehicle or equipment, remove protective film and stickers, fuel or charge it, check fluids and function, fit plates or adjust the item to the customer (e.g., ski bindings, tool attachments), and attach rental/delivery paperwork in the lot, service lane or rental yard.

sources.title: Nimble Launches Next-Gen Robotic 3PL Service, Working Towards a Fully Autonomous Fulfillment Network
sources.claim: Nimble Robotics' robotic cells autonomously pick individual retail items and pack them into shipping bags/boxes at production volume in fulfillment warehouses, for brands including Best Buy, Victoria's Secret and Puma.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: e-commerce pick-and-pack. Same physical act as preparing a purchase for handover - grasping apparel/hardline retail items and enclosing them in a bag or box - on merchandise identical to store stock, but in a robotic cell.

sources.title: Sparck Technologies equips WebstaurantStore with CVP Impack auto-boxing machines
sources.claim: The Sparck CVP Impack auto-boxing machine autonomously measures each order, builds a right-sized box around it, tapes, weighs and labels it at up to 500 boxes/hour; multiple units purchased and run by WebstaurantStore.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: order packaging. Boxing and labelling purchased goods is the same output a salesperson produces when boxing merchandise for a customer; same objects and precision, with the work conveyed to the machine.
