sources.system: Pearson RPC-MX configurable robotic palletizer with integrated labeling/strapping
sources.title: RPC-MX Configurable Robotic Palletizer - Pearson Packaging Systems
sources.claim: Robotic palletizing cells automatically stack cartons and integrate automatic pallet labeling and strapping/wrapping, producing a labelled, secured, staged pallet without an operator.

sources.title: Robotic arm pumps gas autonomously | GlobalSpec
sources.claim: Autofuel's robotic arm refuels cars at a gas station without human assistance, but the vehicle must carry a specialized fuel cap the arm can manipulate; shown at a pilot station in Denmark.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: vehicle refueling. Covers only the fueling step of rental/delivery vehicle prep, and only on vehicles fitted with a special cap.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: The most capable autonomous in-store manipulation deployed at scale is Telexistence's TX SCARA, which restocks bottles and cans onto convenience-store shelves in 300 FamilyMart stores; it handles standardized drink containers, not customer order preparation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store shelf restocking. Cited as the boundary of demonstrated autonomous manipulation inside a live retail store (E2): a fixed-base arm placing uniform beverages, well short of preparing a customer's mixed purchase.

sources.title: Accenture Invests in Sanctuary AI to Bring AI-Powered, Humanoid Robotics to Work Alongside Humans
sources.claim: Sanctuary AI's Phoenix humanoid performed retail prep-type tasks (packing merchandise, cleaning, tagging, labeling, folding) during a week-long pilot at a Mark's store in Langley, BC, but the sources do not establish autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (in-store packing, tagging, folding of merchandise), but autonomy is not established, so it cannot support a positive judgment; recorded as the closest in-store attempt.

tasks.label: Demonstrate use or operation of merchandise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Consumer electronics / appliance sales floor: a shopper asks to see a TV, laptop, tablet, phone, headphones, or a small kitchen appliance work. The salesperson unlocks or powers the display unit, runs it through menus and features, plays content or brews a cup, hands it to the customer and answers follow-ups.

Hardware / home-improvement / lawn-and-garden store: demonstrating a cordless drill, saw, pressure washer, mower, or grill in the aisle, at a demo bench, or in the outdoor lot — inserting a battery or bit, starting the tool, making a test hole or cut on scrap, showing safety features.

Furniture, mattress, or home-goods showroom: working a recliner handle, converting a sofa bed, raising an adjustable bed base, showing soft-close drawers or a lift-top table, letting the customer try the piece.

Beauty / cosmetics counter in a department or big-box store: applying or demonstrating a product on the customer — a lipstick or foundation swatch, nail polish, a hair styling tool — on the customer's hand, face, or hair.

Apparel, footwear, jewelry, sporting-goods and hobby merchandise: showing how a garment or shoe fits and adjusts, sizing a watch band, shifting a bicycle's gears, setting up a tent, stringing or playing an instrument, running a treadmill console — hands-on with the customer and often on the customer's body.

Vehicle or powersports dealership: walkaround of a car/ATV/boat with doors, hood and tailgate opened, infotainment and driver-assist features operated, seats and towing gear shown, followed by a demonstration drive on public roads with the customer.

sources.title: How Artly's Barista Bot helped MUJI transform its retail experience
sources.claim: Artly's Barista Bot robotic arm is deployed inside MUJI retail stores (Portland, New York, Vancouver, Toronto), operating standard coffee-making equipment in front of shoppers and running autonomously most of the time from a fixed station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing drinks with standard consumer/commercial coffee equipment in a retail store. It substantiates the physical core of an appliance demonstration — a machine running a consumer appliance through its full operating cycle, in view of store customers — from a purpose-built station placed inside a store.

sources.title: A VLA that Learns from Experience
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's RL-trained VLA ran a robot making espresso drinks on a professional espresso machine for a full working day (5:30am-11:30pm) without interruption, at practically useful throughput and reliability.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: operating a professional espresso machine (grinding, tamping, portafilter, buttons, milk). The objects, precision and multi-step sequence match what a salesperson does when demonstrating a small appliance's operation; the work is done at a fixed, set-up station.

sources.title: MATT the Smart Device Test Automation Robot
sources.claim: MATT is a commercial device-testing robot that physically operates smartphones, tablets and other consumer devices held in a fixture — tapping, swiping, pinching and pressing buttons — replicating human finger interaction under machine control with AI computer vision.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: exercising a consumer device's user interface. Showing a customer how a phone, tablet or console works consists of the same physical acts (taps, swipes, button presses) on the same objects; MATT does them on devices presented in a fixture.

sources.title: Hilti's Overhead Drilling Robot Brings Further Automation to the Jobsite | Engineering News-Record
sources.claim: The Hilti Jaibot is a commercially deployed semi-autonomous construction robot that carries a standard cordless rotary hammer drill and, after being positioned by a worker, drills the planned holes automatically on real jobsites.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: running a hand-held power tool to make holes of specified size. A hardware-store demonstration is the same physical act — trigger the tool, control feed, produce a clean hole or cut in a test workpiece — with the tool held by the machine.

sources.title: Introducing Helix 02: Full-Body Autonomy
sources.claim: Figure's Helix 02 model autonomously unloads and reloads a dishwasher ..., opening appliance and cabinet doors and handling contents end-to-end with no resets or human intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: actuating household mechanisms — appliance doors, racks, cabinet handles. Demonstrating a recliner lever, sofa-bed frame or drawer glide requires the same class of handle-pulling and hinged-mechanism actuation on similarly sized furniture-scale objects.

sources.title: Target shoppers can get a $10 manicure from a robot at 2 Fort Worth stores
sources.claim: Clockwork installed fully autonomous nail-painting kiosks inside Target stores, where a customer inserts a finger into the machine and cameras plus algorithms guide precise polish application in about ten minutes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: applying a cosmetic product to a customer's body in a store. Demonstrating a beauty product on the customer is the same physical act — precise application of polish/pigment onto a small body surface presented to the machine.

sources.title: AI humanoid robots now selling cars at dealerships as Chery debuts Mornine | Fox News
sources.claim: Chery/AiMOGA's Mornine humanoid works as an 'intelligent sales consultant' in car showrooms, explaining vehicle specifications, leading walkaround tours and serving refreshments, but it is not reported to operate the vehicles themselves or conduct demonstration drives.
sources.transferJustification: Directly relevant to the vehicle-showroom instance: it shows the reach of today's deployed retail sales robots is conversation, guidance and drink service — not physical operation of the merchandise being sold.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's π0.5 can control a mobile ... perform household tasks in entirely new, unseen homes, but its authors note it does not always succeed ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general object manipulation in settings taken as found. It marks the frontier of unstructured-environment manipulation and shows reliability is still below the standard an employer would accept for a customer-facing product demonstration.

tasks.label: Ticket, arrange, and display merchandise to promote sales.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/softlines store: salesperson tickets new arrivals with a tagging gun or adhesive price tickets, hangs garments on racks in size/color order, folds and stacks tables and shelves, and sizes/straightens the fixtures during the shift, working around customers on the sales floor.

Uniform packaged goods (bottled/canned drinks, cartons of standard packaged product) replenished and faced on standard store shelving or a refrigerated display case in a convenience/drug/general-merchandise store, pulled from crates or backroom stock, front-faced and rotated per planogram.

Hardlines set-out: varied boxed and blister-packed merchandise (electronics, hardware, housewares) unpacked from cartons and placed on shelves and peg hooks, price stickers applied to items and shelf-edge price tags/strips installed, plus building a planogram endcap or floor stack.

Small high-value items (jewelry, watches, phones, cosmetics): individually ticketed, arranged on pads/trays inside locked glass display cases and countertop fixtures, restocked and re-set neatly between customer showings.

Big-ticket showroom or lot: furniture, mattresses, appliances, or vehicles moved and positioned into display rows/vignettes on the sales floor or lot, with price tags, spec cards, or window stickers attached.

Visual/promotional display building: window and feature displays, dressing mannequins and forms, seasonal vignettes with props, hanging signage and promotional graphics, judged on appearance to promote sales.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores (NVIDIA Blog)
sources.claim: TX SCARA autonomously restocks bottled and canned beverages onto convenience-store display shelves from the chilled backroom, succeeding automatically >98% of the time with remote operators handling exceptions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf replenishment and facing of packaged retail merchandise. It is the 'arrange and display merchandise' portion of this task for uniform packaged goods, using the same objects (retail packaged drinks), the same shelf-placement precision, and a live retail store.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: TX SCARA was mass-produced and installed in 300 FamilyMart convenience ..., i.e. a real multi-store retail deployment rather than a lab demo.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above: in-store replenishment/arrangement of packaged merchandise on display shelving.

sources.title: Telexistence Expands Beverage Shelf-Stocking Service with "TX Ghost" Robots
sources.claim: Telexistence expanded its beverage shelf-stocking robot service with TX Ghost, with pilots running in 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo as of late 2025; the company describes its robots as both remote-controlled and AI-driven, so autonomy of this newer unit is not established.
sources.transferJustification: Shows continued in-store shelf-stocking robotics, but autonomy is unclear so it is treated as teleoperated and not relied on for positive judgments.

sources.title: Simbe Marks 10 Years of Tally the Robot
sources.claim: The robots actually deployed at scale on US retail sales floors are autonomous shelf-scanning/inventory robots that sense pricing and stock errors; they have no manipulator and do not ticket, arrange, or display merchandise.
sources.transferJustification: Negative/context evidence: establishes that in-store retail robots at scale perform sensing only, bounding what can be claimed at E2 for manipulation-based merchandising.

sources.title: Accenture Invests in Sanctuary AI to Bring AI-Powered, Humanoid Robotics to Work Alongside Humans
sources.claim: A humanoid performed retail tasks including tagging, labeling and folding merchandise in an operating clothing store, but the week-long trial used Sanctuary's pilot/teleoperation approach rather than autonomous operation.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the task (tagging, labeling, folding store merchandise) but piloted/teleoperated, so it cannot support a positive judgment at any tier.

sources.claim: Commercial garment-finishing machines automatically print and apply labels/tickets to garments as they pass through ..., producing folded, ticketed, stack-ready apparel on a production line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ticketing and folding apparel. Same objects (garments), same operations (attach price/label ticket, fold to retail presentation), performed with the work fed to the machine on a purpose-built line.

sources.title: Hanging conveyor system fashion logistics – GarmentFlow®
sources.claim: Automated garment-on-hanger conveyor/sorter systems transport, separate and pick hanging garments at high throughput in distribution centers, sequencing them by size/style/store for store-ready hanging presentation.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: arranging hanging garments in order on rails. Comparable objects (garments on hangers) and the same output (garments sequenced by size for display), achieved in a purpose-built machine environment.

sources.title: Label Printer Applicators and Labeling Systems from Weber Packaging
sources.claim: Self-contained print-and-apply labeling systems automatically print and apply pressure-sensitive labels ... products moving along a conveyor line, at production speeds and around the clock.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: ticketing merchandise with printed price/promotional labels. Same act (apply a printed price ticket to an item) with the item presented to the machine, which is precisely the E1 counterfactual for ticketing.

sources.system: ACPaQ robotic mixed-case palletizer (Swisslog with KUKA robots)
sources.title: ACPaQ Robotic Mixed Case Palletizer - Swisslog
sources.claim: Robotic mixed-case palletizers build stable, store-ready pallets sequenced to individual store planograms, i.e. machines arrange varied retail cases into a specified display/replenishment order.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: arranging assorted retail merchandise into a planogram-specified stack (display pallet / floor stack). Same objects (retail cases), same organizing rule (planogram), with the work brought to the robot cell.

sources.title: Amazon unveils the next generation of fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously detects, selects and handles individual retail products across a very large and diverse assortment inside fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: picking varied individual consumer goods and placing them into designated receptacles. Comparable objects and placement precision to arranging small merchandise in a fixture, in a fenced purpose-built cell.

sources.date: deployed since 2018-2019 (Lyon, Gatwick); Trimble case study retrieved 2026
sources.title: Trimble GNSS/INS powers autonomous parking robot, "Stan."
sources.claim: The Stan robot autonomously lifts and moves passenger vehicles and parks them densely into designated positions in airport car parks, without a driver.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving and positioning vehicles into planned display/parking rows. Same object class (passenger vehicles) and the same placement act needed to arrange a dealership display line, in a robot-only lot zone.

tasks.label: Inventory stock and requisition new stock.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Chain/big-box sales floor (grocery-adjacent, drug, general merchandise, club, hardware): associate walks assigned aisles, scans shelf-edge barcodes or counts facings against the system, flags out-of-stocks, low stock and phantom inventory, and triggers/submits replenishment orders. Standard gondola shelving, fixed planogram, customers and carts present.

Apparel/footwear/sporting-goods specialty store cycle count: count hanging and folded garments, shoes and accessories on racks, tables and wall displays (plus fitting-room strays), reconcile against the inventory system, and requisition replenishment from the DC. Merchandise typically RFID- or barcode-tagged.

Backroom/stockroom backstock check: counting cartons, totes and overstock on steel shelving and pallets behind the sales floor, verifying quantities of specific SKUs, then requesting a transfer or vendor order. Narrower aisles, carts and u-boats present, barcoded cases.

Small independent retailer (boutique, gift shop, small hardware/pet store): salesperson walks the floor eyeballing and hand-counting assorted, often untagged merchandise on tables, pegboards, bins and shelves in a small idiosyncratic space, writes a reorder list and places it with reps or vendor portals.

Big-ticket retail (furniture, appliances, motor vehicles): salesperson physically verifies units present on the showroom floor, in the attached warehouse, or on the outdoor lot (model/serial/VIN, condition, floor samples), reconciles with the DMS/inventory system and orders units from the manufacturer or distributor.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally, an autonomous shelf-scanning robot, is deployed across 17 Harmons grocery stores ... capture shelf-level product availability, pricing and placement data, replacing manual associate inventory scanning on the sales floor.

sources.title: Schnuck Markets to Deploy Simbe Tally Inventory Robots Chainwide - Robotics 24/7
sources.claim: Schnucks deployed Tally chainwide; the robot's real-time inventory data fed the grocer's automated replenishment system, streamlining ordering, ... detected 14x more addressable out-of-stocks than manual scans.

sources.title: Inventory Replenishment | Simbe
sources.claim: Simbe markets Tally as replacing manual stock audits and feeding ordering systems, i.e. the scan-to-reorder loop that constitutes the requisition half of this task.

sources.title: How a robot named Tally is helping BJ's boost the customer experience
sources.claim: Tally is deployed chainwide across BJ's Wholesale Club's 244 clubs, an environment of high racks, changing inventory and constant member traffic - general-merchandise big-box, not just grocery.

sources.claim: Sam's Club completed a chainwide rollout of nearly 600 robotic Inventory Scan towers on BrainOS-powered autonomous floor scrubbers that capture shelf inventory data as they roam club aisles during operations.

sources.title: PAL Robotics' StockBot at Decathlon stores (IFR case study)
sources.claim: PAL Robotics' StockBot RFID autonomous mobile robot counts stock and records item locations in Decathlon sporting-goods stores worldwide, navigating during opening hours among moving customers.

sources.title: MetraLabs presents TORY - the world's first RFID inventory robot in continuous live operation (RFID Journal)

tasks.label: Exchange merchandise for customers and accept returns.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routine receipted return at a store service desk or register: customer hands over a small, standardized item in resalable condition (tagged apparel, sealed box, cosmetics, boxed toy) with receipt or order QR; associate scans the tag/receipt, gives it a quick look-over, refunds to original tender, and drops the item in the go-back/restock bin.

Returned consumer electronic device (phone, tablet, earbuds, smart watch) that must be checked: associate confirms model/serial, powers it up or checks for cracks and wear, decides restock vs. defective/RTV, and completes the refund.

Other opened-box merchandise return (small appliance, power tool, printer, assembled toy): associate opens the carton, verifies all accessories, manuals and parts are present, checks for use or damage, decides disposition (restock, defective bin, vendor return), then refunds.

Even exchange: customer swaps an item for a different size, color, or a working replacement of the same SKU; associate takes the returned unit, fetches or dispenses the replacement, verifies it matches, completes the zero-dollar exchange, and handles the returned unit.

Nonstandard or contentious return: no receipt, outside the return window, item visibly worn/used, missing tags, or suspected fraud; associate must apply and explain policy, negotiate with the customer, take ID or seek a manager override, and either deny or process an exception.

Bulky/heavy merchandise return or exchange (furniture, mattress, large appliance, big-screen TV): associate meets the customer at the entrance or loading area, inspects the item for damage, moves it with a dolly or cart to the back, and completes the paperwork/refund.

sources.title: Turn Your Old Phone Into Cash: Everything About ecoATM Recycling
sources.claim: ecoATM self-service kiosks in US retail stores take a consumer electronic device handed over by a member of the public, automatically inspect it (power-on test, screen/button checks, physical condition), price it and pay the customer, retaining the device inside the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Trade-in intake is the same transaction structure as accepting a return: a customer surrenders a retail product at a counter/kiosk, the item's identity and condition are verified against policy, money is issued, and the item is routed into a bin for downstream disposition.

sources.title: EcoATM announces 7.5M devices collected in 2025 - Recycling Today
sources.claim: ecoATM's automated device-evaluation kiosks are deployed at scale inside mainstream US retail stores, collecting millions of devices per year.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes commercial scale and in-store siting of the automated intake/inspection kiosk cited for condition assessment of returned consumer electronics.

sources.title: ecoATM recycled 7.5M phones in 2025 as payouts hit $1.5B - Resource Recycling
sources.claim: The ecoATM kiosk performs model identification and condition grading on-site with imaging and electrical diagnostics before quoting a price, i.e. the accept/value decision is made by the machine.
sources.transferJustification: Same as above: automated identification plus condition assessment plus payout is the decision core of accepting a returned item for refund.

sources.system: TOMRA reverse vending machines (Basic Line / R1 / T9)
sources.title: Tomra markets new reverse vending machine line for improved retailer and consumer convenience
sources.claim: TOMRA reverse vending machines in supermarkets accept goods handed back by customers, identify and count each item, reject ineligible ones, physically convey and sort the accepted items to the backroom, and issue the refund — explicitly positioned as a replacement for manual human handling.
sources.transferJustification: Deposit return is a customer-facing merchandise return: the machine takes custody of a barcoded retail good, verifies eligibility against the retailer's policy, refuses non-qualifying items, refunds the customer, and moves the item into back-of-store storage — the same start-to-accepted-output loop as instance 0.

sources.transferJustification: An exchange is a return intake plus a hand-over of the replacement unit; this machine performs both physical halves (accepting the returned item into robotic storage and dispensing an item to the customer) at a purpose-built in-store terminal.

sources.system: Cleveron robotic click-and-collect lockers at Zara

sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic system autonomously detects, identifies and handles individual products drawn from an inventory of millions of diverse retail items inside fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the item-generalization gap in the kiosk evidence: identifying and physically moving arbitrary loose retail merchandise into the correct destination container is exactly the put-away step after a return is accepted, demonstrated in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Nimble - Fully Autonomous Fulfillment
sources.claim: Nimble's mobile-manipulator robots autonomously pick and handle apparel, lingerie, footwear and beauty products in operating fulfillment centers.
sources.transferJustification: Shows autonomous robotic handling of soft goods (the dominant returned category) in a purpose-built cell, supporting the item-handling portion of an apparel return once the transaction is authorized.

tasks.label: Clean shelves, counters, and tables.

instances.label: Convenience store, grocery, or pharmacy front end during a shift with customers present: the salesperson sprays and wipes the checkout counter, the register/card-reader surround, and nearby shelf edges and impulse displays, working around the POS terminal, bags, and small merchandise, in short bursts between customers.

Specialty retail sales floor (apparel, electronics, hardware): dusting and wiping merchandise shelving, gondolas, and display fixtures — lifting boxes, folded goods, and small items off the shelf, wiping the deck and shelf edge, and replacing merchandise in a saleable face-out arrangement.

Jewelry, cosmetics, or phone store: cleaning glass display cases and glass-topped counters to a streak- and fingerprint-free standard with glass cleaner and cloth, working close to small, delicate, high-value merchandise and testers.

Furniture/appliance showroom or auto dealership showroom: dusting and polishing display tabletops, dressers, desks, and appliance/vehicle top surfaces, with staged accessories (lamps, vases, brochures) on them, in an open showroom whose layout is reset frequently.
In-store café, bakery, or sample counter: wiping seating tables and the food service counter between customers — crumbs, drink rings, and light spills — to a food-service sanitation standard.
Opening or closing routine with the store closed to customers: clearing counters and wiping down all counters, tables, and back-stockroom shelving as a deep clean.

sources.title: Primech AI Introduces Hytron, the World's Most Advanced Autonomous Restroom Cleaning Robot, to North America at CES 2026
sources.claim: Primech AI's Hytron is a fully autonomous mobile restroom-cleaning robot that cleans and sanitizes sinks, mirrors, countertops and surrounding high-contact surfaces inside commercial facilities, with deployments reported in Singapore, Hong Kong and Macau.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cleaning restroom countertops and mirrors in an institution-controlled facility. Transfer to retail counter wiping is partial: comparable flat hard surfaces, cloth/water application and low positional precision, in a facility of the same tier; but Hytron's fixture-level architecture is engineered for standard restroom layouts and it does not lift or replace objects sitting on the surface.

sources.title: Primech AI Secures Government Collaboration for Hytron Autonomous Cleaning Robot Deployment in Singapore Schools

sources.transferJustification: Same system as evidence 0; establishes deployment maturity in an institution-controlled facility (school).

sources.title: Robots now wipe tables, sort trash, open doors at Google offices

sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping cafeteria/café tables in a corporate campus. Objects (café tabletops, crumbs, cups), precision demands, and the institution-controlled indoor environment are closely comparable to wiping tables and counters in an in-store café.

sources.system: Robotic table wiping via RL and whole-body trajectory optimization (Everyday Robots platform)

sources.transferJustification: Related task: wiping a table surface clean of spills and crumbs. Same physical action, tool contact and surface type required to clean a counter or table presented to a robot in a fixtured cell.

tasks.label: Open and close cash registers, performing tasks such as counting money, separating charge slips, coupons, and vouchers, balancing cash drawers, and making deposits.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: End-of-shift close at a chain store (apparel, general merchandise, electronics): salesperson pulls the till from the register, carries it to the back office, counts bills and coins, runs the POS/Z report, reconciles takings to the report, records over/short, separates any checks, charge slips, coupons and gift vouchers, and bags the day's cash for deposit.

Start-of-shift opening: retrieve the assigned till from the store safe, count the starting bank into denominations against the standard float (e.g., $150-$300), sign the accountability log, seat the drawer in the register and open it for trade.

Mid-shift cash pickup/drop and drawer change at a busy store: remove excess large bills from the drawer, count them, write the drop slip, drop the sealed envelope into the safe, and draw replacement coin/small bills so the register keeps trading.

High-volume location (warehouse club, big-box, high-traffic dealership) cash office: one person consolidates several registers' tills at once — thousands of dollars in mixed bills, heavy coin, checks — counts and verifies each, reconciles all registers to the day's sales, and prepares the consolidated deposit and next-day floats.

Bank deposit run: prepare the deposit slip, seal the bag, leave the premises and drive to the bank branch or night depository off-site, hand over or drop the bag and obtain a receipt, then file the receipt back at the store.

Small independent or specialty store (boutique, jewelry, furniture showroom) closing with paper-heavy media: cash plus personal checks, store gift certificates/vouchers, layaway and charge slips, manufacturer coupons; counted by hand at the counter, entered in a handwritten log or spreadsheet, discrepancies chased against sales tickets.

tasks.label: Bag or package purchases and wrap gifts.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/specialty store wrap desk or register: salesperson folds a garment or handles shoes/accessories, adds tissue paper, places item(s) plus receipt in a paper or reusable shopping bag, and hands it across the counter to the waiting customer. Items are unfixtured, arrive in any orientation, and the customer may ask for separate bags or no bag.

General merchandise, drug, convenience or small grocery register: bagging a mixed basket at checkout speed - cans, bottles, boxed goods, produce, chilled items, loose small goods - sequencing heavy under light, avoiding crushing, double-bagging where needed, keeping pace with the scanner and the queue.

Fragile/breakable goods (glassware, ceramics, cosmetics, wine, framed photos): each piece individually wrapped in tissue or bubble, padded, boxed or placed in a rigid carrier bag so it survives being carried home.
Complimentary/seasonal gift wrap of a standard rectangular boxed purchase at a wrap counter: select paper, cut, fold and tape around the cuboid box, add ribbon or a bow and a gift tag.

Gift wrap of an irregular, non-boxed or oversized purchase (a bottle, plush toy, sports equipment, awkward electronics blister pack): improvised boxing or paper folding, ribbon tied by hand, to a presentation standard the customer accepts on sight.

Bulky, heavy or high-value merchandise (small appliance, lamp, framed art, furniture component, boxed electronics): protective wrapping or shrink/blanket wrap, boxing or bagging over the item, taping and labeling for customer carry-out or transfer to the loading area.

tasks.label: Help customers try on or fit merchandise.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Apparel/department store sales floor: associate sizes up a customer by eye, pulls garments in additional sizes and colors from racks or the stockroom, removes hangers/security tags, helps the customer into a jacket or dress at the fitting room, checks shoulder, sleeve and waist fit by hand, and fetches alternates while the customer waits.

Shoe store: associate measures the customer's foot on a Brannock device, retrieves boxes from the stockroom, unlaces the shoe, uses a shoehorn to help the customer put it on, laces and ties it, presses the toe box and heel to judge fit, has the customer walk, then swaps sizes or widths.

Optical, jewelry or watch counter: associate places eyeglass frames on the customer's face and heats/bends temples and nose pads for fit; or slips rings on a finger with a ring sizer, clasps necklaces, and sizes a watch band on the wrist by removing links.

Bridal, suit or formalwear shop: associate takes tape-measure body measurements, helps the customer into a gown or suit jacket (zipping, buttoning, adjusting the shoulders), pins hems and sleeves, and marks alterations while the customer stands on a platform.

Sporting goods / bike shop: associate fits a bike helmet on the customer's head and adjusts straps and retention dial, checks ski or skate boot shell fit and liner, or sets saddle height and reach while the customer sits on the bike.

Big-ticket showroom (furniture, mattress, appliance, auto): associate helps the customer 'try' the merchandise — reclining a chair, adjusting an adjustable bed base or mattress firmness, positioning a car seat and mirrors for a test sit/drive — and checks the fit to the customer's body.

sources.system: Hybrid control robot-assisted dressing system (Kinova-class arm with Polaris tracker, ZED camera, Rasa dialogue)
sources.developer: University of Sheffield / King's College London research group (Rafiq, James, Xu, Hierons, Dogramadzi)
sources.title: Hybrid Control Strategies for Safe and Adaptive Robot-Assisted Dressing
sources.claim: Robot-assisted dressing — helping a seated person put a garment onto an arm — remains a laboratory research problem requiring external optical tracking of the garment and pose estimation of a cooperative seated user, with a single pre-specified garment and no size selection or fit assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Closest related task to helping a customer try on merchandise: a robot physically assists a human into a garment. It substantiates only a lab-instrumented, single-garment sleeve-dressing demo, not retrieval of sizes, fit judgement, or repeated interaction with an unfamiliar customer, so it does not carry over to the retail task even in a purpose-built cell.

sources.title: Meet Phoenix: A Versatile General-Purpose AI-based Robot That Just Entered The Workforce
sources.claim: The most advanced humanoid trial inside an actual apparel retail store covered back-of-house tasks (picking, packing, folding, tagging, labeling, cleaning) and was run by a human remotely piloting the robot, not autonomously, and did not include fitting merchandise to customers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly in the target environment (apparel store) and occupation, showing that even the frontier in-store humanoid work is teleoperated and limited to merchandise handling, never customer-contact fitting.

sources.developer: Brain Corp (with Walmart, Sam's Club, Kroger)

sources.claim: Robots actually deployed at scale in US retail stores perform floor cleaning and shelf inventory scanning; customer-facing store robots are limited to greeting, wayfinding and information kiosks, with no system that physically fits merchandise to shoppers.
sources.transferJustification: Establishes the deployed retail robotics frontier in the same setting as the task: autonomous store robots handle floors and shelf data, not garment handling or customer fitting.

instances.label: Counter rental of small, standardized, self-contained catalog units in a retail store: DVDs/games, power banks, small consumer electronics and AV gear, hand tools. Home-improvement tool-rental center or equipment yard: carpet cleaners, floor sanders, tile saws, tillers, ladders, lifts, trailers. The associate recommends the right machine for the job, writes the contract, retrieves heavy powered equipment from the yard, demonstrates safe operation and attachments, and helps load it into the customer's truck; on return checks fuel/hours, inspects for damage, and cleans the unit.

Fitted recreation-gear rental in a ski/snowboard, bike or watersports shop: size the customer, select boots and skis, set binding DIN from weight/height/ability, fit a helmet, adjust saddle/PFD, give a safety brief; on return inspect, wipe down, and route damaged gear to tuning.

Apparel rental in a formalwear, bridal or costume store: measure the customer, pull sizes from the stockroom, run the try-on and fit check, pin or flag alterations, bag the garments for pickup, and process returns into the cleaning cycle.

Rent-to-own or furniture/appliance rental showroom: walk the customer through floor models, demonstrate the appliance, complete the lease agreement, then pull the boxed unit from the stockroom and load it into the customer's vehicle or schedule delivery and in-home setup.

Event/party and bulky multi-item rental counter: pull a mixed order of tables, folding chairs, linens, tents, dishware or moving equipment from warehouse racks, stage it, walk the count with the customer and load their van or trailer; on return count, inspect for damage and route linens for cleaning.

instances.label: Exterior-only survey of a single-family home for a homeowners quote/renewal: agent drives to the property, walks/photographs the dwelling, roof, siding, foundation, detached garage/shed, and yard hazards (pool, trampoline, tree overhang, debris), notes roof material/condition, construction type and apparent age, and records whether the risk is acceptable. Private residential lot, taken as found.

Home inspection that includes an interior walkthrough: agent enters the house to look at the electrical panel (fuses, knob-and-tube, recalled panels), furnace/boiler, water heater age, plumbing, wood stove, attic/basement, and general housekeeping, in addition to a quick exterior look; occupied, cluttered, stairs and closed doors.

Small commercial risk survey for a retail store, restaurant, office or small warehouse: construction class (frame/joisted masonry), roof and exterior, fire protection (extinguishers, sprinklers, hood systems), exits, wiring, storage/housekeeping and occupancy hazards, during business hours.

Vehicle inspection for auto physical-damage coverage: walk-around of the customer's car at the agency lot or the customer's driveway, recording VIN and odometer, photographing existing dents/scratches/glass and tire condition, to confirm the vehicle is an acceptable risk.

Exterior-focused survey of a rural, farm or wildfire-exposed property: acreage and access road, outbuildings/barn roofs, brush and defensible space, tree cover, distance to hydrant/fire station, fencing and outdoor storage; large parcel, no site services.

sources.title: Drone-Based Inspections—The New Standard for Residential Insurance Claims
sources.claim: EagleView Assess is a commercially deployed drone inspection product for residential insurance property inspections in which the drone flies the capture pattern autonomously over an ordinary house and machine learning produces measurements and condition/damage findings.
sources.transferJustification: Same objects (residential roofs/exteriors) and same output medium as an agent's exterior risk inspection; the product is built for insurance property inspection, differing only in that the findings feed a claim rather than an underwriting decision.

sources.title: FAQ | Loveland Innovations
sources.claim: Loveland Innovations' IMGING builds an autonomous flight plan from operator-defined property areas and then flies a DJI drone autonomously over a whole property, capturing and stitching imagery for insurance property inspections.

sources.title: How to use 3D Capture with Skydio X10 – Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio 3D Scan is generally available adaptive-scanning software that lets Skydio drones autonomously plan and fly complete coverage of an arbitrary, previously unseen structure or scene, used by construction and DOT customers.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous close-range structure documentation of bridges, buildings and towers. It transfers because the objects (building envelopes, roofs, facades) and required imagery detail match an exterior property risk inspection, in the same unstructured outdoor settings.

sources.title: The Definitive Guide to Roof Condition for Property Insurers - CAPE Analytics
sources.claim: AI condition scoring computed from high-resolution aerial imagery of individual homes and commercial buildings is used by insurers as the basis for quoting, underwriting eligibility and renewal decisions, showing that imagery-derived condition assessment is accepted in place of a person's on-site look.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robot: this is the analytics layer that turns the imagery a drone captures into the risk judgment the task calls for; it is cited only to establish that image-derived condition findings meet the employer's acceptance standard.

sources.title: Wildfire Risk Model | Z-FIRE™ by ZestyAI
sources.claim: ZestyAI's property-level wildfire model extracts structural characteristics, defensible space and surrounding fuels from aerial imagery by computer vision and is filed and approved for insurer rating and underwriting.
sources.transferJustification: Not a robot: cited to show that the exposure characteristics an agent walks a rural parcel to observe (brush, defensible space, building materials) are extracted from overhead imagery and accepted for underwriting.

sources.system: UVeye Atlas / Artemis drive-through inspection systems
sources.title: How It Works - UVeye
sources.claim: UVeye's automated drive-through inspection systems are installed in dealership service lanes, fleet yards and rental operations, where a vehicle driven through the arch is scanned by cameras and AI in seconds to produce a full exterior, tire and underbody condition report without a human inspector.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: dealership/fleet condition capture. It transfers because the objects (customer vehicles), the findings (existing damage, glass, tires) and the documentary output are the same as an agent's pre-insurance photo inspection.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics Robot Dog Spot Inspects for Safety Hazards
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with Orbit performs autonomous inspection rounds inside operating industrial facilities, including AI-based safety-hazard checks such as spotting spills or propped-open emergency doors, but these are pre-configured missions at sites where the robot is permanently installed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility inspection rounds. Cited for context only — it is a repeated taught route at a single installed site, not a first-visit risk survey of a novel building interior, so it does not substantiate the interior-survey instances.

instances.label: Exterior survey of a customer's pitched-roof single-family home: walk the property, measure roof plane dimensions and setbacks (tape measure/ladder or laser), determine pitch and azimuth with an inclinometer and compass, note vents/chimneys/skylights and roof material and condition, and run a shading assessment (Solar Pathfinder/SunEye) so a designer can lay out an array. Conditions as found: fences, trees, dogs, sloped ground, weather.

Preliminary desk/remote suitability screening of a prospect's property before or instead of a truck roll: pull satellite/aerial imagery and LIDAR into design software (Aurora, Scanifly, EagleView), trace roof planes, estimate usable area, tilt, azimuth and annual solar access, and decide whether the site is worth pursuing.

Interior/electrical portion of the home assessment: locate and open the main service panel and meter, read busbar and main breaker ratings and photograph the labels and breaker layout, check available breaker spaces, and enter the attic or crawl space to check rafter size/spacing, sheathing condition and a conduit/wiring route from roof to panel.

Ground-mount or carport siting at a residence, farm or rural lot: pace or measure the available open area, check terrain slope and drainage, take compass orientation, judge tree-line shading through the day, and measure the distance from the array area to the service point for the trench/interconnection run.

Commercial or institutional flat-roof assessment (warehouse, school, church, small office): access the roof through the building, measure roof area and parapet setbacks, map HVAC units, skylights, drains and other obstructions, note membrane type and condition, and evaluate shading from adjacent structures for a rooftop PV layout.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: material handling in a warehouse. Relevant to moving sample stock, but the robot works between fixed pick/place points (cobot output, conveyor), not picking varied sample SKUs off ordinary shelving or carrying goods into customer premises.

tasks.label: Check stock levels and reorder merchandise as necessary.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Routed visit to a chain supermarket account: the rep walks aisles, endcaps and refrigerated sets checking on-shelf quantities and gaps for their own SKUs, glances at backroom overstock, then writes a replenishment order on a handheld during store hours with shoppers and staff present.

Visit to a warehouse club, supercenter or mass merchandiser: rep checks display pallets, floor stacks and overhead steel for their items across a very large sales floor, reconciles counts against the retailer's system, and submits the order for the next delivery.

Chain convenience store / gas-station account with a standardized planogram: rep counts facings on a few small shelf sets and in cooler doors, checks a small standardized back-stock area, and keys the reorder into a handheld.

Independent small retailer (bodega, liquor store, small hardware or gift shop): idiosyncratic layout, product stacked wherever it fits, crowded back room with mixed cases on the floor; rep counts shelf and back-stock units and writes the order.

Foodservice/hospitality account (restaurant, bar, cafeteria): rep counts cases, kegs, bottles and partial cases in the walk-in cooler, dry storage and behind the bar, amid other vendors' goods stacked as found, then writes the week's order.

Checking the rep's own company's stock position: verifying on-hand quantities of racked, labeled inventory in the distributor's warehouse/DC (or the rep's van stock) before committing customer orders, and triggering a replenishment order to the manufacturer.

sources.title: Simbe's Tally Inventory Robot Deployed in Harmons Stores Following Pilot Success
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally, an autonomous shelf-scanning robot, is deployed across 17 supermarket locations of grocer Harmons, capturing real-time shelf-level data on ... to replace manual stock verification.
sources.transferJustification: The rep's stock check is SKU-level counting of on-shelf inventory in a retail aisle; Tally performs exactly that perception task autonomously in the same aisles, producing the availability data the reorder decision rests on.

sources.title: BJ's Wholesale Club to Power Up Shelf-Scanning Robots at All Locations
sources.claim: Tally autonomously roams club aisles ... at BJ's Wholesale Club, which contracted to deploy it in all 237 clubs, collecting shelf data on in-stock status, placement and price.
sources.transferJustification: Same object class (packaged consumer goods on club shelves and pallets) and same output (per-SKU availability and quantity) as a rep's stock check in a club or big-box account.

sources.title: Beyond Grocery: How Autonomous Intelligence is Transforming Retail
sources.claim: In club stores Tally scans bulk product and overhead steel/overflow storage, i.e. the reserve stock a rep would otherwise count manually.
sources.transferJustification: Covers the overstock/back-stock portion of a rep's count in club and big-box formats, where reserve inventory sits in racking above the sales floor.

sources.title: Inventory Replenishment — Simbe use cases
sources.claim: Simbe documents Tally's robot-collected inventory data feeding retailers' ordering systems for automated replenishment, closing the loop from stock check to reorder.
sources.transferJustification: The reorder half of the task is an order-entry step; this documents the robot's counts being passed into ordering systems rather than to a human order writer.

sources.title: Simbe's New Brand Insights Solution Offers Real-Time Data for Vendors
sources.claim: Simbe Brand Insights delivers robot-collected, SKU-level shelf availability and out-of-stock data directly to direct-store-delivery partners and CPG vendors — the same information a wholesale rep collects on a store call.
sources.transferJustification: Explicitly serves the wholesale/DSD rep's stock-visibility function with robot-collected store data, showing the perception work transfers to the vendor's reorder decision.

sources.system: Brain Corp Inventory Scan on BrainOS-powered Tennant scrubbers
sources.title: Sam's Club Installs Brain Corp. Inventory Scanners on Nearly 600 Robotic Scrubbers
sources.claim: Sam's Club completed a chain-wide rollout of Brain Corp Inventory Scan towers on nearly 600 autonomous Tennant floor scrubbers, capturing stock-level, pricing and product-location data as the robots move autonomously through the club.
sources.transferJustification: Chain-wide autonomous capture of product stock levels in a big-box club is the perception step of the rep's stock check in that same format.

sources.title: Battle of the bots: Kroger pilots autonomous inventory scanning robots
sources.claim: Badger Technologies' autonomous inventory-scanning robots monitor on-shelf availability in supermarket chains including Stop & Shop, The Giant Company and Woodman's, with Kroger piloting aisle-scanning bots.
sources.transferJustification: Second independent vendor performing autonomous per-SKU on-shelf availability checks in the same supermarket environment where reps check their stock.

sources.title: HomeBase USA deploys Simbe's Tally robot to two stores
sources.claim: Simbe's Tally has been deployed beyond grocery into home-improvement retail stores, showing the shelf-scanning stock check works across non-grocery retail sales floors.
sources.transferJustification: Extends demonstrated coverage from grocery to hardlines retail, the format of many non-technical wholesale accounts.

sources.title: Pilot project takes automated inventory management to the next level (DC Velocity)
sources.claim: Verity's inventory drones autonomously fly warehouse aisles at Maersk sites, scanning pallet barcodes and reconciling counts with the warehouse management system; Maersk extended the system to warehouses with pallet storage.
sources.transferJustification: Checking on-hand stock of racked, labeled cases in a distributor warehouse is the same counting-and-reconciliation output the rep needs before committing orders or reordering.

sources.title: Autonomous warehouse drones streamline inventory control (TechTarget)
sources.claim: Gather AI's autonomous warehouse drones count inventory including barcodes, lot codes, expiration ... at customers such as Geodis and WinSupply.
sources.transferJustification: Case-level counting of stacked cases against a system of record is the same measurement a rep makes when counting cases in a stockroom; demonstrated in racked, labeled institutional storage.

sources.title: Gather AI adds warehouse intelligence to inventory visibility
sources.claim: Gather AI released depth-sensor-based case counting able to handle partial and mixed pallets, with obstacle avoidance for items such as a forklift parked in an aisle.
sources.transferJustification: Counting partial and mixed case stacks is the core measurement in a stockroom count; demonstrated only where stock is racked and presented in labeled locations.

tasks.label: Plan, assemble, and stock product displays in retail stores, or make recommendations to retailers regarding product displays, promotional programs, and advertising.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket / grocery sales floor during store hours: rep builds a promotional secondary display for their brand — erects a corrugated floor stand or end-cap unit (or stacks a pallet display), cuts cases open, loads and faces product, attaches the header card and price sign, and clears cardboard. Shoppers, carts and store staff move through the aisle.

Convenience store, small grocer or liquor store: rep pulls the brand's backstock and restocks/faces its shelf section or reach-in cooler doors, loading from behind so older stock sells first, straightening and blocking facings. Layout is the standard chain fixture set; work happens while the store is open.

Chain drug, mass-merchant or supermarket aisle: rep executes a section reset to a new planogram for the category — strips the old set, moves shelf brackets/shelves, applies new shelf strips, tags and shelf talkers, and re-lays product per the schematic, often overnight or early morning with store approval.

Advisory sales call: rep meets the store manager, category buyer or owner, walks the store, and recommends display locations, promotional programs, ad features and space allocation, presenting planograms/promo calendars and negotiating commitments. No product is physically handled beyond gesturing at shelves.

Large seasonal or multi-SKU promotional build: rep assembles a big holiday floor stack / multi-tier corrugated display carrying several SKUs, inserts shelf separators and dividers, loads dozens of cases, adds branded signage and cutouts, in the store's promotional zone or lobby.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA restocking robot was mass produced and installed in 300 FamilyMart convenience ..., restocking bottles and cans into refrigerated display shelves under autonomous AI control, with rare remote VR takeover only to recover errors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing and facing packaged beverages in a retail store's chilled display. Transfers to the rep's cooler/shelf restocking instance — same objects (cans/bottles/packaged goods), same shelf geometry, same in-store setting.

sources.title: Telexistence Wins the Prime Minister’s Award at the Japan Startup Awards 2025 – TELEXISTENCE inc.
sources.claim: As of 2025 Telexistence states its GHOST beverage-restocking robots have automated the majority of beverage ... work in convenience stores, with the service expanded to 7-Eleven stores in Tokyo.
sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as TX SCARA: in-store stocking of packaged drinks into the retailer's display case, showing the capability is still commercially operating in 2025.

sources.system: Comau NJ40 / NS12 robotic display-building line (Siscodata integration)
sources.title: Robots assemble, pack, and stack grocery retail displays at 40/hr | Packaging World
sources.claim: At the Number1 co-packing facility, six-axis robots automatically erect corrugated box-pallet and tray displays used for retail grocery promotions and then fill them with product, inserting separators and closing/gluing the packs, at roughly 40 displays per hour inside a guarded production cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling and filling the very promotional displays the rep would build — same corrugated display blanks and cased grocery products, to shippable retail-display quality, with the work fixtured and presented to the machine.

sources.title: Robots assemble, pack, and stack grocery retail displays at 40/hr | Packaging World
sources.claim: A second robot group on the same line fills the erected displays with a range of packaging formats using automatically changed grippers, i.e. the machines both build and stock mixed-format retail promotional displays.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: stocking a promotional display with multiple SKUs/formats — the multi-SKU seasonal build instance, executed with the display fixtured in a purpose-built cell.

sources.developer: Pepperidge Farm (Campbell Soup) with packaging integrator

sources.claim: Pepperidge Farm runs robotic case packing that loads cases, trays and retail-ready displays with bagged snack product in its plant, a commercially deployed purpose-built cell.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: filling retail-ready display units with the product later merchandised in store; corroborates that display stocking is routinely completed by machines when work is brought to a fixtured cell.

sources.system: TriVex SL & SLi case & tray packer
sources.title: TriVex SL & SLi Case & Tray Packer | Products | Douglas Machine
sources.claim: Douglas Machine sells the TriVex SL/SLi robotic case and tray packer specifically for retail-ready packaging, with SCARA-arm collation and case erecting/sealing options, as a current commercial product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: erecting and filling retail-ready display trays; shows the fixtured-cell display-building capability is current commercial equipment, not only a legacy installation.

sources.developer: University of Padova / KTH / Animum AB
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator (arXiv:2509.11740v2)
sources.claim: A 2026 research system using an off-the-shelf mobile manipulator achieved over 98% success across more than 700 supermarket shelf stocking pick-and-place events, but only in laboratory conditions replicating a supermarket with ArUco markers, and the authors report performance and cost remain inferior to human workers.
sources.transferJustification: Directly the stocking half of the task, but validated only in a marker-instrumented lab replica — evidence for a purpose-built setting (E1) and explicit evidence that unaided in-store performance is not yet at worker level.

tasks.label: Provide product samples, coupons, informational brochures, or other incentives to persuade people to buy products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warehouse-club/supermarket food demo: worker staffs a demo cart in a store aisle for a multi-hour shift, keeps the product hot/fresh, keeps a tray of sample cups filled, hands samples to a steady stream of shoppers, delivers a short pitch, answers questions, points to the display and offers the coupon/deal, and keeps the station food-safe and clean.

Handout of pre-packaged samples, branded items and coupons in a controlled indoor venue (mall concourse, club-store entrance, hotel/office lobby, casino floor, restaurant, cafeteria, showroom): the promoter roams or stands with a tray, greets passersby, gives a scripted pitch and puts the sample/coupon in their hand.

Trade show or convention booth: promoter works the aisle in front of the booth, hands brochures, spec sheets, discount codes and swag/samples to attendees, engages them with a short pitch, answers basic product questions and captures contact details for follow-up.

Outdoor street team / festival / campus / stadium-gate sampling: promoter works a sidewalk, plaza, tailgate lot or festival ground in variable weather and crowds, intercepts pedestrians, hands out product samples, flyers and coupons, and delivers a brief pitch.

In-store non-food demonstration with consultative sampling (cosmetics/fragrance/skincare counter, supplements, small electronics): one-on-one conversation with a shopper about their needs, sometimes applying or demonstrating the product, then giving a sample sachet/trial size plus a coupon to close the sale.

sources.title: KettyBot - The Future of Delivery and Reception | Pudu Robotics
sources.claim: Pudu's KettyBot, a commercially sold autonomous service robot with SLAM navigation, has a Cruise Mode in which it roams a defined area offering customers free snacks and drinks from its trays while broadcasting promotional messages — i.e., roving sample-and-promotion handout inside restaurants and retail venues.

sources.title: Promoter | PROMOBOT
sources.claim: Promobot markets and sells its V.4 service robot in a 'promoter' configuration for exhibitions, conferences, expos and malls; listed functions include giving information on company and services, printing receipts/coupons on its built-in thermal printer, answering questions, and navigating autonomously among people.

sources.title: PROMOBOT — autonomous service robot
sources.claim: Promobot units are deployed in shopping centers where the robot autonomously approaches shoppers, tells them about stores and discounts, and steers them to a store — the persuasion-plus-incentive element of the task in a structured retail venue.

sources.title: Robot.com turns autonomous robots into mobile advertising network with launch of R-ads platform
sources.claim: Robot.com (formerly Kiwibot) runs a robotic advertising/sampling network: fleets of autonomous ground robots roll through campuses, conference venues and city streets carrying brand creative and handing samples to passersby, with 100+ brand activations across 20+ countries and 500+ robots deployed.

sources.title: Serve Robotics Becomes First Autonomous Vehicle Company to Commercially Launch Level 4 Self-Driving Robots
sources.claim: Serve Robotics operates commercial sidewalk robots at SAE Level 4 autonomy — routinely navigating public sidewalks and handing goods to people at the curb without human intervention in designated areas.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sidewalk delivery. It establishes that outdoor pedestrian-environment navigation and handing a small consumer package to a person on a public sidewalk is done autonomously at commercial reliability — the physical core of outdoor street sampling.

sources.title: Media Partnerships Case Studies | Kiwibot & Nickelytics | The Ad Council
sources.claim: An Ad Council campaign used a fleet of Kiwibot sidewalk delivery robots as roving promotional media on Howard University's campus, covering 130+ miles of high-traffic campus paths over a month and reaching 140k people.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile outdoor brand promotion. Same robots, same outdoor campus/sidewalk setting and same promotional purpose as street sampling; it shows sustained unattended promotional operation among pedestrians.

sources.system: Blendid / Jamba by Blendid robotic kiosk
sources.title: Jamba Expands Robotic Smoothie Kiosk to Second Location
sources.claim: Blendid's foodOS-driven robotic kiosk autonomously prepares fresh smoothies to order and holds them for pickup by consumers, deployed inside Walmart stores, a shopping mall and a university — a self-contained, purpose-built station that prepares and hands a fresh food/beverage portion to a member of the public.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic preparation and hand-off of a food/beverage serving to a shopper in a retail location. It is the sampling station rebuilt around the machine — product loaded into the fixture, portions produced and presented to the consumer at the window.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves drinks at Kennedy Space Center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM, a stationary dual-arm robot using an AI vision closed-loop control system, prepares and serves drinks to the public at retail stores, casinos, stadiums and event venues, having served more than 16,000 drinks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic beverage preparation and hand-off to consumers at retail and event venues. Same objects (cups/servings), same precision, same customer-facing hand-off as a sampling station where the product is brought to the machine.

sources.title: Asda pilots automated free sample vending machine
sources.claim: Asda piloted an automated free-sample dispensing machine in a supermarket, letting shoppers collect free product samples without a human demonstrator present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended free-sample distribution to shoppers. The output is identical to the demonstrator's — a sample plus trial offer in the shopper's hand — with the work brought to a purpose-built dispensing station.

tasks.label: Keep areas neat while working and return items to correct locations following demonstrations.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warehouse-club or supermarket food-sampling demo: between and after samples the promoter wipes the demo cart and counter, discards used cups, napkins and toothpicks, washes/sanitizes utensils, tongs and the griddle or toaster oven, restocks sample supplies, and carries unused product cases back to the correct cooler or shelf location before packing the cart at shift end; work happens in a busy aisle with shoppers and carts, under health-code sanitation rules.

Big-box or specialty retail non-food demo (vacuum, kitchen appliance, TV/electronics, toy): after each demo the promoter repacks the demo unit and accessories into its box, coils cords, sweeps up demo debris (dirt, water, product residue), and returns demonstrated units and customer-handled merchandise to their exact planogram shelf positions, facing the display.

Cosmetics, fragrance or skincare demonstration at a department-store or beauty-retailer counter: sanitize brushes, applicators and testers between customers, wipe mirrors, trays and countertop, discard used cotton pads and wipes, and return each tester and product to its precise slot in the display case or under-counter drawer.

Trade show or convention booth demonstration: between scheduled presentations reset the booth - return demo units, tablets, literature, giveaways and samples to their staged positions or carrying cases, straighten table covers and signage, clear cups and packaging - then repack everything into crates at teardown.

Mobile or outdoor promotion (street team, festival, farmers market, sampling tent or branded vehicle): tidy the tent and table during the event, collect litter and empty sample containers from around the site, return unused product to coolers, and pack signage, tables and product back into the vehicle, leaving the site as found; crowds, weather and uneven ground.

sources.title: Amazon robotics: Meet the robots inside fulfillment centers
sources.claim: Amazon's Sparrow robotic arm autonomously picks individual products out of containers and places them into specific designated totes in fulfillment centers; deployed in production sites and able to handle a large share of Amazon's item catalog.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: goods-to-robot item sortation and put-away. It is the E1 form of 'return items to correct locations' - varied consumer packaged goods presented to a fixed robotic station are identified and placed into the correct designated receptacle at production reliability.

sources.title: Dishcraft Introduces Automated Dishroom for Commercial Kitchens | Hospitality Technology
sources.claim: Dishcraft's purpose-built robotic dishroom cleans dishware loaded onto a cart, inspecting each piece with computer vision for food residue; sold as a commercial system for corporate and institutional kitchens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: washing food-service ware. Cleaning the utensils, trays and dishware used in a sampling demo is the same object class and cleanliness standard, done in a purpose-built machine to which the load is presented - the E1 presentation assumption.

sources.system: Robotic table wiping (RL + whole-body trajectory optimization) on an Everyday Robots mobile manipulator
sources.title: Robotic Table Wiping via Reinforcement Learning and Whole-body Trajectory Optimization (arXiv 2210.10865)
sources.claim: A mobile manipulator autonomously wipes tables to clean crumbs and spills, planning wiping actions from visual observation of the soiled surface.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: surface wiping. Keeping a demo counter or booth table neat requires exactly this - removing crumbs and spills from a flat work surface - with comparable objects and precision.

sources.title: Alphabet's X has 'Everyday Robots' test fleet that autonomously performs office maintenance tasks
sources.claim: A prototype fleet of over 100 mobile manipulators performed chores autonomously in Google offices, including sorting trash and wiping tables ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: trash sorting and table wiping inside a human work facility. Closest E2 analogue to tidying a demo area, but a research prototype fleet performing isolated sub-steps, not employer-accepted completion of a whole cleanup.

sources.title: The Worldfolio: Telexistence: Revolutionizing robotics
sources.claim: Telexistence TX SCARA restocks bottled and canned drinks into their correct shelf positions in FamilyMart convenience-store coolers, running autonomously the large majority of the time with rare remote takeover; deployed in hundreds of stores.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing merchandise into correct shelf locations in a store. It shows the capability only inside a dedicated rail-mounted installation in the walk-in cooler handling uniform bottles and cans, not on an open sales floor with mixed merchandise.

sources.title: Brain Corp: Sam's Club Deploying Autonomous Robots
sources.claim: Hundreds of BrainOS-powered Tennant autonomous floor scrubbers clean the floors of Sam's Club and Walmart stores; this is the manipulation-free extent of deployed 'neatness' robotics on a retail sales floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: keeping a retail area clean. Establishes what is actually deployed in an E2 store - floor scrubbing only, with no pick-and-place of merchandise and no counter or equipment cleaning.

sources.title: Helix: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Generalist Humanoid Control
sources.claim: Two Figure 02 humanoids running a single Helix vision-language-action policy autonomously put away unfamiliar grocery items into a fridge and cabinets in a home-like kitchen at the developer's facility.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: putting varied consumer goods away in their proper storage places. Comparable objects and precision to returning demo merchandise, but a staged demo in a developer mock kitchen rather than sustained employer-quality work.

sources.title: A VLA with Open-World Generalization (pi-0.5)
sources.claim: Physical Intelligence's pi-0.5 policy drives a mobile manipulator to tidy kitchens and bedrooms in homes never seen during training, though the developers state the model is far from perfect and often makes mistakes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: general tidying and putting objects away in unstructured settings. Nearest E3 evidence for this task, but the developers characterize reliability as well below a worker-acceptable standard.

sources.date: case study page dated 2026-04; robot in service since ~2022
sources.title: Angsa Robotics Uses Swift to Increase Efficiency of Autonomous Trash Picking Robots
sources.claim: Angsa's outdoor robot autonomously detects and collects small litter from grass and gravel areas such as parks and open-air festival grounds, avoiding obstacles and needing no beacons or boundary wires.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: outdoor litter collection at event sites. Covers only ground litter on lawn and gravel; it cannot pack promotional gear, product or signage, so it does not complete the outdoor cleanup instance.

tasks.label: Demonstrate or explain products, methods, or services to persuade customers to purchase products or use services.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warehouse-club or supermarket sampling demo cart (Costco/Sam's Club/Kroger style): worker wheels a cart to an assigned aisle spot, heats or preps that week's rotating item (convection oven, griddle), portions it into cups, hands samples to passing shoppers with a short scripted pitch, answers questions, points shoppers to the pallet, keeps food-safety logs, restocks and breaks the station down.

Fixed in-store tasting/sampling counter with a fixed product line: wine-and-spirits tastings at a liquor store, coffee/smoothie or beverage sampling table, packaged-sample table; worker pours or assembles the sample from a set menu of stocked items, gives product information and a recommendation, and encourages purchase of the featured SKU.

Retail sales-floor pitch at a featured-product display in a big-box or appliance/electronics store: worker stands beside the coffee machine, TV, appliance or service-plan display, engages passing shoppers, explains features and benefits, answers questions and steers customers to buy; little skilled manipulation of the merchandise itself.

Hands-on demonstration requiring skilled operation of the merchandise or application to the customer: running a vacuum over spilled dirt, cooking with a blender/cookware/knife set at a store or fair booth, showing a cleaning product on a stain, or applying cosmetics/skincare to a customer's hand or face at a beauty counter, while narrating and closing the sale.

Trade show, expo or mall-kiosk promotion: worker staffs a booth or kiosk in a convention hall or mall concourse, attracts passersby, delivers the product/service presentation, hands out literature, swag or small samples, answers questions and captures leads or sign-ups.

Field/event promotion in unstructured settings: brand ambassador handing out samples and pitching at a street festival, sidewalk, campus quad, tailgate or sporting-event plaza; or an in-home / party-plan demonstration (vacuum, water filtration, cookware) in a customer's living room.

sources.title: Wakefern adds sampling kiosks to 95 stores | Grocery Dive
sources.claim: Freeosk automated sampling kiosks stand unattended on grocery and club store floors and dispense product samples to shoppers with on-screen product messaging and purchase tracking; the company reported roughly 2,000 devices in US stores including Sam's Club and Wakefern banners as of January 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated in-store product sampling. It performs the physical core of a demonstrator's sampling shift - putting a sample of the promoted item into a shopper's hand together with the brand message - in the same store aisles where human demonstrators work, but from a purpose-built machine station rather than a roving cart.

sources.title: Low-Touch to No-Touch: Freeosk Solves the 'New Norm' Dilemma of Instore Product Sampling
sources.claim: Freeosk kiosks were explicitly positioned and enhanced as a machine substitute for person-to-person in-store sampling when human sampling was suspended.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store product sampling. Establishes that retailers and brands accept machine-dispensed sampling in place of the human demonstrator's sample hand-off, which is the physical output of the sampling instance.

sources.date: 2022-03 launch; still operating per 2024-12 and 2025-01 coverage
sources.title: RoboBurger, a Robot Burger Chef in a Vending Machine Format, Launches Nationally | Hospitality Technology
sources.claim: RoboBurger is a fully autonomous robotic burger kiosk that grills and assembles a burger from scratch and serves it to walk-up customers; it operates in a Simon shopping mall in Jersey City and at St John's University.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended hot-food preparation and hand-off to walk-up consumers. It substantiates that a purpose-built machine station can cook and serve hot food portions to the public, the physical production step of a hot-food sampling demo.

sources.title: Blendid teams with Jamba on robotic smoothie maker in Walmart store | Retail Customer Experience
sources.claim: Blendid operates autonomous robotic food kiosks inside Walmart stores that select, measure, blend and hand fresh smoothies to shoppers without staff.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic preparation and serving of fresh food/beverage portions to shoppers inside a retail store - the same objects (cups, ingredients), same store-floor environment, and same hand-off as an in-store beverage sampling demo.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics Introduces Scorpion, an AI-Powered Single-Arm Beverage Service Robot
