instances.label: Food/beverage sampling station in a supermarket or warehouse club: retrieve the demo cart and supplies from the back room, wheel it to an assigned aisle end or entry area, wipe/sanitize the surface, drape the cart skirt or tablecloth, set up an induction burner or toaster oven and plug it in, lay out sample cups, napkins, product cases and a price/feature sign so the station draws shoppers.

Non-food product demonstration area in a store (electronics, cookware, cosmetics, vacuums): unbox demo units and accessories, arrange them on a table or vendor display fixture in an attention-getting layout, connect power/water, stage samples and literature, and place branded signage and pricing.

Trade show / consumer expo booth setup in a convention center hall: assemble retractable banner stands or a modular pop-up panel display, drape the skirted table, position lighting and a monitor, lay out product samples, giveaways and brochures, and align everything within the assigned booth footprint before doors open.

Vendor-rep merchandising of a promotional display in a retail store: erect a corrugated floor shipper or set up an endcap, load product into the display, attach the header/topper sign and shelf talkers, and face/front the products neatly before and during the shift.

Mall kiosk or pop-up shop: set out and arrange merchandise and testers on a kiosk counter or small display case each morning, position signage and samplers, and restore/restock the arrangement between customers.

Outdoor street team / festival or farmers-market promotion: erect a pop-up canopy tent and weight it, unfold folding tables, drape covers, hang or stake banners, and lay out product samples in wind and variable ground conditions.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA is deployed in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores, autonomously restocking and placing beverages on cooler shelves from a fixed track, with remote operators taking over only in rare failure cases.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: shelf restocking/facing in a retail store. It shows the product-placement portion of arranging a display can be done in a store, but only on a rail-mounted rig against a fixed, known cooler shelf; it cannot move carts, drape cloth, assemble signage or build a demo station, so it does not substantiate whole-instance display setup in a store.

sources.system: Stretch 3 stocking/fronting system ('From Pixels to Shelf')
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator

sources.transferJustification: Related task: placing and fronting retail products on a shelf. Comparable objects (packaged consumer goods) and precision to arranging product on a display, but demonstrated only in a marker-instrumented lab mock-up, supporting a purpose-built (E1) setting rather than a live store.

sources.title: Walmart and Symbotic work together to implement high-tech automation system into distribution network

sources.title: Automated Palletizing & Depalletizing Systems | Toyota Automated Logistics
sources.claim: Commercial vision-guided robotic palletizing cells build mixed-SKU pallets to stored patterns, switching patterns automatically and handling varied case sizes and packaging types to create store-ready loads.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: pattern-based placement of assorted product presented in sequence. Establishes that, when inputs arrive fixtured and sequenced in a purpose-built cell, robots reliably arrange heterogeneous consumer goods into a prescribed display layout at commercial reliability.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: assembling a knock-down consumer structure from parts laid out in a fixtured workcell — comparable to erecting a banner stand, modular booth panel or folding display rack when the components are presented in known poses. sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous manipulation of flat textiles (grasping, separating, spreading, folding) at a fixed dual-arm station — the closest demonstrated analogue to draping a table skirt or cloth over a fixtured demo table, and only demonstrated at such a fixed station.

Community organizations and outdoor public venues: county fair or festival booth, farmers market, campus/street sampling team, presentation at a community or senior center. Layout varies by site, weather and crowds uncontrolled, samples and literature handed to passersby.
In-home party-plan demonstration or on-site client visit: present and use the product for a small invited group in a private residence or a customer's own premises, tailor the pitch, take orders.

Off-site outdoor event sampling (festival, farmers market, tailgate, parking-lot promotion): load a van, drive to the site, unload on grass or asphalt, erect a pop-up canopy and folding tables, set out coolers, product, and branded fabric skirting in wind and weather, then strike everything and reload.

In-home or on-site personal demonstration (vacuums, water filtration, cookware, home improvement products; home-party demos): carry cases from the vehicle into a customer's home, unpack, assemble the demo unit and small display materials on the customer's floor or table amid household clutter, then disassemble and repack after the presentation.

tasks.label: Practice demonstrations to ensure that they will run smoothly.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Warehouse-club/grocery sampling demo: before the shift the demonstrator sets up the demo cart in the aisle, tests the induction burner or toaster oven, cooks a practice batch of the sample food, checks portioning, timing and holding, and runs through the sample hand-off and pitch until the sequence flows.

Housewares/appliance demo (vacuum, cookware, kitchen gadget, cleaning product) at a big-box store or home/fair show booth: the promoter rehearses the multi-step product routine with the actual merchandise - assembling it, staging the prop mess or ingredients, operating it, resetting it - to verify it works, fix snags, and time the routine to the crowd cycle.

Trade show / consumer-electronics or B2B booth at a convention center: the demonstrator sets up devices, laptops and AV, runs the scripted demo end to end several times before doors open, troubleshoots connectivity or software hiccups, and times the loop so it fits a 5-minute booth visit.

Cosmetics, skincare or personal-care counter in a department store: the demonstrator practices the application technique on a mannequin head, a colleague or their own hand, lays out testers, tools and sanitizing supplies, and rehearses the talking points so the live application runs cleanly.

Off-site preparation before a party-plan, farmers-market, mall-kiosk or in-home direct-sales demo: the promoter unpacks and assembles the demo kit at home or in a garage, runs the full demonstration alone, spots what fails or runs long, and reworks the sequence and packing order.

sources.title: Next-gen Digit humanoid wants to automate logistics tasks - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Agility Robotics' Digit humanoid performed autonomous tote-handling demonstrations in a replica warehouse cell inside the company's booth at the ProMat trade show - a robot executing a rehearsed promotional routine on a show floor.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: performing a demonstration routine at a trade show booth. Closest analogue to a demonstrator's booth routine, but the robot only replays an engineered pick-and-place cell with fixtured totes; the human engineers, not the robot, rehearse, diagnose and adjust the demo.

sources.title: Self-Improving Robots: End-to-End Autonomous Visuomotor Reinforcement Learning (arXiv:2303.01488)
sources.claim: MEDAL++ is a research system in which a robot arm autonomously practices a manipulation task in a lab, repeatedly doing and undoing it to improve without human resets.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot 'practicing' to improve reliability. Transfer fails: practice targets a single short lab manipulation skill on a fixed tabletop rig, not an end-to-end product demonstration with merchandise, appliances, timing and spoken patter, and it is a lab research result rather than a rehearsal that certifies a demo is show-ready.

sources.title: Meet ADAM, the Nvidia-Powered NHL Arena Bartender Robot | Technology Magazine
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM dual-arm robot autonomously prepares and serves drinks in customer-facing venues such as arenas and coffee shops, performing a fixed-menu routine in front of the public.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: crowd-facing beverage preparation in a public venue, similar in spirit to a sampling demo. It does not substantiate this task because ADAM executes a pre-engineered fixed-menu recipe from a fixed kiosk; it does not rehearse a new demonstration, judge whether it runs smoothly, or revise the routine.

sources.title: About Miso Robotics | AI Kitchen Innovators
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy autonomously runs the fry station in commercial restaurant kitchens at chains including White Castle and Jack in the Box.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous cooking of a food product in a structured facility - the manipulation core of a food-sampling practice batch. Falls short here because Flippy works only at a purpose-built fry station with dedicated hoppers and baskets, and performs no rehearsal, no self-assessment of a demo's smoothness, and no presentation.

sources.title: Use Case: Dry Run - Opentrons Documentation
sources.claim: Opentrons lab robots offer a 'dry run' mode in which the robot steps through a protocol without reagents so the operator can check it before the real run.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a machine executing a rehearsal pass of a routine before the real one. Transfer fails: the dry run is a scripted replay on a fixed labware deck that a human watches and judges; the robot neither authors nor evaluates the routine, and the objects bear no resemblance to demo merchandise or an audience-facing pitch.

tasks.label: Instruct customers in alteration of products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Big-box, warehouse-club or department-store sales floor: demonstrator shows shoppers how to modify a product for their use — swapping blender or vacuum attachments, resizing a watch band, reconfiguring a tool, adding a filter — handing it over so the shopper tries it while the demonstrator corrects them; crowded aisle, varied shoppers, product pulled from stock.

Trade show, expo or vendor-day booth: manufacturer's rep instructs prospects in reconfiguring or customizing the demo unit (changing dies, blades, settings, modular parts) to fit the prospect's described application; noisy hall, short interactions, prospects handling the unit.

Fabric, craft, sewing-machine or specialty store: demonstrator instructs customers in altering garments or projects — hemming, changing presser feet or needles, adjusting patterns, fitting accessories — with the customer at the machine and the demonstrator guiding fabric and hands.

Mall kiosk, farmers-market stand or managed fair/festival booth: promoter instructs buyers in customizing the item just purchased (resizing jewelry, applying a screen protector or trim, adjusting straps, seasoning/curing cookware), with weather, crowd and improvised table setup.

Customer's business premises (salon, restaurant kitchen, repair shop, dealership): rep visits and instructs the staff in altering or reconfiguring the product for their workflow, using the customer's own units and space.

In-home party or private demonstration (kitchenware, cutlery, cosmetics, home products): demonstrator instructs guests in altering the product — resharpening, changing blades, mixing or tinting a custom shade, adapting a component — in a private home taken as found.

sources.system: Galbot G-1 / 'Xiao Gai' autonomous store humanoid

It does not transfer, because the robot handles standardized packaged inventory and never modifies a customer's product or coaches a customer through performing an alteration.

sources.title: Nestlé to use humanoid robot to sell Nescafé in Japan
sources.claim: Pepper humanoids were deployed in over a thousand Japanese appliance stores to promote and sell Nescafé coffee machines through conversation and screen content, with no dexterous manipulation of the products.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-store product promotion by a robot. It does not transfer to instructing customers in alteration, because Pepper only speaks and displays media; it cannot pick up, alter, or hand over a product, which is the substance of hands-on alteration instruction.

sources.title: Ulta Beauty Introduces Five-Step Robotic Manicure by Robotics Firm 10Beauty

It does not transfer: the machine executes one fixed procedure on the customer's hands and explicitly relies on human staff for customer education and customization, the instructional core of this task.

sources.title: TeachBot: Towards teaching robotics fundamentals for human-robot collaboration at work
sources.claim: TeachBot, a robotic instructor that lectures and demonstrates to workers on a manufacturing line, is the closest autonomous robot-as-instructor system, but it teaches robotics fundamentals using pre-programmed motions and exists as a research study rather than a deployed product.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: a robot autonomously instructing humans in a hands-on procedure. It does not transfer, because the curriculum and demonstration motions are pre-programmed for one fixed subject, so it cannot diagnose a customer's product and teach an alteration on varied consumer goods.

tasks.label: Work as part of a team of demonstrators to accommodate large crowds.

instances.label: Weekend food/beverage sampling program in a warehouse club or supermarket: a dozen demonstrators staff carts around the store, one covers a neighbor's cart during peak, cooking/portioning samples, handing them to a crowd pressing around the cart, restocking, answering questions and pushing the featured SKU.

Trade show or convention booth staffed by a team of product promoters during peak floor hours: rotating scheduled demos of the exhibited merchandise (equipment, gadgets, vehicles), hands-on trials with attendees, fielding technical questions, handing literature/swag and capturing leads while queues build.

Non-food in-store demo/roadshow team (cookware, vacuums, cosmetics, consumer electronics) in a big-box or department store: a lead presenter draws a crowd with a staged demonstration while teammates run one-on-one product trials, apply samples to customers, and close sales.

Brand activation team at a controlled venue (mall atrium, arena concourse, convention party, corporate event): several promoters serve drinks/snacks/swag to heavy foot traffic, keep the line moving, restock, and deliver a short pitch to each guest.

Outdoor street/festival team sampling in public space (sidewalk, campus quad, tailgate lot, parade route): promoters fan out with branded coolers or carts, work a moving, uncontrolled crowd in weather, hand product and coupons, and regroup to restock from a van.

tasks.label: Stock shelves with products.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Supermarket or mass-merchant sales floor: a brand demonstrator/promoter replenishes the shelf section of the product being promoted during store hours - pulls backstock or a U-boat cart from the backroom, cuts open corrugated cases, places units on gondola shelves per planogram, faces and date-rotates existing stock, and breaks down cardboard while shoppers move through the aisle.

Club store / mass-merchant road show or promotional event: the promoter keeps a pallet display, end cap or dump bin stocked - moving cases from a pallet in the aisle, cutting trays, stacking heavy units neatly on the display, and keeping it faced and shoppable through the day.

In-store sampling/demo station: the promoter keeps the demo cart/table stocked with sellable product, coupons and literature, and tops off the adjacent shelf or side-stack display between customer interactions, in a crowded aisle with a cart, cooler and a small stock of mixed items.

Beverage/snack brand rep at a convenience or grocery store: loads bottles, cans and single-serve packs into refrigerated cooler shelves and a small branded rack, rotating older stock forward, working from cases delivered to the store.

Trade show or convention booth: the promoter unpacks shipping cases and stocks booth shelving, product tables and giveaway bins before doors open, then restocks them repeatedly through the show day in a rented hall with standard booth fixtures.

Outdoor or pop-up venue (farmers market stand, festival tent, mall-entrance kiosk, sidewalk table): the promoter sets out folding tables/racks and stocks them with product, coping with uneven ground, wind, weather and no fixed layout.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores
sources.claim: TX SCARA, a rail-mounted robot arm, autonomously restocks refrigerated beverage shelves with bottles and cans in FamilyMart convenience stores; mass deployment to 300 stores began August 2022, with ~98% automatic success and up to 1,000 containers per day.

sources.title: Restocking robots deployed in 300 Japanese convenience stores - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Trade press confirms the deployment: GORDON AI runs the robot autonomously during routine shelf-restocking in 300 Japanese convenience stores, with remote teleoperated recovery only for dropped or misplaced items.

sources.title: Telexistence Expands Beverage Shelf-Stocking Service with "TX Ghost" Robots
sources.claim: Telexistence continued and expanded its beverage shelf-stocking service in 2025 with TX Ghost robots piloting at select 7-Eleven stores in ..., restocking chilled backroom shelving.

sources.date: 2026 (page current July 2026; Auchan CFC live Nov 2025)
sources.title: The technology Re:Imagining online grocery - Ocado Group
sources.claim: Ocado's On-Grid Robotic Pick uses machine vision and learned grasping to pick and densely pack tens of thousands of distinct grocery SKUs autonomously in purpose-built fulfilment centres; it is rolled out across 14 CFCs with over 350 million picks, and Luton picks ~50% of volume robotically across 45,000 SKUs.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic grocery order picking and packing. It handles the identical object class a promoter shelves (bottles, boxes, bags, fragile packaged goods across 45,000 SKUs) at human-comparable precision inside a purpose-built cell where the work is presented to the arm - the E1 counterfactual for shelf stocking.

sources.system: 'From Pixels to Shelf' mobile manipulator (ROS2 perception, behavior trees, MPC, ArUco-referenced shelves)
sources.title: From Pixels to Shelf: An Integrated Robotic System for Autonomous Supermarket Stocking with a Mobile Manipulator
sources.claim: An integrated autonomous mobile manipulator for supermarket shelf stocking achieved over 98% pick-and-place success across 700+ stocking events in a laboratory replicating supermarket conditions, while the authors state current autonomous systems remain inferior ... human workers in performance and cost.

sources.title: ACPaQ Robotic Mixed Case Palletizer - Swisslog
sources.claim: Swisslog's ACPaQ is a commercially sold robotic cell that depalletizes single-SKU inbound pallets and builds sequenced, store-friendly mixed-case pallets in distribution centres.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: building store-ready case stacks. Case-level grasping, sequencing and neat stacking of the same corrugated cases a promoter stacks onto a pallet display, performed in a fixtured cell where cases are presented - the E1 counterfactual for display stocking.

sources.title: DHL Group signs MOU with Boston Dynamics for additional 1,000-robot deployment and accelerates cross-business automation strategy
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Stretch autonomously handles floor-loaded corrugated cases in logistics facilities at up to 700 cases per ...; DHL signed an MOU in May 2025 for up to 1,000 additional units after proven deployments.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile robotic case handling. Shows sustained autonomous handling of mixed corrugated cases at commercial rates - the material a promoter moves when stocking pallet and bin displays.

sources.title: Galbot picks up $153M to commercialize G1 semi-humanoid - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Galbot's G1 wheeled dual-arm robot autonomously grasps and hands over packaged retail goods in small unmanned stores in Beijing, but these are purpose-built robot-operated store formats rather than ordinary staffed sales floors.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous grasping of packaged retail products from store shelving. Demonstrates shelf-level manipulation of promoter-type merchandise, but only inside stores built around the robot, so it does not substantiate work on ordinary staffed sales floors.

sources.title: Shelf-scanning, AI-powered robots hit supermarket aisles to mixed reviews | Packaging Europe
sources.claim: The retail robots deployed at scale on staffed supermarket sales floors (Simbe Tally, Badger Marty) are shelf-scanning inventory robots without manipulators; they flag out-of-stocks for human associates to fill rather than stocking shelves themselves.

tasks.label: Wear costumes or sign boards and walk in public to promote merchandise, services, or events.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Street-corner/sidewalk sign work: a promoter wears a sandwich board or holds a large arrow/banner sign on a public sidewalk or median outside a tax office, mattress store, apartment complex or restaurant, pacing a block-long stretch for a 3-5 hour shift, waving at passing motorists and pedestrians in heat, wind or rain.

Performative street promotion: sign spinner flipping and twirling an arrow sign, or a costumed waver (Statue of Liberty, chicken suit) dancing at a busy intersection to draw the attention of drivers and passersby to a nearby business, several hours per shift on a public corner.

Outdoor costumed mascot at a grand opening, car-lot sale, street fair or storefront sidewalk: wearing a full character suit, waving, high-fiving and posing for photos with children, handing out balloons/coupons, working an uncontrolled outdoor crowd in a parking lot or on a sidewalk.

Indoor roaming promoter inside a shopping mall, trade-show hall, stadium concourse or casino: wearing a branded costume or sign board, walking set routes past shoppers, distributing flyers/samples/coupons and steering people to a booth or store, on premises controlled by the venue operator.

Costumed character roaming a theme park, family entertainment center or big-box store interior: greeting guests, posing for photo ops and interacting with children while a handler manages the crowd, over repeated timed sets during the day.

sources.claim: Serve Robotics' autonomous sidewalk robots are sold to brands as mobile out-of-home advertising: the Ad Council's Smokey Bear campaign was carried on the robots as they operated on Los Angeles sidewalks.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous sidewalk food delivery. Transfer: the robot performs the same physical act as a sandwich-board walker - carrying branded signage at walking pace along public sidewalks among pedestrians and traffic for a shift - and the promotional impressions are the product explicitly sold to the advertiser.

sources.transferJustification: Same transfer as above: the paid deliverable is mobile branded signage moving through public streets, which is the output an employer buys when hiring a sign-board walker.

sources.claim: Serve's robots operate at Level 4 autonomy in designated service areas, i.e. without a human operator supervising or intervening.

sources.title: Serve Robotics has deployed 2,000+ delivery robots across the U.S. - The Robot Report

sources.title: KettyBot Pro will provide personalized customer service, says Pudu Robotics - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Pudu's KettyBot Pro is a commercially deployed autonomous mobile robot for restaurants, hotels, malls and retail that roams with an 18.5-inch ad screen to attract, greet and guide customers and display promotional content; the robot has autonomous path planning.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: reception/delivery robot with mobile advertising display. Transfer: the promoter's core output - moving through a venue carrying promotional signage, hailing passers-by and steering them to the product - is the robot's marketed function, in the same indoor human venues (malls, hotels, stores).

sources.title: RoboAds introduces the world's first mobile advertising robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: RoboAds' RoboSignage is a mobile advertising robot built to roam indoor public venues (airports, malls, trade shows, metro stations) displaying advertising, navigating autonomously with two lidar scanners for obstacle avoidance.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same task performed by a machine: moving through a venue carrying a sign/ad display to promote merchandise. The article is vendor-sponsored trade content, so it is used as supporting rather than decisive evidence.

sources.system: Sota social robot promotional station (Ritsumeikan University field experiment)
sources.title: Behavioral Assessment of a Humanoid Robot When Attracting Pedestrians in a Mall (Int. J. Social Robotics)
sources.claim: In a real shopping mall, an autonomously behaving humanoid robot ran 6-hour promotional shifts attracting pedestrians and delivering advertising information to 5,000+ passers-by, with performance comparable to or better than human advertisers doing the same job.
sources.transferJustification: Same task class: drawing the attention of passers-by and conveying promotional information in a public-facing venue, benchmarked directly against human advertisers. The robot sat at an instrumented station in a mall corridor, so it covers the attention/engagement component rather than locomotion.

sources.developer: ATR / Osaka University (Shi, Satake, Kanda, Ishiguro)
sources.title: A Robot that Distributes Flyers to Pedestrians in a Shopping Mall - International Journal of Social Robotics
sources.claim: A humanoid robot was developed and field-tested distributing promotional flyers to uncooperative pedestrians in a real shopping mall, using a behavior model derived from human distributors.

sources.title: NVIDIA's Blue vs Disney Droids (BDX): Robotics Evolution
sources.claim: Disney's free-roaming BDX character droids in its theme parks - the closest deployed analogue to a roaming costumed mascot - are driven by an off-stage operator with a handler nearby, not by autonomous behavior.
sources.transferJustification: Negative evidence for the costumed-mascot instances: the most advanced deployed roaming character robot still requires a human puppeteer, so mascot meet-and-greet work is not substantiated as autonomous.

sources.title: Creepy Elon Musk 'Robot Dog' Spotted Roaming San Francisco Streets | eWeek
sources.claim: A costumed quadruped robot (Unitree Go2 with a silicone Elon Musk head) was sent through downtown San Francisco streets to promote an upcoming art exhibition and engaged passers-by; press called it autonomous but published no control details.
sources.transferJustification: Directly on-task (costumed robot walking in public to promote an event), but autonomy is unverified and it was a short publicity stunt, so it is treated as teleoperated and cannot support a positive judgment.

sources.title: Robot.com turns autonomous robots into mobile advertising network with launch of R-ads platform
sources.claim: Robot.com markets an advertising network of mobile robots that carry brand campaigns and hand out samples, claiming 500+ robots operating on campuses, warehouses and city streets across 100+ brand activations.
sources.transferJustification: Same task performed by machines (mobile branded signage and sample handout in public), but the article is press-release derived and does not establish per-activation autonomy, so it is supporting only.

roles.title: Models
roles.description: Model garments or other apparel and accessories for prospective buyers at fashion shows, private showings, or retail establishments. May pose for photos to be used in magazines or advertisements. May pose as subject for paintings, sculptures, and other types of artistic expression.

tasks.label: Pose for artists and photographers.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial studio photo shoot: model wears sample garments/accessories in a rented or in-house photography studio (seamless/cyc wall, strobes, stylist and art director present), holds and changes poses and facial expressions on the photographer's direction, hits marks with garments styled and pinned, over a multi-hour call, for e-commerce, catalog or advertising imagery of a human wearing the product.

On-location editorial or advertising shoot outdoors or in a found location (city street, beach, location house), with variable light, weather, wind and passers-by; the model walks, moves and poses dynamically in wardrobe while the photographer shoots continuously.

Life/figure modeling for an art class at an art school, atelier or community studio: model takes short gesture poses and sustained 20-30 minute held poses (nude or draped) on a stand under fixed lighting, while students draw, paint or sculpt the human figure from life; must hold and reprise poses accurately across breaks.

Sitting for a painter or sculptor in the artist's private studio: long periods of stillness in a single pose across multiple sessions, pose and lighting set by the artist, informal setting that varies from artist to artist.

Showroom / retail-establishment informal shooting: lookbook and fit photos, casting polaroids and social/behind-the-scenes content shot at a brand showroom, agency or retail store, with quick changes and simple standing/turning poses.

sources.title: As Robot Mannequins Fail To Scale, Virtual Fitting Room Fits.me Thinks It's Found The Answer | TechCrunch
sources.claim: Fits.me built shape-shifting robot mannequins that were dressed in garments and photographed in a studio rig to generate fit imagery for online retailers; the approach was expensive and did not scale, and the imagery was headless torso fit visualisation rather than model photography.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: serving as the physical subject of studio garment photography. It is the closest robotic analogue to a model posing for a photographer, so it bounds what robots deliver: a headless, expressionless morphing torso used only for fit visualisation, produced under program control, not accepted model imagery.

sources.developer: AIST (National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology), Japan
sources.title: HRP 4C humanoid robot on the runway at japan fashion week | designboom
sources.claim: The HRP-4C humanoid was presented at Japan Fashion Week in Tokyo and could imitate a supermodel's expressions, gait and poses only to a limited degree; it appeared unclothed in a special section and its creators acknowledged it needed more work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: appearing before an audience and cameras as a fashion model. It is the canonical attempt at a robot occupying the model's role; the pre-programmed, admittedly limited result shows robots do not deliver a model's posed human-figure output.

sources.system: Humanoid robots at MACH33: Physical AI Fashion Show
sources.title: Even Robots Need Style As Catwalk Shows Off Humanoid Fashions | Forbes
sources.claim: At Galaxy Corp's MACH33 Physical AI Fashion Show in Seoul (May 2026), humanoid robots in designer outfits walked and posed on the catwalk in choreographed routines alongside human models, who were still used for the show.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: being dressed and photographed as a fashion subject. The most recent, highest-profile robot-as-model event: the robots performed scripted choreography as a novelty and appeared beside, not instead of, human models, so it does not substantiate delivering a model's posed imagery.

sources.system: Generative-AI digital models/avatars (e.g., H&M digital twins)
sources.developer: various fashion brands and AI imaging vendors
sources.title: Models feel hemmed in by AI | Cornell Chronicle
sources.claim: Where models are being displaced in 2025-2026, the substitute is software image generation and digital avatars, not any embodied robotic system; human models still physically pose for the underlying photography and scans.
sources.transferJustification: Context for the negative judgment: the only demonstrated substitution path for a model's posing work is software-only image synthesis, which is excluded from robotic systems, confirming that no embodied machine performs the posing itself.

tasks.label: Assemble and maintain portfolios, print composite cards, and travel to go-sees to obtain jobs.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Local go-see/casting circuit: the model carries the portfolio book and a stack of comp cards, travels by subway, on foot or by car to 3-6 client offices, casting studios and showrooms across the city, waits in line, hands over the card, is looked at, measured, sometimes tries on a garment or walks, and is photographed on a phone. Weather, transit and building access vary daily.

Out-of-market trip: pack garment bag, book and cards, fly or drive to another market (LA, Miami, Paris) for a week of go-sees; navigate an unfamiliar city and unfamiliar client premises, appear in person at each appointment.

Assembling/maintaining the physical portfolio book at home or at the agency: gathering new prints and tear sheets cut from magazines, deciding with the agent which images stay, having 9x12 prints made, and inserting/reordering the sheets in the book's sleeves (or ordering a newly bound book).

Producing a run of composite cards: image selection and layout finalized with the agency, file sent to a comp-card printing service; the cards are printed on a digital press, trimmed to 5.5x8.5, checked and boxed at the print facility; the model checks the proof and the delivered batch.

Distributing marketing materials: dropping boxes of comp cards at the agency, leaving cards and mini-books at client offices and casting calls, and mailing card packets to photographers and clients around town.

sources.system: Horizon Smart Factory Lights Out Zone (Canon imagePRESS V1000 / Konica Minolta AccurioPress + AGVs + iCE StitchLiner Mark V)
sources.title: Horizon Smart Factory 2024 - The Complete Guide
sources.claim: Horizon's 2024 Smart Factory ran a 'Lights Out Zone' in which cut-sheet digital presses, AGVs and robotic finishing equipment produced finished booklets from press to pallet with no human labor, demonstrating fully automated print production and finishing in a purpose-built line.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: unattended production of printed, finished paper products. Comp cards and portfolio pages are the same substrate class (coated sheets) printed and trimmed on the same equipment, so press-to-pallet automation transfers directly to a comp-card or book print run.

sources.title: Duplo DC-618 Slitter Cutter Creaser | All-in-One Print Finishing
sources.claim: The Duplo DC-618 is a fully automated slitter/cutter/creaser used in digital print shops to trim printed sheets into finished business cards and postcards in a single pass at up to 23 sheets ....
sources.transferJustification: Related task: cutting printed sheets into business cards and postcards. A model's composite card is a 5.5x8.5 in card printed on the same digital stock and finished on the same class of machine, so the capability transfers.

sources.system: SigmaLine III digital book production line
sources.title: Muller Martini - SigmaLine lll
sources.claim: Muller Martini's SigmaLine III links digital printing and finishing into one system producing gathered book blocks fully automatically from the PDF file, down to a run of one copy.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: making a one-off bound book of pages from a supplied file. A model's portfolio book is a curated one-off book of images; producing it as a bound book in a print line is the same physical operation on comparable page stock.

sources.system: Imaging Solutions FastBook / Photobook Technology layflat album binding systems
sources.date: 2017-07 (line still marketed and resold as of 2025-10)
sources.title: A Look at Photobooks - By Don Piontek (Printing Impressions)
sources.claim: Photo album and photobook assembly — gluing prints to pages and mounting them into books — is performed by automated finishing machines from vendors such as Imaging Solutions and Photobook Technology rather than by hand.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mounting photographic prints into a book. Assembling a model's portfolio book is the same handling of photographic prints into page positions at comparable registration precision, done here on a purpose-built photo-finishing line.

sources.system: Serve Robotics Gen 3 sidewalk delivery robot
sources.title: Serve Robotics has deployed 2,000+ delivery robots across the U.S. - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Serve Robotics operates a fleet of more than 2,000 sidewalk delivery ... across seven US metro areas that carry small parcels and food orders to customer addresses with SAE Level 4 autonomy and a reported 99.8% completion rate.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous last-mile parcel delivery on public sidewalks to a recipient at an address. Dropping a packet of comp cards at an agency or client address is the same object class (small flat package) and the same unstructured urban route.

tasks.label: Pose as directed, or strike suitable interpretive poses for promoting and selling merchandise or fashions during appearances, filming, or photo sessions.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial photo/video session in a rented studio: model wears sample apparel or accessories, takes direction from the photographer through dozens of poses, angles and expressions, holds them for lighting, changes looks repeatedly, and delivers usable e-commerce/catalog/advertising imagery of a human wearing the merchandise.

On-location shoot for editorial, lifestyle or campaign work  ebebeach, park, rented house, city sidewalk, posing and moving in ambient weather and light, around bystanders and traffic, adapting poses to found scenery.

Runway show or live fashion presentation at a fashion-week venue, hotel ballroom or store event: fittings, walking the catwalk in a sequence of designer looks, pausing and posing at the end of the runway, quick changes backstage, on cue with music and lighting.

Retail establishment, showroom, trunk show or trade-show appearance and private showing for buyers: wearing sample garments, walking the floor, striking poses for shoppers/buyers, letting buyers inspect fit and drape, answering questions, repeated outfit changes over several hours.
Fine-art / life modeling: holding sustained static poses (5-40 minutes, often undraped) as the subject for painters, sculptors and drawing classes in an art studio or college classroom.

sources.title: Humanoid robot makes runway debut at Shanghai Fashion Week - Xinhua
sources.claim: A Unitree G1 humanoid walked the catwalk in clothing alongside human models at Shanghai Fashion Week (March 2025) as a novelty appearance; control mode was not stated, and Unitree event robots are commonly piloted with a handheld controller.

sources.title: Paris Fashion Week's Most Important Model Wasn't Human (TIME, via NewsBreak)
sources.claim: Noetix's 118 cm N2 robot walked a Paris Fashion Week venue in three vintage outfits before press in October 2025; it was limited to single-level venues because it struggles with stairs, and its control mode was not established.

sources.system: Unitree G1 / H1 at Mach33 Physical AI Fashion Show
sources.title: Humanoid robots join human models in rampwalk at Seoul fashion show
sources.claim: At the Mach33 'Physical AI' show in Seoul (May 2026), Unitree G1/H1 robots wearing designer clothing walked the runway together with human models; the robots supplemented rather than replaced human models and the control mode was not disclosed.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: presenting garments on a catwalk. Cited to show the state of the art, which still pairs robots with human models as spectacle rather than substituting a robot for a model presenting a collection.

sources.title: Japanese Robot Mannequins Move Shoppers To Buy
sources.claim: Flower Robotics' 'Palette' robot mannequin was installed in Japanese department store windows, sensing nearby shoppers and replaying motion-captured model poses to display clothing; it is a fixed-base, upper-body mannequin with no human likeness, walking, outfit changing, or buyer interaction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: posing to display merchandise inside a retail establishment. Cited because it is the only autonomous robotic 'poser' actually deployed in stores; it displays garments but cannot deliver a live model's appearance, outfit changes, or buyer interaction.

sources.title: Lil Miquela, Shudu, Bermuda and Sophia The Robot: CGI and Robot IT Girls Who Will Become the Influencers of the Future - DLA Piper IPT Italy
sources.claim: Hanson Robotics' Sophia posed for fashion magazine covers (Elle Brazil, Cosmopolitan India), the closest case of a robot doing a fashion photo session; Sophia's appearances are scripted/operator-assisted and the shoots traded on novelty rather than substituting for a model.

sources.title: Euveka - Scalable and connected robot mannequins
sources.claim: Euveka sells software-controlled robotic mannequins that morph to thousands of body shapes for garment fit and display; this is the mature robotic form of wearing a garment for the trade, but it yields headless torso/garment output, not on-model imagery or interpretive posing.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: presenting apparel on a body form in a studio/fitting setting. Cited to test the E1 counterfactual for studio sessions — bringing the garment to a fixtured machine still yields mannequin imagery, not model imagery.

sources.title: Humanoid robot starts work at Japanese department store (Reuters via Yahoo Finance)
sources.claim: Toshiba's Aiko Chihira android, dressed in a kimono, made a retail appearance greeting shoppers at Mitsukoshi's Nihonbashi department store; it was a stationary android running looped, pre-programmed speech and motions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: an in-store promotional appearance while wearing the merchandise. Cited because it is the closest deployed retail appearance by a humanlike robot, yet it is stationary, scripted, and does not model garments for buyers.

tasks.label: Follow strict routines of diet, sleep, and exercise to maintain appearance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Daily exercise block: the model works out at a commercial gym or fitness studio (weights, cardio, pilates/boxing class) for 60-90 minutes, adjusting intensity to keep body measurements within agency-specified limits.

Diet adherence: planning, shopping for, preparing and actually eating controlled portions/macros across the day at home, plus hydration and skipping alcohol/sugar; the model's own body composition and skin are the output.
Sleep routine at home: keeping a consistent early bedtime, 7-9 hours of sleep, screen and caffeine cut-offs, and skincare before/after sleep to avoid puffiness or dark circles before castings.
Intensified pre-booking prep in the days before a runway show, swimwear or fitting shoot: extra cardio, water manipulation/deloading, stricter eating, early nights, timed to a specific call time.
Maintaining the routine while traveling for castings/shoots: hotel-room workouts or unfamiliar gyms, sourcing compliant food in airports and foreign cities, sleeping across time zones.

sources.system: RobotLAB gym and wellness robots (autonomous floor scrubbers, service robots)
sources.title: Gym Robots for Fitness Center Automation | RobotLAB
sources.claim: Commercially deployed 'gym robots' in fitness facilities perform cleaning, security and front-desk service functions; no marketed system performs a member's training, eating or sleeping regimen for them.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: facility cleaning and customer service inside a gym. Cited only to show what robots actually do in this instance's setting; capability does not transfer, because the task's output is a change in the model's own body produced by the model's own exertion, which a cleaning or service robot cannot supply.

sources.title: Miso Robotics develops smaller, faster Flippy | Restaurant Dive
sources.claim: Food-preparation robots are installed in a small number of quick-service restaurant kitchens, cooking fried items in a fixed, purpose-built station.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated cooking. Cited to bound the closest robotic capability to the diet instance. It does not transfer: preparing food is at most a sub-step, while the instance requires the model to ingest controlled portions and sustain the resulting body condition, which no machine can do in the worker's place.

tasks.label: Apply makeup to face and style hair to enhance appearance, considering such factors as color, camera techniques, and facial features.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Pre-job prep at home or a hotel room: the model self-applies a full 'camera-ready' face (skin prep, foundation/concealer, brows, eyes, lip) and blow-dries/styles their own hair at a bathroom mirror before arriving on set, matching the brief given by the client (natural/clean-girl, no visible texture on camera).

Commercial / e-commerce / catalog shoot with a hair-and-makeup room at a photo studio: the model does their own makeup and hair, adjusting for studio strobes and lens (mattifying, contour intensity, brow definition) and re-styling hair between multiple looks over a several-hour call.

Backstage at a runway show, trade show, or promotional event: the model self-applies or heavily touches up makeup and restyles hair under time pressure at a crowded shared mirror station, to a look specified by the show's key artist.

On-location shoot (outdoors, street, client premises): the model re-applies makeup between setups for sweat, wind, rain and shine, and restyles wind-blown hair, working from a kit with no dedicated station and variable light.

Self-produced digital content at home: self-tape/polaroids, brand social posts, or live-shopping streams where the model creates a full look (sometimes editorial or themed glam) and styles hair specifically for the phone/ring-light camera.

sources.title: LUUM Precision Lash Brings Beauty Service Automation to Ulta
sources.claim: LUUM Precision Lash is a commercially deployed robotic system that applies eyelash extensions to live clients in retail shop-in-shop studios (Ulta, Nordstrom), with a human lash artist prepping and evaluating but not driving the applicator; it performs one narrow cosmetic service and no other makeup or hair work.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: precision cosmetic application on a live human face (lash extensions) at a purpose-built station. It is the closest deployed analogue to a model doing eye makeup, but it covers only lash extensions with the client reclined and head positioned; it does not apply foundation, contour, eye or lip makeup, and does nothing with hair, so it cannot substantiate completion of the whole task.

sources.title: US beauty-tech firm LUUM introduces next-generation AI lash robot
sources.claim: LUUM's next-generation lash robot is scaling into Ulta Beauty and Nordstrom locations after thousands of live client sessions, confirming real deployment of robotic lash application in retail beauty facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Same related task as above (robotic lash extension service); establishes maturity and environment (retail salon studio) but still only a single cosmetic sub-service, not full-face makeup or hair styling.

sources.developer: Grupo Boticário with CESAR Innovation Hub
sources.title: AI and Robotics Revolutionize Lipstick Application
sources.claim: Grupo Boticário's Smart Lipstick is a prototype robotic arm that autonomously applies lipstick to a user whose head is fixed on a chinrest, using computer vision to map the lips; it applies lipstick only.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic application of one cosmetic product to a fixtured human face. It shows the E1-style fixture case (chinrest) but covers only lip color, not base, eyes, or hair, and remains a prototype.

sources.title: HOME | Gemma (gemmarobotics.com)
sources.claim: Gemma Robotics markets a touchless airbrush makeup robot claiming full-look application, but the product is presented as a beta with a waitlist and the claims are company marketing without an independent demonstration of autonomous, worker-quality application.

sources.developer: MIT CSAIL and Harvard Soft Math Lab
sources.title: RoboWig: A Robot That Can Help You Untangle Your Hair
sources.claim: MIT CSAIL/Harvard's RoboWig is a research robot arm with a sensorized soft brush that autonomously plans and executes detangling brush-outs, tested on wigs in the lab; it detangles hair but does not create a style.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic manipulation of human hair (brushing/detangling). It is the closest robotic hair-handling capability found, but it is a lab demonstration on wigs limited to detangling; it does not blow-dry, curl, pin, or finish a camera-ready style.

sources.title: Haircutting Robots: From Theory to Practice
sources.claim: A 2025 peer-reviewed perspective on haircutting robots frames the field as emerging, proposing supervised-autonomy business models and a framework for future deployment — i.e., no fielded robotic hair cutting/styling service exists.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic hair work in salons. Cited to establish the state of the art for the hair-styling half of this task: it is prospective, not deployed, so no cited system can deliver a finished hairstyle.

tasks.label: Work closely with photographers, fashion coordinators, directors, producers, stylists, make-up artists, other models, and clients to produce the desired looks, and to finish photo shoots on schedule.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: High-volume e-commerce/catalog studio day: rented commercial photo studio, model wears 30-80 garments, works with photographer, digital tech, stylist and dresser; takes continuous verbal direction on pose and expression, does rapid changes, hits the shot list on schedule.

Advertising/beauty campaign or brand shoot in a studio with client, art director, producer, hair and make-up artists: sits for hair/make-up, is dressed and re-styled between setups, poses expressively to a creative brief, handles product, absorbs client feedback and iterates until approved shots are captured within the booked day.

On-location editorial/lifestyle shoot: city street, beach, park, or a private house location; model moves, walks, and poses dynamically on uneven ground in variable weather and light, coordinating with photographer, stylist and crew while the light window closes.

Designer runway show: fittings with the designer and stylist, hair and make-up call, backstage quick changes with dressers, rehearsal, walking the runway on cue in sample-size garments, plus backstage/lookbook stills.

Showroom, trunk show, or retail informal modeling for buyers and clients: puts on sample garments, walks and poses for buyers, moves so garments show drape and fit, changes looks repeatedly, responds to client requests during the appointment.

Fine-art sitting: posing for painters, sculptors, or an art class in a studio or classroom; holds static poses for 20+ minutes under the artist's direction, adjusts angle and limb placement on instruction, resumes the identical pose after breaks.

sources.title: Paris Fashion Week's Most Important Model Wasn't Human
sources.claim: Noetix Robotics' N2 humanoid walked a catwalk at a Paris Fashion Week venue dressed in a waistcoat and pearls, modeling three outfits as a novelty appearance rather than presenting a designer collection.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: presenting apparel on a runway. It bears on this task because it is the closest thing to a robot performing a model's on-set duties, but the robot only walked a short scripted segment in custom robot-scale clothing and did no fittings, styling, or direction-taking.

sources.title: Robots on the runway: Humanoid stuns Shanghai Fashion Week - CGTN
sources.claim: A Unitree G1 humanoid and robot dog walked the Shanghai Fashion Week runway alongside human models in a staged, choreographed showcase.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: appearing on a runway with human models. The robot was an exhibit interacting with a human model who placed a necklace on it; the human models still performed the modeling work, so it does not show a robot completing a model's collaborative duties.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoids at Mach33 Physical AI Fashion Show
sources.title: Even Robots Need Style As Catwalk Shows Off Humanoid Fashions
sources.claim: At the Mach33 Physical AI Fashion Show in Seoul, humanoid robots in designer outfits walked and posed beside human models in synchronized choreography.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: posing and walking for an audience/cameras. Choreographed group routines in custom-made robot garments are not evidence of taking live direction from a photographer or stylist, nor of wearing human sample garments.

sources.system: StyleShoots Live automated robotic photo studio
sources.title: Automated Studio 'Live' Is Set To Take Photography Jobs In Product, Catalogue, & Fashion
sources.claim: StyleShoots Live is a commercially deployed robotic automated studio for fashion e-commerce that automates camera, lighting and processing, but the shoot still requires a human model (talent) plus make-up and dressing facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: producing e-commerce apparel imagery in a purpose-built automated photo cell. It is the most machine-structured version of a catalog shoot in commercial use, and the model role in it remains human, showing no robotic system fills the model's place even at E1.

sources.title: Euveka Launches Morphable Robot Mannequins
sources.claim: Euveka's robot mannequin is a commercially sold, software-controlled shape-changing mannequin used by apparel brands for fit and pattern work; it displays garments but cannot pose, dress itself, or take on-set direction.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: holding and displaying garments on a body form (fit modeling). It is the closest robotic substitute for a body in apparel work, but it is used for fit and patternmaking, produces no posed on-figure imagery, and cannot collaborate with a shoot crew.

tasks.label: Dress in sample or completed garments, and select accessories.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commercial photo/video studio shoot (editorial, catalog, e-commerce): model changes in a dressing area into a series of sample or completed looks brought on rolling racks, fastens zippers, buttons, hooks and belts, puts on hosiery and shoes, and picks jewelry, bags and other accessories from the stylist's options to complete each look, changing every 15-30 minutes.

Runway show or fashion presentation, backstage: model is dressed in assigned designer samples (often unfinished, pinned, delicate) with a dresser's help, does rapid quick-changes between looks, and puts on the assigned shoes, hats and jewelry per the look board before walking.

Showroom, market appointment or fit session at a brand/design house: model repeatedly puts on and takes off sample garments for buyers, designers and technical designers, adjusts closures and drape, and pairs the sample with accessories from the showroom's stock.

Retail establishment, trunk show or trade-show/promotional modeling: model dresses in completed retail garments in a store fitting room or booth back area, selects coordinating accessories from the merchandise on hand, and re-dresses into new outfits several times during the day while on the floor with customers.

On-location shoot (outdoor street, beach, ranch, client property): model changes in a trailer, tent or van from wardrobe trunks, dresses in garments and layers appropriate for wind, cold or terrain, and selects accessories and footwear from the wardrobe kit between setups.

sources.system: Unitree G1 humanoid at Shanghai Fashion Week (NMTG show)
sources.title: The future of fashion: Robots on the runway - CGTN
sources.claim: Humanoid robots have appeared as 'models' on fashion runways wearing designer clothing, but they are dressed by human crews beforehand and there is no indication they don garments or choose accessories themselves; their runway behavior is walking/choreography.
sources.transferJustification: Closest public instance of a robot occupying a model's role; cited to show that the garment-donning and accessory-selection steps of the task were performed by humans, not the machine.

sources.system: MIT CSAIL robot-assisted dressing system (state-estimation jacket dressing)
sources.developer: MIT CSAIL / Honda Research Institute Europe / University of Edinburgh
sources.title: Robots dress humans without the full picture | MIT News
sources.claim: The nearest robotic capability to putting a garment on a body is robot-assisted dressing: a research robot arm pulled a jacket sleeve onto a seated person's arm in a laboratory, handling one sleeve of one loose garment under controlled conditions.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (dressing a human) shows the state of the art in garment-onto-body manipulation; it is a single-sleeve lab result with a human partner, so it does not transfer to a machine dressing itself in fitted samples and selecting accessories.

sources.system: Figure 02 humanoid running the Helix VLA model
sources.title: Helix Learns to Fold Laundry
sources.claim: State-of-the-art autonomous humanoid deformable-fabric manipulation is limited to folding towels/laundry on a fixed table in a controlled demo setting.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (garment handling) marks the frontier of autonomous cloth manipulation by a humanoid; folding flat items on a table is far short of donning fitted garments on one's own body, fastening closures, and choosing accessories.

sources.title: KAIST and Stanford Build Robotic Clothing That Puts Itself On the Wearer
sources.claim: A robotic garment with embedded air-powered 'vine' actuators can pull itself onto a human wearer in about ten seconds, but it dresses a person and requires purpose-built actuated clothing rather than designer samples.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (automated donning of clothing) is cited because it is the only 2026 system that puts clothing on a body autonomously; it assists a human wearer with specially fabricated garments and so cannot substitute for a model dressing in sample garments and choosing accessories.

instances.label: Suburban resale single-family showing: agent meets a buyer couple at a listed house, accesses it via lockbox, walks room by room, and advises on layout suitability, visible condition issues (roof, HVAC age, water stains), neighborhood, and how the asking price compares to recent comparable sales.

Urban condo/apartment tour day: agent drives buyers to 3-5 units back to back in elevator buildings, walking each unit and advising on floor plan tradeoffs, light and noise, HOA fees and rules, building reserves, and relative value across the units seen.

Buyer-side attendance at the scheduled professional home inspection under contract: agent walks the property with the buyer and licensed inspector, listens to findings in attic/crawlspace/mechanical areas, and advises the buyer on severity, likely repair cost, and whether to request credits, repairs, or terminate.

New construction or open-house walkthrough: agent accompanies buyers through builder model homes or an active open house, advising on upgrade packages, lot premiums, builder reputation, HOA/CDD costs, and whether the price and incentives represent value versus resale alternatives.

Rural, land, or distressed/fixer-upper showing: vacant property with utilities off, overgrown lot, possible pests, mud or debris; agent walks the parcel and structure with the buyer advising on well/septic, access, renovation feasibility and after-repair value.

Live remote showing for an out-of-area buyer: agent physically walks the property alone while streaming video and narrating, answering the buyer's questions in real time and advising on suitability and value at the buyer's request.

instances.label: Accompanied buyer showing of an occupied resale single-family home: agent meets the clients at the curb, retrieves the key from a Supra/combination lockbox, unlocks and opens the house, leads the clients room by room past the sellers' furniture, pets and clutter, opens closets, the garage and the attic hatch, points out finishes, HVAC age, roof and yard, answers unscripted questions, then relocks and secures the home.

Showing of a vacant or staged listing (empty house or townhouse) taken as found: agent opens with lockbox key or smart-lock code, walks buyers through empty rooms and unfinished basement/garage, operates lights, faucets and appliances to demonstrate condition, discusses defects and renovation potential, then locks up.

Showing a condominium or apartment unit inside a professionally managed building: agent signs in at the front desk, escorts clients through lobby, elevator and corridors, unlocks the unit, walks them through it and through shared amenities (gym, pool deck, parking), explaining HOA rules, assessments and building features.

Hosting an open house or a new-construction model home / builder sales gallery: the property is already open, staged and kept to a presentation standard for the event or for posted hours; the agent greets walk-in visitors, leads them along a set route through the rooms and explains floor plan, finishes, options and neighborhood.

Tour of commercial, office, retail or industrial space: agent badges or unlocks a vacant suite or warehouse, walks the prospect and sometimes their contractor through it, explaining clear height, dock doors, power service, HVAC, load capacity, build-out potential and parking; may involve stairs, mechanical rooms and roof access.

Showing agricultural land or rural acreage: agent drives or walks the client over unpaved tracks, opens farm gates, crosses fields, fence lines, irrigation ditches and outbuildings in whatever weather, explaining acreage, soil, water rights, easements and access.

sources.system: temi robot museum guide (National Heritage Board / GovTech deployment)
sources.title: Meet Temi – your friendly museum guide who happens to be a robot | GovTech Singapore
sources.claim: The temi service robot works as an autonomous museum guide at Changi Chapel and Museum, leading visitors along a pre-mapped route through exhibits and narrating explanatory content on its own; the venue was retrofitted (stickers on glass doors, a gateway to trigger automatic doors) to support it.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: leading visitors on a guided walkthrough of a venue and explaining what they are seeing. It transfers to hosting walk-in visitors in a fixed-layout, institution-controlled model home or sales gallery — same mapped indoor route, same pre-authored feature explanations, same public audience.

sources.title: LG Cloi GuideBot Enhances Customer Service at DFW | Aviation Pros
sources.claim: LG's CLOi GuideBot operated in DFW Airport's Terminal D, moving autonomously among travelers, guiding them to points of interest and presenting facility information on its screens.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: escorting members of the public through a large indoor facility while presenting information about it. Shows deployed guide robots handle crowded, institution-controlled premises, but only on pre-mapped routes with pre-authored information.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with Spot Arm (Autowalk)
sources.title: The Next Step in Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot can open doors autonomously during pre-taught Autowalk inspection missions inside industrial facilities — the current limit of client-independent autonomous door manipulation in a commercial robot.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: moving through a building and operating doors under autonomy. It bounds what deployed systems physically do — doors on taught routes in industrial plants, with no key or lockbox handling and no client-facing presentation.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics releases Spot and Orbit 5.1 with new Spot Cam - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Spot's autonomous door-opening feature is in limited beta deployment inside customer facilities, with roughly 2,500 doors opened across 18 beta customers as of early 2026.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous navigation and door operation inside buildings; establishes the recency and scale of the only deployed autonomous door-opening capability, all on taught missions inside industrial/commercial premises.

sources.title: Take a home tour with a Zenplace robot | CNBC
sources.claim: The one robot product marketed for residential showings, Zenplace, is a telepresence device: a remote human leasing agent speaks through the screen and drives the robot around the home, i.e. continuous teleoperation rather than an autonomous showing.

instances.label: Periodic condition check of a vacant single-family listing: agent lets self in with lockbox, walks all rooms looking for water leaks, stains, mold smell, vandalism, pests, thermostat/utility status, lights out, dirt or debris from prior showings; then texts/calls the owner and books a cleaner or handyman.

Pre-listing walkthrough of an occupied home with the seller present (furniture, pets, children, clutter): agent tours the house judging what must be repaired, painted, replaced or decluttered before photos, discusses items with the owner, and lines up contractors.

Final walkthrough / repair-verification visit before closing with the buyer present: confirm negotiated repairs were actually completed to standard, run faucets and appliances, test HVAC and garage door, check for move-out damage or removed fixtures, and get remaining items fixed before settlement.

Roof and exterior-structure condition check at a residential listing (after a hailstorm or before listing): assess shingles, flashing, gutters, siding, chimney for damage requiring repair, and report to the owner or order a roofing contractor.

Grounds and curb-appeal check at a listing: overgrown lawn and shrubs, weeds, downed branches, uncollected trash and flyers, unshoveled snow, cracked driveway, broken fence gate, burnt-out exterior lights; then arrange lawn, snow or cleanup service.

Condition inspection of a commercial or multifamily space inside an institution-managed building (vacant office suite, retail bay, or condo unit in a professionally managed building with fixed layout and controlled access): note damaged finishes, leaks, HVAC/lighting faults, and file the maintenance request with building management or the owner.

sources.title: Boston Dynamics releases software updates to Orbit fleet management platform, Spot robots
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics Spot with the Orbit platform autonomously patrols facilities, captures images at points of interest, and AI analysis flags conditions such as spills, missing fire extinguishers and equipment wear — i.e., an autonomous condition round of the premises that produces actionable maintenance findings.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility inspection rounds. Transfer: the robot walks the premises on a repeatable route inside an institution-controlled building, visually judges whether conditions are out of order, and raises the finding for maintenance action — the same activity as an agent's condition round of a vacant, unoccupied space, with comparable objects (floors, fixtures, equipment) and no fine manipulation.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Spot's autonomous inspection missions are deployed at commercial scale across working facilities, with customers running thousands of unattended data-collection missions covering industrial assets in factories and power plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: scheduled industrial inspection rounds. Transfer: establishes that autonomous premises-walking inspection with anomaly reporting is a deployed, reliable capability in institution-controlled facilities (E2), not a one-off demo.

sources.title: A Retrospective on Uses of Boston Dynamics' Spot Robot
sources.claim: Spot's manipulation work — opening doors and picking up objects — is performed under manual operator driving, not autonomously, indicating that hands-on checks (opening cabinets, operating fixtures/appliances) are not autonomous today.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: mobile manipulation during inspection. Transfer: a final walkthrough requires operating faucets, appliances, doors and windows; the leading deployed inspection robot does this only under manual control, so such checks are not autonomously supported.

sources.title: How Swiss Robotics Company ANYbotics and SAP Are Turning Dirty, Dusty, and Dangerous Industrial Inspections into Business Insights
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal runs fully autonomous inspection rounds in industrial plants, collecting visual, thermal, acoustic and gas-leak data to monitor equipment condition, detect anomalies and feed plant maintenance workflows.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous plant inspection rounds integrated into maintenance workflows. Transfer: same structure as the task — traverse the premises, detect leaks/overheating/faults, and notify maintenance — performed in an institution-controlled facility kept to a working standard (E2).

sources.title: EagleView and Skydio Announce General Availability of Virtual Claims Inspection Solution
sources.claim: Skydio's House Scan software autonomously scans residential roofs on ordinary private homes, and EagleView Assess turns the capture into automated measurement and damage detection used by insurance adjusters — an as-found residential property exterior condition assessment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: insurance roof damage inspection. Transfer: identical premises (an as-found single-family home exterior), identical output (identified roof/exterior damage requiring repair) that an agent would relay to the owner or use to order a roofer; the flight and scan planning are autonomous and the damage detection automated.

sources.title: Cobalt Robot Expands Facility Security Capabilities
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor robots autonomously patrol commercial premises such as office buildings and detect things out of place — including water leaks, spills and doors or windows left open — and notify a remote specialist.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor building patrol with anomaly reporting. Transfer: the robot walks a managed commercial building's interior, spots leaks/spills/open openings, and reports them for action — the core of a condition check of a space in an institution-managed building, with only occasional remote human involvement.

sources.system: Boston Dynamics Spot with reality-capture payload
sources.title: Automated Construction Site Documentation
sources.claim: Spot conducts programmed Autowalk reality-capture missions on construction sites without operator intervention, living on site with a self-charging dock, but the output is documentation for human review rather than an accepted condition-and-maintenance determination.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: jobsite reality capture. Transfer is limited: it shows autonomous navigation of an unstructured site (E3), but the deliverable is scan data for human interpretation, not an inspection verdict plus maintenance arrangement.

sources.title: Teleop, not autonomy, is the path for 1X's Neo humanoid
sources.claim: Consumer humanoid home robots shipping into private homes rely on human teleoperation for most household work, and no humanoid has been shown completing a household task end-to-end autonomously.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous work inside private homes. Transfer: the leading home-deployed robot depends on teleoperation in exactly the setting (occupied dwellings) where most instances of this task occur, so occupied-home walkthroughs are unsupported.

instances.label: Preview of an occupied, furnished resale single-family home on the market: agent drives to the address, opens the Supra/combination lockbox, walks the whole interior (rooms, closets, basement, stairs, garage) plus yard around the seller's belongings and pets, judges condition, finishes, odors, noise, layout and client fit, then locks up.

Preview of vacant land/rural acreage or of a commercial or retail suite: walking a parcel and checking access, terrain, boundaries and utilities, or touring a leasable suite in an office/retail property to check size, condition, buildout and services.

sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot runs operator-recorded Autowalk inspection missions autonomously and on schedule through industrial facilities, carrying sensors that capture facility and asset condition data — the closest deployed analogue to walking a building to document its state.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine facility walkthrough/condition documentation. It transfers to previewing a property because both require traversing an interior on foot, climbing stairs, and imaging rooms and fittings to report condition; the objects (doors, floors, fixtures, equipment) and precision demands are comparable.

sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot can autonomously open doors with its arm during Autowalk missions, letting it move room to room inside a building without a human present.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: interior inspection rounds. Door opening is the specific access step a property walkthrough needs; the doors and handles are the same class of objects found in homes and suites.

sources.title: [VIDEO] Construction Progress Documentation Solution Puts Robotic Dog to Work on Jobsites | For Construction Pros
sources.claim: Spot equipped with a 360-degree camera autonomously walks a jobsite on a recorded route capturing consistent 360 photo documentation of building interiors, piloted with a general contractor on a real terminal project.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: construction progress documentation. The deliverable — a walked-through visual record of a building's current state — is the same kind of artifact an agent gathers when previewing a property, and the built interiors are comparable.

sources.title: The Next Step in Safe, Autonomous Robotic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Levatas' visual AI runs on Spot's captured imagery to detect abnormal conditions and raise alerts through Boston Dynamics' Orbit, turning robot-collected imagery into an automated condition assessment rather than raw footage.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated defect/anomaly reporting from robot imagery. It supports the 'assessment' half of a property preview: the machine produces an evaluated condition report, not only pictures.

sources.title: Skydio 3D Scan Autonomous Drone Inspection | Skydio
sources.claim: Skydio drones autonomously fly complete 3D scans of structures with no prior map or GPS, planning their own flight paths to capture the whole exterior of a building.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous exterior structure inspection. It transfers to the curb/exterior portion of a property preview — roof, siding, lot — where the objects imaged and the resolution needed are the same as in roof and building inspections.

sources.title: Exyn Brings Level 4 Autonomy to Drones - IEEE Spectrum
sources.claim: Exyn's Level 4 autonomous drones explore and map interior spaces they have never seen, without GPS, base station, or human input during flight, and are deployed in underground mining and structure mapping.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous mapping of unknown interiors. Shows a machine can traverse and record an unmapped indoor volume, the navigation core of walking through a property it has not visited before; it still must be carried to and launched at each site by a person.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor robot performs 24/7 autonomous patrols of corporate offices and other multi-tenant facilities, running scheduled facility checks and environmental ... along its route.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous indoor patrol and facility check in office buildings. It shows autonomous corridor/room traversal and anomaly noting in human-occupied commercial premises, the navigation setting of a commercial-suite or condo-building preview.
