tasks.label: Modify or improve filing systems or implement new filing systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Incremental in-place modification of an existing paper filing scheme in a business office (law firm, clinic front office, HR, school district): the clerk adds or splits categories, prints and applies new folder/tab labels, purges superseded material to retention rules, and re-sequences a drawer, cabinet or shelving section while the office stays in use. Output = physical folders relabeled and correctly ordered in the organization's own cabinets, plus an updated file index.

Full re-implementation of a paper classification scheme in a high-volume records department (hospital HIM, county clerk, insurance claims): convert alphabetic to color-coded terminal-digit or new numeric scheme across tens of thousands of charts/folders on open shelving — relabel each folder, re-sequence into new shelf positions, reconcile against the index, over weeks in an institution-controlled records room.

Paper-to-digital conversion implementing a new electronic filing system: document prep (remove staples/clips, unfold, insert separator sheets), scanning on production equipment, naming/indexing into the new DMS taxonomy, QC of images, then boxing or shredding originals. Mixed record types, folders and binders of varying condition.

Implementing a new storage arrangement for records: new cabinets/shelving installed or inactive records moved to a records-storage room or offsite records center — selecting records, packing and labeling boxes/containers, building a box-level index and location map, and transferring containers into the new storage system.

Electronic-only restructure of the shared-drive or DMS filing structure: design a new folder taxonomy and naming/metadata conventions, bulk move and rename thousands of electronic files, set permissions and retention flags, and document the scheme for users. Desk work at a workstation, no handling of paper.

tasks.label: Track materials removed from files to ensure that borrowed files are returned.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Records room of a hospital, law firm or agency: a requester asks for a paper file; the clerk pulls it, records the charge-out (barcode scan into a records-tracking system, or a handwritten out-card), inserts an out-guide in the shelf gap, and when the file comes back checks it in against the log and refiles it.

Departmental/front-office active files: co-workers pull folders themselves and leave an out-card or sign a sign-out sheet; the clerk keeps the charge-out log current, spot-checks the drawers, and records folders as returned when they reappear at the counter.

Periodic reconciliation/audit of the file room: walking the aisles and drawers, checking which folders are absent or misfiled, matching what is on the shelves against the charge-out log, and producing a list of files still outstanding.
Overdue recovery: running the outstanding-file list, phoning or emailing borrowers, walking to their offices to retrieve folders off desks and credenzas, and clearing the charge-out record.

Off-site records center or archive: boxes and folders charged out to client departments, barcode-scanned out and shipped by courier, tracked against due dates, then received back, verified and re-shelved in a warehouse-style facility.

tasks.label: Perform periodic inspections of materials or files to ensure correct placement, legibility, or proper condition.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General business/government office file room: clerk walks rows of lateral shelving and cabinet drawers, opens drawers, thumbs through hanging folders and guide cards to verify alphabetic/numeric sequence, pulls and re-inserts misfiles, notes split folders, dog-eared papers and faded or peeling labels for replacement.

Health-information / clinic or insurance chart room: periodic audit of open-shelf color-coded terminal-digit chart folders - scanning end-tab color breaks for misfiles, checking that loose reports inside are fastened and not protruding, and pulling worn or overstuffed jackets for re-foldering.

Off-site records center or warehouse-style archive: periodic inventory/condition audit of barcoded cartons on pallet racking - confirming each carton's barcode matches its assigned rack location, and flagging crushed, water-stained, over-full or unlabeled boxes for re-boxing; output is an exception report.

Active case files at a workstation (law office, insurance, court, HR): clerk pulls a batch of files and pages through them to confirm each document belongs in that file and is in required order, spots faded thermal-fax/carbon copies or smudged forms needing re-copying or scanning, and replaces torn folders.

Archive, library special collection or vital-records vault: periodic preservation survey of stored documents, ledgers, maps and microfilm - checking for mold, brittleness, insect damage, fading ink, improper enclosures and items shelved out of their collection location; damaged items pulled for conservation or reformatting.

tasks.label: Retrieve documents stored in microfilm or microfiche and place them in viewers for reading.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Public library / historical society / genealogy reading room: a patron requests a specific newspaper reel; the clerk locates the labeled reel box in a microfilm cabinet drawer, carries it to a reader-scanner station, threads the open 35mm reel onto the take-up spool, advances to the requested date, and refiles after use.

County recorder, courthouse or vital-records office: clerk pulls an indexed microfiche card (deeds, plats, birth/death records) from a fiche tray or panel file, slides it into the reader-printer's glass carrier stage, positions the grid coordinate for the requester, then refiles the card in sequence.

Corporate, bank, insurance or utility records department: clerk retrieves a labeled 16mm self-threading M-type microfilm cartridge from a cabinet or rack, drops it into a motorized reader/scanner slot, runs to the indexed frame for the requested account document, and returns the cartridge to its slot.

Records center or archive vault: clerk pulls reels or boxes from shelving in a storage room or off-site vault (step stools/ladders, high shelves, dusty boxes, mixed carton labeling), carts them to a reader station in the reading room, and loads them for staff or researcher review.

Legacy or nonstandard media: unlabeled/mislabeled reels, jacketed fiche and aperture cards mixed in the same drawer, film that is brittle, curled, wound backwards, torn or affected by vinegar syndrome; the clerk must identify the item, rewind or splice it, and improvise a carrier so it can be viewed at all.

tasks.label: Operate mechanized files that rotate to bring needed records to a particular location.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: General business/office records room: a request comes in for a specific file; the clerk keys the location into a powered vertical carousel or rotary power file (e.g., Lektriever/Rotomat), the unit rotates the shelf to the access window, and the clerk pulls the folder, logs it out, and hands it to the requester.

Healthcare medical-records or insurance/claims department: high-volume daily pull list; the clerk repeatedly cycles the powered carousel to bring successive charts/claim files to the access opening, pulls each, checks it out in the tracking system, and stages them on a cart for delivery.

Refiling returned records: the clerk takes a stack of returned folders back to the mechanized file, cycles the unit shelf by shelf, and interfiles each folder in correct alphanumeric sequence in densely packed shelves, verifying order.

Maintaining the contents of the mechanized file: loading newly created folders into the unit, shifting/creating space in tight shelves, and purging or transferring inactive files out of the unit into transfer boxes for off-site storage.

Records centre or off-site archive: the clerk operates powered mobile (compactor) shelving or a large mechanized file, pressing controls to bring the correct bay/aisle into position, then retrieves record boxes or file folders, barcode-scans them out, and loads them onto a cart.

sources.system: AutoStore / Swisslog SynQ at FBI Central Records Complex

sources.claim: Follow-up reporting confirms the FBI records automation is in production use and retrieves paper files at high volume and accuracy, establishing worker-quality reliability for automated record retrieval.

sources.transferJustification: Related task (order picking): extracting one requested item from a machine-presented bin is the same act as removing the requested folder once the mechanized file has rotated it to the access point — comparable object size, precision, and machine-fixtured presentation.

sources.title: BD Rowa™ - dispensing robots & digital selling solutions
sources.claim: BD Rowa Vmax dispensing robots store individually identified flat cartons in dense chaotic shelving inside an enclosed machine and, on request, pick the named item and deliver it to ... specified output point at the counter; roughly 15,000 units are in commercial service.
sources.transferJustification: Related task (pharmacy dispensing): retrieving one named flat item from dense indexed storage and delivering it to a particular output location is functionally what a mechanized file operation produces — machine-controlled storage, indexed lookup, delivery to the point of use.

tasks.label: Issue room keys and escort instructions to bellhops.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Upscale full-service city hotel, single party arriving with luggage: clerk finishes registration at the desk, encodes two keycards into a printed key jacket with the room number, and hands the packet to the bell attendant standing at the desk with a one-line instruction ('Mr. Lopez to 1412, three bags'). Ordinary lobby conditions.

Resort or multi-building campus property: keys for a villa, casita or outbuilding are issued to bell/valet staff along with routing and handling instructions (which building and path, golf-cart transfer, VIP amenity in room, number of bags). Front desk or arrival pavilion, sometimes open-air.

Group, tour or convention arrival: keys pre-encoded in bulk against a rooming list, sorted into labeled packets, and issued to the bell captain together with luggage-pull and room-delivery instructions before or as the coach arrives.

Post-check-in dispatch: room not ready at arrival or luggage checked with the bell stand; later the clerk issues the room key (or a duplicate after verifying the guest) to a bell attendant with instructions to take the bags and/or the guest up to the room.

Peak arrival rush with exceptions: several parties and several bell attendants at the desk at once, room changes and re-encoded keys, upgrades, guests interrupting; the clerk must match each key set and each set of escort instructions to the right attendant and party amid queueing and noise.

tasks.label: Date-stamp, sort, and rack incoming mail and messages.

instances.label: Mid-size hotel: carrier drops the daily bundle of letters and flats at the front desk; clerk date-stamps each piece, separates guest mail from department/management mail, and slots it into the pigeonhole rack behind the desk, interleaved with check-ins.

Large hotel/resort back-office mailroom: high daily volume of mixed letters, flats and interoffice envelopes; clerk date-stamps, sorts by department and by registered guest/room, and racks into labeled slots or department trays.

Guest messages: phone, fax or hand-written messages for guests; clerk time/date-stamps the slip or printout, matches it to the registered room, and places it in the room's key/message slot or message rack.
Parcels and courier deliveries for guests: clerk receives boxes and envelopes, logs and date-stamps the label/receipt, and shelves them in the package rack or back storage area by guest name.
Small motel front desk: a handful of mail pieces arrive intermittently at a cluttered shared counter; clerk stamps, sorts and racks them between other duties, with no dedicated mail station.

tasks.label: Deposit guests' valuables in hotel safes or safe-deposit boxes.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Mid-scale/full-service hotel front desk: a guest hands over cash, a passport, a phone or jewelry; the clerk seals it in a numbered envelope, has the guest sign the safe-deposit register, unlocks a box in the safe-deposit unit behind the desk with guard key plus guest key, places the item inside, relocks and hands the guest the key.

Luxury hotel or resort: high-value valuables (watches, jewelry, large sums of cash, group passports) deposited into a larger back-office safe or vault-style safe-deposit installation; formal signed receipt, sometimes witnessed by a second staff member, with the guest re-depositing and withdrawing repeatedly over a multi-night stay.

Limited-service motel or small independent property: guest asks the clerk on duty to hold cash, keys or a passport; the clerk writes a log entry and puts the sealed envelope into a small office safe or drop safe at the back counter, often single-staffed at night.

Bulky or awkward valuables that will not fit a safe-deposit box - a laptop bag, camera gear, a briefcase, a shipped parcel - taken behind the desk and locked into a secure back-office storage room or large safe, tagged with a claim ticket.

Peak check-in/check-out rush: the deposit request is interleaved with a queue of arriving guests; the clerk must verify the guest's identity and room, complete the deposit and paperwork quickly, and keep the safe area secure while other transactions are underway.

Deployed at 24SAFE, a private vault service in Prague.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: depositing a customer's valuables into a locked safe-deposit box with identity verification and an audit record - same objects (cash, jewellery, documents) and same accepted output (item secured in a numbered box, retrievable by the depositor) as a hotel clerk's safe-deposit transaction.

instances.label: Early-morning setup of the full complimentary breakfast at a limited-service hotel: clerk pulls product from back storage/walk-in, loads pastries, bagels and muffins into display bins, fills cereal dispensers, sets out whole fruit, yogurt and milk on ice, readies the juice machine, turns on waffle irons and toasters, loads hot eggs and sausage into chafers or hot wells, and stacks plates, bowls, tongs, cutlery, napkins and signage on the buffet counter.

Setting up the lobby/breakfast-area coffee and tea station at the start of service: brewing urns or airpots of regular and decaf, hot water for tea, stocking cups, lids, sleeves, stirrers, sweeteners, creamer and the tea bag selection, and wiping the counter before guests arrive.

Refreshing the coffee/tea station repeatedly through the shift: checking pots, dumping and re-brewing stale or empty urns, refilling cups, lids, condiments and tea bags, wiping drips at a station in the lobby that guests use around the clock.

Replenishing and tidying the breakfast area during service with guests moving through: refilling pastry trays, cereal, fruit and juice, swapping an empty chafer pan, restocking plates and cutlery, wiping spills on counters and tables, and clearing abandoned dishes and trash.

Breaking down after breakfast: pulling, dating and storing perishables, discarding waste, emptying and washing coffee urns and juice/cereal dispensers, cleaning waffle irons and toasters, wiping and sanitizing counters and tables, and restocking the storage room for the next day.

Small off-peak refreshment setups: afternoon cookies or packaged snacks, an iced tea/lemonade or infused-water dispenser, and a fresh pot of lobby coffee for an evening reception, laid out on a side table or lobby counter.

sources.title: Richtech Robotics' ADAM serves drinks at Kennedy Space Center - The Robot Report
sources.claim: Richtech's ADAM is a commercially deployed dual-arm robot barista/bartender that autonomously makes and serves espresso drinks, teas and cocktails from a fixtured station in cafes, casinos, arenas and hospitality clients including Hilton.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: robotic beverage service. The accepted output of the clerk's coffee/tea work is hot beverages available to guests; ADAM produces the same drinks from cups, beans, milk and water presented in fixed positions at its own purpose-built station.

sources.title: Cheers to AI: ADAM Robot Bartender Makes Drinks at Vegas Golden Knights Game | NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: ADAM is deployed at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas and runs its perception and control stack on board, detecting cups and calibrating its workspace in real time rather than being teleoperated.
sources.transferJustification: Same beverage-service transfer as the prior item; substantiates that the station robot operates autonomously in a live hospitality venue.

sources.title: Scaling craft coffee: How ClickHouse powers Artly's barista bots
sources.claim: Artly operates fully autonomous robotic barista bots in commercial coffee shops (Seattle, Bellevue, Portland), brewing a full menu of espresso drinks, matcha and refreshers from a countertop/kiosk workspace.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: preparing and dispensing coffee and tea beverages. Same objects (cups, beans, milk, hot water) and same accepted output as a hotel coffee station, achieved inside a purpose-built machine workspace.

sources.title: AI Flying Off the Shelves: Restocking Robot Rolls Out to Hundreds of Japanese Convenience Stores | NVIDIA Blog
sources.claim: Telexistence's TX SCARA autonomously restocks refrigerated beverage shelves in hundreds of FamilyMart convenience stores, working on a track in the back room with over 98% automatic success and only rare remote intervention.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: replenishing a self-service display with packaged drinks and snacks. Comparable objects and precision, but only inside a rail-mounted, purpose-built cooler workspace whose crates are staged by staff.

sources.system: Chef Robotics meal assembly robot / Chef+
sources.title: We've Raised a $43.1M Series A to Accelerate Our AI-Enabled Robot Deployments | Chef Robotics
sources.claim: Chef Robotics' meal-assembly robots are deployed in food production facilities, dispensing portions of varied ingredients into trays moving on fixtured production lines; tens of millions of servings produced.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: portioning food into serving containers. Shows food-handling automation exists as a single fixed dispensing station over a conveyor with human-filled hoppers, not as staging of a multi-item self-serve buffet with dishware and equipment.

sources.title: Miso Robotics develops smaller, faster Flippy | Restaurant Dive
sources.claim: Miso Robotics' Flippy autonomously works a fry station inside fast-food kitchens, but installations remain a single purpose-built cell at roughly a dozen restaurants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: hot food preparation for service. Demonstrates commercial hot-food robots occupy one dedicated fixtured station (fryer plus hoppers) and do not stage, transport or arrange a service area.

sources.title: Hotel Industry Executives Turn to Delivery Robots | Relay Robotics
sources.claim: Robots actually deployed in US hotels (Marriott, Hilton, Westin, Holiday Inn) are autonomous wheeled delivery units that transport items through corridors and lobbies; they carry payloads but perform no manipulation of food, dishware or equipment.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: in-hotel material handling. Establishes the current ceiling of hotel-floor (E2) robot capability — navigation and transport only, with no arms to set up or replenish a food service area.
